abstract: In chickens and humans, classical class I molecules of the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) have a spectrum of correlated properties, including cell surface expression and peptide repertoire. Understanding the impact of these promiscuous generalists and fastidious specialists is of considerable interest. The promiscuous BF2 molecule from the chicken B21 haplotype, BF2*21:01, binds a wide range of peptides by remodelling the peptide-binding site, allowing co-variation of the anchor residues at peptide positions P 2 and P c-2 , and binding of an anchor residue at Pc. Using in vitro refolding assays with peptides and peptide libraries, determining thermostability and crystal structures, and analysing a chicken B21 cell line by immunopeptidomics, we found that BF2*21:01 will accommodate many possible combinations at P 2 and P c-2 , as well as several hydrophobic amino acids at P c . However, marked preferences for particular peptide lengths, particular amino acids at the three anchor residues, and particular combinations of amino acids at P 2 and P c-2 as well as at P 3 and P c-3 together lead to high frequencies of major peptides while still allowing the possibility of presenting a wide peptide repertoire. These simplifying principles may eventually allow predictions of pathogen peptides with stable binding for this iconic promiscuous class I molecule, as well as providing the data for more sophisticated peptide prediction methods.

title: Cell death in context: From mechanisms to interventions.
abstract: When, how, and why cells die, and what happens when they survive, have profound consequences for development, immunity, and disease. To coincide with the Cell Press Symposium "Taking programmed cell death from mechanisms to interventions," we bring together perspectives from researchers across career stages and areas of cell death research. From emerging mechanisms and consequences of cell death to opportunities for therapeutic intervention, these voices highlight a rapidly evolving field and the questions that will shape its future.

title: HRS dephosphorylation at membrane contact sites promotes sorting within multivesicular endosomes.
abstract: HRS is a receptor tyrosine kinase substrate and ESCRT machinery component. It enables sorting of ubiquitylated cargo into multivesicular endosomes (MVEs) for lysosomal degradation but also functions in receptor recycling. We show that co-depletion of its ESCRT-0 binding partners, STAM1 and STAM2, recapitulates defects in EGF receptor (EGFR) sorting onto intraluminal vesicles (ILVs) but does not mirror the increased MVE size evident after HRS depletion. Using mutagenesis of the endogenous gene or introduction of APEX2-tagged HRS variants, we find that HRS Y329/334 phosphorylation is dispensable for EGFR sorting and MVE size control. AnnexinA1 mediates ER:endosomal membrane contacts and promotes EGF-stimulated ILV formation. We show that reduced ILV formation on AnnexinA1 depletion is accompanied by increased HRS phosphorylation, likely through reduced HRS dephosphorylation by ER-localised PTP1B. Conversely, Y329/334 mutation renders ILV formation insensitive to AnnexinA1 depletion. Our data suggest that rapid HRS dephosphorylation at ER:MVE contacts promotes efficient ILV formation.

title: Sex-biased enhancers shape transcriptional sex differences across human tissues.
abstract: Sex differences influence human physiology and disease susceptibility, yet the regulatory mechanisms underlying sex-biased transcription remain unclear. Here we present eModule, which quantifies enhancer RNA (eRNA) transcription from Genotype-Tissue Expression (GTEx) RNA-seq data to identify sex-biased active enhancers across 41 human tissues. We find that 47% of transcriptionally active enhancers are sex-biased in at least one tissue. These enhancers are tissue-specific, often organized into super-enhancers with chromatin signatures, and associated with rewiring of transcription factor (TF) regulatory networks. Evolutionary analyses reveal that many sex-biased enhancers are primate-specific and derived from transposable element (TE) exaptation, with contributing TE families enriched for binding sites of sex-associated TFs. Sex-biased enhancers also harbor variants linked to traits with sex differences and are inferred to regulate therapeutic target genes. Our findings position sex-biased enhancer activity as a regulatory layer shaping sex-biased transcription, with implications for regulatory evolution, GWAS interpretation, and sex-informed precision medicine.

title: Tau-driven hyperexcitability of locus coeruleus noradrenergic neurons underlies sleep fragmentation and cognitive decline in mice.
abstract: Early sleep disruption is a hallmark of preclinical Alzheimer's disease (AD), but its underlying mechanisms are unclear. The locus coeruleus (LC) dopamine-β-hydroxylase noradrenergic (LCDBH) neurons are vulnerable to early tau pathology in AD. Using P301S transgenic mice and cell-type-specific tau overexpression models, we show that pathological tau accumulation selectively increases the intrinsic excitability of LCDBH neurons. Tau-induced neuronal hyperactivity disrupts sleep homeostasis, reduces non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep and slow-wave activity, increases sleep fragmentation and microarousals, and delays both anesthetic induction and sleep onset. Furthermore, tau overexpression in LCDBH neurons leads to significant recognition memory deficits. Notably, optogenetic suppression of LCDBH-tau neuronal activity reverses sleep disturbances and rescues cognitive dysfunction. Our findings demonstrate that tau-driven hyperexcitability of LCDBH neurons is a core driver of early sleep and cognitive impairments in AD, providing a mechanistic insight and potential target for preclinical AD treatment.

title: The DUF2439/RADIF domain of ZGRF1 is a RAD51 interactor and facilitator.
abstract: DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) are extremely toxic DNA lesions that can cause loss of genetic information and cell death if left unrepaired. During S and G2 phases of the cell cycle, DSBs can be repaired by homologous recombination (HR). The human zinc finger GRF-type containing 1 (ZGRF1) helicase and RAD54B translocase both promote HR. Here, we report that the DUF2439 domain, shared by ZGRF1 and RAD54B, interacts with RAD51 in vitro, and provides resistance to the DNA interstrand-crosslinking agent mitomycin C (MMC). Furthermore, the DUF2439 domain is necessary for recruitment of ZGRF1 to MMC-induced foci. Finally, we show synergistic roles for ZGRF1 and RAD54B in facilitating homology-directed repair of a defined DSB, consistent with the reduced survival of double-mutant cells after treatment with MMC or the PARP inhibitor talazoparib. Based on these results, we propose that the DUF2439 domain recruits ZGRF1 and RAD54B to DNA lesions, where they facilitate RAD51 function to promote HR.

title: Brain-wide activity imaging with electron microscopy reveals a distributed brain network for processing threatening somatosensory stimuli.
abstract: To understand how brains work, neural activity must be overlayed onto synaptic-resolution circuit architecture. Recent advances in light-sheet microscopy (LSM) enable whole-brain, cellular-resolution imaging of activity of all cell bodies; however, most neurons from such datasets cannot be identified. In most organisms, neurons are identifiable based on their projections (and not based on cell body position), which, when densely labeled, cannot be resolved using LSM. Here, we present a novel methodology to overcome this by combining whole-brain activity imaging with subsequent volume electron microscopy imaging of the same brain to visualize neuronal projections and identify neurons with interesting activity. We used this approach to identify brain neurons that process input from multisensory (nociceptive and mechanosensory) Basin interneurons that trigger vigorous escape in Drosophila larvae in response to threatening somatosensory stimuli. After whole-brain imaging of neuronal activity during Basin activation, we imaged the same brain with an enhanced focused ion-beam electron microscope (eFIB-SEM). We registered the functional and anatomical volumes and reconstructed (in the eFIB-SEM volume) the projections of neurons that responded to Basin activation to determine their developmental lineage and identity. This revealed a distributed network for processing threatening somatosensory stimuli that trigger vigorous escape spanning 25 distinct lineages and many distinct brain areas. Our workflow provides a powerful framework for mapping neuronal activity onto structure across an entire brain, yielding novel insights into the distributed central processing of somatosensory stimuli.

title: Hyperdivergent haplotypes control melanic camouflage in a polymorphic moth.
abstract: A majority of moths use melanic pigmentation to blend into the visual environment, and some species display genetically controlled color polymorphisms that provide tractable systems for dissecting the genetic basis of camouflage. Here, we leveraged the natural polymorphism of Anticarsia gemmatalis moths to map a major-effect gene that controls melanic variation and study its developmental roles using expression and loss-of-function assays. Genome-wide association mapping identifies the ivory:mir-193 non-coding RNA locus as a major locus of melanic variation, with highly divergent haplotypes differentiating the Light and Dark morphs. Second, the expression of ivory:mir-193 prefigures the melanic coloration of each morph and suggests that cis-regulatory variation at this locus determines the difference in adult pattern. Finally, CRISPR disruption of the ivory promoter and mir-193 hairpin region each abolishes melanic scale pigmentation, demonstrating that this lnc-pri-miRNA module is required for dark-scale differentiation. These findings corroborate the emerging role of ivory:mir-193 as a key factor in the development of melanic patterning and highlight its unique propensity to repeatedly drive phenotypic variation of adaptive potential in butterflies and moths.

title: Illusory cold desensitizes touch.
abstract: In Jack London's To Build a Fire, the doomed protagonist notes that "the tremendous cold had already driven the life out of his fingers… dead fingers could neither touch nor clutch." Indeed, our hands are numbed when exposed to cold, a desensitization process traditionally attributed to biophysical and physiological effects on mechanoreceptor and afferent responses.1 Yet perception is not based solely on sensory inputs and often reflects prior beliefs and expectations.2 Accordingly, the mere experience of coldness, given its association with tactile desensitization, conceivably modulates touch independent of physical effects. We dissociated the physical and subjective influences of cooling on touch by leveraging the thermal referral illusion,3,4,5,6,7 in which cooling of the index and ring fingers induces an illusory perception of coldness that is referred to the middle finger, which did not experience local cooling. We found that both veridical and illusory cold elevated tactile detection thresholds. Threshold shifts scaled with subjective ratings of cold intensity, which varied with thermal adaptation. Thermal referral induction did not result in changes to skin temperature, ruling out indirect physical effects on the tested finger. To account for cold effects on touch, we implemented a computational model incorporating both physical and subjective factors by simulating changes in tactile afferent spiking activity8 and modulation of decision computations, respectively. The model reproduced empirical cooling effects on afferent responses9 and recapitulated psychophysical detection patterns. Our results reveal that subjective thermal perception contributes to cold-induced attenuation of touch, highlighting how multimodal experiences and expectations shape somatosensation.

title: Tubulin autoregulation factors recruit γ-tubulin to non-centrosomal MTOCs for neuronal microtubule nucleation.
abstract: Neuronal function and survival depend on stereotyped non-centrosomal microtubule (MT) arrays. How these arrays form remains poorly understood. Here, we found that two factors previously implicated in tubulin mRNA turnover control neuronal MT content through γ-tubulin-dependent nucleation. In C. elegans neurons, loss of scaper, ttc5, or both reduced MT numbers to a similar degree as depletion of γ-tubulin, the main MT nucleator. Using conditional single-cell degradation alleles and endogenous tagging, we find that scaper and ttc5 are required to recruit γ-tubulin to non-centrosomal MT organizing centers (MTOCs). SCAPER is also instructive, as its overexpression raises γ-tubulin levels at nucleation sites and increases MT density. SCAPER, TTC5, and γ-tubulin are dispensable for developmental axon growth but play essential roles during regeneration, where SCAPER recruits γ-tubulin to a growth-cone-localized MTOC to orient MT nucleation. Last, SCAPER is required for activity-dependent MT nucleation in rat hippocampal neurons, suggesting a conserved role. These findings reveal mechanisms governing neuronal cytoskeleton assembly and function and suggest potential crosstalk between tubulin autoregulation and MT nucleation.

title: Tubulin autoregulation mediator TTC5 regulates neuronal morphology and migration.
abstract: Microtubule dynamics are essential for neuronal development, yet how neurons regulate tubulin levels remains poorly understood. Tetratricopeptide repeat domain 5 (TTC5) mediates tubulin autoregulation, the co-translational degradation of tubulin transcripts in response to excess soluble tubulin, and TTC5 mutations cause cerebral atrophy with speech and motor impairment. Here, we show that tubulin autoregulation is active in induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived cortical neurons and depends on TTC5. TTC5 loss, or structure-guided mutations that disable autoregulation suppress microtubule polymerization, axonal outgrowth, and arborization, while enhancing cellular motility. Motility changes extend to non-neuronal cells, where they alter focal adhesion dynamics and can be rescued by manipulating soluble tubulin levels. Furthermore, downregulation of TTC5 interactor and autoregulation mediator S-phase cyclin A-associated protein in the endoplasmic reticulum (SCAPER) also suppresses neurite outgrowth and enhances motility. In vivo, TTC5 loss in mouse cortical projection neurons disrupts axon and dendrite arborization and causes hypermigration, recapitulating the cellular phenotypes observed in vitro. Patient-derived TTC5 disease mutants phenocopy this motility dysregulation, directly linking loss of TTC5 function to neurological deficits seen in patients. Together, these findings establish TTC5 as an essential regulator of neuronal morphogenesis and connectivity, with direct implications for TTC5-associated neurodevelopmental disease.

title: Learning-dependent hippocampal-striatal reorganization during sequential decision-making in pigeons.
abstract: Adaptive sequential decision-making requires animals to learn how actions shape future states and rewards while adjusting behavioral strategies as experience accumulates. Although the hippocampus is implicated in state-structure representation and the striatum in value learning, how learning strategies evolve from exploratory sampling to efficient exploitation and how hippocampal-striatal interactions reorganize alongside this transition remain unclear. We trained six pigeons of undetermined sex to perform a probabilistic two-step decision task while simultaneously recording behavioral choices and hippocampal-striatal local field potentials. Strategy evolution was tracked using a dynamic reinforcement-learning framework in which model-based, model-free, and weighted model-based/model-free models were fitted across sliding windows. Hippocampal-striatal functional coordination was assessed using phase-locking analysis, and directed predictive influence was quantified using kernel Granger causality. The weighted model best explained choice dynamics, indicating a shift from model-based-like control during early acquisition toward model-free-like control during later stable performance. This behavioral shift was accompanied by two complementary neural changes: hippocampal-striatal phase coordination increased across learning, whereas hippocampus-to-striatum directed predictive influence decreased and covaried positively with model-based-like strategy weight. Direction-ratio analysis showed that hippocampus-to-striatum remained the predominant direction throughout learning, indicating reduced influence rather than directional reversal. After acquisition, hippocampus-to-striatum directed influence was not uniformly reduced but remained relatively preserved during rare, low-value, unrewarded, or less expected events. Together, these findings reveal a learning-dependent reorganization of hippocampal-striatal dynamics, in which increasing functional coordination is accompanied by reduced but condition-dependent hippocampal-to-striatal influence as behavior becomes more stable and efficient.Significance Statement Adaptive learning requires coordinated changes in behavioral strategy and neural interactions as animals progress from exploration to stable performance. Here, we show that pigeons gradually shifted from flexible, model-based-like control toward more stable, model-free-like behavior during sequential learning. In parallel, hippocampal-striatal interactions underwent a complementary reorganization: phase coordination progressively increased, whereas hippocampus-to-striatum directed predictive influence decreased with declining model-based-like control. Importantly, this directed influence remained relatively preserved during rare, low-value, or unrewarded events. These findings link behavioral strategy transition to the dynamic reorganization of hippocampal-striatal interactions, revealing how neural systems may simultaneously support efficient learned behavior while retaining sensitivity to behaviorally informative events.

title: Multiple combinations of GPCR activation gate the induction of NMDAR-independent LTD in mouse visual cortex.
abstract: Activity-dependent synaptic weakening, including long-term depression (LTD), is a fundamental mechanism underlying experience-dependent circuit remodeling. At excitatory synapses, two mechanistically distinct forms of LTD have been identified: NMDAR-LTD, triggered by activation of NMDA receptors, and mGluR-LTD, mediated by group I metabotropic glutamate receptors. NMDAR-LTD is the best-characterized form and has been described in numerous brain regions. In contrast, in cortical synapses mGluR-LTD has been investigated primarily in the hippocampus, where it requires mGluR5 activation and its molecular mechanisms are well established. Although NMDAR-LTD is also well documented in the neocortex, mGluR-LTD remains comparatively poorly characterized, particularly in primary sensory cortices, despite growing evidence that mGluR signaling contributes to sensory deprivation-induced synaptic remodeling. We examined mGluR-LTD in slices of primary visual cortex of rats and mice of all sexes and found that layer II/III pyramidal neurons do express an NMDAR-independent LTD. Like in CA1, mGluR-LTD in V1 depends on mGluR5 activation and ongoing protein synthesis regulated by FMRP. Unlike CA1, however, where activation of mGluR5 alone is sufficient to induce mGluR-LTD, induction in V1 requires the co-activation of at least two neuromodulatory receptors, including mGluR5 together with muscarinic, noradrenergic, or serotonergic receptors. This more stringent gating mechanism may reflect the tighter constraints on synaptic plasticity in the neocortex, consistent with the view that the hippocampus and neocortex are specialized for rapid and gradual learning, respectively.Significance statement At excitatory synapses, two mechanistically distinct forms of long-term depression (LTD) have been identified: NMDAR-LTD and mGluR-LTD. While NMDAR-LTD is widespread, mGluR-LTD has been studied primarily in the hippocampus and remains poorly characterized in sensory cortices, despite evidence that mGluRs contribute to sensory deprivation-induced synaptic remodeling. This study shows that an NMDAR-independent form of LTD can be induced in visual cortical slices. Unlike hippocampus, where activation of mGluR5 alone is sufficient to induce mGluR-LTD, induction in visual cortex requires the co-activation of at least two neuromodulatory receptors, including mGluR5 together with muscarinic, noradrenergic, or serotonergic receptors. This stricter gating mechanism may reflect the tighter constraints on synaptic plasticity in the neocortex, consistent with its role in gradual, rather than rapid, learning.

title: Opioid-glutamate interactions modulate intrinsically rewarded communication in European starlings.
abstract: Affiliative, non-sexual vocal communication is essential for social learning and bonding, yet relatively little is known about its neural bases. Past research on songbirds demonstrates that song produced in affiliative, non-sexual flocks correlates positively with a bird's intrinsic reward state, and the link between song and reward is regulated by mu opioid receptors (MORs) in the medial preoptic area (MPOA). RNAseq studies also reveal a strong positive association between affiliative song and glutamatergic gene expression in MPOA, with NMDA receptor 1 (GRIN1) and glutamate receptor scaffolding protein (Shank2) correlating strongly with affiliative singing. In male European starlings we tested the hypothesis that MOR-glutamate interactions in the MPOA regulate affiliative communication. Peripheral administration of the MOR agonist fentanyl increased affiliative singing and calling behavior while reducing stress-related behavior, beak wiping. The effects on vocal but not stress-related behavior were prevented by administration of the NMDA receptor antagonist MK-801. c-Fos mapping revealed that fentanyl increased neural activity in caudal MPOA (cMPOA) and interconnected regions implicated in social behavior, song production, and reward, and that these effects were reversed by MK-801. To identify a local site of MOR-glutamate interaction, we used AAV shRNA to downregulate Shank2 in MPOA. This manipulation prevented fentanyl from stimulating affiliative singing behavior, also without affecting stress reduction, suggesting that MOR-glutamate interactions in the MPOA facilitate social communication but not associated stress reduction. Together these findings provide the first experimental evidence that MOR-glutamate interactions within the MPOA, particularly the cMPOA, contribute to affiliative, rewarding vocal communication.Significance Statement Affiliative, non-sexual vocal communication is fundamental to social cohesion and well-being, yet its neural mechanisms are poorly understood. This study identifies a critical role for interactions between mu opioid receptors and glutamatergic signaling in promoting non-sexual, rewarding vocal communication. In a songbird experimental system, we demonstrate that NMDA receptor activity and the postsynaptic glutamate receptor scaffolding protein Shank2 are required for opioid facilitation of affiliative song. Our findings further reveal the medial preoptic area, particularly its caudal subdivision, to be an important site of this opioid-glutamate interaction. Together, these results extend opioid-glutamate interaction frameworks beyond classic reward circuits and suggest the existence of a conserved neural mechanism supporting affiliative social behavior across vertebrates.

title: Physiological Representation of Social Evaluation: Modeling Human Eye Movements, Pupillary, and Neuronal Responses to Faces.
abstract: Face-based social evaluations are ubiquitous and consequential, yet it remains unclear how these evaluations are represented in spontaneous physiological responses. Across four studies (222 participants: 142 females, 57 males, 23 unreported; 503 neurons), we used a data-driven modeling framework to examine how facial appearance shapes eye movements, pupillary responses, and neuronal activity during face viewing. We asked what these responses reveal about the underlying social evaluations. Pupillary responses and hippocampal firing during saccades were driven by facial variation associated with an integrated combination of valence and power evaluations; fixation duration on the eyes and hippocampal firing during fixations were more selectively tuned to threat-related evaluations; amygdalar firing primarily tracked approachability-related valence. A prospective validation study confirmed that novel faces synthesized along these modeled directions elicited the predicted physiological responses in new participants. We also found evidence of individual differences: social anxiety selectively heightened the sensitivity of pupillary responses to face evaluations. These findings suggest that distinct physiological responses across attention, autonomic arousal, and medial temporal lobe activity reflect distinct but related facets of face-based social evaluation.Significance Statement Everyday social decisions hinge on split-second impressions of unfamiliar faces. When we see a face, we instantly judge the person's likely intention (positive ↔ negative valence) and social influence (high ↔ low power). Across four complementary studies, we show that these evaluative processes are reflected in physiological responses to faces across overt attention, autonomic arousal, and subcortical neuronal firing. Different physiological systems reflected partially distinct but related facets of social-evaluative meaning, including integrated valence-and-power, threat-related, and approachability-related evaluation.

abstract: Vagus nerve stimulation has shown promising neuroprotective and anti-inflammatory effects in progressive neurodegenerative disorders such as Parkinson’s disease. However, its invasive nature introduces procedural and device-related risks. Here we introduce a magnetoelectric particulate system for oral delivery and non-invasive vagus nerve stimulation through the gut. The system comprises a magneto-responsive nickel ferrite core and a piezoelectric barium titanate shell, conjugated with capsaicin to specifically target TRPV1 receptors, ensuring effective adherence to the stomach lining after oral administration. Upon magnetic field stimulation, the particles generate electrical pulses that activate vagal afferent fibres, engaging the nucleus tractus solitarius in the brainstem via the gut−brain axis. This activation enhances norepinephrine production in the locus coeruleus and dopamine synthesis in the substantia nigra. Vagal efferent activation triggers the cholinergic anti-inflammatory pathway, mitigating both neuroinflammation and systemic inflammation. This non-invasive approach demonstrates potential for alleviating motor symptoms and non-motor anxiety in Parkinson’s disease, offering valuable insights into its mechanisms and clinical applications.

abstract: The ER membrane complex (EMC) facilitates insertion of integral membrane proteins into the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) lipid bilayer. Recent years have seen significant progress in understanding the structural aspects of EMC, but the identity of EMC-client proteins and EMC’s functional roles throughout evolution remain less well understood. Here we delete the essential EMC3 subunit in the liver and adipose tissues of mice and examine the impact of EMC loss-of-function in a range of metabolic and lipid homeostasis models. The absence of EMC3 in either the liver or adipose tissues results in defective storage of triglycerides and perturbations in lipid droplet (LD) homeostasis. EMC-deficient adipose tissues have reduced ability to mediate fat storage in mice on a high-fat diet and are unable to support non-shivering thermogenesis. Proteomic analyses of EMC3-deficient tissues show reduced levels of FITM2, a key regulator of LD biogenesis and ER homeostasis, identifying FITM2 as an EMC client. Deletion of EMC3 in the Drosophila fat body reveals similar defects in LD homeostasis, which can be rescued by a FITM2 mutant whose biogenesis was EMC-independent. Together, our results indicate that the EMC plays a key evolutionarily conserved role in the biogenesis of machinery maintaining triglyceride storage in metazoans.

abstract: Aging-related cognitive decline, including impairments in spatial orientation and memory, has been linked to dysfunction within the hippocampus and medial entorhinal cortex (MEC). However, the cellular and molecular alterations underlying MEC aging remain poorly understood. Here, we show that old mice exhibit a reduced proportion of grid cells and decreased spatial stability. Transcriptomic profiling of the MEC using 10x Genomics Visium technology reveals 1664 differentially expressed genes between young and old mice. Among these, Bglap3 is identified as a marker gene for a subpopulation of layer III neurons that showed an age-associated reduction in cell number. Chemogenetic silencing of Bglap3 + neurons in young mice impairs spatial tuning of MEC neurons. Together, these findings elucidate cellular and molecular mechanisms contributing to age-related MEC dysfunction and suggest that the loss of Bglap3 + neurons may underlie spatial coding deficits in aging.

abstract: Spatiotemporal compartmentalization is a powerful cellular strategy for concentrating biomolecules, buffering noise, and creating local niches, that enable robust information-processing and reaction cascades. While compartments formed by coacervation are known to modulate catalytic activity, how reaction kinetics and interphase mass transfer between the coacervate and the surrounding phase jointly regulate catalysis within these dynamically evolving compartments remains poorly understood. Here we introduce synthetic coacervate-containing droplets (CCDs)—microfluidically generated arrays of single droplets containing single coacervates in equilibrium with the dilute phase—to investigate coupled reaction-diffusion dynamics under confinement. Using CCDs formed by complex coacervation of oppositely charged polyelectrolytes, we quantify guest molecular partitioning and enzymatic dephosphorylation reactions within single droplets. By integrating spatiotemporal imaging, bulk kinetics, and mathematical modeling, we quantitatively link enzymatic activity to dynamic molecular redistributions across phases, revealing how reaction-driven fluxes regulate enzymatic reactions within biphasic droplets and demonstrating the noise buffering capability of the coacervate phase.

abstract: Plants must continually balance growth with arrest, especially under stress. Auxin signaling acts as a central regulatory hub in this process, yet the mechanisms that dynamically tune auxin signaling in real time remain unknown. Here, we use the light-gated, Ca 2+ -permeable Channelrhodopsin 2 variant XXM2.0 to optogenetically impose defined Ca 2+ signatures on Arabidopsis root cells. Repetitive light activation triggers cytosolic Ca 2+ signals that in turn suppress membrane depolarization and Ca 2+ transients triggered by exogenous auxin. Moreover, prolonged optogenetic Ca 2+ stimulation affects auxin-responsive transcriptional reprogramming. As phenotypic output, reversible inhibition of root growth by suppressing cell division and elongation is observed. We further identify a candidate CaM7–CNGC14 module that likely mediates Ca 2+ -dependent gating of responsiveness to exogenous auxin as well as Ca 2+ -dependent root growth inhibition. Our study thus introduces a synthetic biology approach to decompose calcium–auxin crosstalk in plant cells, and demonstrates that optogenetically imposed cytosolic Ca 2+ signals act as dynamic regulators of auxin susceptibility in roots.

abstract: Chromosomal position is known to influence gene expression, yet its impact on the function of genetic circuits remains largely unexplored. Here, we expand the scope of positional effects by showing that circuit function can be reprogrammed solely through spatial positioning. Using bacteria as a living chassis, we engineer 219 spatially distinct genetic circuits of four different types—three regulatory cascade circuits and a toggle switch. We show that spatial positioning can not only modulate circuit performance but also switch circuits between different dynamics, giving rise to new operational modes as circuit complexity increases. A mathematical model parameterized from experimental data predicts three distinct functional regimes for the toggle switch and links chromosomal position to switch stability through noise. This reprogramming is fundamentally mediated by changes in gene expression noise, moving beyond simple Boolean (on/off) or analog (more/less) interpretations of gene regulation and towards stochastic and probabilistic principles for cellular computation.

abstract: Androgenetic alopecia affects over 1.5 billion individuals, causing progressive hair loss with psychological and quality-of-life burdens. Current pharmacological treatment for androgenetic alopecia faces challenges due to systemic side effects from oral medications or limited efficacy of topical applications. Herein we develop a comb-shaped bioelectronic system, named “Detangle”, for efficient androgenetic alopecia treatment during daily hair combing. This system features electronic teeth embedded with height-differentiated electrodes and integrated drug-loading modules, which generate an enhanced electric field penetrating up to ~9 times deeper into hair follicle regions than conventional external application. We show that the localized electric field synchronizes electro-stimulating hair follicles, and electro-delivering vascular endothelial growth factor A encoding plasmid and steroid 5-alpha-reductase 2 targeting siRNA into follicular cells to promote angiogenesis and suppress androgen synthesis. Through the synergistic regulation of cellular metabolism, the system significantly increases hair restoration efficacy in an androgenetic alopecia mouse model, improving the outcome from ~70% to nearly 100% within one month compared to conventional topical minoxidil treatment. The Detangle system proves safe and effective for deep tissue delivery in dermatology.

abstract: Repair of double-strand breaks via non-homologous end joining requires the synapsis of DNA ends. APLF is emerging as an important repair factor, capable of forming synaptic bridges in the presence of the Ku70/Ku80 heterodimer. However, only a single one-to-one interaction between Ku70/Ku80 and APLF has been reported to date, which is fundamentally insufficient for synapsis. Moreover, it remains unclear how APLF-mediated bridging of Ku70/Ku80 heterodimers is prevented in the absence of double-strand breaks. Using a combination of single-molecule techniques, including Mass Photometry, Atomic Force Microscopy, and Magnetic and Optical Tweezers, we demonstrate that APLF-mediated synapsis requires threading of at least two Ku70/Ku80 heterodimers per DNA end. We show that this requirement stems from the need for a simultaneous interaction of two poly(ADP-ribose) binding Zinc Fingers in APLF with threaded poly(ADP-ribosyl)ated Ku70/Ku80s on a single DNA. We further provide evidence that long non-coding RNA NIHCOLE cooperatively binds up to four Ku70/Ku80, consistent with a synapsis efficiency enhancement mechanism based on the bridging of two Kus70Ku80s bound on both sides of the break. Our results propose a model for the physiological significance of Ku70/Ku80 threading and a regulatory mechanism based on multivalency that restricts APLF-mediated bridging to DNA-bound Ku70/Ku80.

abstract: Due to the assumed plasticity of the immature brain, early-life brain alterations are thought to lead to better recoveries in comparison to the mature brain. Despite clinical needs, how neuronal networks and associated behaviors are affected by early-life brain stresses, such as pediatric concussions, have been overlooked. Here we provide first evidence in male mice that a single early-life concussion durably increases neuronal activity in the somatosensory cortex into adulthood, disrupting neuronal integration while the animal is performing sensory-related tasks. This represents a clinically relevant mechanism that was previously unappreciated for understanding impairment of sensory-related behavior performance. We also demonstrate that pharmacological modulation of the endocannabinoid system a year post-concussion is well-suited to rescue neuronal activity and plasticity, and normalizes sensory-related behavioral performance. These findings identify persistent alterations in cortical sensory processing following early-life concussion and demonstrate that neuronal and behavioral deficits remain amenable to pharmacological intervention long after injury.

abstract: Proper organ development requires the coordination of cell type-specific differentiation programs with general maturation processes through precise spatiotemporal gene regulation. In plants, where RNA polymerase pausing is not well established, alternative mechanisms must ensure this coordination. Here, using single-cell resolution transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility data, we reconstruct developmental trajectories of the Arabidopsis root ground tissue to investigate these mechanisms. We describe phased transcriptional landscapes governing the transition from stem cell to early differentiation, in which chromatin accessibility marks the activation of key developmental regulators. A major transcriptional switch in the late meristematic zone, underpinned by extensive chromatin remodeling, drives the transition from cell division to differentiation. Leveraging machine learning to examine integrated transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility trajectories, we identify GATA transcription factors (TFs) as central coordinators of this switch; a role we validate experimentally. We show that the GATA TFs sit at the tipping point of a feedback-driven bistable system that integrates inputs from auxin and cytokinin to balance proliferation and differentiation, ensuring temporal precision in root development at both the tissue and organ scales.

abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition. Although the gut microbiome has been implicated in ASD, prior studies have insufficiently addressed clinical heterogeneity. Here, we perform shotgun metagenomic sequencing on stool samples from 720 children with ASD (median age 8 years, 87% male) and 151 matched controls. Children with ASD are stratified into three severity groups using 14 symptom subscales covering core features and co-occurring psychopathologies. Microbiome composition is significantly associated with clinical severity and individual symptoms; however, the proportion of microbiome variance explained by these clinical factors is modest (R 2 = 0.0017–0.0065). Children with higher severity show reduced abundance of Lachnospiraceae bacterium AM48_27BH, a short-chain fatty acid producer, together with reduced predicted capacity of GABA-related modules (GABA synthesis II, putrescine degradation and GHB degradation), while NAD+ salvage pathways show trend-level associations with severity. Sensory atypicalities have the largest number of associated microbial markers and show trend-level links to reduced predicted capacity for degradation of excitatory neurotransmitters. These findings demonstrate that gut microbiome composition varies across the ASD severity spectrum and that different symptom domains differ in their relevance to microbiome alterations. Whether alterations in GABAergic metabolism contribute to clinical severity, and whether microbial features are preferentially linked to sensory atypicalities, remain to be tested in mechanistic and longitudinal studies.

abstract: Inositol-requiring enzyme 1α (IRE1α) and the downstream spliced form of X-Box Binding Protein 1 (XBP1s) have been identified as tumor promotors. However, how IRE1α–XBP1s signaling affects tumor progression in a non-cell autonomous manner remains unclear. Here we show that the hepatocyte IRE1α–XBP1s axis unexpectedly inhibits liver metastasis by confining local metainflammation. Genetic ablation of IRE1α or XBP1 in mouse hepatocytes exacerbates liver metastasis due to the accumulation of inflammatory monocytes (IMs). Mechanistically, a non-canonical Forkhead box O1 (FoxO1)-glutamine synthetase (GS) pathway endows the IRE1α- or XBP1-null hepatocytes with the metabolic activity to secrete glutamine, which is necessary and sufficient for IM fitness. Reintroduction of hepatocyte XBP1s or blockade of glutamine metabolism effectively reduces IMs and mitigates disease progression. Importantly, clinical patient survival with liver metastases positively correlates with hepatocyte XBP1s expression. Our study defines a paradigm of hepatocyte–IM interaction that can be leveraged to treat liver metastasis.

abstract: Neuromuscular compartments provide the functional substrate for finger-specific motor control, yet their in vivo three-dimensional (3D) architecture remains unresolved because of the absence of clear fascial landmarks for imaging. Here, we present a multimodal imaging framework combining ultrasound and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to provide volumetric compartment segmentation and in vivo architectural reconstruction of the flexor digitorum superficialis. During isolated finger flexion, tissue movement directions estimated from dynamic ultrasound delineate compartment contours, which are mapped into a 3D MRI reference to generate volumetric compartment masks. Using these masks as constraints, tractography reconstructs 3D fiber trajectories and yields compartment-specific architectural measurements. In ten healthy individuals, compartment topology and fiber orientations were consistent with classic cadaveric anatomy, and estimated compartments accurately predicted surface electromyography amplitude distributions. This framework provides 3D fiber trajectories and quantitative parameters for finger-specific computational models, establishing a foundation for subject-specific neuromuscular digital twins and next-generation neuromuscular interfaces.

abstract: Evolutionary relationships among homologous enzymes can be leveraged to introduce large numbers of amino acid substitutions for improved functional properties. Here, we combine evolution-informed design (EVdesign) with rational design to engineer improved poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) hydrolases (PETases). Designs derived from multiple PETases reveal strong parent-dependent differences in success and performance, with Thermobifida fusca Tf Cut2 emerging as the most design-amenable scaffold. Increasing sequence diversification reduces the number of active enzymes but broadens performance variance, enabling discovery of high-performing outliers. Four rational mutations overcome a thermostability bottleneck in Tf Cut2 and this variant provides a robust scaffold for iterative EVdesign, which further improves activity. Overall, we experimentally test 603 designs from eight parent PETases. More than 400 variants containing 12-68 substitutions were able to depolymerize PET, nearly all outperforming their parent enzymes, and many approach benchmark LCC-ICCG performance in partial conversion assays. These results establish EVdesign as a robust strategy for generating diverse, high-activity enzymes.

abstract: GWAS have identified thousands of SNPs associated with different human phenotypes. Most SNPs are located in non-coding regions of the genome, where a small subset of causal SNPs is thought to contribute to risk by regulating transcription. However, identification of such causal variants remains challenging due to linkage disequilibrium, where blocks of SNPs are inherited together. Here, we perform a massively parallel reporter assay called SuRE in human neural stem cells to assess the transcriptional regulatory potential of 7.1 million SNPs. We identify 7,002 SNPs with regulatory potential (emVars) among the 484,057 SNPs with sufficiently high expression. These emVars are enriched in enhancers and often coincide with binding sites for transcription factors, such as ZBTB33, YY1, and ETS factors. We overlap SuRE data with eQTL data to pinpoint likely gene-regulatory variants. Additionally, combining SuRE data with GWAS for seven neuropsychiatric phenotypes identifies 187 emVars in risk loci containing 183,186 SNPs assessed by SuRE. In conclusion, our SuRE dataset provides a rich source to prioritize genetic variants that may be relevant for complex human phenotypes.

abstract: The hippocampus serves as a hub of cognition, and its subfields differ in their susceptibility to aging and neurological disorders. Here, we established normative references for hippocampal and subfield volumes using 3D T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans from 34,789 healthy individuals (range from 4 to 85 years), revealing varied peak ages (27.4-40.1 years) across subfields. We then mapped the hippocampus and its subfields across various neurological disorders (mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, cerebral small vessel disease, and multiple sclerosis) by deriving personalized deviation (centile) scores from these references in 3,521 patients. These centile scores captured disease-specific hippocampal abnormalities, supported disease classification, and were associated with cognitive performance, longitudinal cognitive outcomes, and disease progression across disorders. Finally, a personalized hippocampal health report was developed to facilitate clinical translation. These findings demonstrate the value of hippocampal and subfield normative references for personalized diagnosis, cognitive assessment, and prognostic evaluation across neurological diseases.

abstract: Schizophrenia spectrum disorders have substantial genetic liability, but their stable incidence and clinical heterogeneity leave open contributions from non-genetic mechanisms. Though autoimmune encephalitis demonstrates that anti-neural antibodies can cause psychosis, encephalitis antibodies are uncommon in schizophrenia. Here we show that multi-platform autoantigen profiling of cerebrospinal fluid and plasma detects rare, anti-neural autoantibodies in schizophrenia spectrum disorders. By antibody profiling the cerebrospinal fluid of 32 schizophrenia spectrum participants and 32 neuropsychiatrically unaffected controls by brain tissue immunostaining, immunoprecipitation–mass spectrometry, phage display immunoprecipitation sequencing, and plasma by complementary protein microarrays, we identify three autoantibodies, including to alpha-crystallin B. The anti-alpha-crystallin B antibody preferentially recognizes phosphorylated serine-45 and is absent from the cerebrospinal fluid of individuals with untreated multiple sclerosis, a disease with frequent antibodies to unphosphorylated alpha-crystallin B. These findings do not define autoimmune psychosis as a new disease but support broader autoantibody searches in psychotic disorders.

abstract: Low-digestible carbohydrates (LDCs), including dietary fibers and sugars that resist absorption, are generally considered beneficial for the gut microbiota. However, we show that acute overconsumption of certain LDCs, particularly low-digestible sugars (LDSs), such as arabinose, lactulose, and polyols commonly used as sugar substitutes, can compromise colonization resistance against the common foodborne pathogen Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium. LDS overconsumption results in elevated fecal pathogen loads, systemic dissemination, and colitis in infected mice. Mechanistic analysis of arabinose overconsumption revealed that rapid fermentation acidifies the intestinal environment, perturbs the microbiota, alters gut-luminal short-chain fatty acid levels and elevated amino acid availability, which can support pathogen growth. Additionally, this perturbation impacts virulence by broadening tissue tropism (e.g. expansion to small intestine) and selecting for invasive Salmonella . Unlike antibiotic perturbations, Salmonella colonization requires SPI-1 and SPI-2 Type-III-secretion systems, linking virulence to pathogen fitness. These findings reveal how dietary perturbations can impact the gut ecosystem in ways that not only compromise colonization resistance but also enhance pathogen virulence.

abstract: Bacterial conjugation drives horizontal gene transfer and accelerates the spread of antibiotic resistance. In F-plasmid systems, the bifunctional relaxase-helicase TraI initiates transfer by nicking plasmid DNA through its trans-esterase activity and subsequently unwinding the plasmid via its helicase domains. Previous evidence suggested that two TraI molecules act cooperatively, yet how their activities are spatially and temporally coordinated has remained unclear. Here, we report the cryo-EM structure of a functionally asymmetric TraI homodimer and show that dimerisation is mediated predominantly by single-stranded DNA. Trans-esterasedriven duplex melting at the origin of transfer by one TraI molecule enables helicase loading by a second TraI molecule onto the transfer strand of the intact plasmid. Although the trans-esterase domain is intrinsically active, the host factor IHF inhibits nicking until helicase loading occurs. These findings uncover a regulatory loop coupling strand nicking with helicase engagement, defining a unified mechanism for initiating conjugative DNA processing.

abstract: Protein-protein interactions (PPIs) in diseased tissues represent a promising class of potential drug targets. However, PPIs are typically identified in live cells, lysate, and genetically engineered model organisms, limiting their translational value to human disease. Here we describe MAP-IT, an optimized photocatalytic carbene-based proximity labeling method for direct PPI mapping in primary human tissue sections, which bypasses the need for model organisms in the initial discovery step. We use MAP-IT to profile PPIs in situ for cell surface and nuclear target proteins, identify and orthogonally validate new interactors of EGFR in colon cancer, and couple light-powered MAP-IT labeling with spatially patterned visible light irradiation guided by neural network image segmentation to map location-specific protein interactomes.

abstract: Numerous undescribed species face extinction before formal scientific recognition. Despite research advances, the exceptional bat diversity of the Neotropics remains overlooked, with accelerating habitat loss threatening unrecognized lineages with silent extinction, requiring urgent conservation prioritization. Here, we integrate molecular species delimitation, phylogenetic inference, ecological niche modelling, and spatial conservation analyses to identify 95 Neotropical bat lineages that may represent undescribed species within 45 complexes, revealing that at least one-fifth of the recognized taxa may harbor hidden diversity spanning the entire evolutionary spectrum. This overlooked diversity faces a countdown to extinction: 62% of complexes face imminent habitat loss, and most are projected to lose over 50% of their suitable habitat by 2070. At current description rates, formally recognizing this diversity would take decades, a timeframe these putative species cannot afford. We develop a Hidden Species Richness (HSR) Index that pinpoints ten hidden diversity hotspots where undescribed richness coincides with significant human threats and extreme climate vulnerability. These hotspots highlight regions where research efforts are most needed, transforming crises into priorities. This race against extinction requires immediate taxonomic attention to document this biodiversity before it vanishes.

abstract: Sexual maturation and fertility of the malaria-causing parasite, Plasmodium spp., are critical to transmission between hosts. This developmental process involves an intricate gene expression regulatory network that drives gametocyte commitment, development, and the production of male and female gametes. Here, we characterize the role of the CCCH-type zinc-finger protein Plasmodium falciparum Male Development 3 ( Pf MD3) in the formation of gametes. Genetic disruption of Pf MD3 reveals a male fertility defect that decreases infectivity to mosquitoes. Molecular characterization of Pf MD3 reveals its binding to mRNA transcripts is associated with male gamete development through a specific RNA sequence. Gametocyte proteins encoded by these Pf MD3-bound transcripts decrease significantly in Pf MD3 knockout parasites, suggesting that Pf MD3 impacts translation. In addition to RNA-binding, Pf MD3 also interacts with proteins involved in mRNA processing and nuclear export that influence translational regulation. This study establishes Pf MD3 as an RNA-binding protein that impacts lineage-specific translation and male gamete fertility.

abstract: An age-related neurovascular impairment in nitric oxide (NO)-mediated vasodilation and reciprocal Piezo1-dependent vascular vasoconstriction may precede the accumulation of soluble brain proteins such as amyloid-β (Aβ) and disruption of brain fluid homeostasis in Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Preclinical studies suggest that restoring these pathways can enhance neurofluid transport and improve cognitive outcomes. In this study (EudraCT 2021-000625-27), we investigated the effects of sublingual NO and Piezo1-targeted whole-body vibrations (WBV p ) in healthy adults ( n = 29) using multimodal neuroimaging and blood biomarker analysis. The combined intervention (NO+WBV p ) was associated with correlating changes in brain fluid dynamics and increased blood levels of soluble brain-derived proteins (Aβ 40&42 , GFAP). These effects increased with age and the magnitude of NO-induced hypotension. The interventions were well tolerated under controlled experimental conditions. Overall, the findings are consistent with transient redistribution of brain-derived proteins toward circulation, suggesting a potential non-invasive approach to increase neurofluidic solute efflux in humans. Pre-specified primary endpoints, changes in circulating brain-derived protein concentrations, brain fluid imaging and brain pulsation measures, were met. Secondary outcomes included physiological analyses.

abstract: Spatial transcriptomics measures gene activity while preserving the locations of cells within tissue. A key analysis step is to divide the tissue into spatial domains, but the performance of computational methods varies considerably across datasets, and no single method consistently performs best. Here we show that a large language model can compare spatial domain maps and identify the better-performing methods. We developed L-STAR, which visually compares and ranks candidate methods, then builds a consensus map from the highest-ranked results. Across datasets representing different tissues, species, and technologies, L-STAR matched expert annotations more closely than individual methods or consensus analysis using a fixed set of methods. Its rankings were reproducible and generally stable when image colors or presentation order changed. L-STAR also provided rationales for its comparisons and assigned biologically meaningful names to the detected domains. These findings show that large language models can make spatial transcriptomics analysis more adaptive, robust, and interpretable.

abstract: Capturing the fine details of behavior when animals perform complex tasks, such as prey pursuit and capture, in natural environments is a challenging endeavor. For birds of prey, commonly used tracking approaches, such as lightweight GPS and inertial measurement units, cannot simultaneously track the bird’s position and the fine details of body part motion or moving external objects. Here we designed a head-mounted, tetherless, 4π camera system which, combined with a high-resolution environmental scan, enabled detailed three-dimensional measurement of both head position and orientation in freely flying Harris’s hawks ( Parabuteo unicinctus ) performing aerial pursuit in the wild. This stable head-mounted imaging approach enabled reconstruction of flight trajectories in natural environments, detailed quantification of head motion, optic flow and target position, while the bird tracked and captured airborne targets.

abstract: De novo peptide sequencing enables peptide identification from fragmentation spectra without relying on sequence databases. However, incomplete spectra create ambiguity, making unambiguous identification challenging. Recent deep learning advances have produced numerous de novo models that predict sequences and refine peptide-spectrum matches under such conditions. Yet, their relative strengths, weaknesses and ability to handle spectrum ambiguity remain unclear. Here we benchmark eight state-of-the-art models on three publicly available proteomics datasets, comparing performance using established metrics and quantifying inter-model agreement. We assess post-processing approaches, including iterative refinement, rescoring and reranking, for their ability to improve identification accuracy, and perform an error analysis to identify common mispredictions and their causes. Model performance varied, with considerable overlap of correct identifications. Post-processing yielded no or only modest improvements. Most sequencing errors were model-independent and driven by limited fragment ion coverage, a limitation also observed in database searches with large search spaces.

title: Hypothalamus-driven brain health through metabolic flexibility.
abstract: Organismal physiology depends on continuous, non-hierarchical communication among cells, tissues, and organs. We argue that this communication rests on metabolic flexibility-the capacity of cells and tissues to adapt substrate use to changing energetic demands-and that the hypothalamus serves as the central hub coordinating this flexibility across the body. Using hypothalamic agouti-related protein (AgRP) and pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC) neurons as a model, we show these melanocortin neurons do more than regulate hunger and satiety: by integrating metabolic, hormonal, and immune signals, they shape reward, learning, executive function, and social behavior, while imposing coordinated metabolic states on peripheral tissues. When this flexibility is lost, as with aging or overnutrition, body-brain communication becomes rigid, driving cognitive decline, chronic inflammation, and neurodegenerative disease. We propose that signals from the body are not peripheral modifiers of brain function but fundamental determinants of it, with direct implications for hypothalamus-centered strategies to preserve brain health across the lifespan.

title: Redox-dependent remodeling of mitochondrial nucleoids contributes to bioenergetic decline during neuronal aging.
abstract: Why mitochondria progressively fail in aging neurons remains a fundamental question in neurobiology. Although bioenergetic decline and oxidative stress are hallmarks of aging, whether redox signaling remodels mitochondrial nucleoids (mt-nucleoids) to impair neuronal bioenergetics remains unclear. Using aged mouse neurons and human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived neurons, we demonstrate that redox-driven mt-nucleoid remodeling underlies reduced mtDNA transcript abundance and bioenergetic decline. Combining minimal photon fluxes (MINFLUX) nanoscopy with single-molecule transcription mapping, we identify distinct mt-nucleoid architectures governed by mitochondrial transcription factor A (TFAM)-mediated mtDNA compaction. Aging-associated oxidative stress drives mt-nucleoid remodeling from compact, transcriptionally active structures toward decompacted forms with reduced mtDNA transcript abundance and impaired mitochondrial ATP production. This remodeling involves species-specific TFAM redox mechanisms: cysteine oxidation promotes human TFAM polymerization, whereas methionine oxidation weakens mouse TFAM-mtDNA interactions. Notably, expressing an oxidation-resistant TFAM variant restores mt-nucleoid organization, mtDNA transcript abundance, and ATP production in aged neurons, identifying mt-nucleoid architecture as a potential target for preserving neuronal bioenergetics during aging.

title: A Baltic Sea microbiome-derived Type III polyketide synthase produces host-protective alkylresorcinols in E. coli.
abstract: Marine microorganisms are a prolific source of novel polyketide synthases (PKSs) that generate structurally diverse and functional polyketides. Here, we identify a novel type III PKS, ArsMB, from Pontimonas sp. via metagenomic mining of a Baltic Sea microbiome. Heterologous expression of arsMB synthetic gene in an Escherichia coli host that lacks a native type III PKS, combined with a two-step strategy to boost acyl-CoA precursor availability in a glucose-mineral medium, enabled the in vivo synthesis of two cell-associated alkylresorcinols, identified by GC-MS as 5-pentadecyl-1,3-benzenediol (ars1) and 5-tridecyl-1,3-benzenediol (ars2). The product profile is consistent with a tetraketide alkylresorcinol biosynthetic pathway utilizing C16 and C14 acyl starter units, drawn from the host acyl-CoA pool. In agreement, AlphaFold2-based structural modeling predicts a Cys139/His275/Asn308 catalytic triad and a long hydrophobic substrate tunnel compatible with long-chain acyl starter units. E. coli producing the amphipathic cell-associated alkylresorcinols ars1/ars2 exhibited increased resistance to muralytic digestion by endolysins and to hydrogen peroxide. These findings expand the known repertoire of marine-derived type III PKSs and highlight the biotechnological potential of ArsMB-derived alkylresorcinols.

title: A deep genetic structure phylogenomically frames the closest algal relatives of land plants.
abstract: Discerning the nature of the last common ancestor of land plants (embryophytes) and algae allows to retrace the adaptations that ushered in the conquest of land by plants. For this, the closest streptophyte algal relatives of embryophytes hold key information. Albeit initially coming as a surprise due to their plain body plans, all major phylogenomic efforts have concluded that the Zygnematophyceae are the algal sisters to land plants. The Zygnematophyceae are the streptophyte algal class with the greatest species richness and while we now have ample genome information on a few select members of zygnematophytes, our understanding of the genomic divergence as well as genetic potential for key traits is limited by a lack of phylodiverse data that accounts for this diversity and integrates it into a phylogenomic framework. We here sequenced 43 new transcriptome datasets for the Zygnematophyceae and built a phylogenomic tree based on a total of 104 zygnematophyceaen transcriptomes and 2243 loci. We recover a deep genetic structure for the Zygnematophyceae: Despite the deep split between Spirogyrales and their unicellular sister group Desmidiales, most Spirogyrales emerged after pronounced genetic divergence, accommodating the attainment of multicellularity and divergent traits such as unique cell and plastid division. Overall, our data capture signatures of massive ancient radiations that could only be revealed thanks to a phylodiverse sampling. Recognizing the deep genetic divergences and a vast evolutionary history of the Zygnematophyceae are key to illuminate the nature of the algal progenitors of land plants.

title: A split nozzle and two-protein chain-like fibers define the tail architecture of Pseudomonas aeruginosa podophage A1002.
abstract: Phage therapy offers unique advantages against antibiotic-resistant bacteria. However, high-resolution structural studies of phages targeting Pseudomonas aeruginosa-a top-seven global pathogen-particularly podophages, remain severely limited, directly impeding structure-based development of novel antimicrobials. In this study, we utilize cryo-EM to resolve the high-resolution intact structure of mature phage A1002, a podophage infecting carbapenem-resistant P. aeruginosa. Based on density maps combined with AlphaFold3 predictions, we identified 11 structural protein components from the head to the tail. Phage A1002 exhibits a distinctly elongated tail morphology distinct from other reported podophages. Notably, the A1002 nozzle employs a distinct assembly strategy, featuring the unique nozzle-rope protein and nozzle-base protein, which may have evolved through modular evolution and horizontal gene transfer. Furthermore, the nozzle-rope protein provides 11 adsorption sites for fiber dimers, and these dimers are assembled from two proteins, giving rise to two types of dimers: dimers 1-7 correspond to fiber I (gp40), and dimers 8-11 correspond to fiber II (gp41). The nozzle-rope protein and these dimers combine to form a chain-like fiber. The tail tube comprises a double-layered, elongated tube structure that functions to simultaneously increase tail length and provide docking sites for six chain-like fibers. These distinctive structural features provide the molecular basis for A1002's broad-spectrum infection of drug-resistant P. aeruginosa and offer a novel molecular blueprint for rational design of structure-guided phage therapeutics.

title: An open-source eye-tracking system adaptable to diverse terrestrial vertebrates reveals state-dependent visual acquisition in lizards.
abstract: Gaze shifts are fundamental to visual exploration and processing, yet empirical knowledge is largely confined to a small number of model species, limiting our understanding of general principles of visual acquisition across animals. Here, we introduce a versatile, low-cost, and open-source framework design for eye-tracking in small, freely moving animals. Leveraging photogrammetry, 3D modeling, and 3D-printing, we produce headmounts adaptable to diverse head-eye geometries, as we demonstrate for lizards, turtles, and mice. Detailed recordings in Pogona vitticeps, a laterally eyed ectotherm with a high-acuity retina, reveal a rich oculomotor repertoire with kinematics closely resembling the saccadic main sequence in primates. We found both movement-coupled large binocular saccades, which exhibited a strong axial bias as well as small, isotropic, and monocular saccades suggesting a capacity for visual exploration of local details. Visual acquisition strategies were strongly tied to behavioral states with periods of active sampling (3-5 Hz saccades) separated by periods of ocular stillness lasting many seconds and suggesting a visual acquisition strategy distinct from those commonly described in endothermic model species. Furthermore, active states were correlated with pupil constriction in contrast to mammals and similarly to birds. Our results demonstrate the utility of our experimental approach for understanding visual acquisition across terrestrial vertebrates. Such a multi-perspective view on natural visual acquisition across species will be essential for developing a generalized understanding of vision, its ecological functions, and its evolutionary trajectory.

title: Aromatic profiles and 15-LOX inhibitory effects of Australian and New Zealand Manuka honeys.
abstract: Manuka (Leptospermum) honeys from Australia (Aust) and New Zealand (NZ) contain high levels of aromatic compounds, though only a subset are true phenolics in that they contain a hydroxyl group attached to an aromatic ring. Consequently, the traditional Folin-Ciocalteu Total Phenolic Content (FC-TPC) assay fails to detect many non-phenolic aromatic compounds that may confer health benefits. This paper quantified both phenolic and non-phenolic aromatic compounds in monofloral manuka honeys using high-performance liquid chromatography with diode array detection (HPLC-DAD) and the FC-TPC assay. In addition, this study evaluated the capacity of the honeys to inhibit 15-lipoxygenase (15-LOX), an enzyme that causes peroxidation of long chain polyunsaturated fatty acids. Australian (n = 7) and New Zealand (n = 6) Leptospermum scoparium (L. scoparium) honeys showed the highest total aromatic concentrations by HPLC-DAD (>2100 mg/kg), significantly exceeding those of L. liversidgei (n = 5), L. whitei (n = 5), and L. speciosum (n = 3) honeys. The FC-TPC assay identified higher phenolic levels in L. scoparium and L. polygalifolium honeys than in the other species studied. Sugar free Australian and New Zealand manuka honey aromatic extracts were potent inhibitors of 15-LOX enzyme, with IC50 values recorded at <15% of stock solutions (total extractables from 20.0 g of honey dissolved in 1.0 mL of 50% aqueous ethanol). Australian (IC50, 13.2 ± 0.7%) and New Zealand (13.1 ± 1.9%) L. scoparium honeys were more potent in inhibiting 15-LOX than L. liversidgei (IC50, 37.5 ± 6.3%) and L. speciosum (IC50, 36.6 ± 10.5%). Overall, this study demonstrates that HPLC-DAD provides a more comprehensive assessment of aromatic compounds in manuka honey than the FC-TPC assay and highlights the potential contribution of these compounds to anti-inflammatory activity.

title: BAG3 genetic variant is associated with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction phenotypes.
abstract: Genetic variations are involved in determining heart failure (HF) phenotypes. While variants within the BAG3 gene have been associated with HF in European populations, the impact of specific single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) within the BAG3 gene in determining phenotypes of HF with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) in Southeast Asian populations is unknown. Therefore, in this study, we identified BAG3 SNPs and investigated their biological and clinical relevance in determining HFpEF phenotypes among an Indonesian HFpEF cohort. We conducted a study involving 36 patients with HFpEF and 30 healthy individuals. We detected the presence of rs196326 and rs2240777 SNPs in our cohort. However, the rs2234962 polymorphism, which has been associated with HF and cardiomyopathy in Western populations, was absent in our Indonesian cohort. We found that the rs196326 SNP was significantly associated with relative wall thickness (RWT), with patients carrying the CG genotype displayed significantly lower RWT. Additionally, the rs196326 CG/GG genotypes were correlated with higher serum N-terminal pro B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) and lower Caspase-3 levels. Our study showed that the BAG3 rs196326 polymorphism was significantly associated with HFpEF phenotypes in the Indonesian population. This highlights the importance of identifying population-specific as genetic markers of disease severity.

title: Clinical and ocular factors associated with visual field progression following optic disc haemorrhage in glaucoma.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: To investigate the structural and clinical factors linked to visual field (VF) progression in glaucomatous eyes after the initial detection of optic disc haemorrhage (DH) in patients with primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG).
METHODS: This study included 92 eyes of 92 patients who presented with at least one optic DH on stereoscopic optic disc and red-free photography. The included patients had a minimum follow-up of 3 years after initial detection of DH and at least 5 reliable standard automated perimetry investigations. VF progression was assessed using event-based guided progression analysis (GPA). Baseline demographic, clinical, and ocular parameters were examined using Cox proportional hazards regression to identify the independent predictors of functional deterioration.
RESULTS: Among the patients, 32 (34.8%) showed VF progression and 60 (65.2%) remained stable. In univariate analysis, recurrent DH, longer axial length, thinner central corneal thickness (CCT), and intraocular pressure (IOP) fluctuation were significantly associated with VF progression. In multivariate analysis, recurrent DH (HR 4.008, p < 0.001), longer axial length (HR 1.287, p = 0.005), thinner CCT (HR 0.865, p = 0.005), and greater IOP fluctuation (HR 1.997, p = 0.032) remained independently associated with VF progression.
CONCLUSIONS: Recurrent DH, longer axial length, thinner CCT, and greater IOP fluctuation were independently associated with VF progression following optic DH. These factors may help identify glaucomatous eyes at higher risk of progression and support closer clinical monitoring after the initial detection of DH.

title: Clinical outcomes after fully visualized transforaminal endoscopic spine surgery in patients with lumbar disc herniation stratified by paraspinal muscle degeneration: A retrospective cohort study.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate pain and functional outcomes after fully visualized transforaminal endoscopic spine surgery in patients with lumbar disc herniation (LDH) stratified by preoperative paraspinal muscle degeneration, and to examine whether degeneration grade was associated with 2-year outcomes.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 129 patients with single-level LDH who underwent surgery between December 2021 and December 2023 and had complete preoperative, 1-month, 6-month, and 2-year follow-up data. Two blinded spine surgeons independently graded bilateral multifidus fatty infiltration from 0 to 4 on axial T2-weighted MRI at the mid-disc level; linearly weighted kappa was 0.967(95% CI, 0.937 to 0.989). Longitudinal outcomes were analyzed using covariate-adjusted patient-level random-intercept mixed-effects models with degeneration grade treated as a categorical factor, followed by adjusted 2-year regression and post hoc sensitivity analyses.
RESULTS: Of 136 screened patients, 129 were included after excluding 2 with incomplete records and 5 lost to follow-up. The cohort included 64 men and 65 women, with a mean age of 57.36 ± 11.63 years; grades 0-4 included 13, 25, 33, 32 and 26 patients, respectively. All grades improved substantially. In covariate-adjusted mixed models treating grade as a factor, the grade effect was significant for back pain VAS (P < 0.001), leg pain VAS (P = 0.010), and ODI (P < 0.001). The time-by-grade interaction was nominally significant for leg pain VAS (P = 0.036) but not after false-discovery-rate adjustment (q = 0.053), and not significant for back VAS and ODI. Each one-grade increase was associated with higher 2-year back pain VAS (β = 0.114, 95% CI, 0.001 to 0.227, P = 0.048) and ODI (β = 1.001, 95% CI, 0.168 to 1.833, P = 0.019), but not leg pain VAS.
CONCLUSIONS: Fully visualized transforaminal endoscopic spine surgery was associated with substantial pain relief and functional improvement across all multifidus degeneration grades. More severe degeneration showed modest prognostic associations with residual back pain and disability, but the estimated effects were smaller than published minimal clinically important differences. These findings should inform cautious counseling and hypothesis generation rather than be used as a standalone surgical decision rule.

title: Duration and barriers of physical education teaching in primary schools in 6 French departments.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Regular physical activity plays an important role in preventing sedentary lifestyles and reducing the risk of chronic diseases. In French primary schools, Physical Education (PE) represents the main compulsory opportunity for structured physical activity during school hours. This study aimed to assess self-reported weekly PE duration among primary school teachers in six French departments and to identify teacher- and school-related factors associated with PE duration, as well as the main obstacles to PE delivery reported by teachers.
METHODS: Between March 2021 and June 2024, as the survey implementation in the different areas took place, an anonymous online questionnaire was sent to primary school teachers in six French departments about the time spent teaching PE and their professional habits in this subject.
RESULTS: A total of 1,967 responses (overall response rate 3.9%) were collected and analysed: mean weekly PE duration reached 2 h 23 min ± 1 h 04 min in preschool and 2 h 28 min ± 51 min in elementary school, both below the mandatory programme durations. Higher PE duration was associated with longer seniority, fewer pupils in class, longer peri-activity around PE (transportation, locker room), multigrade class, suburban schools, the implementation of APQ (Activité Physique Quotidienne, a novel compulsory subject focused on daily physical activity), a higher feeling of competence and fewer obstacles declared.
CONCLUSIONS: In this sample of primary school teachers from six French departments, self-reported PE duration was below the durations recommended by nationals programmes, consistent with previous French studies. Because of its cross-sectional nature, self-report survey conducted in a limited number of departments, no causal relationships can be inferred and the findings should not be generalized to France as a whole. Nonetheless, this study identifies several teacher- and school-related factors associated with PE duration that may warrant further investigation, including through longitudinal or intervention research. Given the essential role of physical activity in the health of children and future adults, addressing barriers to PE delivery in schools remains a public health priority.
