title: Effects of music medicine on anxiety among primigravida mothers of preterm neonates: The CalM MOM randomised controlled trial protocol.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preterm birth and Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) admission are significant stressors that heighten maternal anxiety. Although RCTs have reported that music-based interventions used alongside usual care (UC) are effective and low-cost in reducing maternal anxiety, evidence from India remains limited.
OBJECTIVE: Primary objective is to assess the impact of listening to recorded classical Indian Instrumental Saraswati Veena music (Ragas Kalyani and Hindolam) (30-minutes/day over 7-days) alongside UC on maternal anxiety (STAI-state anxiety) of primigravida women with preterm neonates in the NICU. Secondary objectives measure changes in anxiety (Perinatal Anxiety Screening Scale (PASS)), maternal-infant bonding, breast milk volume, and neonatal body weight.
METHOD: This three-arm parallel-group, superiority RCT among primigravida mothers with anxiety (screened using PASS) of preterm neonates (30-36 weeks of gestation, admitted to NICU) delivered vaginally at Government Lady Goschen Hospital, Mangalore. The intervention arm will receive Music Medicine (MM), the comparator arm Nature Sounds (NS), and the control arm UC. Participant blinding is not feasible (auditory intervention), and they serve as their own outcome-assessors (self-reported questionnaires); investigators and the independent statistician will remain blinded. Personnel interacting with participants are blinded to study objectives; enrolment/allocation staff blinded to the randomization sequence, and assessment staff blinded to group identity. Randomization will employ a STATA-generated, permuted stratified block design stratified by baseline anxiety severity and gestational age (Allocation concealment: Sequentially Numbered, Opaque, Sealed Envelopes; Allocation Ratio: 1:1:1). Sample size (66/arm; total N = 198) was determined through a simulation-based power analysis (5,000 iterations, base-R), assuming an MCID of 4 (MM) and 2 (NS) on the STAI, residual SD of ~8, powered at 80% (α = 0.05). Blinded sample-size re-estimation will be conducted at 50% enrollment completion. Primary powered analysis will employ ANCOVA (baseline-adjusted), and Secondary (exploratory) analyses will utilize a linear mixed-effects model for longitudinal continuous data with time × group interaction.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical Trial Registry of India; CTRI/2025/06/088896; URL: https://ctri.nic.in/Clinicaltrials/pmaindet2.php?EncHid=MTM0Mzg0&Enc=&userName= Protocol version: Version 03, July 07, 2026.

title: Endoscopic necrosectomy of infected pancreatic Walled-Off Necrosis using two types of Lumen-Apposing Metal Stents.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lumen-apposing metal stent (LAMS) placement enables transmural drainage of walled-off necrosis (WON) with secure anchoring and provides endoscopic access for subsequent necrosectomy. This study compared the efficacy and safety of two commercially available LAMS designs (Hot-Axios vs. Micro-Tech) in patients with infected WON.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed patients with infected WON who underwent endoscopic ultrasound (EUS)-guided LAMS placement followed by endoscopic debridement at our center between August 2020 and June 2025.
RESULTS: Thirty-one patients were included (Hot-Axios, n = 21; Micro-Tech, n = 10). The overall necrosectomy success rate was 80.65% (25/31). Necrosectomy success was numerically higher with Hot-Axios than with Micro-Tech (85.71% vs. 70.00%), but the difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.358). There was a statistically significant difference in the incidence of complications between the two groups (P = 0.007); bleeding occurred more frequently in the Hot-Axios group (33.33% vs. 0%), whereas stent migration was more common in the Micro-Tech group (0% vs. 20.00%).
CONCLUSIONS: In conclusion, endoscopic necrosectomy for infected WON using LAMS is feasible and effective. Hot-Axios may provide more secure fixation and better resistance to migration; however, it may carry a higher risk of bleeding.

title: Enhancing medical image segmentation with HCE-Net: A heterogeneous feature collaborative extraction network.
abstract: Medical image segmentation occupies a pivotal role in clinical diagnosis and therapeutic planning. Conventional segmentation techniques struggle to accommodate the intricate representational attributes of medical images, while prevailing deep learning segmentation models predominantly adopt homogeneous single encoders and linear feature fusion paradigms, thereby exhibiting inherent limitations in contextual modeling, fine-grained feature excavation, and contour segmentation accuracy. To address such dilemmas, this paper proposes a Heterogeneous Collaborative Feature Extraction Network (HCE-Net). Establishing a dual-path heterogeneous encoding architecture, this network excavates complementary feature representations in a parallel manner. An Orthogonal Fusion Module (OFM) is elaborately devised to integrate Sobel edge priors with multi-scale convolutions, enabling the precise capture of edge and contour characteristics. A Diversified Receptive Field Module (DFM) is constructed to consolidate multi-scale detail manifestations and preserve global contextual cues. Furthermore, Adaptive Aggregation Connection (AAC) is embedded within skip connection branches to supplant conventional simplistic concatenation, efficaciously mitigating the technical bottleneck of heterogeneous feature fusion. Comparative experiments conducted on three publicly accessible medical datasets, encompassing dental radiographs, pulmonary CT scans, and retinal vascular images, demonstrate that HCE-Net substantially elevates segmentation accuracy, enhances boundary integrity, and ameliorates the general robustness of the model. It manifests distinguished application prospects across diverse medical image segmentation scenarios.

title: Equivalent linearization modeling and experimental validation of natural frequency and vibration isolation performance in metal braided hoses.
abstract: Metal braided hoses are widely used in the petroleum industry, marine engineering, aerospace, and other fields for their excellent displacement compensation and vibration damping. Stiffness properties have attracted most of the research so far, while the dynamic behavior of the hose remains comparatively understudied. This paper therefore establishes single-degree-of-freedom axial and bending dynamic models based on the Bouc-Wen hysteresis model and linearizes the nonlinear equations through energy-equivalent linearization, using the energy dissipated by the hysteresis loop. The linearized equations are solved analytically and validated against frequency sweep tests. The model predicts axial natural frequencies of 11.91 Hz and 19.60 Hz for the first two modes and 13.2 Hz for the first bending mode, all close to the measured values, so the equivalent linearized model can be considered reliable for engineering calculation in the low-frequency range. Experiments on hoses with different diameters, lengths, and braiding-layer numbers further show that the bellows size mainly determines the hose stiffness: larger bellows are stiffer but damp less, and adding braiding layers improves damping only until the accompanying increase in stiffness weakens isolation. In the measurements, the two-layer DN25 hose reached the highest axial vibration level difference of 12.83 dB, the longer DN25 hose reached 25.46 dB in bending, and the stiffer DN50 hose isolated much less, at 7.27 dB axially. These quantitative results provide concrete guidance for the design and application of metal braided hoses.

title: Examining individual and school-level predictors of positive attitudes towards condom use among adolescents in Tanzania: An exploratory analysis using hierarchical linear modeling.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Adolescents shoulder a disproportionate burden of poor sexual and reproductive health (SRH) outcomes in many lower-income countries, including Tanzania. Availability, access, and use of contraception, including condoms, reduces unintended pregnancies and sexually transmitted infections. Research indicates that early attitudes can influence future behavior, yet little is known about young adolescents' attitudes toward condom use. This study examines whether and how knowledge, beliefs, and sociodemographic factors influence attitudes toward condom use among adolescents in Tanzania.
METHODS: Data are from a school-cluster randomized controlled trial with Standard 7 adolescents in two Tanzanian districts. Using an analytic sample of 1,057 adolescents from 20 primary schools, descriptive analysis and hierarchical linear modeling (HLM) were conducted to parse out individual- and school-level influences that shape attitudes towards condom use.
RESULTS: Individual and aggregate characteristics of the school environment were associated with attitudes toward condom use. At the individual level, more positive attitudes were associated with being male, having access to condoms, and having knowledge about condom use and pregnancy prevention. At the school-level, more positive attitudes were associated with a larger male population in classes, greater breadth of pregnancy knowledge among students, and having relationships with trusted adults.
CONCLUSIONS: Findings suggest that adolescents largely turn to peers and adults for information and guidance regarding condoms. In turn, the views and beliefs of others can influence attitudes towards condom use. Schools might be an effective unit of change for interventions to facilitate more group-based education about the prevention of negative SRH outcomes.

title: Exogenous tryptophan aggravates experimental lung fibrosis through activation of AKT-mTORC1 pathway.
abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is marked by aberrant lung remodeling and excessive extracellular matrix (ECM) accumulation. Previously, we observed elevated tryptophan (TRP) levels in the lungs of IPF patients, but its role in fibrogenesis remained unclear. This study examines whether TRP modulate the severity of lung fibrosis by measuring ECM component expression in TRP-treated lung fibroblasts. The activities of key TRP metabolism enzymes, tryptophan hydroxylase (TPH-1) and indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase (IDO/TDO), were also assessed in IPF lung. Exogenous TRP administration in bleomycin-exposed mice significantly exacerbated lung damage and fibrosis. TPH-1 levels were elevated in lung tissues and primary fibroblasts of IPF patients compared to controls, while IDO/TDO expression showed no significant differences between two groups. TRP treatment increased fibroblast proliferation and upregulated collagen, fibronectin, and α-smooth muscle actin expression, whereas TRP deprivation reduced these ECM component levels. Additionally, TRP upregulated the AKT-mTORC1 and TGF-β1 signaling pathways in IPF fibroblasts. These findings indicate that elevated TRP levels contribute to IPF pathogenesis and suggest that targeting the TRP pathway could offer therapeutic potential for lung fibrosis including IPF.

title: Folding without glutamine: Proteome-scale removal of a canonical amino acid.
abstract: All known life uses a canonical alphabet of 20 amino acids, yet which residues are structurally essential remains untested at proteome scale. Isoleucine was recently eliminated from ribosomal proteins in Escherichia coli, establishing that amino acid alphabet reduction is feasible. Here we ask whether an entire amino acid can be eliminated from a proteome, and develop a computational framework to identify the best target. Using two independent approaches - ProteinMPNN structure-based probabilities and multiple sequence alignment conservation - we define "keep-score" as the fraction of positions where the native residue is optimal. Both methods converge on an unexpected candidate: glutamine has the lowest keep-score, with proline and glycine the highest - counter to substitution-matrix intuition. Glutamine's low keep-score is not explained by a single obvious substitute; glutamate is preferred in only 14% of replacements. Removing this target proteome-wide, we replaced every glutamine across 4,148 proteins with ProteinMPNN-optimal alternatives and modeled the resulting sequences with AlphaFold2. The recoded proteome maintained native-like structures: 85.5% of models exceeded a TMscore of 0.8, indistinguishable from the 85.9% baseline for rebuilt native sequences. Orthogonal validation - ESMFold predictions, Rosetta energy calculations, and conformational ensemble comparisons - revealed no evidence of systematic misfolding attributable to glutamine removal. As a consistency check, a glutamine-free TEM-1 β-lactamase designed with ProteinMPNN conferred ampicillin resistance in E. coli, indicating fold preservation can extend to biological function. Evolutionary evidence further supports these findings: 24% of E. coli proteins have glutamine-free orthologs in prokaryotic genomes, and glutamine ranks lowest in keep-score in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. These results show that an entire amino acid can be removed from a proteome with folds broadly preserved, establishing keep-score as a general framework and glutamine as the primary candidate for recoding. Crucially, this reflects a computational analysis of structural replaceability, not a demonstration of biological dispensability.

title: Genotypic variation and root traits associated with hypoxia tolerance in quinoa (Chenopodium quinoa Willd.).
abstract: Waterlogging-induced hypoxia is becoming an increasingly important constraint to crop production under climate change. Although quinoa (Chenopodium quinoa Willd.) is recognized for its tolerance to drought and salinity, its response to hypoxia remains poorly understood. This study evaluated the effects of hypoxia on growth, root development, biomass accumulation, and individual seed yield in 28 quinoa genotypes. Hypoxia reduced plant height by 31%, leaf area by 47%, root length by 39%, and shoot dry weight by 37% (mean hypoxia tolerance index 0.69, 0.53, 0.61, and 0.63); shoot dry weight remained 44% lower after recovery, whereas root diameter increased by 28% under hypoxia. Correlation analysis revealed that root length and root surface area were positively associated with individual seed yield, whereas root diameter was negatively related to several growth traits, highlighting the importance of maintaining root development under hypoxia. Permutational multivariate analysis of variance across 19 traits attributed 37.1% of overall phenotypic variation to genotype, 30.0% to oxygen regime, and 18.8% to their interaction (each p = 0.001), and hierarchical clustering on hypoxia tolerance indices resolved three genotype groups with contrasting trait profiles. Under hypoxia, Amachuha and Isluga produced the highest individual yields, followed by EDK4 and Chadmo. Under genotype-level validation (leave-one-genotype-out, leave-one-cluster-out, and highland-versus-lowland cross-ecotype splits), no model predicted the individual yield of genotypes excluded from training better than the mean yield of the training genotypes under the same oxygen regime, so trait-based yield prediction does not transfer to unseen quinoa genotypes. These findings provide valuable insights into the mechanisms of hypoxia tolerance and identify promising genetic resources for breeding quinoa cultivars adapted to waterlogging-prone environments.

title: Global sensitivity analysis for stochastic models of infectious diseases: Re-emergence of yellow fever virus in the Americas as a case study.
abstract: Emerging infectious diseases are a persistent public health threat that challenge deterministic, mechanistic modeling approaches. Because outbreaks initially start with a low number of infected hosts, their dynamics are highly stochastic, making traditional deterministic methods, e.g., ordinary differential equations, unable to qualitatively or quantitatively capture the transmission dynamics. In place, stochastic models are used, such as Markov chain models, but these models present their own challenges. Often, to infer a quantity of interest with stochastic models, we need to sample the model's distribution many times over, introducing an additional source of noise to our analysis. This additional noise makes the inference of our quantity of interest more difficult and computationally expensive. Here, we show how novel tools from the field of uncertainty quantification can be used to efficiently separate these two channels of noise, allowing us to make rigorous statistical inferences about processes important for disease emergence. We illustrate these techniques with a model of yellow fever virus spillover in the Americas, a virus that has seen rapid re-emergence amongst multiple hosts and vectors in South America over the last decade. We show that only a handful of parameters' uncertainties greatly affect variation in cumulative disease incidence. In particular, uncertainty in patch connectivity and non-human primate latency has the greatest impact on the variation of cumulative disease incidence of yellow fever virus across patches.

title: Infant presence and mother-infant conflict predict fetal loss in wild mandrills.
abstract: Female fitness depends on reproductive pace and offspring survival, both of which are determined by the ability to balance resource allocation between current and future reproduction. Using 11 years of data on 356 pregnancies (52 of which resulted in fetal loss) from 117 wild female mandrills, we show that females who conceive while still caring for a young infant experience a greater probability of fetal loss as well as increased mother-infant behavioral conflict in the form of maternal rejection. In addition, females whose infants throw more tantrums show a greater probability of fetal loss, consistent with observations from other species where living offspring can interfere in parental reproduction. Finally, females who lose a fetus show greater subsequent reproductive success (produce more surviving infants and show shorter inter-birth intervals) than females who give birth but their infants die soon after birth. These findings suggest that fetal loss may represent an adaptive physiological response to the energetic constraints imposed by overlapping gestation and maternal care, potentially limiting the fitness costs associated with short inter-birth intervals and concurrent investment in multiple dependent offspring.

title: Innovative ohmic-sous vide cooking technique for enhancing physicochemical, textural, and sensory attributes of Arabian camel (Camelus dromedarius) meat.
abstract: This study evaluated the effects of ohmic-sous vide (OS) and conventional sous vide (SV) cooking on the physicochemical, color, textural, and sensory properties of Arabian camel (Camelus dromedarius) meat. Meat samples were cooked at 70, 80, and 90 °C for 30, 60, 90, and 120 min using a 2 × 3 × 4 factorial design. Compared with SV cooking, OS cooking produced significantly higher pH, cooking loss, water activity, yellowness (b*), total color change (ΔE), hue angle, and chroma values, whereas lightness (L*), redness (a*), and shear force were significantly lower (p < 0.001). Increasing cooking temperature and time generally increased pH, cooking loss, yellowness, total color change, hue angle, and chroma, while decreasing lightness, redness, water activity, and shear force. Sensory evaluation showed that OS cooking significantly improved overall acceptability (p < 0.001) and tenderness (p = 0.01) compared with SV cooking. In contrast, cooking method did not significantly affect flavor or juiciness (p > 0.05). Increasing cooking temperature and time improved overall acceptability, tenderness, and flavor but progressively reduced juiciness. Meat cooked at 90 °C for 120 min received the highest overall acceptability, tenderness, and flavor scores, although this treatment also resulted in the lowest juiciness. In conclusion, OS cooking improved tenderness and sensory acceptability compared with conventional SV cooking; however, these benefits were accompanied by greater cooking loss and changes in meat color. These findings highlight the potential of OS cooking for improving camel-meat tenderness while emphasizing the need to optimize processing conditions to balance tenderness, moisture retention, color, and sensory quality.

title: Knowledge gap in vertebrate genetic diversity in a northern remanent of neotropical rainforest.
abstract: Los Tuxtlas Biosphere Reserve is one of the last remaining areas of primary tropical rainforest in Mexico. This fragile ecosystem heavily reduced by human perturbations is part of the Mesoamerican hotspot. The reserve harbors many endemic species. Thus, identifying, cataloging, and studying the biodiversity of this ecosystem has been of utmost importance. A promising approach for fast species identification to assess biodiversity is the use of DNA barcoding techniques. However, these techniques are limited by reliable DNA databases. Using novel Perl scripts, we generated a barcoding database to assess mitochondrial sequence availability in public databases for 903 vertebrate species that inhabit the reserve. Of these, 39 species had no sequences, 189 had complete mitochondrial genomes sequenced and the rest were partially sequenced. We studied over 80,000 sequences spanning 16 mitochondrial genomic markers and found 5 well-studied markers (COI-5P, CYTB, ND2, 16S rRNA and 12S rRNA) with more than 50% species coverage. The COI-5P region and CYTB were the best studied and most recommended markers for barcoding studies, and 7 additional markers have been preferred for one or more specific taxonomic groups. The remaining markers were almost exclusively sequenced as part of whole mitochondrial genomes. The best-known taxonomic group was mammals while the least known was reptiles. We also evaluated the sequencing frequency distribution for endemic, threatened and trade-restricted species driving interests in ecological research. In general, most species within each group were less sequenced when compared to the mean of all species, skewed by a few highly sequenced species of ecological interest. The most sequenced species are trade-restricted species, especially threatened species. This is driven by ecology-based research in the area. Finally, our results highlight a lack of barcoding research in local and endemic species of the Mesoamerican hotspot focusing on specific species but ignoring the wider range of biodiversity.

title: Knowledge, attitudes, and organ donor registration among medical and health sciences students: A cross-sectional study in Ras Al Khaimah, UAE.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Healthcare students serve as frontline ambassadors in promoting public awareness and shaping attitudes toward organ donation. This study assessed knowledge, attitudes, and organ donor registration among university students in Ras Al Khaimah, UAE, and identified factors associated with organ donor registration.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among undergraduate health sciences students using a structured self-administered questionnaire to collect data on sociodemographic characteristics, knowledge of organ donation and transplantation, attitudes, and donor registration status.
RESULTS: The study included 428 students. The mean knowledge score was 7.77 ± 2.85 out of 19, indicating gaps in understanding of the definition of brain death, donor eligibility, and legal requirements. The mean attitude score was 41.58 ± 6.61 out of 65, suggesting generally positive attitudes towards organ donation, although concerns regarding organ misuse, body disfigurement, lack of trust, and fear of reduced quality of medical care were reported. Only 28.0% of participants were registered as organ donors, with a lack of awareness (39.0%) being the most frequently reported barrier among non-registered students. In multivariable logistic regression analysis, non-Arab students had lower adjusted odds of registration than Arab students, including Emiratis (aOR = 0.149, 95% CI: 0.072-0.310, p < 0.001). Compared with medical students, pharmacy (aOR = 0.050), dentistry (aOR = 0.032), and nursing students (aOR = 0.024) had significantly lower adjusted odds of registration (all p < 0.001). Students with a medical parental educational background also had lower adjusted odds of registration than those with a non-medical parental background (aOR = 0.129, 95% CI: 0.063-0.264, p < 0.001). Knowledge and attitude scores were not significantly associated with registration.
CONCLUSION: Despite generally positive reported attitudes toward organ donation, self-reported donor registration remained low, highlighting a discrepancy between stated willingness and registration behavior. Educational and awareness initiatives should address knowledge gaps, misconceptions, trust-related concerns, and perceived barriers to registration.

title: Light meal consumption among university students in China: A multi-regional cross-sectional study of behavioral patterns, influencing factors, and service optimization strategies under supply-side heterogeneity.
abstract: This study surveyed 270 college students from seven major geographic regions of China and, using multiple ordinal logistic regression, structural equation modeling (SEM), importance-performance analysis (IPA), and K-means clustering, examined their light meal consumption behavior, its determinants, and service optimization pathways. Results show that light meal consumption is characterized by diversified demands, regular-meal-oriented timing, rigid price sensitivity, and functionalized categories; specific dietary needs are the core driver of consumption frequency (B = -1.985, p < 0.001), whereas grade, gender, monthly living expenses, and campus supply conditions are not significant. In universities without a light meal supply, consumption intention follows an "attitude-norm/control-intention" multiple mediation pathway, with subjective norm showing the strongest direct effect (β = 0.392). In universities with a light meal supply, supply-demand gaps across all six service dimensions are highly significant (p < 0.001), with taste and variety falling into the IPA improvement quadrant as core shortcomings. K-means clustering identifies three student groups in supplied universities (high-satisfaction loyal, differentiated rational, and low-satisfaction wait-and-see) and two in non-supplied universities (high-demand expectant and low-demand wait-and-see). The findings confirm that intrinsic health demands, rather than external supply conditions, are the core driver; peer effects are a key lever; taste and variety are the primary bottlenecks to repeat purchases; and student heterogeneity necessitates stratified strategies.

title: Long COVID prevalence among U.S. adults: A state-level ecological analysis of associations with SARS-CoV-2 incidence, COVID-19 hospitalization rates, COVID-19 vaccine coverage, and multimorbidity.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Long COVID has emerged as a major public health concern in the United States, yet geographic variation in its prevalence remains poorly understood. This study examines how state-level differences in COVID-19 vaccination, SARS-CoV-2 infection burden, severity of acute COVID-19 (measured by hospitalization rates) and multimorbidity burden relate to adult Long COVID prevalence in the United States.
METHODS: We conducted an ecological analysis using data from the 2023 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS), from which we estimated state-level prevalence of self-reported Long COVID among adults. These estimates were linked with publicly available data on SARS-CoV-2 incidence, COVID-19 hospitalizations, COVID-19 vaccine coverage, and a multimorbidity indicator (defined as ≥3 chronic conditions associated with increased risk of severe COVID-19, e.g., diabetes, obesity, chronic kidney disease). Multivariable linear regression models were used to assess the association between these factors and Long COVID prevalence, adjusting for state age and sex distributions. Rubin's rules were applied to propagate the uncertainty in the estimates of Long COVID and COVID-19 vaccine coverage through regression analyses.
RESULTS: All examined factors-including SARS-CoV-2 incidence, COVID-19 hospitalization, COVID-19 vaccine coverage, and multimorbidity prevalence-varied by state. In univariable analyses, vaccine coverage and multimorbidity prevalence were significantly associated with Long COVID prevalence. In the multivariable model, vaccine coverage and SARS-CoV-2 incidence were significant; however, after accounting for uncertainty in Long COVID and vaccine coverage estimates, only higher vaccine coverage remained significantly associated with lower Long COVID prevalence.
CONCLUSIONS: Higher State-level variation in COVID-19 vaccine coverage was consistently associated with lower adult Long COVID prevalence. These ecological findings support further investigation of vaccination and other state-level determinants of Long COVID burden and may inform population-level strategies for addressing Long COVID.

title: Multimodal computer vision and machine learning for predictive monitoring of planar-flow casting of amorphous steel foils.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Planar-flow casting (PFC) is widely used for manufacturing amorphous steel foils, where small variations in process conditions can rapidly affect foil quality. Existing monitoring approaches primarily rely on heuristic measurements or offline inspection, providing limited capability for quantitative process prediction and early identification of unstable operating conditions.
METHODOLOGY/PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: We present a multimodal computer vision and machine learning framework for predictive monitoring of industrial PFC using synchronised visible and infrared imagery acquired during full-scale production. More than 300,000 RGB and thermal image frames collected from approximately 200 production runs were processed to extract process-informed geometric, thermal and texture descriptors, including ridge density, ridge width, reflection characteristics and thermal-gradient features. Conventional image-processing baselines were compared with gradient-boosted decision trees (XGBoost) and a multimodal deep-learning fusion model combining RGB, infrared and process metadata. Both learning-based approaches substantially improved prediction of the nozzle-to-wheel gap compared with conventional computer-vision heuristics, achieving mean absolute errors of approximately 0.01 mm and R2 values of approximately 0.97. In contrast, prediction of the optical-flow-based melt-flow proxy remained substantially more challenging, indicating that this variable is influenced by factors not fully represented in the available imaging modalities. Feature-importance, calibration and ablation analyses demonstrated that ridge-density and thermal-gradient descriptors contributed most strongly to predictive performance, while complementary analyses showed that unstable production exhibited broader ridge-width distributions and larger edge-to-centre thermal gradients than stable operation.
CONCLUSIONS/SIGNIFICANCE: The proposed framework provides accurate, interpretable and non-contact predictive monitoring for industrial planar-flow casting while offering quantitative insights into process behaviour beyond conventional image-based inspection. The results demonstrate the value of combining multimodal imaging with machine learning for intelligent monitoring of advanced manufacturing processes and establish a foundation for future real-time process control and digital manufacturing applications.

title: PIVKA-II and hematological parameters in hepatocellular carcinoma and non-malignant chronic liver disease: A case-control biomarker comparison in a hepatitis-endemic population.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early detection of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains challenging in hepatitis-endemic settings such as Pakistan, where surveillance commonly relies on ultrasonography and alpha-fetoprotein (AFP), both of which have limited sensitivity for early-stage disease. This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of serum Protein Induced by Vitamin K Absence or Antagonist-II (PIVKA-II), complete blood count (CBC) parameters, and CBC-derived hematological indices for discriminating HCC from non-malignant chronic liver disease (CLD).
METHODS: We conducted a case-control biomarker study involving 160 adults with CLD at Liaquat University Hospital, Sindh, Pakistan, between October 2025 and March 2026, including 74 patients with established HCC and 86 with non-malignant CLD. Serum PIVKA-II was measured using electrochemiluminescence immunoassay. CBC-derived neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio, systemic immune-inflammation index, and red cell distribution width-to-platelet ratio were calculated. Between-group differences were assessed using non-parametric methods, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis evaluated discriminatory performance. Benjamini-Hochberg correction was applied to prespecified families of multiple comparisons.
RESULTS: PIVKA-II demonstrated the strongest discriminatory performance, with an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.753 (95% CI, 0.670-0.827). At a cutoff of >82.1 mAU/mL, sensitivity was 86.4% and specificity was 56.0%. Platelet count (AUC, 0.642) and the RDW-to-platelet ratio (AUC, 0.638) also demonstrated significant between-group differences that remained significant after false discovery rate correction, although their discriminatory performance was modest. PIVKA-II discrimination was substantially higher among patients with vascular invasion (AUC, 0.853) and advanced BCLC stage C/D disease (AUC, 0.853) than among those with early/intermediate BCLC A/B disease (AUC, 0.571). A combined model incorporating PIVKA-II, lymphocyte percentage, and platelet count yielded an AUC of 0.784, but did not significantly improve discrimination compared with PIVKA-II alone (p = 0.166). Bootstrap validation showed minimal optimism in the overall AUC; however, the optimal PIVKA-II cutoff demonstrated substantial variability, with a 95% percentile range of 58.7-715.8 mAU/mL. This was corroborated by an independent 10-fold cross-validation analysis, which yielded a comparable mean AUC of 0.751 for PIVKA-II (optimism = +0.002).
CONCLUSION: PIVKA-II demonstrated fair diagnostic discrimination between HCC and non-malignant CLD, with relatively high sensitivity but limited specificity. Its substantially lower performance in early/intermediate-stage disease and the marked instability of the optimal cutoff indicate that PIVKA-II should be considered a complementary biomarker rather than a standalone diagnostic test. Larger multicenter studies with standardized control populations and independent external validation are needed to establish robust population-specific thresholds and determine the incremental clinical value of combining PIVKA-II with hematological parameters.

title: Pain, sensory acceptability, and treatment compliance following cryotherapy and topical anesthetics in children: A randomized clinical trial.
abstract:
UNLABELLED: This randomized clinical trial aimed to compare the effects of cryotherapy, anesthetic spray, and gel on pain, anxiety, physiological responses, taste acceptability, and treatment compliance in children aged 7-10 years undergoing their first dental treatment. 100 healthy children were randomly allocated into four groups: 10% lidocaine spray, 20% benzocaine gel, cryotherapy with distilled water cooled to +4 °C, and lidocaine spray cooled to +4 °C. Following topical application, buccal infiltration anesthesia was administered. Anxiety, pain, and physiological responses were assessed using the Modified Dental Anxiety Scale and Facial Image Scale, Wong-Baker FACES Pain Rating Scale, and pulse-oximeter. Taste acceptability and treatment compliance were evaluated using a three-point Hedonic Scale and the FRANKL Scale. Repeated Measures ANOVA, Mann-Whitney U, and Kruskal-Wallis tests were applied. No significant differences were observed among the groups in anxiety, pain, pulse rate, oxygen saturation, or taste acceptability (p > 0.05). Pulse rate increased from the pre-operative to the post-operative period in all groups (p = 0.006), with no significant group × time interaction. FRANKL scores were significantly higher in the cryotherapy-distilled water group compared with the gel and cooled-spray groups (p = 0.001), a finding considered exploratory. Pain and anxiety outcomes following cryotherapy did not differ significantly from those of the topical anesthetic agents, while treatment compliance was higher, suggesting that cryotherapy may be a promising non-pharmacological option, pending confirmation in non-inferiority trials.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07198022.

title: Patterns of tobacco product single and co-use - Findings from the Population Assessment of Tobacco and Health Study (PATH) wave 7 data.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to comprehensively assess and describe exclusive and combined use patterns across the full range of tobacco products, including emerging ones, to inform tobacco product surveillance.
METHODS: We analyzed Wave 7 data (collected between January 2022 and April 2023) from the Population Assessment of Tobacco and Health Study, including 10,453 youth and 29,645 adults. We reported the frequency and weighted prevalence of current use across up to eleven tobacco products and used UpSet plots to visualize intersections of current tobacco use. We also examined the intersections among current nicotine pouch users, as a secondary analysis. Among current tobacco users, we fit multinominal logistic regression models to assess the association between sociodemographic characteristics and tobacco use patterns, with the single-product use as the reference category.
RESULTS: Among youth, we identified 41 distinct patterns of single and combined use, representing 6.0% of the U.S. youth overall; single-, dual-, and poly-use accounted for 4.9%, 0.8%, and 0.3%, respectively. Compared with single-product users, dual-users were more likely to have lower annual household incomes, and poly-users were more likely to be male. Among adults, we identified 183 distinct patterns of single and combined use, representing 24.7% of US adults overall; single-, dual-, and poly-use accounted for 17.2%, 5.5%, and 2.0%, respectively. Compared with single-product users, dual- or poly-users were more likely to be older, male, non-Hispanic Black, and have low annual household income.
CONCLUSIONS: Tobacco surveillance and research should routinely assess a broad range of products, including emerging products, and explicitly characterize co-use patterns. Our findings support policies and intervention strategies that address multiple-product use and target high-risk subgroups, rather than focusing on single-product use.

title: Practice leadership development in intellectual disability services: A qualitative study of practice leaders' experiences.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Leadership in intellectual disability services is recognised as having a key role in achieving positive outcomes for people with intellectual disabilities, service quality and workforce wellbeing. However, limited research has explored how leadership capability is developed and enacted by practice leaders within everyday service contexts.
METHODS: This study reports the qualitative findings from a national mixed‑methods evaluation of a bespoke Clinical Leadership Programme for practice leaders in intellectual disability services in Ireland. Following ethical approval, individual semi‑structured interviews were conducted with fourteen participants who completed the programme. Data were analysed using inductive content analysis.
RESULTS: Participants described leadership development as a transformative process involving shifts in professional identity, confidence and legitimacy rather than the acquisition of discrete leadership skills. Reflection emerged as an important mechanism underpinning leadership development, supporting participants to move from reactive and task‑focused approaches towards more intentional, relational and ethically grounded leadership practice. Participants described the programme as reducing professional isolation and facilitating peer learning relationships that promoted psychological safety and supported learning within a community of practice. Participants also described changes in leadership enactment characterised by greater staff engagement, relational conflict management and the extension of person-centred values to staff teams. Re-engagement with education was viewed as an important outcome, reframing learning as an ongoing component of leadership development and professional growth. However, participants identified systemic challenges, including administrative burden, role overload and compliance-driven organisational cultures, as constraining the enactment of leadership in practice.
CONCLUSION: Leadership development in intellectual disability services was described as an identity-based, relational and contextually constrained process. Reflective, practice-based and context-specific leadership programmes may support leadership capacity development; however, participants emphasised that the enactment of leadership in practice also requires supportive organisational structures and cultures.

title: Prediction of late blight severity in a large panel of potato genotypes using low-altitude aerial images and machine learning methods.
abstract: Potato (Solanum tuberosum L.) is a staple crop crucial to global food security, yet its production is severely threatened by late blight (LB), caused by Phytophthora infestans, one of the most destructive plant diseases worldwide. Breeding programs for LB resistance have traditionally relied on labor-intensive and subjective visual assessments, which limit scalability and consistency, particularly in early-generation trials. Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based remote sensing combined with machine learning (ML) offers a promising alternative for objective, high-throughput disease phenotyping. This study evaluated the potential of this technology to estimate LB severity at the genotype level across two large potato trials in Peru comprising 2,745 breeding clones and 492 genebank accessions. We compared vegetation index-based approaches with a ML framework that integrates K-means clustering and Kernel Ridge Regression (KRR). While NDVI correlated strongly with visually assessed LB severity, particularly at advanced stages, the multispectral KRR approach outperformed linear NDVI models by capturing nonlinear relationships between spectral response and disease progression. Best linear unbiased estimates (BLUEs) of LB severity from both models were strongly and consistently related to the area under the disease progress curve (AUDPC), particularly in later UAV acquisitions. Selection coincidence with AUDPC-based rankings was substantially higher at intermediate to advanced stages of disease progression, indicating that a single UAV inspection at those stages captures enough phenotypic variation to distinguish genotypes. UAV-based multispectral phenotyping integrated with ML, therefore offers a practical, scalable alternative to the time-consuming visual assessments traditionally used in potato breeding programs.

title: Profiles of mental health indicators among Ukrainian people recently bereaved in the context of the full-scale Russian invasion.
abstract: Bereavement research has frequently focused on psychopathology, while comparatively less attention has been given to well-being as a component of mental health. This study is the first to examine mental health profiles based on ICD-11 Prolonged Grief (PG) symptoms, posttraumatic stress (PTS) symptoms, and well-being in a sample of Ukrainians bereaved during the full-scale Russian invasion. Participants were 290 adults (Mage = 34.3, SD = 9.1 years), who had lost a loved one on average 5.3 months earlier. Over a third (35%) had lost a partner or child, due to illness (43%) or war (40%). The majority of participants (55%) scored above the threshold of clinically relevant PG symptoms. Latent profile analyses identified three distinct mental health profiles: (1) low PG symptoms/low PTS symptoms/high well-being (13%), (2) moderate PG symptoms/low PTS symptoms/moderate well-being (57%), (3) high PG symptoms/low PTS symptoms/low well-being (30%). People evidencing the third profile were more likely to have experienced the loss of a close person (partner or child) and to have been forcibly displaced compared to people in other profiles. Notably, the distribution of these profiles differs from previous studies, where profiles marked by low symptoms and high well-being were typically most common. Moreover, PG and well-being appeared to lie on opposite ends of a single continuum rather than functioning as distinct dimensions, providing limited support for the dual-continua model. This pattern suggests that Ukrainians may be facing unique challenges due to ongoing war-related stressors. Identifying those most in need of support and highlighting potential intervention targets are particularly important in under-resourced populations where access to care is limited.

title: Relational learning cues, music receptivity, and performance self-efficacy among piano masterclass participants: A PLS-SEM and fsQCA study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Performance self-efficacy is important for musical learning, yet research on its correlates in masterclass settings has mainly emphasized instruction and individual practice. Drawing on social cognitive theory and relationship-interaction-based brand equity, this study examined whether five relational cues in piano masterclasses-brand personality, reciprocity, courtesy, relationship status, and relationship energy-were associated with participants' performance self-efficacy and with affective and attentional music receptivity.
METHODS: A cross-sectional online survey was completed by 382 adult and adolescent participants with piano-masterclass experience in mainland China. PLS-SEM tested the hypothesized structural paths. Model evaluation included HTMT, full-collinearity VIFs, SRMR, and ten specific indirect associations estimated with 5,000 two-tailed bias-corrected and accelerated (BCa) bootstrap samples. fsQCA results were examined under stricter frequency, consistency, PRI, and calibration specifications.
RESULTS: Reciprocity, courtesy, relationship status, and relationship energy were positively associated with performance self-efficacy, whereas brand personality had no significant direct association. Affective receptivity was positively associated with reciprocity, courtesy, status, and energy; attentional receptivity was positively associated with personality, reciprocity, and status. Both receptivity dimensions were positively associated with self-efficacy. Seven of ten specific indirect associations had BCa intervals excluding zero. The baseline fsQCA solution contained seven configurations; stricter robustness specifications yielded fewer configurations, although recurring combinations of relational cues and music receptivity remained.
CONCLUSION: Performance self-efficacy in piano masterclasses was associated not only with instructional content but also with relational and experiential cues. Affective and attentional music receptivity represented distinct intervening statistical pathways. Because the survey was cross-sectional, retrospective, and based on convenience recruitment, the results do not establish causality or temporal mediation and should be generalized cautiously beyond this predominantly adult, highly educated, music-trained sample.

title: Resource allocation under uncertainty and equity constraints in Parkinson's disease care: An econometrically grounded machine learning framework.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To apply an integrated causal-inference and welfare-optimization framework to Iranian Parkinson's disease (PD) inpatient insurance claims, estimating how resource-allocation decisions relate to recovery, discharge risk, cost and financial burden; testing whether these relationships vary across patient subgroups; and assessing whether budget-neutral reallocation could improve efficiency and equity simultaneously.
SETTING: Six provinces of Iran, using de-identified administrative inpatient claims obtained from the Iran Health Insurance Organization for admissions with a primary or secondary diagnosis of PD during the 2023-2025 observation period.
DESIGN: Retrospective claims-based cohort study. Transaction-level records (n = 21,121) were aggregated into 1,813 hospitalization episodes and analyzed through a six-stage pipeline: gradient-boosted predictive models; double machine learning and augmented inverse-probability weighting for average treatment effects, restricted to an admission-time-only, pre-treatment severity adjustment; causal forests for subgroup heterogeneity; concentration-index decomposition for socioeconomic inequality; constrained integer-linear-programming optimization for reallocation scenarios; and bootstrap, E-value and design-effect sensitivity analyses.
RESULTS: Predictive models showed acceptable-to-strong discrimination (recovery, AUC-ROC 0.709; unsuccessful-discharge proxy, AUC-ROC 0.870) and explained 81.3% of variance in total cost. Prolonged length of stay, treated as an exploratory, within-episode exposure rather than a causal one because it is realized during the hospitalization itself, was associated with a 6.4-percentage-point lower discharge proxy and 200% higher cost (E-value limit 1.93-4.04). Higher insurance-coverage generosity, the study's pre-treatment, policy-assignable exposure, was associated with an approximately 40% reduction in cost (E-value limit 2.19) and no significant change in the discharge proxy; effects were consistent across age, severity, hospital sector, rurality and socioeconomic rank, with an attenuated estimate in a small private-hospital subgroup. Recovery was concentrated among higher-socioeconomic episodes, while cost, out-of-pocket burden and length of stay were concentrated among lower-socioeconomic episodes; age and hospital ownership, not disease severity (which contributed only -0.8% to +6.2% of the observed gradients), were the leading correlates. A coverage-based, budget-neutral reallocation scenario reached 35.8% of the cohort within the observed budget. Ninety-eight percent of significant associations remained robust to plausible within-patient clustering, the principal limitation arising from the absence of a patient identifier in these claims data.
CONCLUSION: Insurance-coverage generosity showed the strongest evidence of a causal, cost-reducing effect, while socioeconomic inequity in PD hospitalization outcomes was driven primarily by administrative rather than clinical-severity factors. The reallocation scenarios illustrate model-based, budget-neutral efficiency-equity gains and should be read as decision-support for phased piloting, not as empirically demonstrated policy effects. Patient-level claims linkage and validated clinical severity measures are needed to extend this framework toward genuine longitudinal outcomes.

title: Rigorous nested cross-validation and external generalization-gap analysis of a machine-learning classifier for U-251 glioblastoma cytotoxicity.
abstract: Glioblastoma remains difficult to treat, and drug-repositioning strategies require efficient methods to evaluate chemical libraries. Here, we developed a machine-learning binary classifier for compound activity against U-251 glioblastoma cells using a corrected single-center dataset of 236 compounds evaluated under a standardized cell-viability assay. Compounds were labeled as active or inactive using a predefined viability criterion (<50% vs. ≥ 50%) within a single-point screening framework using 10 µM as the upper screening concentration. To reduce optimistic bias and information leakage, we used repeated nested cross-validation in which preprocessing, feature selection, and hyperparameter optimization were performed within the training folds. ExtraTrees was selected based on Matthews correlation coefficient, showing moderate internal performance (ROC-AUC, 0.76; balanced accuracy, 0.66; MCC, 0.36). Structural analyses using nearest-neighbor Tanimoto similarity and Bemis-Murcko scaffolds indicated that the training set was scaffold-diverse with limited series bias. However, when the locked model was applied to an independent external set of 53 compounds, all compounds were classified as inactive, resulting in zero sensitivity, balanced accuracy of 0.5, and MCC of 0. The external ROC-AUC based on continuous prediction scores was 0.37, indicating poor threshold-independent ranking performance. Nearest-neighbor Tanimoto similarity did not explain prediction correctness or rescue active-compound recovery. Y-randomization supported the presence of a non-random internal signal, whereas scaffold-grouped cross-validation suggested that internal ROC-AUC was not solely driven by scaffold leakage. Overall, this study provides a reusable dataset and reproducible workflow, and highlights a substantial generalization gap between internal validation and external prediction in small chemical machine-learning datasets.

title: Route optimization for urban hazardous materials transportation under time-varying road networks.
abstract: This paper investigates a time-dependent urban hazardous materials (hazmat) transportation routing optimization problem, where vehicles depart from a distribution center to serve a set of customers. The decision variables include both the travel path and the departure time at each node, with the option for vehicles to wait if necessary. The objective is to minimize both the total transportation risk and cost, which consists of travel costs and overtime penalty costs. To address this, we propose PPO-MOEA/D, a reinforcement-learning-based approximation algorithm that enhances the performance of the conventional MOEA/D. To reduce computational complexity, we introduce a preprocessing strategy for departure-time decision identification and optimization, focusing only on critical nodes. Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) is utilized to dynamically generate high-quality initial solutions and adaptively select crossover and mutation operators, improving evolutionary efficiency. Extensive experiments on instances with varying scales demonstrate that optimizing departure times significantly reduces transportation risk. Compared to the traditional MOEA/D, PPO-MOEA/D shows superior performance in terms of convergence speed, solution quality, and computational efficiency. Additionally, we analyze the trade-off between computational cost and solution quality across different population sizes and investigate how total transportation risk varies across time periods.

title: Secondary school students' perspectives on their school food environments and their proposed solutions for improvement: Case study in Northern Benin.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The food environment within and around schools plays a critical role in shaping secondary school students' current and future eating behavior, food choices, and perceptions of healthy diets. However, little is known about how secondary school students in low-income settings perceive these environments and how such perceptions may influence their food practices.
METHODS: A qualitative study was conducted in the municipalities of Natitingou (urban) and Boukombe (rural), Northern Benin, to explore secondary school students' perceptions of their school food environments. In each municipality, two focus group discussions were held: one with lower-secondary students (11-15 years), and one with upper-secondary students (14-19 years), ensuring equal gender representation. Discussions addressed the types of foods available within and around schools, students' food preferences and perceptions, and suggestions for improving their food environments. Data were analyzed thematically.
RESULTS: Students reported access to a wide variety of foods within and near their schools, particularly in urban settings. However, most of these foods were energy-dense and high in sugar, while fruit and vegetables were rarely available. Participants perceived their school food environments as largely unhealthy, citing inadequate food hygiene practices and poor vendor sanitation as major concerns.
CONCLUSION: Findings highlight the need to integrate secondary school students' perspectives into efforts to improve school food environments in Benin. Policies promoting the availability of nutritious foods and strengthening hygiene standards in and around schools could support healthier dietary behaviors among students. Future research should examine how these environments and perceptions influence secondary school students' long-term nutrition and health outcomes.

title: Sex and educational inequalities across functional ability trajectories in Chile: A sequence analysis of a 17-year national panel.
abstract:
CONTEXT: Research on disability and functional ability has increasingly moved from cross-sectional descriptions toward longitudinal analyses of intra-individual change. This shift has shown that functional ability follows heterogeneous pathways, encompassing stability, progressive deterioration, fluctuating limitations, partial recovery, and death. However, evidence remains concentrated in high-income countries, and fewer studies have examined long-term functional ability trajectories in Latin American contexts marked by rapid population aging and high socioeconomic inequality. In addition, comparisons across sex and educational groups require trajectory typologies that are constructed in a way that makes group comparisons methodologically comparable.
METHODS: We used six observation points from the Chilean Social Protection Survey, a nationally representative longitudinal survey, covering the period 2004-2020. The analytic sample included 2,681 individuals aged 46-65 at baseline, contributing 16,086 person-wave observations. Functional ability was measured through self-reported limitations in activities of daily living and classified into five states: no limitation, low limitation, middle limitation, high limitation, and deceased. We reconstructed individual functional ability sequences over 17 years and applied optimal matching followed by hierarchical clustering. To ensure comparability across sex and educational groups, trajectory typologies were estimated within each baseline age group using the full age-group-specific sample. We then examined how membership in these pooled trajectory types varied by sex and educational attainment, referencing the composition of each trajectory type to the overall composition of its baseline age group.
FINDINGS: Across the four baseline age groups, detailed trajectories were grouped into three broader types: mostly non-declining, progressive-declining, and equivocal-declining. Mostly non-declining trajectories were prevalent in all age groups, although their internal composition changed with baseline age, moving from stable good functional ability in younger age groups toward preserved functional ability before death in older age groups. Progressive-declining trajectories were especially visible among respondents aged 56-60 at baseline and remained substantial among those aged 61-65. Equivocal-declining trajectories were more frequently composed of women, most markedly among respondents aged 61-65 at baseline, and of respondents with primary education or less in the three younger age groups. Sex differences in trajectory membership were statistically significant in all age groups, while educational differences were statistically significant in the first three age groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Long-term functional ability trajectories in Chile are heterogeneous and socially patterned. By deriving pooled trajectory typologies within each baseline age group before comparing sex and educational groups, and by referencing group composition to the marginal composition of each age group, this study provides comparable evidence on how functional aging unfolds across socially stratified groups in an understudied Latin American context.

title: Sex difference in survival benefits of immune checkpoint inhibitors in advanced non-small cell lung cancer: A meta-analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether sex influences the survival benefit of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains uncertain.
METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and Scopus up to April 1, 2026, for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing ICIs with chemotherapy and reporting overall survival (OS) or progression-free survival (PFS) stratified by sex. A random-effects model was used for meta-analysis.
RESULTS: Sixty-three publications (reporting 42 phase 3 RCTs) involving 25,827 patients (18,772 male; 7,055 female) were included. Compared with chemotherapy, ICIs significantly improved both OS and PFS in males (OS: HR 0.74 [95% CI 0.71-0.78]; PFS: HR 0.59 [95% CI 0.54-0.64]) and females (OS: HR 0.83 [95% CI 0.77-0.90]; PFS: HR 0.76 [95% CI 0.66-0.86]). Pooled treatment-by-sex interaction analyses demonstrated significantly greater OS (interaction HR = 0.90 [95% CI 0.84-0.97]; P = 0.01) and PFS (interaction HR = 0.82 [95% CI 0.73-0.92]; P = 0.0006) benefits in males than in females. In subgroup analyses, sex‑based differences in OS reached statistical significance in patients receiving ICI monotherapy (P = 0.02), including those treated with anti‑PD‑1 monotherapy (P = 0.04) and those with PD‑L1 expression ≥50% (P = 0.02). However, these differences did not persist after the False Discovery Rate (FDR) correction (adjusted P = 0.07, 0.10, and 0.07, respectively). In contrast, sex‑based differences in PFS remained statistically significant after FDR correction in the ICI monotherapy (adjusted P = 0.001), anti‑PD‑1 monotherapy (adjusted P = 0.001), and PD‑L1 ≥ 50% (adjusted P = 0.004) subgroups. No significant sex‑based differences in either OS or PFS were observed among patients treated with ICI plus chemotherapy.
CONCLUSIONS: Although ICIs are superior to chemotherapy in both sexes, the PFS benefit of ICI monotherapy appears to be attenuated in females relative to males. Given the imbalances in baseline confounders coupled with the underrepresentation of females in the included trials, these findings should be interpreted with caution and warrant confirmation in future RCTs designed specifically to investigate sex‑based differences.

title: Short-video content perceptions, intention, and self-reported behavior in special forces-style tourism: Evidence from Chinese generation Z university students.
abstract: Special Forces-style tourism is an emerging high-intensity, low-cost travel phenomenon among young people in China. Drawing on a modified Theory of Planned Behavior, this study analyzes survey data from 526 Chinese Generation Z university students using PLS-SEM and fsQCA. Perceived content appeal, perceived content trustworthiness, attitude, and perceived behavioral control are positively associated with intention, which is positively associated with self-reported behavior; short-video platform usage intensity strengthens this association. fsQCA identifies two configurations for high and eight for low self-reported behavior. Intention, perceived content trustworthiness, perceived behavioral control, and platform usage intensity form the common core of both high-outcome configurations, while low perceived content trustworthiness appears in six low-outcome configurations. No single condition is necessary, and the results indicate configurational asymmetry.

title: Soil amendments reshape alpine meadow microbial communities across degradation gradients by modulating nutrient availability.
abstract: Climate change and overgrazing have led to the continued degradation of alpine meadows on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, thereby severely impairing the ecosystem services provided by these grasslands. Soil amendments are an important strategy for restoring degraded grasslands; however, the regulatory effects of different amendment measures across varying degradation gradients and the underlying microbial response mechanisms remain unclear. This study systematically investigated the effects of three soil amendments (humic acid, superabsorbent polymer, and Bacillus subtilis) on soil physicochemical properties and microbial community structure in mildly, moderately, and severely degraded alpine meadows. The results indicated that the regulatory effects of soil amendments are significantly dependent on the degradation gradient: In the severe degradation stage, amendments significantly increased available nutrients, lowered pH, and alleviated alkalization, whereas their regulatory effects were limited in the mild degradation stage. Amendments selectively altered the abundance of microbial groups involved in organic matter degradation, nitrogen cycling, and stress-tolerant symbiosis. Humic acid demonstrated the optimal regulatory effect in the mild degradation stage, whereas superabsorbent polymers and Bacillus subtilis were more suitable for restoration in the moderate and severe degradation stages. Redundancy analysis indicated that bacterial communities were primarily subject to deterministic selection by soil pH, available potassium, and organic matter gradients, with the intensity of environmental selection increasing with increasing degradation severity; fungal communities exhibited significant environmental responses only in the moderate degradation stage, while stochastic processes dominated community assembly in the mild and severe degradation stages. In summary, alpine meadows at various stages of degradation require differentiated remediation strategies. Precise, stage-specific remediation tailored to degradation severity can facilitate synergistic restoration of the soil-microbial system, providing a theoretical basis and practical guidance for restoring degraded alpine meadows on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau.

title: Spreading depolarization drives distant connectivity changes in the focally injured cortex.
abstract: Cortical spreading depolarization (SD), a slow-propagating wave of transient cellular depolarization, reliably occurs after acute brain injury but usually remains undetected. Focal brain injury is known to produce a network-level dysfunction that changes the strength and direction of connectivity far beyond lesion site (connectional diaschisis) that can underlie post-injury neurological dysfunction. We suggested that injury-induced SD could contribute to connectional diaschisis and studied the effects of SD on functional and effective connectivity in neural networks supporting cognitive and sensory functions. Electrographic recordings of cortical activity were obtained in freely behaving rats immediately after focal micro-injury of the frontal cortex. The injury-induced SD propagated over the cortex of the ipsilesional hemisphere but never invaded the contralesional cortex. Strength and direction of connectivity were estimated using non-directional (mutual information function) and directional (transfer entropy) measures calculated for recordings from the retrosplenial (a key hub of the default-mode network) and somatosensory cortex. Mutual information analysis showed initial hypercoupling within the injured hemisphere (during SD) followed by longer interhemispheric decoupling (after SD termination). During post-SD hypoconnectivity, influence of the uninjured cortex on the injured one increased in both cortical regions. The retrosplenial cortex, component of the default-mode network, showed strong interhemispheric coupling during the baseline period and complex changes in connectivity after SD. Therefore, SD arising in the injured cortex disturbs long-range connectivity in distant cortical regions and causes widespread network alterations involving the default-mode network. Given the key role of the network in cognition, connectivity changes produced by injury-induced SD could contribute to the mechanisms of cognitive deficit after brain injury.

title: Spreading the Joy of Literacy: A community-based survey of parents by parents.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Literacy is an important social determinant of health. Failure to develop emergent literacy skills before kindergarten is a risk factor for academic failure, poverty, incarceration, and early death. Reading comprehension depends on both language comprehension and alphabetic decoding skills. The Home Literacy Environment literature tends to focus on reading aloud to develop oral language but less is known about letter-themed tools.
DESIGN: Our hypothesis was that letter-themed toys and books would be acceptable to all families but that lower socio-economic status (SES) households would be less likely to have them. Using methods of Community Based Participatory Research, 3 caregivers with young children living in the City of Rochester, NY, completed IRB training and provided cultural context for decisions throughout this study. We surveyed a convenience sample of 156 caregivers at 10 community events. We showed a poster with pictures of alphabet-themed toys and asked caregivers to count how many they had in the home. ZIP code was used as a proxy for SES.
RESULTS: We surveyed 156 caregivers, excluding 13 responses because of missing information. Of the 143 remaining, 139 (97.2%) thought it was important that a child know most of the alphabet letters before kindergarten. 1 in 4 of our respondents didn't have a single literacy toy in their home and an additional 1 in 6 had only one. We calculated a p value of 0.0004 for the hypothesis that there is a difference by SES in the number of these items in the home.
CONCLUSIONS: Our results are consistent with the hypothesis that joyful letter-themed tools are acceptable to parents in general but that low-SES households are less likely to have them. Closing the gap in early alphabet exposure could contribute to reducing inequities in school success and lifelong health.

title: State-aware adaptive multimodal fusion for ultra-short-term solar irradiance forecasting using sky cloud images.
abstract: As renewable energy penetration continues to increase, accurate ultra-short-term solar irradiance forecasting is essential for improving energy utilization and supporting power system operation. However, irradiance variations are jointly influenced by historical trends and rapid cloud changes, making traditional single-modal methods insufficient for capturing complex dynamics under varying weather conditions. This paper proposes a multimodal solar irradiance forecasting framework based on the collaborative representation of sky cloud images and numerical sequences. The framework introduces a heterogeneous modal state encoding mechanism and a state-aware adaptive selective attention fusion mechanism to enhance interactions between visual weather information and historical physical patterns. Specifically, the numerical modality captures irradiance trends and temporal correlations through dependency modeling, while the image modality extracts cloud structures and evolution features through spatiotemporal representation. The proposed fusion mechanism dynamically adjusts modality contributions according to forecasting conditions, enabling effective integration of complementary information. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework outperforms benchmark models in forecasting accuracy and robustness, validating the effectiveness of combining visual cloud information with numerical evolution patterns for ultra-short-term solar irradiance forecasting.

title: Stimulus-hand proximity shapes conflict processing by task-dependent modulation of distractor activation.
abstract: Placing the hands near stimuli modulates interference effects in conflict tasks. Liepelt and Fischer (2016) found that the direction of this near-hand effect depends on task demands: In a complex number-categorization Simon task, conflict was reduced when visual stimuli appeared near the hand, whereas in a simpler color-discrimination Simon task, conflict increased. They attributed this result pattern to a flexible attentional weighting of bottom-up vs. top-down processing. The present study specified and tested this hypothesis by applying the Diffusion Model for Conflict (DMC) to their data. The DMC assumes two parallel evidence accumulation processes: a transient distractor-based and a constant target-based diffusion process, which combine additively to drive response selection. Across two experiments, model fits revealed that stimulus-hand proximity selectively modulated the strength of distractor-based activation, while other parameters remained relatively stable across hand conditions. Crucially, this modulation mirrored the behavioral pattern: greater distractor activation near the hands in the color task producing increased conflict, but reduced activation near the hands in the number task leading to reduced conflict. These findings suggest that conflict is shaped by stimulus-hand proximity through selective adjustment of distractor-based processing, not target-based processing: location signals are typically amplified near the hands but down-regulated under higher cognitive demands. The results further illustrate how embodied manipulations can selectively impact specific processing components as mapped within a formal decision-making model.

title: Strengthening continuity of care for multiple long-term conditions in India through integrated referral and follow-up systems (SYNC-RF): A mixed-methods study protocol.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Multiple long-term conditions (MLTC) or multimorbidity are becoming increasingly common in low- and middle-income countries, such as India, placing demands on constrained primary healthcare systems that are still predominantly organised around acute care and single-condition management. Weak referral, counter-referral, and follow-up processes contribute to fragmented care and poor continuity for people living with MLTC. This programme of work aims to develop an integrated referral and follow-up model for people with MLTC who seek care in the primary healthcare system in India.
METHODS: This sequential, multistage mixed-methods research programme will be conducted in three interlinked phases. First, a systematic review of global literature will be conducted, which will synthesise evidence on referral and follow-up models or systems for providing MLTC care. Second, a convergent mixed-methods assessment will be undertaken in Jodhpur district, Rajasthan, including facility assessments of Primary Health Centres and linked referral facilities, a cross-sectional survey of adults with MLTC, and in-depth interviews with patients, caregivers, healthcare providers, and policymakers. Quantitative data will be analysed using descriptive and inferential statistics, while qualitative data will be analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Third, an integrated referral and follow-up model, SYNC-RF (SYstem for Navigation, Coordination, Referral, and Follow-up), will be developed based on the triangulated evidence and refined through expert consultation to ensure feasibility and contextual relevance.
CONCLUSION: The study will generate context-specific evidence on gaps, barriers, and enabling factors affecting referral and follow-up for MLTC care. The integrated model developed through this research is expected to strengthen continuity of care, improve coordination across various levels of the health system, and improve health outcomes for those living with MLTC.

title: Temporal and climatic drivers of uncomplicated malaria in Ghana: Regional Generalised Additive and Generalised Additive Mixed Model analysis.
abstract: Malaria remains a major public health challenge in Ghana despite recent reductions in cases attributable to various interventions, with disease endemicity varying across regions due to diverse seasonal and temporal factors that support mosquito proliferation. This study used Generalised Additive Models and Generalised Additive Mixed Models to explore the nonlinear effects of climatic conditions on uncomplicated malaria in Ghana. Monthly aggregated malaria cases from the District Health Information Management System II and average monthly rainfall and temperature data from the Ghana Meteorological Agency, covering 2012-2023, were analysed. Region-specific models incorporating climate variables were developed, fitted, and validated against observed data using model diagnostics to identify the most suitable model for each region. Using region-specific Negative-Binomial Generalised Additive Models and Generalised Additive Mixed Models fitted with a population offset, the analysis revealed complex temporal patterns in malaria incidence across Ghana, driven primarily by seasonality and long-term trend, which were significant predictors in all ten regions. Regions within the Coastal and Transitional Forest zones exhibited bimodal peak malaria seasons, while the Guinea Savannah showed a unimodal peak. Independent effects of rainfall and temperature were comparatively weak and largely non-significant, but significant interactions between rainfall and temperature emerged in the Ashanti, Eastern, and Central regions, with higher rainfall combined with temperatures around 27-28 °C associated with higher malaria incidence in the Eastern region, reflecting region-specific climatic influences. These findings point to the dynamic and heterogeneous nature of malaria in Ghana, underscoring the need for region-specific control strategies tailored to local climatic conditions. A key recommendation is the systematic integration of meteorological data into the National Malaria Data Repository to enable continuous monitoring and support timely, evidence-based intervention. Future research should incorporate socio-economic factors, intervention coverage, vector surveillance, and demographic characteristics to build a more comprehensive understanding of malaria in Ghana.
