title: The human hippocampus supports auditory coding and multisensory integration.
abstract: The hippocampus receives convergent input from multiple sensory systems, yet in humans it has been studied almost exclusively through vision. Here we examine how the hippocampus contributes to sensory processing beyond the visual modality and to the multisensory integration of visual information with these other modalities. Participants were exposed to multiple repetitions of short naturalistic movie clips, each presented in four formats: auditory-only, visual-only, congruent audiovisual, and incongruent audiovisual (audio and video from different movies). Using high-resolution fMRI, we measured univariate activation and multivariate representations across the longitudinal axis and subfields of the human hippocampus. Whereas univariate analyses detected only visual responses across hippocampal subregions, with no activation for auditory stimuli and no benefit of congruent stimuli, multivariate analyses revealed robust representations of both auditory and visual scenes. The posterior hippocampus showed enhanced pattern similarity for congruent stimuli relative to unisensory stimuli, especially in the left hemisphere, demonstrating multisensory facilitation. The anterior hippocampus showed crossmodal decoding between auditory and visual versions of the same clip, driven by the right hemisphere, suggesting a more abstract representation. Finally, whole-brain searchlight analyses revealed parallel effects in cortical regions known to support multisensory integration. These findings advance understanding of auditory and multisensory coding in the human hippocampus, revealing specialization and lateralization along its longitudinal axis.

title: The influence of ensemble size and composition on the performance of combined real-time COVID-19 forecasts.
abstract: During infectious disease outbreaks, short-term forecasts can play an important role for both decision makers and the general public. While previous research has shown that combining individual forecasts into an ensemble improves accuracy and consistency, practical guidance for organisers of multi-model prediction platforms on how to construct an ensemble has been scarce. In particular, it is not entirely clear how ensemble performance relates to the size of the underlying model pool, a relevant question when relying on voluntary contributions from modelling teams that face competing priorities. Furthermore, the exact composition of an ensemble forecast may influence its performance. Ensembles can either include all models equally or, alternatively, discriminate based on past performance or other characteristics. Using data from the European COVID-19 Forecast Hub we investigated these questions, with the aim of offering practical guidance to organisers of multi-model prediction platforms during infectious disease outbreaks. We found that including more models both improved and stabilised aggregate ensemble performance, while selecting for better component models did not yield any particular advantage. Diversity among models, whether measured numerically or qualitatively, did not have a clear impact on ensemble performance. These results suggest that for those soliciting contributions to collaborative ensembles there are more obvious gains to be made from increasing participation to moderate levels than from optimising component models.

title: The role of lipocalin-2 in lung homeostasis, inflammation response, and recovery following organic dust exposure.
abstract: Agricultural industry workers are frequently exposed to harmful dust particles and consequently have a higher risk of developing chronic lung inflammatory conditions such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Lipocalin-2 (LCN-2) is an innate immune protein with paradoxical roles in both pro- and anti-inflammatory responses at mucosal sites; however, its role in the lung during homeostatic and inflammatory states, such as those induced by inhaled dusts, remain unknown. Here, we investigated the role of LCN-2 in a murine model of organic dust exposure-induced lung inflammation using wildtype C57Bl/6 (WT) and LCN-2 knockout (KO) mice exposed repetitively to extracts of dusts (DE) collected from swine confinement facilities. Repetitive DE exposure consisted of fifteen days of intranasal instillations with and without a three-day recovery period. Through these investigations, we identified an important function of LCN-2 in regulating tissue homeostasis and recovery following inflammatory injury in the lung. Additionally, compartmentalized effects on T cell and macrophage levels were observed in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) vs. lung tissue in DE-exposed LCN-2 KO mice versus WT mice. Ablation of LCN-2 resulted in deficits in resolving histopathological markers of inflammation, and decreased levels of IL-10 after DE. Exogenous IL-10 administration partially rescued indicators of inflammation in LCN-2 KO mice after DE exposure. Taken together, these investigations highlight a novel role for LCN-2 in regulating lung homeostasis, inflammation response, and repair following organic dust-induced inflammation that may be mediated, at least in part, by IL-10.

title: Unveiling the neuroinflammatory potential of aspartame in Alzheimer's disease: A comprehensive network toxicology and experimental validation approach.
abstract: Aspartame, a widely used artificial sweetener, has raised significant concerns regarding its safety, especially in light of the rising incidence of Alzheimer's Disease (AD). However, systematic investigations into aspartame's potential neurotoxicity and its role in AD pathology remain limited. In this study, we employed an integrated approach combining network toxicology predictions, molecular docking, and in vitro validation to explore the neurotoxic mechanisms of aspartame in AD. By analyzing multiple public databases through network toxicology, we identified 185 common targets between aspartame and AD. Protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis further highlighted 10 core hub genes, including KDR, CCNE1, and GSK-3β. Molecular docking predicted favorable interactions for key targets such as GSK-3β (-5.002 kcal/mol) and KDR (-5.613 kcal/mol), with other hubs showing moderate binding affinities. In vitro experiments demonstrated that aspartame dose-dependently reduced BV2 microglial cell viability and triggered a pro-inflammatory response. Specifically, aspartame increased the production of nitric oxide (NO) and pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6), while upregulating the expression of GSK-3β, iNOS, TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6, similar to LPS-induced inflammation. These findings suggest that aspartame may induce a pro-inflammatory response in BV2 microglial cells through multiple signaling pathways, although the relevance of these findings to human neurological safety remains to be established. This study provides a basis for further investigation into the neurological safety of aspartame and proposes a novel paradigm for evaluating the neurotoxic potential of food additives using an integrated systems toxicology approach.

title: Using brewing industry byproducts to create feed additives for aquaculture-raised rainbow trout under thermal stress.
abstract: The aquaculture industry helps meet the seafood demands of a rapidly growing human population. The goal of this study was to determine the effects of feed additives, generated from byproducts of the beer brewing industry, on the growth rate, production parameters, and intestinal bacterial composition of aquaculture-raised rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss). Two prevalent brewery byproducts, brewer's spent yeast (BSY) and brewer's spent grain (BSG), were converted into high-value fish feed additives. To increase nutritional value of the byproducts, BSY was treated with exoenzymes, and BSG was used to cultivate black soldier fly (BSF; Hermetia illucens) larvae, which was treated with proprietary chitinases. During a seven-week trial using a recirculating aquaculture system, 22.15 ± 0.24 g (mean ± standard error) fish were randomly separated with 12 fish/tank in quadruplicate for each of the six diets (48 fish per diet), and tanks were randomly assigned diets. Survival rates were recorded daily, and fish were weighed every two weeks to track growth rates, adjust feed amounts, and calculate feed efficiency at the tank level. Fish intestinal mucosa swabs were collected at the beginning and end of the trial to analyze changes in the bacterial communities. Due to a malfunction in the chiller that maintained cool water temperatures, temperature and dissolved oxygen became substantial chronic (two week) and then acute (12-24 hr) stress factors near the end of the trial. Therefore, the research focus shifted to understand the impacts of thermal and oxygen stress on fish fed these novel feed additives. Clear changes in the structure of the bacterial intestinal community were observed in the fish between the start and end of the study as evaluated by 16S rRNA gene analysis. Results suggest that fish fed three of the experimental diets benefitted by having higher survival rates and growth rates when subjected to the unplanned stress.

title: Variation in recommendations for management of pediatric fever and neutropenia across databases and languages: A systematic review of clinical practice guidelines.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fever with neutropenia (FN) is a common complication of cancer therapy associated with significant morbidity, mortality, and resource use. Clinicians currently may access multiple Clinical Practice Guidelines (CPG) for FN in children to guide decision-making, however variation in content could impact care globally. We performed a systematic review and content analysis of CPG to assess the impact of databases searched and publication language on the quantity, quality, and content of recommendations identified for pediatric FN.
METHODS: We conducted a systematic search of PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science databases to identify evidence-based CPG published in the last 10 years addressing FN in children. We categorized CPG by language, extracted recommendations, characterized recommendation type (diagnostic, prognostic, or treatment), direction, and agreement with a recently developed international guideline. Methodological quality was assessed using the AGREE-II instrument and comparison between English and non-English CPG was performed using the Mann-Whitney U test. Comparisons of recommendation type (treatment, prognosis, diagnosis) and agreement with a reference guideline were assessed using the Chi-square test.
RESULTS: Fourteen CPG met inclusion criteria. Ten were published in English and four in non-English languages. There was no significant difference in methodological quality between language categories across AGREE-II domains except for scope and purpose (95.2% versus 90.5%; p = 0.036). Each database contained one unique guideline and only 36% (5/14) of the CPG were indexed in three databases. Percentage agreement between recommendations covered by 14 CPG and the reference CPG ranged between 33% and 100%.
CONCLUSIONS: Using pediatric FN as an index topic, we found that language or database restrictions limit the quantity and content of recommendations. Since CPG have variable methodological quality regardless of source, clinicians should design appropriate search strategies based on context. We recommend a broad search strategy when healthcare context or disease prevalence differs across settings.

title: Vivaray Hb pro non-invasive hemoglobin device: A prospective diagnostic accuracy study measuring agreement with a calibrated blood cell counter.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-invasive hemoglobin measurement offers a painless and rapid alternative to conventional blood-based testing. The Vivaray Hb pro is a handheld photoplethysmography-based device designed for point-of-care hemoglobin assessment without blood sampling. We evaluated the clinical performance of the Vivaray Hb pro by comparing device-generated hemoglobin values with those obtained from a calibrated laboratory blood cell counter.
METHODS: In this cross-sectional, non-randomized clinical performance study, participants aged ≥8 years were prospectively recruited. Hemoglobin was measured non-invasively using the Vivaray Hb pro and compared with venous blood samples analyzed on a calibrated Coulter counter. Agreement between methods was assessed using Bland-Altman analysis, including regression-based evaluation for proportional bias. Mean difference, mean absolute error (MAE) and proportions of measurements within tolerance limits were also calculated. Complete paired measurements were available for 763 individuals.
RESULTS: Bland-Altman analysis returned a mean difference of -0.40 g/dL. The bias was hemoglobin-dependent, being higher than the true value at low hemoglobin levels and underestimation at higher levels. Regression-based analysis showed proportional bias (β1 = -0.178), indicating decreasing difference with increasing hemoglobin concentration. The MAE was 1.5 g/dL but was lower (1.2) in the clinically predominant ranges of 8.1-13 g/dL.
CONCLUSION: The Vivaray Hb pro can function as a useful non-invsive screening and point-of-care assessment device for measuring hemoglobin, particularly in settings where rapid, painless and repeatable measurements are desirable.

title: Weekly sales forecasting using time series decomposition with irregular seasonality: A case study of Sony TV sales in the United States.
authors: Arthur Matsuo Yamashita Rios de Sousa
abstract: In the practice of sales forecasting, alongside high accuracy, simplicity and interpretability are desirable qualities in a predictive model. Here, we use time series decomposition to construct a simple and interpretable forecasting method for weekly sales, taking as a case study the total weekly sales of Sony TV units in the United States. The main challenge is to properly address irregular seasonality arising from the way a year is divided into weeks and from floating holidays and events. As a solution, we propose the concept of 'analogous weeks', a general framework for grouping weeks that are similar according to some criteria, which encodes seasonality and already accounts for calendar effects. By incorporating this notion into the time series decomposition and forecasting, we achieved yearly average percentage errors of less than 10% for the 1-week-ahead forecast and less than 15% for forecast horizons of up to 26 weeks, accuracy levels comparable to or better than those of other established seasonal models, namely Prophet and SARIMAX, particularly at longer forecast horizons.

title: Yield determinants in rice under organic and conventional production systems: Implications for selection strategies.
abstract: The persistent yield gap remains a major challenge in organic agriculture despite its increasing importance for sustainable food production. The present study compared the performance of 80 diverse rice genotypes (62 landraces  and 18 modern varieties) under two contrasting production systems (organic and conventional). The experiment was conducted during the Kharif seasons of 2023 and 2024 using an alpha lattice design (8 × 10) with three replications. Agro-morphological and yield-related traits were analysed through pooled mixed-model analysis of variance (ANOVA), genetic variability parameters, correlation and path coefficient analyses, as well as principal component analysis (PCA). The results revealed significant genotypic variation and differential trait expression between the two production systems, with the relative contribution of agro-morphological traits to grain yield varying between production systems. Integrated analysis of genetic variability, correlation, path coefficient analysis, and principal component analysis identified production system-specific trait combinations associated with grain yield. Under the conventional production system, flag leaf breadth (FLB), number of productive tillers per plant (NPTP), hundred seed weight (HSW), and flag leaf length (FLL) were prominent traits, with strong positive direct effects in path analysis, whereas leaf area (LA), NPTP, HSW, plant height (PH), and days to 50% flowering (DFF) were prominent under the organic production system, also showing positive direct effects in path analysis. Genotypic best linear unbiased prediction (BLUP) estimates identified Ponmani samba (G40), Varakkal (G60), and Sengalapattu sirumani (G49) with the highest yield BLUP estimates under the organic production system, whereas Mani samba (G29), TKM1 (G80), and Bavani (G6) showed the highest yield BLUP estimates under the conventional production system. Milagu samba (G31), Polinel (G39), and Ponmani samba (G40) consistently ranked among the top-performing genotypes based on yield BLUP estimates across both production systems, indicating their potential as breeding materials for further evaluation.

title: eNAMPT is a plasma biomarker of COVID-19 severity and ARDS progression linked to increased immune effector cell expression.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic highlighted the critical unmet need for novel targets, biomarkers, and effective pharmacotherapies to reduce the severity/mortality of COVID pneumonia and progression to acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). Extracellular NAMPT (eNAMPT) is a druggable DAMP and TLR4 ligand centrally involved in ARDS pathobiology. We explored the utility of plasma eNAMPT measurements as a potential COVID-19 biomarker linked to ARDS progression and disease severity and investigated the potential cellular source for eNAMPT release/secretion in COVID-19 subjects.
METHODS: A plasma biomarker panel of inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, IL-6, IL-8, IL-1RA, TNF-α), DAMPs (eNAMPT, MIF) and vascular proteins (ANG-2, PSGL-1) were evaluated in three distinct COVID-19-positive cohorts (Miami, Arizona, Tampa) (n = 277) and healthy control subjects (n = 214). Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) publicly available on peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) in a subset of Tampa COVID-19 survivors (n = 18) and an autopsied COVID lung tissue database was separately analyzed for biomarker gene expression.
RESULTS: Plasma biomarkers, including eNAMPT were significantly elevated in COVID-19 subjects compared to healthy controls (p < 0.0001), with IL-1RA, IL-6 and eNAMPT exhibiting the strongest diagnostic performance. Biomarker levels (all except IL-8, MIF) were higher in COVID-19 ARDS cases vs COVID-19 pneumonia (n = 154, AUC 0.71-0.79, p < 0.05) and were significantly elevated in COVID non-survivors (IL-6, IL-1RA, TNF-α, eNAMPT, ANG-2, PSGL-1) compared to survivors (p < 0.05). NAMPT gene expression was significantly upregulated in COVID-19 PBMCs compared with healthy controls, most evident within the CD14 + monocyte cluster. Relative to lung tissue from non-COVID-19 infected, NAMPT gene expression was increased in specific COVID-19 lung cell populations, including neutrophils, CD16 + monocytes, conventional dendritic cells (cDCs), fibroblasts, endothelium, and alveolar macrophages.
CONCLUSION: Our study corroborated the utility of this biomarker panel for diagnostic and severity assessment in COVID-19- associated ARDS and as a strategy for subject stratification in therapeutic trials of eNAMPT-neutralizing therapies. We further identified NAMPT expression in immune effector cells that correlates with COVID-19 severity and lethality. Together, these findings suggest NAMPT plays a key role in sustaining inflammatory activation and impairing lung regeneration in fatal COVID-19.

title: Coacervate droplets as a liquefier for the solid-to-liquid transition of RNA aggregates.
abstract: Biomolecular condensates are functionally gated by their material properties. While RNA is a primary structural scaffold, its sequence-specific interactions can aberrantly drive condensates into dysfunctional solid aggregates. Yet, actively reversing this solidification to restore function remains a fundamental challenge, impeding progress in synthetic biology and therapeutics interventions. Here, we establish that complex coacervates can be engineered as liquefiers to actively remodel solid RNA-peptide aggregates into functional liquid droplets. Integrating systematic experiments with all-atom simulations, we decode a multiscale mechanism: coacervate infiltration at the micrometer scale mediates molecular buffering at the nanometer scale, which fluidizes the crosslinked network to drive macroscopic liquefaction. This capability is governed by a design rule, where coacervates formed by small-molecular anions exhibit optimal efficacy. We deploy this principle to functionally rescue silenced RNA within a model of pathologically solidified ribonucleoprotein assemblies. Our work provides a general framework for the active, compositional control of biomolecular phase behavior, with direct implications for managing pathological aggregation and engineering functional condensates in synthetic and living systems.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Cooling fast and slow: Characterizing the effects of vitrification in cryo-EM and the subsequent recovery of equilibrium populations.
abstract: Single-particle cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM), a powerful class of techniques in structural biology with the potential to resolve molecular ensembles, requires that samples be vitrified to protect them from the high vacuum of the electron microscope. However, the effects of vitrification on biomolecular ensembles are unknown. To study them, we carried out extensive molecular dynamics simulations (over 50 ms) of the Trp-cage miniprotein at equilibrium and undergoing rapid cooling. We simulated seven cooling rates spanning three orders of magnitude, with the slowest coolings matching experimental rates. By inspecting molecular mobility and density-temperature trajectories for water with and without protein, we found that water vitrification is unaltered by the protein. To track protein conformation changes, and to relate them to kinetics, we made a Markov State Model (MSM) of Trp-cage from 5.4 ms of equilibrium sampling at 277 K. We observed that MSM states with a characteristic time longer than the duration of the nonequilibrium cooling tend to be more robust to artifacts induced by such cooling. Critically, although we observe that some states vanish in the equilibrium ensemble at 230 K, none do in our nonequilibrium cooled ensembles. To account for these perturbations, we developed a thermodynamic inference framework for recovering equilibrium populations from vitrified ensembles. These results indicate that cryo-EM has the capacity to be an accurate technique for the study of biomolecular ensembles.

title: Core effectors of the Fusarium pan-effectome contribute to host specificity.
abstract: Fusarium fungi cause economically important diseases of cereal crops, including Fusarium head blight, ear blight, and root rot. Central to these interactions are secreted effector proteins that manipulate host biology to promote infection. In turn, plants have evolved to recognize effector activity to activate immune responses and restrict disease. Despite their importance, the diversity, conservation, and evolution of Fusarium effectors remain poorly understood. Here, we present the Fusarium sambucinum Species complex Effector Compendium (FUSEC), a sequence-defined pan-effectome constructed from 188 high-quality genomes representing 27 species. FUSEC comprises 4,057 sequence-defined effector families, including a conserved soft-core repertoire of 235 families present in at least 95% of isolates. Structure-guided comparisons reorganized these conserved families into 184 structure-defined groups, revealing relationships that extend beyond sequence similarity and identifying similarities to numerous experimentally characterized fungal (a)virulence factors. Despite their broad conservation, soft-core families exhibited substantial within-family sequence diversity, and analyses of diversifying selection identified 44 candidate families undergoing adaptive evolution. Functional screening revealed that the majority of these candidates altered wheat immune responses, and CRISPR-Cas9-mediated gene deletions in Fusarium graminearum demonstrated that multiple conserved effectors contribute to cultivar-dependent Fusarium head blight severity.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Coupled outward and inward oxide growth during metal oxidation.
abstract: Metal oxidation is traditionally described as a dichotomy: oxide scales grow either outward via cation diffusion or inward via anion diffusion, with the dominant pathway determined by the prevailing point defects in the oxide lattice. Here, we demonstrate that these two modes are not mutually exclusive but intrinsically coupled within a single oxidation process. Using in situ environmental transmission electron microscopy to monitor the oxidation of copper-a canonical cationic system-we directly visualize simultaneous oxide propagation at both the O2/Cu2O surface interface and the buried Cu2O/Cu interface. Complementary simulations reveal the mechanistic origin of this behavior. Outward cation transport during surface oxide growth injects a sustained flux of vacancies into the underlying metal lattice, which facilitates inward oxygen incorporation and drives oxide growth at the buried interface. This vacancy-mediated feedback couples cationic and anionic transport process, providing a unified framework in which surface cationic growth directly enables inward anionic-driven growth. By identifying vacancy injection as a key mediator of interfacial mass transport, this work provides a mechanistic basis for predicting oxidation kinetics and defect-regulated solid-state transformation pathways in reactive environments.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Dissociation of gravity and limb dynamics in motor control.
abstract: Human movements remain accurate across substantial variations in mechanical loading, yet how the nervous system anticipates and compensates for intrinsic and extrinsic forces when generating muscle commands remains unresolved. Because the forces acting on the body are complex and nonlinear, dynamical modeling provides a powerful framework for identifying the computations underlying motor control. Here, we exploited parabolic flight to dissociate gravitational loading from intrinsic limb dynamics and directly test how these mechanical components are represented in motor commands. We analyzed kinematics and shoulder muscle activity from nine participants performing visually guided pointing movements in microgravity (0g), normogravity (1g), and hypergravity (2g). Inverse dynamics revealed that the gravity-independent component of muscle torque remained invariant across gravitational conditions. In striking contrast, muscle moments estimated from muscle activation showed systematic scaling of not only static but also phasic components with gravitational load, particularly during movement deceleration. This divergence arises because activation-derived muscle moments capture cocontraction, and thus impedance-related control, that is absent from net torques obtained by inverse dynamics. Gravity-dependent regression analyses further showed that muscle activation could be reconstructed from a compact set of mechanical variables dominated by gravity-dependent torque and movement velocity, revealing a low-dimensional structure of motor control. Together, these findings support a control architecture in which motor commands integrate predictive compensation for limb dynamics with gravity-dependent regulation of muscle cocontraction. This dual strategy provides a mechanism for maintaining stable and accurate movement across changing mechanical environments and offers a unified framework for understanding motor control under variable external loads.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Engineered T cell-agonist chimera for logic-gated STING activation and augmented cancer immunotherapy.
abstract: The efficacy of adoptive T cell therapy against solid tumors is markedly hindered by the immunosuppressive microenvironment. Here, we demonstrate that stimulator of interferon genes (STING) activation in tumor-associated macrophages (TAM) enhances the intratumoral infiltration and cytotoxicity of adoptive T cells. We next design a TAM-targeted nanoagonist and engineer a T cell-agonist chimera (SNTC) via covalent surface anchoring, to achieve synchronized biodistribution of STING agonist with adoptive T cells. The nanoagonist is locally released in tumor tissue in response to the elevated reduction potential on T cell surface, followed by intracellular glutathione-mediated restoration of STING agonist in TAM, thereby enabling AND logic-gated STING activation. SNTC not only reshapes tumor stroma and immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment to augment adoptive T cell function but also enhances the antigen presentation ability of TAM to activate endogenous T cells. SNTC elicits robust antitumor efficacy in melanoma tumor-bearing mice, resulting in over 40% survival beyond 60 d. Moreover, combining tumor-infiltrating T lymphocyte (TIL)-based SNTC with immune checkpoint blockade therapy leads to sustained tumor regression in mouse model of orthotopic pancreatic tumor. Collectively, SNTC holds translational potential to optimize STING activation for adoptive T cell therapy of cancer.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Epigenetic aging during the COVID-19 pandemic: A prospective longitudinal study with prepandemic baseline data in children, adolescents, and adults.
abstract: Psychosocial stress is a risk factor for aging-related diseases. The COVID-19 pandemic placed a psychosocial burden on individuals, potentially increasing the risk for aging-related diseases for which epigenetic clocks are used as early biomarkers. Based on four epigenetic clocks (DunedinPACE, GrimAge2, Horvath, and PedBE), we investigated whether epigenetic aging changed during the pandemic and whether these changes were associated with objective and subjective pandemic-related stressors and preexisting individual risk factors for poorer physical and mental health. We used prospective longitudinal data (n = 1,028), including repeated salivary DNA collection from children (n = 359, MAGE = 9.5 y), adolescents (n = 385, MAGE = 15.5 y), and adults (n = 284, MAGE = 24.3 y). Saliva was collected before the first phase of containment measures in Germany in March 2020 and after the second phase in 2021. We observed significant increases in epigenetic age acceleration (PedBE: b = 0.17, P < 0.0001; GrimAge2: b = 0.08, P < 0.0001) and pace of aging (DunedinPACE: b = 0.13, P < 0.0001) across all age groups. Prepandemic physical health and parental socioeconomic status, but not objective pandemic stressors, were significantly associated with this change. In adolescents, higher perceived pandemic burden was associated with a larger increase in pace of aging (DunedinPACE: b = 0.04, P = 0.01). Together, these findings suggest that prepandemic individual risk factors for poorer physical and mental health are accompanied by measurable increases in epigenetic aging during the COVID-19 pandemic, with adolescence representing a sensitive phase to its psychosocial burden.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Extracellular polymeric substances drive Curvibacter host adaptation and cospeciation with Hydra.
abstract: The interactions between hosts and their microbial symbionts play a crucial role to host physiology. Bacteria can adapt to specific host environments over evolutionary timescales, leading to cospeciation and the formation of specialized host-microbe relationships. Understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying these adaptations provides key insights into the evolution of symbiosis and the stability of microbial communities. This study investigates the cospeciation and molecular adaptations of Curvibacter to its host Hydra, a well-established model for the study of host-microbe interactions. We provide strong evidence of cospeciation, as demonstrated by phylogenetic congruence between different Hydra species and their corresponding Curvibacter symbionts, along with preferential recolonization of germ-free Hydra by their native Curvibacter strains. Comparative genomic analyses reveal that host-associated Curvibacter strains exhibit distinct metabolic and biosynthetic adaptations compared to their free-living relatives. Specifically, the enrichment of proteins linked to host glycan interactions, extracellular polymeric substances (EPS), DNA metabolic processes, ABC transport, sugar metabolism, and bacterial chemotaxis highlights specialized adaptations of Curvibacter symbionts within the Hydra glycocalyx. Importantly, some of these signatures are only detectable within the Hydra vulgaris-associated Curvibacter subgroup, emphasizing the need to examine host-specific adaptations at a finer taxonomic resolution. Functional experiments identify a symbiont-specific EPS operon as a factor for host colonization, thereby establishing its role in facilitating symbiont specificity and stability. These findings provide insights into the molecular mechanisms driving host-microbe coevolution and highlight the evolutionary forces shaping microbial specialization within host-symbiont relationships.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Forcing dataset updates impact regional but not global Earth radiation budget trends in the GFDL AM4 climate model.
abstract: The availability of up-to-date forcing datasets is critical for reconciling Earth system model simulations with contemporary observations. With the newly released CMIP7 forcing dataset, which extends the historical record through 2021, this study provides a systematic evaluation of how using updated forcings over the "middle-of-the-road" SSP2-4.5 scenario forcings influences the simulated radiation budget in the GFDL AM4 climate model. The updated forcing dataset used in the atmosphere model does not improve the agreement between the simulated global-mean top-of-the-atmosphere radiation trends and the satellite-observed trends. Regionally, we identify pronounced shifts in radiative energy partitioning between atmosphere and surface. Specifically, during 2001-2021, accelerated reductions in sulfate and black carbon aerosols over East Asia drive a significant decline in atmospheric solar absorption that matches observations, while a substantial increase in organic aerosols at higher latitudes induces a localized increase in atmospheric absorption that does not match observations. The substantial influence of localized forcing changes on simulated regional climate underscores the necessity for routine updates of forcing datasets.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Geochemical signatures of magnetite are conserved in diverse populations of environmental magnetotactic bacteria.
abstract: Magnetotactic bacteria (MTB) synthesize intracellular magnetite nanoparticles in a genetically controlled manner. They may represent some of the earliest biomineralizing organisms on Earth, and a unique window into ancient life and the environments that hosted it. Yet, identification of their mineralogical remains in ancient rocks is highly challenging due to the lack of reliable and lasting proxies. Previous results obtained from laboratory cultures of single strains of MTB revealed trace element and Fe isotope patterns that are not shared by any other source of magnetite, which could be used as reliable proxies for the identification of ancient MTB. However, the environmental relevance of these previous findings for environmental and mixed population of MTB is unknown. We report the trace element and Fe isotope compositions of magnetite extracted from environmental MTB collected in the water column of Lake Pavin, France, and show that the most distinctive geochemical traits (enrichment in Mo, Se, Sn, and light Fe isotopes) of magnetite produced by MTB cultivated in the laboratory are conserved in environmental populations. They represent potential biological signatures that can be searched in ancient rocks and coupled with magnetic and mineralogical tracers to support the presence of MTB and reconstruct their emergence and evolution.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Hepatocyte-derived exosomal miR-122 mediates liver-to-brain crosstalk and neuroinflammation in alcohol-exposed Alzheimer's disease mice.
authors: Bruna de Araujo Cardoso Dos Santos
abstract: Neuroinflammation and microglial activation are common features in Alzheimer's disease (AD) and excessive alcohol consumption. Alcohol induces liver damage and inflammation, and altered serum aminotransferases have been reported in patients with AD. Small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) and their cargo are emerging as mediators of intercellular communication in AD and alcohol-induced liver injury. However, the effects of alcohol use on AD progression remain to be elucidated. In this study, we evaluated the effects of repeated binge drinking on the liver and brain in the APP/PS1 mouse model of AD. Alcohol-exposed APP/PS1 mice showed elevated serum alanine aminotransferase levels, indicating liver injury absent in controls, along with increased pro-inflammatory cytokine expression in both liver and brain. Alcohol increased the biogenesis and release of sEVs in AD mice and in mouse hepatocytes. These sEVs were enriched in mature miR-122-5p that is predominant in hepatocytes. In vivo, miR-122-5p was detected in the brain of alcohol-exposed AD mice suggesting EV-mediated miR-122-5p transfer to the brain. Microglial uptake of hepatocyte-derived sEVs was confirmed in vitro. sEVs from alcohol-treated hepatocytes sensitized BV-2 microglia to LPS stimulation, significantly enhancing CCL2, CXCL2, CCL3, and TNF-α production. Transfection of microglia with a miR-122-5p mimic partially recapitulated the pro-inflammatory sensitization by sEVs from alcohol-exposed hepatocytes, which was reversed by miR-122-5p inhibitor delivery. ADAM10, a miR-122-5p target, was reduced in both wild-type and AD brains after alcohol exposure, with cell-specific effects. These results suggest that alcohol-induced hepatocyte-derived sEVs may modulate liver-to-brain signaling via miR-122-5p and contribute to neuroinflammation in AD.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: How 20th-century immigrants did not have to change their last names in order to become American.
abstract: Reports of parents' names in Social Security Application records allow us to quantify at a population level the extent and nature of historical last name changes by immigrants. Our analysis of European, Middle Eastern, and Asian immigrants of the early to mid-20th-century finds that more than 80% kept their last names. Computational linguistic analysis shows that most of those who did change preserved their surname's ethnic signal, leaving only about 5% of all immigrants trying to disguise their foreign origins. Of these, Jewish immigrants had the highest rate of ethnicity-concealing last name changes; Italian, Japanese, and Chinese immigrants all had the lowest. Our proposed framework helps understand the variation: name changes were rarest where ethnic community networks were densest and where passing as unmarked was least credible-as among visibly non-White immigrants. Our findings challenge the dominant assimilationist narrative that immigrants in this era had to shed their foreign identities to enter the American mainstream. "Becoming White" by adopting an English surname was not a large part of historical immigrant experience. Rather, the overwhelming majority of immigrants chose to openly preserve their ethnic origins. Our results also suggest that nominal record linkage of historical immigrant populations may be more feasible than previously assumed.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Hypothalamic lncRNA Synage prevents age-related sperm quality decline by suppressing A-type potassium currents in GnRH neurons.
abstract: Age-related decline in male fertility, including diminished sperm quality, poses significant risks to offspring health and is exacerbated by modern trends toward delayed parenthood. Focusing on the hypothalamus-pituitary-testis axis, which governs hormonal control of male reproduction, we identified Synage, a long noncoding RNA expressed in the hypothalamic medial preoptic area (mPOA). We found that Synage expression in gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) neurons decreases with age, correlating with reduced sperm quality and male fertility. mPOA-targeted Synage_B (brain-specific isoform) supplementation increases serum testosterone and improves sperm count and progressive motility in 12-mo-old mice. Conversely, conditional deletion of Synage in GnRH neurons in young mice reduces GnRH neuron firing, decreases serum LH and testosterone levels, impaires sperm quality, and reduces male fertility. Mechanistically, Synage interacts with the heat shock protein HSPA8 and stabilizes the HSPA8-KCHIP4 interaction. Synage loss increases KCHIP4 abundance and its association with the Kv4.2 channel, promoting Kv4.2 membrane recruitment and enhancing A-type potassium currents (IA), thereby reducing GnRH neuronal excitability. Consistent with this model, GnRH neurons from 12-mo-old mice also exhibit reduced excitability. Together, these findings support a role for age-dependent Synage loss in reproductive decline, at least in part through dysregulation of the HSPA8-KCHIP4-Kv4.2 pathway and reduced GnRH neuron excitability. These findings identify Synage as a candidate regulator of reproductive aging and motivate further investigation of its translational potential.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Rapid target engagement of KRAS G12C tricomplex inhibitor RO3903 overcomes resistance and drives durable tumor regression.
abstract: The clinical durability of first-generation KRAS G12C inhibitors is constrained by resistance mechanisms, primarily the rapid, receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK)-mediated reactivation of KRAS to its drug-insensitive, guanosine triphosphate (GTP)-bound (ON) state. Here, we perform a systematic comparative characterization of clinical and investigational KRAS G12C inhibitors, including Sotorasib, Adagrasib, Divarasib, and Elironrasib, and our structurally optimized tricomplex ON inhibitor, RO7783903 (RO3903). We demonstrate that the covalent tricomplex inhibitors RO3903 and Elironrasib effectively outpace dynamic nucleotide cycling, conferring resilience to potent RTK stimulation and overcoming the secondary KRAS mutations that drive clinical resistance to guanosine diphosphate (GDP)-bound (OFF) state inhibitors. Notably, RO3903 potently inhibits tumor growth in a dose-dependent manner across multiple preclinical models, including an orthotopic intracranial model. Furthermore, RO3903 exhibits synergistic efficacy when combined with inhibitors targeting OFF-state KRAS G12C, YAP-TEAD, EGFR/MET, or FAK, as well as with anti-PD1 antibody and anti-PD1/VEGF bispecific antibody immunotherapies. The high potency, fast target engagement, and brain tumor inhibition of RO3903 position this molecule as a valuable tool reagent and a promising partner for combination strategies to achieve durable tumor regression.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Rising cell-free DNA level tracks cancer-associated methylation signal and improves multicancer detection.
abstract: Cancer patients carry more circulating cell-free DNA (ccfDNA)-small DNA fragments shed into the blood-than healthy people. Most of this excess comes not from the tumor itself but from immune cells, suggesting that it would simply dilute the much smaller amount of tumor-derived DNA in a blood sample. Using a study of 1,480 previously untreated participants across 43 hospitals-including patients with 14 cancer types spanning all stages, patients with benign growths, and healthy volunteers-we show the opposite: as total ccfDNA rises, it becomes enriched, not diluted, in fragments carrying cancer-associated DNA methylation signatures, independent of cancer type, disease stage, and a broad panel of demographic, clinical, and technical covariates. In fact, total ccfDNA explains more variance in cancer-associated methylation signal than the disease stage itself. This basic biological finding suggests a coupling between immune cell activity and tumor methylation. It also has a practical implication: we show that rising ccfDNA concentration is associated with higher cancer detection sensitivity, even within disease stages and particularly in early-stage disease-stage I sensitivity varied from 0.55 in the lowest ccfDNA concentration tertile to 0.85 in the highest, and stage II from 0.59 to 0.86. This suggests that ccfDNA concentration should be considered as a stage-independent stratification variable for benchmarking cancer-detection tests. Interestingly, similar behavior was observed in patients with symptomatic benign lesions, suggesting a broader biological response to abnormal tissue growth and not something unique to malignancy.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Senescent CD8 T effector memory cells are functionally impaired, enriched in aging and disease, and a barrier to immunotherapy.
abstract: Senescent cells play important roles in various biological processes that promote fitness and health; however, their timely elimination by immune cells is critical to maintain tissue homeostasis and prevent disease. Despite this, senescent cells accumulate systemically with age, suggesting that certain immune cells also become senescent and dysfunctional during aging. In support of this, we previously demonstrated that CD8 T cells, immune cells capable of targeting senescent cells, increasingly develop characteristics of senescence with advancing age in humans. Here, we characterized the senescence state of human SA-βGal-expressing (SA-βGalhigh) CD8 T effector memory (EM) cells, their functional capabilities, and their enrichment in aging and disease. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed that SA-βGalhigh CD8 T cells with unique transcriptional signatures develop in all stages of T cell differentiation, including in CD8 TEM cells, which increased in abundance with human aging. SA-βGalhigh CD8 TEM cells expressed various classical markers of senescence and were significantly impaired in their ability to proliferate, produce cytokines, and eliminate senescent human stromal cells. Gene signatures of senescent SA-βGalhigh CD8 TEM cells were enriched in CD8 T cells from older human donors, patients with age-related disorders, cancer, and in smokers. Furthermore, we show that T cell senescence is distinct from and dominant over T cell exhaustion, limiting the response of CD8 TEM cells to immune checkpoint blockade. Collectively, our study demonstrates that senescence impairs CD8 TEM cell function and reveals the involvement of senescent and dysfunctional CD8 TEM cells in aging, disease, smoking, and responses to immunotherapy.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Spontaneous gas film expansion at an oil-water interface.
abstract: Spontaneous interfacial separation of oil and water, by inserting a gas film between the two liquids, is thermodynamically unfavorable because the oil-water interface is replaced by oil-gas and water-gas interfaces with a higher combined interfacial energy. Here, we demonstrate that microstructural confinement enables this transition after bubble introduction through the coupling of wetting, capillarity, and gas transport. Spontaneous oil imbibition into a water-submerged micropillar array, together with local contact-line pinning, deforms the oil-water interface into a metastable meniscus and generates a local pressure deficit in the confined oil. This deficit, combined with the bubble's interfacial configuration, lowers its air partial pressure and promotes dissolved-air uptake from the surrounding water. Geometric confinement, reduced oil pressure, and low oil-gas interfacial tension favor bubble lateral invasion of adjacent oil-filled cells over vertical extrusion. As the gas front advances, meniscus relaxation and oil redistribution promote further wetting, renewing the capillary conditions that support gas film propagation. We develop a coupled transport-capillarity framework that captures these morphological transitions and predicts a characteristic timescale for gas film evolution, determined by the interaction among geometry, capillarity, and gas-phase transport. Spatially varying the microstructure further controls the propagation pathway and morphology of the gas film. These findings show how favorable wetting can support an energetically costly interfacial transformation through a confinement-induced capillary pressure field, providing a general mechanism for gas-mediated separation in confined multiphase systems.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Subcellular compartment determines signal dominance: Endosomal cAMP overrides concurrent plasma membrane RhoA activation from a single receptor.
abstract: Cells convey information not only via the identity of activated signaling pathways but also through the subcellular location where those signals originate. Whether spatially distinct signals from a single activated receptor compete to determine net cellular output has remained unclear. Here, we demonstrate this principle for a G-protein-coupled receptor (GPCR), showing that endosomal and plasma membrane signals from a single activated receptor are not merely distinct but functionally opposed, with endosomal signaling predominating to reverse the net cellular output. Using the adhesion GPCR GPR64/ADGRG2 as a model system, we show that ligand activation engages two spatially distinct G-protein pathways that are not just additive but functionally opposed: plasma membrane G13/RhoA activation and Gs/cAMP production that persists from endosomes following receptor internalization. The endosomal cAMP pool actively overrides concurrent plasma membrane RhoA activation, resulting in net RhoA inactivation, an outcome that is completely reversed by pharmacological blockade of endocytosis or endosomal Gs inactivation. In parathyroid cells, where GPR64 is highly expressed, this endosomal signal dominance suppresses parathyroid hormone secretion independently of extracellular Ca2+ levels. These findings support a model in which the subcellular compartment, rather than pathway identity, determines the dominant signal and the overall cellular response of a single activated receptor, with implications for understanding the complexity of GPCR signaling.

title: Thermodynamic stabilization of substrate protein within the GroEL:ES chaperonin cage.
abstract: The adenosine triphosphate (ATP)-regulated GroEL/ES chaperonin of Escherichia coli promotes protein folding by transiently encapsulating unfolded substrate protein in a nano-cage formed by the cylindrical GroEL and the lid-shaped GroES. How this confinement modulates the folding energy landscape, allowing accelerated protein folding unimpaired by aggregation, remains incompletely understood. Prompted by recent observations suggesting that the chaperonin cavity may favor unfolding [I. Korobko et al., Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. U.S.A. 119, e2213170119 (2022)], here we reinvestigated the effect of encapsulation on protein thermodynamic stability. To allow thermal unfolding of an encapsulated substrate protein, we generated a destabilized variant of maltose-binding protein (MBP) by introducing four mutations, quadruple mutant-MBP (QM-MBP), lowering the melting temperature (Tm) from 63.6 °C to 44.3 °C. GroEL/ES accelerated the slow spontaneous folding of QM-MBP ~20-fold. The protein reached a native-like structure while encapsulated inside GroEL:ES, as demonstrated using hydrogen/deuterium exchange and single molecule fluorescence resonance energy transfer analyses in presence and absence of the ligand maltose. Importantly, confinement in the thermally stable chaperonin shifted the cooperative unfolding transition of QM-MBP to a Tm of 52.4 °C, corresponding to a stabilization by 4.6 kcal mol-1. In-cage thermal unfolding was reversible, indicating that the environment of the chaperonin cavity is conducive to folding. These findings suggest that a thermodynamically stabilizing effect of the GroEL:ES cage contributes to promoting protein folding.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Unpacking transatlantic income inequality.
abstract: This paper uses newly harmonized survey and register data on incomes and labor market outcomes as the basis for consistent comparisons of inequalities across 17 North American and European countries over the period 1995-2021. We examine trends in disposable income inequality in the working-age population, defined as persons aged 25 to 60, as well as its component parts of market income inequality and redistribution through government tax and transfer systems. We adjust incomes to allow for changes in education, population aging, and household structure in each country. We test for convergence across countries in demographically-adjusted disposable income inequality, along with market income inequality and redistribution. There is strong evidence of convergence over time in disposable income inequality across the 17 countries, despite a divergence in the dispersion of market income inequality driven by very heterogeneous trends for hours of work and the number of workers in households across countries. Consistent with this we find a strong convergence across countries in the dispersion of our measure of redistribution. There are reductions over time in inequality-reducing redistribution in the Nordic countries and increases in some other European and North American countries, with the net effect being more similarity across countries, a lower average level of redistribution, and a higher average level of disposable income inequality. These trends are being driven by the bottom 95% of the income distribution. Our results are robust to a variety of alternative specifications including the measure of inequality, trimming of data outliers, and sample period.

title: Evolving perspectives on cardiac innervation: from relay to a complex regulated network.
abstract: Neural control of the heart adjusts cardiac output to the functional demands of the body in order to maintain homeostasis. Sensory afferents monitor blood pressure, metabolites, and other parameters, sending information to the brainstem that then alters the balance of stimulatory sympathetic and inhibitory parasympathetic transmission to the heart. 'Autonomic imbalance' between sympathetic and parasympathetic efferent transmission in the heart is a characteristic of cardiovascular and metabolic diseases that contributes to pathology. In this review, we discuss recent studies related to the peripheral components of the cardiac control circuit. We summarize data from induced pluripotent stem cells, small and large animal models, and human studies that reveal more complexity in peripheral components of this system than previously understood. We also discuss peripheral neuroplasticity in cardiovascular disease and the potential impact of neuromodulation therapies.

title: A Bayesian Optimized Biquad Filter-Burg Model for Real-Time EEG Phase Estimation
abstract: Real-time phase estimation on stimulus-aligned transient EEG is critical for closed-loop neuromodulation systems targeting the theta-band, yet most real-time phase estimation methods have been developed and validated on resting-state, high-fidelity signals in the alpha band. Recent work has pursued deep learning architectures, while individualized classical bandpass filter tuning remains underexplored. This study characterizes the spectral and temporal properties of non-anticipative bandpass filtering and demonstrates the performance gains achieved through individualized tuning. We present a Bayesian-Optimized Biquad Filter-Burg (BOB) model evaluated on EEG recorded during peripheral vibrotactile stimulation of the left median nerve (theta, N=20 healthy subjects) and on resting-state recordings from the Max Planck Institute's LEMON dataset (alpha, N=20 healthy subjects). BOB was benchmarked against the Deep Dual-Branch Complex Neural Network (DBCNN), EEG Phase Prediction Network (EPN), Phastimate, and Phase Estimation with Autoregressive Padding (PEAP) under matched testing conditions: channel selection, individualized optimization, evaluation time points, and an offline reference phase obtained through zero-phase filtering and the Hilbert transform. Under these testing conditions, BOB achieved matched or better performance than these models at a fraction of the calibration time.
comment: 24 pages, 12 figures (9 main, 3 supplements)

title: Ablating Design Choices for Protein Ensemble Generators Across Structural Regimes
abstract: Generative models of protein conformational ensembles inherit much of their design from structure prediction for folded proteins. Ordered and disordered proteins, however, occupy distinct structural regimes, and we investigate how design choices hold up across them. Using a minimal C$α$ flow-matching model, we ablate choices of architecture, sequence conditioning, rigid-body alignment and training source, and evaluate each variant against experimental SAXS and NMR chemical-shift data partitioned into ordered, disordered, multi-domain and transitional proteins. Mixture-of-experts routing, a static pair representation and a disorder probe have no detectable effect, a smaller protein language model performs worse on ordered proteins but not on disordered ones, and alignment in the loss degrades agreement with SAXS. Replacing coarse-grained simulations of disordered proteins with fragment-assembled ensembles improves agreement with chemical shifts at a cost to SAXS, while an equal mixture of the two keeps most of the gain at a smaller cost. This points to the training data, rather than the architecture, as the main constraint.
comment: 13 pages, 2 figures

title: Curriculum unlearning in humans and neural networks
abstract: During learning, humans often benefit from curricula that teach simple rules before exceptions. However, we lack a computational explanation for this phenomenon. Here, using a canonical behavioural task and modelling with neural networks, we develop and test a theory for why simple-to-complex curricula succeed. We show that during learning, both humans and neural networks show simplicity biases, a tendency to learn simple rules that are underfit to the data. In neural networks this bias is accompanied by compression of neural representations. Simple-to-complex curricula help both types of learners overcome this compression, developing representations (and policy) with appropriate dimensionality for the task. We test and confirm a further prediction from this theory: learners that have been pre-exposed to simple tasks and with more compressed initial representations benefit more from curricula. These findings suggest that curricula help with ``unlearning'' of simple rules.

title: Empirical Bayes Flow Matching for Continuous Cryo-EM Heterogeneity
abstract: We address the problem of learning generative priors over high-dimensional latent variables from indirect, noisy observations, with a focus on continuous heterogeneity in cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM). In this setting, 3D atomic structures $x \in \mathbb{R}^{3N_a}$ are never directly observed and must be inferred from 2D projection images $y$ generated by a complex, non-linear forward operator. We propose Empirical Bayes Flow Matching (EB-FM), a method that learns a flow matching prior $p_θ(x)$ directly from observations using a Monte Carlo stochastic approximation Expectation-Maximization framework. EB-FM alternates between an E-step that performs approximate posterior sampling from $p_θ(x \mid y)$ via guided flow-based generation while maintaining persistent latent estimates through stochastic approximation, and an M-step that updates the flow model using these stabilized latent variables as training targets. This approach eliminates the need for pretraining on clean data and naturally accommodates non-linear forward models. We validate our method on controlled inverse problems using two-moons and MNIST data, and demonstrate its effectiveness on simulated cryo-EM data with known poses, showing that EB-FM can recover continuous distributions of protein conformations directly in atomic-coordinate space.
comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. 20 pages, 6 figures, 5 tables. Code: https://daiyral.github.io/Empirical-Bayes-Flow-Matching-for-Continuous-Cryo-EM-Heterogeneity/

title: GINsim 3.1: Qualitative modelling and dynamical analysis of logical regulatory networks
abstract: GINsim is a software for the definition and dynamical analysis of qualitative (Boolean and multi-valued) models of biological regulatory networks. Building on its modular architecture, based on the MDDlib decision-diagram and bioLQM model-manipulation libraries, GINsim version 3.1 introduces new functionalities aimed at the analysis of large logical models: the symbolic computation of trap-spaces, the Booleanisation of multilevel models and the reversal of model dynamics. GINsim 3.1 also extends the estimation of attractor reachability (Monte Carlo and Avatar algorithms), the computation of stable states, as well as model reduction functionalities. Analyses can be applied to perturbed models, and scripted, in particular from the CoLoMoTo interactive notebook. We illustrate the main functionalities of GINsim on a reference multilevel model of regulatory network that control the mammalian cell cycle, including the computation of its stable states and cyclic attractor, the assessment of their reachability, and the identification of the regulatory circuits driving multistability and oscillations. GINsim is freely available under GPL-3.0 at https://ginsim.github.io/, runs on any platform supporting Java, and is interoperable with the other tools of the CoLoMoTo community. Its website provides installation instructions and reference documentation, as well as a repository of Boolean and multilevel logical models.

title: Predicting protein structures at any folding stage from sequence
abstract: Protein structure prediction has largely focused on native conformations, leaving the continuum of unfolded states, folding intermediates, and native structures difficult to access. We present FoldScape, a sequence-conditioned deep learning framework for generating protein conformational ensembles at specified folding fractions $Q$. Trained on approximately one million conformations from 10,000 protein sequences, FoldScape combines coarse-grained folding and all-atom mechanical-unfolding trajectories. It reconstructs three-dimensional $C_α$ chains through hierarchical sliding-window regressions of inter-residue distances, chain-level assembly, and a rectified-flow decoder. By conditioning on folding progress, FoldScape generates conformations from unfolded states through intermediates to native-state structures without protein-specific molecular dynamics at inference. In matched-sample comparisons, FoldScape achieves median conformational-space coverage of 0.989, 0.722, and 0.877 along radius of gyration, fraction of native contacts $Q$, and secondary-structure fraction, respectively, versus 0.05, 0.05, and 0.10 for seed-varied AlphaFold 3 ensembles. Coverage advantages are consistent across the evaluated proteins and robust to binning choices. Reconstruction accuracy remains approximately stable across the evaluated stages of a folding trajectory, and stride-one crop-and-superpose inference extends predictions to chains several times longer than the single-pass limit. Analyses of mechanical-unfolding trajectories show residue-resolved pathways, reproducible extension-conditioned observables across pulling velocities, and geometrically coherent segments in partially unfolded chains. FoldScape extends sequence-based structure prediction beyond a single folded endpoint to controllable conformational-ensemble generation across protein folding.

title: Trail systems self-organize through individual route optimization
abstract: As animals, including humans, walk, they compact the vegetation and ground beneath them, reducing the cost of movement for subsequent travelers. From this positive feedback emerge networks of trails which allow for efficient movement and store generational-scale information about the environment. Models simulating this process show how individuals following local cues produce trail systems with many of the features of real-world networks. However, little has been done to investigate walkers with more complete knowledge of their environment and the abilities to plan their behavior intelligently. Here we introduce a simple general model for trail formation, based on minimizing cost of movement by individuals. As in real environments, our simulations produce a striking variety of complex trail networks. We show that these trail systems optimally connect space according to the spatial needs of the walkers, that the geometry of those trail systems matches theoretical predictions and that the systems they generate may fall into multiple attracting states. As technological advances allow us to quantify trail systems across diverse habitats and species, our model provides a theoretical foundation for empirical research on animal trails and for understanding the emergence of human transportation networks, with implications for urban design.

title: iGC: Antibody Optimization via Reinforcement Learning over a Learned Somatic Hypermutation Prior
abstract: Antibody affinity maturation is a natural optimization process in which B cells acquire mutations through somatic hypermutation (SHM), undergo selection for improved antigen binding, and iteratively evolve toward higher affinity. Computationally modeling this process requires capturing both biologically plausible mutations and antigen-specific selection. However, existing mutation models do not directly optimize binding, while affinity optimization often neglects realistic mutation trajectories. We introduce iGC (in silico Germinal Centers), a two-stage reinforcement learning (RL) framework for antigen-specific antibody optimization. Stage 1 learns an SHM mutation prior from parent-child pairs in B-cell lineage trees and adapts it to a target affinity-maturation dataset. Stage 2 initializes an RL policy from this prior and optimizes antigen binding with Kullback-Leibler (KL) regularization toward the frozen prior. To prevent reward exploitation, including repetitive high-reward substitutions and structurally tolerated framework mutations, we introduce a Reward-Tax Meta-Gradient objective. RewardNet smooths the affinity landscape, while TaxNet penalizes reward overexploitation, jointly defining a learned meta-reward for policy optimization. We evaluate iGC on mutation prediction, SHM consistency, affinity optimization, and mutation diversity. The mutation prior more than doubles the strongest baseline in mutation-site prediction. Following RL optimization, iGC maintains SHM sequence structure. It also achieves a strong exploration-exploitation balance, yielding competitive reward-diversity products across candidate-selection cutoffs. These results demonstrate that iGC integrates biologically plausible mutation generation with antigen-specific affinity selection, providing an in silico framework for iterative antibody affinity maturation.
comment: 10 pages with supplementary documents

title: A Biologically Inspired Attention Model for Neural Signal Analysis
abstract: Understanding how the brain represents sensory information and triggers behavioural responses is a fundamental goal in neuroscience. Recent advances in neuronal recording techniques aim to progress towards this milestone, yet the resulting high-dimensional responses are challenging to interpret and link to relevant variables. Although existing machine learning models propose to do so, they often sacrifice interpretability for predictive power, effectively operating as black boxes. In this work, we introduce SPARKS, a biologically inspired model capable of high decoding accuracy and interpretable discovery within a single framework. SPARKS adapts the self-attention mechanism of large language models to extract information from the timing of single spikes and the sequence in which neurons fire using Hebbian learning. Trained with a criterion inspired by predictive coding to enforce temporal coherence, our model produces low-dimensional latent embeddings that are robust across sessions and animals. By directly capturing the underlying data distribution through a generative encoding-decoding framework, SPARKS matches or exceeds state-of-the-art decoders across diverse electrophysiology and calcium imaging datasets from the motor, visual and entorhinal cortices. Crucially, the Hebbian coefficients learned by the model are interpretable, allowing us to infer directed functional interactions and recover the known functional hierarchy of the mouse visual cortex. Overall, SPARKS unifies representation learning, high-performance decoding and model interpretability in a single framework by bridging neuroscience and AI, providing a powerful and versatile tool for dissecting neural computations and marking a step towards the next generation of biologically inspired intelligent systems.

title: A Comparison and Validation of BIDS Apps for Preprocessing of UCB-J PET data
abstract: Background Preprocessing of Positron Emission Tomography (PET) data can be performed in many different ways and often involves manual steps, resulting in reduced comparability across analyses and pipelines. Apps working on PET data organized according to the Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) seek to automate preprocessing, enabling the application of standardized pipelines that increase comparability and reproducibility. In this study, two of these apps were validated against in-house software. Methods Data were acquired in-house from 14 subjects who received placebo in a randomized controlled clinical trial and underwent two PET measurements using the radioligand [11C]UCB-J. Preprocessing was performed with two BIDS Apps, PETPrep and PICNIC, as well as an in-house software. Arterial blood data were processed using Bloodstream, and [11C]UCB-J total distribution volume (VT) values were calculated using a 1-tissue compartment model using kinfitr. Results VT values for all 9 regions of interest were highly consistent across tools with estimates of Intraclass Correlation Coefficients for consistency ranging between 0.94 and >0.99, although bias between tools measured as signed Percentage Difference was present, ranging from 0.1% - 10.2% depending on the region. Tools performed similarly on test-retest metrics. We observed a negative test-retest bias in [11C]UCB-J VT of unknown origin. Conclusion BIDS Apps produce reliable and consistent results when compared both with each other and with an in-house software optimized for processing and analysis of our in-house data. Region-dependant bias between tools warrants caution for direct comparison of VT between tools. The usage of these apps could enable better comparability across publications

title: A Preventive Effect of Exercise in a Mouse Model of Essential Tremor
abstract: The effects of exercise have not been widely studied for potential benefits in essential tremor (ET), while this has been growing for other neurodegenerative disorders. This study examines the effects of two types of exercise [high-intensity interval training (HIIT) and resistance training (RT)] on mice that were subjected to harmaline injections to trigger tremor. We employed a repeated-measures design with three groups: a HIIT group, a RT group, and a sedentary (SED) control group. Each group received an injection before and after the intervention. Tremor kinetics (power within the 8-14 and 14-29 Hz bands) were assessed using accelerometry. Tremor kinematics were also assessed using high-speed video analysis, for validation. As potential signalling molecules from exercise, we also tested for blood lactate and BDNF in each group. Compared to pre-intervention measurements, we found a significant decrease in power within the 8-14 Hz band combined with an increase in the 14-29 Hz band, for the HIIT group, but not in the RT or SED groups. We also found a change in BDNF concentration for the HIIT group. These results suggest that the HIIT protocol may have helped the animal to shift tremor frequency to higher bands, thereby offering functional resistance to harmaline-induced tremor. This study supports high intensity aerobic physical exercise as a potential therapeutic/preventive intervention for ET, with translational implications for human studies.

title: A VTA-pontine GABA pathway biases locomotor direction via local and distal inhibition
abstract: Locomotor direction in mammals is implemented by descending circuits, yet how midbrain selection systems bias directional motor output remains unclear. Here we define a projection-defined inhibitory pathway from the ventral tegmental area to the oral pontine reticular nucleus (VTAPnO) whose activation is sufficient to drive backward locomotion. These TH- VTA neurons form monosynaptic GABAA synapses locally while projecting to PnO, establishing a dual local-projection inhibitory architecture. Somatic activation reliably induced backward locomotion, and selective stimulation of VTAPnO terminals reproduced the effect. Pathway recruitment produced a rapid transient increase in dopaminergic single-unit activity and frequency-dependent increases in dopaminergic population calcium signals in awake mice. During forced locomotion, chronically recorded VTAPnO neurons were preferentially engaged during reverse compared to forward rotations. Together, these findings reveal a projection-defined midbrain pathway that biases locomotor direction through coordinated local inhibition and distal engagement of a brainstem premotor node.

title: A Whole-Mouse-Brain Model of Coupled Neural Masses: Analysis of Network Dynamics
abstract: Neural mass models coupled through empirical structural connectomes are widely used to simulate whole-brain activity, but the dynamics of the resulting large, delay-coupled networks are rarely analyzed directly. We present a dynamical systems analysis of 434 Jansen-Rit neural masses coupled by the Allen Mouse Brain Connectivity Atlas at the canonical single-node parameter values. Pseudo-arclength continuation of the network equilibria in the global coupling scale and in the baseline external input, with stability determined from the characteristic roots of the delayed linearization by Beyn's contour-integral method, indicates where the network must oscillate and where it can rest. Simulations show that the oscillatory regime is chaotic: the maximum Lyapunov exponent is positive for the empirical connectome, grows with network size and coupling scale, and is insensitive to the conduction delays, but it is suppressed when the arrangement of connection weights is flattened, shuffled, or rewired. The same weight modifications that suppress chaos drive the network toward full synchrony and abolish metastability, as measured by the Kuramoto order parameter. We discuss the consequences of these findings for fitting whole-brain neural mass models to empirical data.

title: A domain-general basal ganglia mechanism for inhibitory control during language comprehension
abstract: Whether controlled language processing involves domain-general or language-specific neural circuits is subject of controversial debate. We tested whether the inhibitory control of linguistic activity shares a common neural process with motor inhibition in twenty humans undergoing intra- and extracranial neural field potential recordings and deep-brain stimulation. Engaging motor and linguistic inhibition simultaneously resulted in a significant behavioral cost, suggesting a shared underlying neural process. Indeed, neural decoders trained during motor inhibition were able to decode linguistic inhibition and vice versa. Depth-electrode recordings from the subthalamic nucleus (STN), a key basal ganglia area for inhibitory control, showed increased {beta}-band (13-30 Hz) activity during both linguistic and motor inhibition. Finally, disrupting the STN via deep-brain stimulation impaired behavioral and neural signatures of both linguistic and motor inhibition. Together, these findings show that the inhibitory control of language and movement share a domain-general mechanism implemented via the subthalamic nucleus of the basal ganglia.

title: A hypothalamo-septo-hippocampal circuit for REM sleep-dependent consolidation of social memory
abstract: REM sleep constitutes a critical window for memory consolidation, yet the brain circuits orchestrating this process remain incompletely defined. Here, we identify a lateral supramammillary nucleus (SuM)-medial septum (MS) projection as a REM sleep-specialized pathway essential for hippocampal memory consolidation. Fiber photometry and optrode recordings revealed that lateral SuM-MS projecting neurons were selectively active during REM sleep. REM-specific optogenetic silencing of this projection impaired consolidation of both social and contextual fear memories. Crucially, silencing of its downstream target, the MS-CA2 pathway, during REM sleep selectively disrupted social memory while sparing contextual fear memory. This functional dissection establishes a hypothalamo-septo-hippocampal circuit (lateral SuM-MS-CA2) dedicated to social memory processing, in parallel to the recently-described direct SuM-CA2 pathway. These results also position the SuM as a REM sleep-hub that routes information via parallel septal pathways to consolidate distinct memory modalities.
