abstract: The vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) ligand and its main receptor VEGFR2 are considered to be essential for endothelial differentiation, proliferation, sprouting and survival . Blood vessels cannot form in growing embryos or tissues when VEGF–VEGFR2 signalling is compromised in all cells . The anti-VEGF antibody, which can block angiogenesis in cancer, wound healing or ischaemic diseases, is among the most widely used antibodies in the clinic. However, vascular resistance to anti-VEGF therapy has been reported . Here we used iFlpMosaics and iSuRe –HadCre to induce and track genetic mosaics of endothelial cells (ECs) lacking VEGFR2 during the entire embryonic and postnatal development. These Vegfr2 -knockout ( Vegfr2 KO ) ECs adapted, proliferated normally and competed with wild-type cells over time, eventually forming a substantial portion of the vascular network in most organs. Vegfr2 KO ECs could not sprout during the first wave of angiogenesis in most tissues, because this process is highly VEGF-dependent and favours growth and mobilization of wild-type ECs. However, owing to their inability to respond to VEGF, Vegfr2 KO ECs became dominant in veins, which represented a long-term and continuous source of ECs for subsequent waves of VEGF-independent angiogenesis. Comparative single-cell RNA sequencing analysis of ECs with acute and long-term loss of VEGFR2 identified both common and organ-specific molecular mechanisms of adaptation and resistance to VEGF signalling loss. These included significant endothelial venousization and upregulation of ligands for VEGFR1 and VEGFR3. VEGFR1 only partially compensated for VEGFR2 loss in capillary ECs, whereas VEGFR3 compensated only in arterial ECs. Loss of the three VEGF receptors did not compromise venous growth. Notably, loss of the master regulator of venous development, NR2F2 (also known as COUP-TFII), significantly compromised expansion of Vegfr2 KO ECs. This work has implications for our understanding of the role of VEGF receptors in angiogenesis and demonstrates venousization as a mechanism of adaptation and resistance to VEGF signalling loss during angiogenesis.

abstract: High-affinity O -linked β - N -acetylglucosamine ( O -GlcNAc)-specific antibodies are crucial for the sensitive detection and functional study of O- GlcNAcylation. Here, we report the development of a nanomolar-affinity O- GlcNAc antibody named EPR19847 by using a degenerate O- GlcNAcylated peptide as the immunogen. The EPR19847 antibody can be used for O- GlcNAc detection, imaging, isolation, and chromatin immunoprecipitation. Using this antibody, O- GlcNAcylated proteins are enriched and identified in mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs). Chromatin immunoprecipitation followed by next-generation sequencing demonstrates that O- GlcNAc is enriched around the promoters of highly expressed genes, and that its genomic distribution is positively correlated with transcription-activating marks including H3K4me3, H3K9ac, and RNA polymerase II in mESCs. Further analysis suggests a high occupancy of O- GlcNAcylation within super-enhancers. We anticipate that EPR19847 will serve as a powerful tool for the highly sensitive detection and systematic functional dissection of O- GlcNAc.

abstract: Artificial intelligence is reshaping scientific discovery across diverse fields. Yet scientific AI remains constrained by data curation, which demands substantial manual effort and deep domain expertise, creating major cost and scalability barriers. Here we present the Agentic Intelligent Data Engine (AIDE), a multi-agent framework that automates data curation for scientific AI. AIDE collects, selects, and organizes data in three stages, providing an end-to-end pipeline that turns a data request into training-ready datasets. We benchmarked AIDE on 14 tasks across biomedical and chemical domains. Scientific AI models built with AIDE-curated datasets matched or outperformed those built with manually curated data, and AIDE’s fully automated preparation delivered significant gains in efficiency and data utilization without compromising quality. These findings provide consistent evidence of AIDE’s applicability across scientific domains and usage paradigms and demonstrate its potential to accelerate scientific AI development and democratize access to scientific AI.

abstract: Despite studies linking metabolism and cancer, our understanding of the metabolite network that drives metastasis remains incomplete. Through a metabolic RNAi-based screen for cell invasion, we identify alpha-aminoadipate (2-AAA), the intermediate metabolite of aminoadipic semialdehyde synthase (AASS) in the saccharopine pathway, as a common pivotal factor in metastasis of human cancers. Metabolite-protein connectivity mapping reveals that 2-AAA binds to SAE1, a crucial component of the SUMO-activating enzyme E1, and enhances SAE1 recruitment to UBA2, facilitating sumoylation. 2-AAA-mediated sumoylation of the RNA polymerase subunit POLR2A then partially promotes cancer cell invasion by inducing the expression of metastasis-promoting genes, including SPG11 and KCTD7 . Targeting AASS with cetalkonium chloride, a newly identified small molecule inhibitor against AASS, attenuates cancer cell invasion and tumor metastasis. Our study highlights the mechanism by which metastasis is mediated by metabolite-driven sumoylation and indicates AASS as an effective therapeutic target for mitigating metastatic cancer progression.

abstract: Magnetic tweezers are a popular biophysical instrument for manipulating and measuring single molecules. Most groups rely on custom-built setups tailored to specific experiments, making it challenging to implement and share software. Typically, image acquisition and hardware control are automated via LabVIEW, while real-time video processing is implemented in C + + /CUDA libraries. Live processing can eliminate the need to store raw video, enabling high throughput, fast acquisition rates, and simplified experimental workflows. However, no open-source general-purpose software framework currently unifies these capabilities for magnetic tweezers experiments. Here, we introduce MagTrack and MagScope open-source Python-based tools designed to fill this gap. MagTrack is an image-processing library that efficiently determines bead positions from magnetic-tweezers videos using CPU or GPU computation. MagScope is a comprehensive software framework offering a graphical user interface, real-time hardware control, data acquisition, and video processing. It is built on a multiprocessing architecture for responsive, high-throughput computation. Together, MagTrack and MagScope offer a fully customizable, end-to-end, open-source Python alternative to proprietary or fragmented systems, enabling laboratories to adapt and extend the framework according to their experimental needs.

abstract: Increased B cell receptor signaling pathways in patients with melanoma correlates with a favorable clinical response to a cancer vaccine expressing multiple tumor-associated antigens. Here, we utilize phage immunoprecipitation sequencing (PhIP-seq) and Rapid Extracellular Antigen Profiling (REAP) assays to analyze the autoantibody profiles of patients with melanoma from a dendritic cell vaccine trial (NCT01622933), before and after vaccination. Patients have significantly elevated breadth and titer of autoantibodies compared to healthy donors. Vaccination results in the induction of de novo autoantibodies, particularly those with a favorable clinical outcome. Reduced serum SDF1-alpha, MIP-1ß, MCP1 and increased circulating monocytes are associated with development of autoantibodies. We identify plasma autoantibody signatures separating melanoma from healthy subjects as well as clinical responders vs non-responders to vaccination treatment. These findings demonstrate the potential for autoantibodies as diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers that predict clinical outcomes in cancer.

abstract: The intestinal mucosa functions alongside trillions of commensal microbes, with immune and epithelial responses contributing to microbiota homeostasis. Both immune and nerve cells are implicated in this microbial balance, but the regulatory functions of epithelial enteroendocrine cells (EEC) are not understood well. Here we show that EEC depletion in mouse colons via Satb2-mediated Neurog3 deficiency enhances goblet cell expression of prominent antimicrobial peptides, with stronger effects in female than in male mice. Mechanistically, serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine; 5-HT) derived from enterochromaffin (EC) cells, an EEC-subtype, acts on sensory neurons to suppress the mucosal levels of calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) under physiological conditions. In the absence of local serotonin, elevated CGRP levels promote mast cell infiltration and interleukin-13 (IL-13) secretion in EEC-depleted mice and enhance antimicrobial gene expression in goblet cells. Our findings thus delineate an epithelial–neuronal–immune axis, wherein EC cells fine-tune goblet cell antimicrobial output to preserve gut microbial equilibrium.

abstract: Microproteins (typically <100 amino acids) regulate diverse cellular processes, yet their small size and low abundance make interactome mapping challenging and particularly sensitive to perturbation by conventional enzyme-based proximity-labeling tags. Here, we developed FlashID, an ultra-compact genetically encoded proximity labeling (PL) system that combines a six-amino-acid tetracysteine tag (CCXXCC, <700 Da) with the turn-on biarsenical photocatalyst FlAsH. Upon tag binding and visible-light irradiation, FlAsH generates singlet oxygen to enable spatially and temporally controlled oxidative labeling of proximal proteins. In side-by-side analyses of the bacterial microprotein AzuC, FlashID recovered the validated interactor GlpD and identified additional physiologically relevant partners that were not captured by TurboID or IP-MS under the conditions tested. FlashID also resolved compartment-specific interactomes of diverse microproteins, including RP11-469A, which we identified as a mitochondrial intermembrane protein that interacts with PHB2 to regulate proliferation. Finally, the extension of FlashID to E. coli , mammalian cells, C. elegans and Arabidopsis thaliana establishes FlashID as a complementary, minimally perturbative platform for decoding microprotein interaction networks in vivo and advancing photocatalytic proximity labeling technologies.

abstract: The intracellular delivery of therapeutic macromolecules remains a major challenge in biomedicine. Capsid-forming proteins are one promising vehicle, but to date, these have required cellular assembly or rely on fusogens for cell entry, limiting their scalability and utility. Here we reconstitute the Drosophila melanogaster Arc1 (dArc1) retroelement-derived capsid entirely from purified recombinant protein components and in vitro transcribed RNA, creating a fully defined, cell-free assembled protein nanoparticle system. We engineered the dArc1 RNA-binding domain to efficiently encapsulate both mRNA payloads and Cas9 ribonucleoproteins. We show that dArc1 capsids bind mammalian cells through a direct interaction with the surface receptor SORCS2. Leveraging this interaction, we demonstrate that intramuscular injection of dArc1 capsids carrying Cas9 gene editors achieves up to 18% exon skipping and restores dystrophin expression in muscle fibers of mdx mice, a model of Duchenne muscular dystrophy. This work demonstrates the potential of in vitro-assembled protein nanoparticles for delivery of molecular cargoes.

abstract: To advance genetic understanding of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), we conduct multi-ancestry genome-wide association studies (GWAS) meta-analyses of 63,415 cases of Europeans and East Asians, and identified 60 previously unreported susceptibility loci. Integrating multi-ancestry transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS), cell type-specific TWAS, alternative splicing, and alternative polyadenylation analyses using RNA-sequencing data from normal colon tissues of 707 Europeans and 364 East Asians, we identify 441 candidate risk genes, including 324 not previously implicated by GWAS or TWAS, of which 291 were further supported by colocalization or summary-data-based Mendelian randomization analyses. These genes converge on pathways central to IBD pathogenesis (e.g., immune regulation), with over half showing transcriptional dysregulation supported by single-cell and spatial omics analyses. We further identify 44 druggable genes linked to 221 approved drugs or Phase II/III clinical-stage compounds. Our findings deepen the understanding of IBD genetics and provide insights for future research relevant to precision medicine for IBD.

abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic inflammatory disorder driven by dysregulated immune responses. Macrophage-mediated inflammation is central to the pathology, and it is important to understand the epigenetic mechanisms involved. By screening epigenetic molecules that are differentially expressed in published human IBD datasets, we find Protein Arginine Methyltransferase 6 (PRMT6) consistently downregulated in IBD samples compared to healthy controls. Co-occurrence of Prmt6 suppression and Il1b induction within the myeloid compartment in colon biopsy samples indicates that PRMT6 limits macrophage-driven inflammation. Concordantly, Prmt6 -deficient mice exhibit increased susceptibility to both DSS- and TNBS-induced colitis, characterized by exacerbated tissue damage and systemic elevation of IL-1β. Transcriptomic profiling confirms that PRMT6 deficiency selectively upregulates Il1b among inflammatory mediators. Mechanistically, PRMT6 suppresses Il1b transcription by interacting with RBBP5 and disrupting SET1A complex assembly, thereby reducing H3K4me3 enrichment at the Il1b promoter, independently of its canonical H3R2me2a catalytic activity. Furthermore, PRMT6 is transcriptionally silenced by the NF-κB subunit p50 during inflammation. Pharmacological inhibition of p50 restores PRMT6 expression, thus protecting mice from DSS-induced colitis in a PRMT6-dependent manner. Our findings highlight PRMT6 as a pivotal epigenetic regulator of the inflammatory response and provide proof of principle for targeting the p50–PRMT6–IL-1β axis in IBD.

abstract: Translatable circular RNAs (circRNAs) have emerged as a promising alternative to conventional mRNA therapy due to their improved stability that results in a prolonged expression window. The translation of circRNAs is mainly driven by internal ribosome entry site (IRES) or IRES-like elements, which is tightly regulated by various trans -acting RNA binding proteins (RBPs). Here we develop a cell-based system to systematically screen RBPs that enhance translation of circRNAs, identifying 68 proteins as putative activators of noncanonical translation. These translation activators are involved in a broad range of biological processes including RNA processing, ribosomal biogenesis, and translation initiation. We further design a machine learning algorithm to extract common sequence features of these activators and predict more potential RBPs with translation activator activities. The newly identified and predicted activators are subsequently validated to promote the IRES-mediated circRNA translation in a context-dependent fashion. Overall, this study provides new insights into IRES-related trans -acting factors and expands the toolbox for engineered RBPs in RNA synthetic biology.

abstract: Computational and mathematical models are frequently used in the design of appropriate experimental protocols for in vitro cell differentiation assays. However, models are limited by typical monotonic dose-responses, preventing them from being used for cytokine effects that are largely non-monotonic. To address this shortcoming, we developed Uncovering Non-Monotonic Antagonistic and Synergistic Combinations (UNMASC), a mathematical model describing non-monotonic dose-response surfaces of cytokine interactions that distinguishes synergy of efficacy and potency. We demonstrate that our approach successfully recapitulates non-monotonic observed dose-response surfaces characterizing in vitro T cell progenitor differentiation. Our results show that interleukin (IL)3 and IL7 have antagonistic effects alone but are synergistic in combination. Altogether, UNMASC can aid in the efficient design of cell generation assays and extends drug interaction surfaces to a broader range of dose-responses.

abstract: Loss of proteostasis can cause protein aggregation and trigger aggrephagy, yet how these biological processes are coordinated remains unclear. Here, we showed that p62 condensates transit from a gel-like to a more liquid-like state in response to proteotoxic stress. VHL was recruited to aggresomes and colocalizes with p62, which is crucial for p62 to perform its distinct functions in aggresome formation and autophagic degradation. Mechanistically, VHL binds to p62 through its IDR1 region and increases the liquid-like properties via IDR2 region. VHL depletion or disease-associated IDR2 mutations impair p62 condensate dynamics, leading to excessive accumulation of aggregated proteins and concomitant KEAP1 sequestration/NRF2 stabilization. A chimeric peptide linking the p62 PB1 domain to VHL IDR2 recapitulates VHL’s fluidity-promoting activity and suppresses tumorigenesis and protein aggregation. Overall, our findings reveal an HIF-independent tumor-suppressive role of VHL in regulating proteostasis and suggest a new treatment for cancer through the targeting of condensate dynamics.

abstract: How transcriptional asymmetry arises in the epiblast before gastrulation remains a central question in mammalian development. Using a targeted CRISPRa screen, we identify Wt1 as a regulator of lineage-associated transcriptional programmes during formative pluripotency. Wt1 is transiently induced during formative pluripotency in vitro and in vivo, coincident with emerging lineage biases. Precocious Wt1 induction advances cells toward post-implantation identity, whereas Wt1 -deficient cells execute naïve exit but show impaired acquisition of formative and lineage-associated programmes. WT1 binds active regulatory elements together with OTX2, OCT4 and FOXO1. Comparison of Wt1 splice isoforms identifies KTS splice status as the major determinant of divergent anterior/neuroectodermal and posterior/mesodermal transcriptional programmes in vitro. In the E5.5 epiblast, Wt1 expression and splice composition align with lineage-biased states, linking isoform usage to anterior bias in vivo. Isoform-dependent programmes are conserved in human pluripotent cells. These findings identify alternative splicing as a mechanism tuning lineage-associated transcriptional bias before gastrulation.

abstract: Preprimary education is central to the global education agenda, including Sustainable Development Goal 4.2. Despite global momentum in low- and middle-income countries, cross-national evidence on long-term outcomes associated with preprimary education legislation remains limited. Here we applied a matrix-completion approach with subgroup and sensitivity analyses using 495 nationally representative surveys from 1990 to 2024, covering nearly 6.7 million women across 117 countries. Eligibility under the legislation was associated with higher educational enrolment and completion, and with more gender-egalitarian attitudes, more favourable empowerment-related behaviours and greater reproductive autonomy. For example, eligibility was associated with higher female primary-school enrolment (1.21 percentage points (pp); 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.52 to 1.91; P < 0.001) and completion (0.75 pp; 95% CI 0.24 to 1.25; P = 0.004), greater disapproval of wife-beating (1.04 pp; 95% CI 0.53 to 1.56; P < 0.001), greater participation in decisions about husbands’ earnings (3.25 pp; 95% CI 2.50 to 4.00; P < 0.001) and greater ever use of contraception (2.96 pp; 95% CI 2.33 to 3.59; P < 0.001). Eligibility under the legislation was also associated with lower rates of adolescent childbearing (−2.41 pp; 95% CI −2.67 to −2.14; P < 0.001) and child marriage (−0.43 pp; 95% CI −0.71 to −0.15; P = 0.003). These findings provide cross-national evidence directly relevant to ongoing policy discussions surrounding Sustainable Development Goal 4.2 and broader global development agendas, while emphasizing the importance of implementation capacity and equitable system expansion.

abstract: Accurate particle picking of macromolecules of diverse types, shapes and sizes in cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) is critical for understanding the molecular architecture of biological systems in their native state. Current deep learning methods have shown potential for identifying macromolecules in tomograms; however, they are vulnerable to annotation noise in the training data and to imbalanced distributions of macromolecule species. Here, to address these limitations, we developed RobPicker, a meta-learning framework that effectively mitigates these issues by automatically learning to correct label errors and by placing greater emphasis on smaller and rarer macromolecule species. In evaluations across diverse cryo-ET datasets with noisy labels and imbalanced species distributions, RobPicker substantially outperforms state-of-the-art methods, particularly in identifying small and rare macromolecules. The robustness and efficiency of RobPicker led to improved resolution in 3D density maps of protein structures, enabling high-resolution cellular structural biology analysis.

abstract: Humans can swiftly learn to recognize visual objects after minimal exposure. Integrating new information with existing knowledge requires forming enduring neuronal representations to enable future recognition. Yet, the neuronal mechanisms in the human brain underlying such rapid perceptual changes remain unclear. Here we recorded single-neuron activity in occipital cortex (OC) and medial temporal lobe (MTL) regions as participants rapidly learned to recognize degraded images. OC and MTL neurons modulated their activity to encode newly learned visual information and reshape perception. Population decoding revealed that OC neurons required additional processing time to resolve the identity of learned images, with delayed neuronal responses in the MTL. Our findings suggest that OC supports recognition after rapid learning via extensive recurrent processing, potentially involving higher-order neocortical areas, without relying on feedback from MTL. These results provide mechanistic constraints for biologically plausible models of visual recognition and few-shot visual learning.

title: P2RX7 drives inflammatory microglia and pathogenic extracellular vesicle secretion in tauopathy.
abstract: P2X purinoreceptor 7 (P2RX7), an ATP-gated ion channel, contributes to Alzheimer's disease (AD) progression, but its molecular mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we show that genetic disruption of P2rx7 mitigates brain atrophy, tau accumulation, and cognitive impairment in PS19 mice. Microglia-specific, but not astrocyte-specific, deletion of P2rx7 suppresses tau propagation. Single-cell RNA sequencing identifies a previously unrecognized first-responding microglial state (FRM) with prominent P2rx7 expression. P2RX7 promotes the transition from FRM to an inflammatory microglial state enriched in extracellular vesicle (EV) biogenesis. P2RX7 increases EV loading of tau and of mitochondrial proteins and DNA, which activate cytosolic DNA sensing and interferon signaling in recipient microglia. Tau-containing microglial EVs disrupt neuronal endolysosomal integrity and facilitate endosomal tau escape and phosphorylation. Thus, P2RX7 regulates the FRM branch point, driving inflammatory microglial transition and EV-mediated spread of tau and toxic mitochondrial molecules and highlighting the P2RX7-EV axis as a therapeutic target in AD.

title: A structural analysis of U.S. homelessness through Markov random fields: Identifying predictors and potential causal links through permutation tests.
abstract: Many researchers who study homelessness argue that traditional frameworks are often too narrow, failing to account for groups outside the reach of social services. Despite historic calls to broaden the scope of sampling to encompass structural forces, only recent advancements have enabled the development of a robust framework for accurate measurement and analysis. This study utilizes Markov random fields (MRFs) to explore the influences of key structural indicators on homelessness from 2007 to 2024. By employing partial correlations, we investigate the interplay among geographic locations at the state-level among the following variables: the job market, median rent, eviction rates, occupancy rates, median income, the construction of new homes, the cost of one-bedroom units, funding from Housing and Urban Development (HUD), and policies under democrat or republican elections (by state). Our findings reveal that rent, income, and the availability of single-bedroom units are the foremost predictors of homelessness rates, underscoring the significance of housing affordability and availability as central determinants. The analysis also distinguishes variation in conditional dependence patterns between states governed by different political parties, even as they change, spotlighting substantial differences in the partial association rates across partisan lines. The results emphasize the need for policy reforms targeted at increasing housing affordability over more long-term strategies, such as the construction of new homes, and suggest that political contexts distinctly shape the effectiveness of structural interventions. These insights offer a valuable framework for policymakers aiming to address the root causes of homelessness through targeted structural reforms. An exploratory lag-1 directed temporal network reveals that the HUD↔homelessness feedback cycle is empirically present especially in Republican-led states; we report this as suggestive (cluster-permutation p = 0.12) and as a hypothesis for future panel-VAR work. We frame the conditional-dependence structure as descriptive rather than causal, state the assumptions a causal reading would require, and provide four supplementary specifications - cluster bootstrap, two-way state-and-year fixed-effects residualisation, nonparanormal transformation, and Fast Causal Inference - that probe each assumption.

title: A three process approach for insomnia-like awakenings.
abstract: Mathematical modelling of sleep is a growing field, with an increasing number of applications to sleep disorders. However, despite its high prevalence and under-diagnosis worldwide, insomnia has not been among these disorders. We chart the development of sleep models and investigate the hypothesis that they can be simply modified to model insomnia, ultimately introducing a new model focusing on nocturnal awakenings as a starting point of insomnia-like behaviour, based on a three process approach. We find that several of these models can make promising steps towards producing nighttime awakenings characteristic of many types of insomnia with minor modifications, but that none can fully reproduce every key criterion with only minor adaptations. In particular, we find that the stability of the sleeping state is an important factor in more complex contemporary neuronal population models' abilities to incorporate awakenings, with both permanently stable and permanently non-stable sleep proving to be obstacles. Instead, we base our new model on the simpler foundational two process model, incorporating an original, quantitative wakefulness drive. We further analyse the sensitivity of its new parameters and the statistical properties of the nighttime awakening phenomena it produces. This new drive includes both physiology-based arousal impulses and environmental and psychological disturbances, and provides the foundation of a new approach to future quantitative modelling of insomnia phenotypes.

title: AVISNet: An edge-computing model for acoustic identification of species from the Doñana bird community.
abstract: The global decline in biodiversity calls for scalable and efficient species monitoring. Birds, as sensitive ecological indicators with rich vocal activity, are particularly well suited for passive acoustic monitoring (PAM), which enables extensive, non-invasive data collection. Yet the large volumes of audio generated by PAM require automated and efficient processing pipelines to extract meaningful biological information in real time. To address this challenge, we integrated automated acoustic species identification directly into embedded devices (i.e., at the edge), enabling autonomous on-site data processing without reliance on cloud-based computation. Our methodology emphasizes model efficiency and leverages lightweight pre-trained architectures (e.g., MobileNet), alongside advanced learning strategies such as knowledge distillation and few-shot learning to overcome data scarcity for under-represented species. This methodology was applied as a case study to acoustic identification of bird species native to Doñana National Park, Spain. We assessed the performance and efficiency of our models at three levels of acoustic data: focal segments, focal recordings, and soundscape recordings. On focal recordings, our models achieve up to 0.70 F1-score in species identification task. At the soundscape level, we evaluated performance using three real-world soundscape datasets, measuring accuracy metrics at both the vocalization and dataset levels. Our lightweight convolutional neural networks achieve high accuracy at the dataset level (F1-score: 0.56-0.72), solid accuracy at the vocalization level (F1-score: 0.29-0.39; mAP: 0.41-0.69), and fast and energy-efficient inference on resource-limited hardware (2.2-4.7× speed-ups vs. BirdNET, 41-71% energy savings). Overall, our results show that these networks achieve functional species recognition performance while substantially reducing inference latency and energy requirements relative to BirdNET, thus enabling on-device deployment on low-power units. The system already scales to 300 + species, with room for further expansion, bridging the gap between general-purpose tools like BirdNET and localized embedded monitoring pipelines.

title: Academic entitlement and student well-being: The mediating role of the impostor phenomenon.
abstract: Despite growing evidence linking academic entitlement to diminished student outcomes, the psychological mechanisms through which entitled academic expectations erode student well-being remain insufficiently understood. The present study examines the mediating role of the impostor phenomenon in the relationship between academic entitlement and well-being among university students. A cross-sectional correlational design was employed with a sample of 864 undergraduate students recruited from Al-Azhar University and Kafr El-Sheikh University in Egypt. Participants completed the Academic Entitlement Scale (AES-28), the Short Clance Impostor Phenomenon Scale (CIPS-10), and the BBC Well-Being Scale (BBC-WBS). Mediation analysis was conducted using the PROCESS macro with bootstrapping based on 5,000 resamples. Results revealed that academic entitlement significantly and positively predicted the impostor phenomenon, which in turn significantly and negatively predicted student well-being. The impostor phenomenon partially mediated the relationship between academic entitlement and well-being, accounting for approximately 23% of the total effect. These findings suggest that entitlement-driven expectations are associated with lower overall well-being (composite score), both directly and indirectly by fostering fraudulence-related self-doubt. Mediation was not tested separately for psychological, physical, and relational well-being. Universities, particularly in comparable Egyptian and collectivist contexts, may consider addressing both entitled academic attitudes and impostor-related cognitions through counseling interventions and pedagogical strategies.

title: An analysis of enrollment rates by admitting service for a secondary analysis of enrollment data from a randomized smoking-cessation trial (FIESTA).
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Enrollment into clinical trials is challenging and has a major effect on the feasibility and the generalizability of a study. We used data from a previously completed hospital-based smoking cessation study to determine if enrollment rates varied by hospital admitting service, specifically comparing Medicine and Psychiatry departments.
METHODS: We examined enrollment in the Financial Incentives for Smoking Cessation (FIESTA) study, which was conducted at the Veterans Affairs New York Harbor Healthcare System. FIESTA tested the effectiveness of financial incentives on smoking cessation among hospitalized patients. A total of 268 patients were eligible, with 182 enrolled in the original FIESTA study. In our secondary analysis, a LASSO approach was applied to the data set to create a model examining admitting service, age, sex, race and ethnicity, education, and number of cigarettes per day and their association with enrollment.
RESULTS: The enrollment rates were higher for patients admitted to the Psychiatry service (80.2%) than to the Medicine and other services (59.9%). Patients with a high school education or less also had a higher enrollment rate (87.2%) than those with higher education (57.7%). Increasing age was associated with lower odds of enrollment (aOR = 0.97, 95% CI: 0.94, 0.99). Hispanic ethnicity appeared to associate with a higher odds of enrollment compared to non-Hispanic White (aOR = 2.52, 95% CI 1.11, 5.75). Higher odds of enrollment were observed among patients admitted to the Psychiatry service (aOR = 2.51, 95% CI: 1.23-5.12), while lower odds were observed among those with higher education (aOR = 0.17, 95% CI: 0.06-0.49).
CONCLUSIONS: This research suggests that smoking cessation programs can effectively enroll a diverse patient population, including typically underrepresented groups such as those with lower education status and those with mental health diagnoses. Such enrollment efforts would enable studies to be more generalizable to the smoking population. Findings also emphasize the potential of urban hospital settings to support equitable enrollment efforts. The present work is a secondary analysis of the FIESTA RCT (NCT02506829). Future research should explore additional demographic factors, such as comorbidities and confidence in quitting, to better understand motivations for participation.

title: Assessment of Pleurotus ostreatus and Pleurotus citrinopileatus mushroom as bioshielding materials for neutron attenuation in medical cyclotron.
abstract: Neutron absorbance efficiency is crucial for radiation shielding and nuclear reactors, with mushrooms like Pleurotus Ostreatus (PO) and Pleurotus Citrinopleatus (PC) enhancing this property due to their nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, cadmium, and carbon content. Processed into 3 × 3 inch blocks at the National Institute of Nuclear Medicine and Allied Science (NINMAS), the mushrooms are dried at 80°C and ground to powder for analysis. Structural studies using XRD, FESEM, FTIR, and UV-vis spectroscopic reveal high carbon and oxygen levels. For the PO, the XRD investigation showed a broad diffraction peak that corresponded to an estimated crystallite size of about 1.34 nm, while PC showed a mostly amorphous structure devoid of clear crystalline diffraction peaks. The FTIR identifies various functional groups, and UV-vis spectra confirm the presence of sulfur and carbon. Neutron interaction mechanisms in mushroom-derived shielding materials involve moderation and scattering by the hydrogen-rich matrix, followed by capture at nitrogen and sulfur sites. HPGe spectroscopic confirms effective neutron interaction and attenuation via the detection of activation products such as K-40 in this study. Both samples show significant K-40 levels of 30 Bq/kg, while Th-232 and U-238 are found to be 2-3 Bq/kg and 5-6 Bq/kg, respectively. The findings demonstrate that these mushroom blocks are not neutron-transparent, but rather contribute to neutron moderation and absorption acts as a bio-shielding materials in the cyclotron facility.

title: Assessment of coronavirus disease 2019 mRNA vaccine response in kidney transplant recipients.
abstract: Kidney transplant recipients are vulnerable to developing severe coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) infection. Although mRNA vaccines have significantly improved outcomes, seropositivity rates remain variable in immunosuppressed patients. This study aimed to evaluate the antibody response to COVID-19 mRNA vaccines, identify factors affecting immunogenicity, and examine the association between antibody titers and subsequent SARS-CoV-2 infection and COVID-19-related hospitalization among kidney transplant recipients. We retrospectively studied 372 adult kidney transplant recipients who received two doses of COVID-19 mRNA vaccine after transplantation and had anti-SARS‑CoV‑2 spike protein receptor-binding domain antibodies measured ≥ 14 days after the second dose and prior to receiving a third dose. We categorized patients based on previous COVID-19 infection, post-vaccination antibody status (seropositive or seronegative), and antibody titers (low or high). Factors associated with poor vaccine response (seronegativity) and with high antibody titers (antibody titer ≥ 121 U/mL) were determined using multivariable regression models. The proportion of patients with subsequent COVID-19 infection was higher in the seronegative group than in the seropositive or previous infection groups (36% vs. 26% vs. 13%, respectively; P = 0.02). Multivariable regression analysis revealed higher odds of poor response to the mRNA vaccine among patients aged > 52 years compared with those aged ≤ 52 years (aOR = 1.94; 95% CI: 1.12-3.36; P = 0.018). Lower odds were observed among male patients (aOR = 0.43; 95% CI: 0.24-0.77; P = 0.004) and those taking azathioprine (aOR = 0.26; 95% CI: 0.07-0.91; P = 0.035). The proportion of patients with subsequent COVID-19 was also higher in the low-antibody group than in the high-antibody group (33% vs. 20%; P = 0.02). Multivariable logistic regression analysis showed lower odds of high SARS-CoV-2 antibody titers among patients aged > 51 years compared with those aged ≤ 51 years (aOR = 0.43; 95% CI: 0.24-0.75; P = 0.003). Higher odds were observed among those of African race (aOR = 2.82; 95% CI: 1.11-7.16; P = 0.03) and South Asian race (aOR = 2.27; 95% CI: 1.08-4.75; P = 0.03) compared with Middle Eastern recipients. Understanding the immunologic response to the SARS-CoV-2 vaccine in kidney transplant recipients is essential for preventing potentially life-threatening infection. Furthermore, identifying transplant recipients with a low vaccine-induced antibody response may help guide the development of individualized immunization strategies.

title: Association between habitual MSG consumption and compulsive eating behaviors in university students: A cross-sectional study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Monosodium glutamate (MSG), a widely used flavor enhancer, increases food palatability and may influence eating behavior. Although considered safe from a toxicological perspective, its potential association with compulsive eating patterns remains unclear. University students are particularly vulnerable to irregular dietary habits and high consumption of ultra-processed foods.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 555 Palestinian university students aged 18-30 years. MSG intake was assessed using a composite dietary exposure scale and categorized into tertiles (low, moderate, high). Food addiction was measured using the Yale Food Addiction Scale (YFAS), binge-eating severity using the Binge Eating Scale (BES), and perceived stress using the Perceived Stress Scale-4 (PSS-4). Logistic regression examined associations between MSG intake and food addiction, while linear regression assessed relationships with binge-eating severity and YFAS symptom counts, adjusting for age, gender, BMI, perceived stress, and academic year.
RESULTS: Food addiction was present in 24.7% of participants and increased across MSG tertiles (15.7% low vs. 33.0% high; p < 0.001). High MSG intake was associated with increased odds food addiction (adjusted OR = 2.75, 95% CI 1.63-4.65, p < 0.001). Higher MSG consumption was associated with greater binge-eating severity (β = 1.25, p < 0.001) and increased YFAS symptom counts, indicating a dose-response relationship. BMI and perceived stress were independent predictors of both outcomes. The adjusted model showed acceptable discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC] = 0.71).
CONCLUSIONS: Higher MSG intake was associated with increased food addiction symptoms and binge-eating severity among university students, suggesting frequent consumption of flavor-enhanced foods is a correlate of reward-driven eating behaviors, warranting further investigation.

title: BanglaHateCorpus: A large-scale bangla benchmark for hate speech classification and a transformer-based deep learning method.
abstract: Hate speech on social media refers to content that threatens, attacks, or dehumanizes people or groups based on specified characteristics, thereby eroding trust, worsening societal divisions, and causing psychological harm to the targeted communities. In digitally connected South Asian societies, strong in-group bonds and online inter-group hatred can rapidly lead to real-world violence, a risk intensified by the proliferation of Bangla texts, highlighting the urgent need for robust detection in this low-resource language. Previous studies have mostly focused on building their datasets by scraping various sources, without emphasizing standardized quality annotation or ensuring classification accuracy. To address these gaps, we introduce BanglaHateCorpus, a unified corpus of 168K examples consolidated from eight public sources, rigorously de-duplicated and annotated through a two-stage, human and LLM-assisted pipeline. Building on this benchmark, we propose BanHateFormer, a novel deep-learning model that embodies state-of-the-art transformer components, and replaces the conventional feed-forward blocks with a Mixture-of-Experts layer followed by a binary classification head. BanHateFormer achieves state-of-the-art classification results, as assessed by accuracy, precision, recall, and macro F1-score with approximately 94.74 times fewer parameters than comparable models, achieving a 91.33% macro F1-score on the BanglaHateCorpus dataset and 78.96% on the transliterated BanTH benchmark. BanHateFormer outperforms BanglaBERT and XLM-RoBERTa by up to 2.57% with three times fewer parameters, and improves macro F1-score by 3.38% on transliterated text, demonstrating strong performance on romanized inputs. BanHateFormer significantly surpasses existing transformer-based models in balancing memory efficiency and high-fidelity outputs, marking a breakthrough in hate speech classification with optimal space utilization.

title: Bayesian efficient coding.
abstract: The efficient coding hypothesis, which proposes that neurons are optimized to maximize information about the environment, has provided a guiding theoretical framework for sensory and systems neuroscience. More recently, a theory known as the Bayesian Brain hypothesis has focused on the brain's ability to integrate sensory and prior sources of information in order to perform Bayesian inference. Although pieces of a connection between these two hypotheses have appeared in prior work, a general formulation that treats the optimality criterion as an arbitrary functional of the posterior distribution - and thereby admits both information-based and other objectives within a single framework - has remained largely implicit. Here we make this formulation explicit, developing a Bayesian theory of efficient coding that defines Bayesian efficient codes in terms of four basic ingredients: (1) a stimulus prior distribution; (2) an encoding model; (3) a capacity constraint, specifying a neural resource limit; and (4) a loss functional, quantifying the desirability or undesirability of various posterior distributions. Classic efficient codes arise as the special case in which the loss functional is the posterior entropy, leading to a code that maximizes mutual information, but alternate loss functionals give solutions that differ dramatically from information-maximizing codes. Within this framework we introduce covtropy, a novel family of losses defined on posterior distributions and parameterized by a single exponent, and use it to show that decorrelation of sensory inputs - optimal under classic efficient codes in low-noise settings - can be disadvantageous for objectives that penalize large errors. We then reanalyze Laughlin's seminal data on contrast coding in the blowfly large monopolar cell, and find that the measured response nonlinearity is better explained by minimizing Lp reconstruction error with p = 1/2 than by information maximization, overturning a forty-year-old interpretation. Bayesian efficient coding thus enlarges the family of codes that are optimal under different objectives and provides a more general framework for understanding the design principles of sensory systems.

title: Case studies on IoT monitoring of debris flow and landslides.
abstract: Aiming at the critical demand for real-time monitoring of slope disasters in mountainous and urbanized regions, this study develops Internet of Things (IoT)-based real-time monitoring systems to resolve the issues of data delay and fragmentation in conventional manual monitoring. Through three engineering cases conducted by the authors, we demonstrate the adaptability of IoT technology in slope disaster monitoring under different instability mechanisms (debris flows and landslides) and geological conditions (artificial-reinforced and semi-natural slopes). Specifically, in Case 1, a novel IoT monitoring system for debris flows integrated with the structural characteristics of rigid barriers is proposed. In Cases 2 and 3, multi-type monitoring sensors and equipment are deployed, including deformation sensors, rainfall gauges and video surveillance devices, to achieve accurate early warnings of rainfall-induced landslides. The novelty of this work lies in proposing a unified IoT architecture scheme applicable to different types of slope disasters. This scheme systematically integrates physico-mechanical sensing devices, a solar-battery collaborative power supply system, video monitoring equipment, data transmission methods, early warning modes, and a cloud-based processing module. Furthermore, the effectiveness of the proposed scheme is validated via successful early warning cases, and this scheme provides an effective technical framework for slope disaster prevention and control.

title: Climate change-driven compound dust storm and heatwave extremes in Central Asia under future CMIP6 scenarios.
abstract: Central Asia (CA) faces rising temperatures and shifting atmospheric conditions, increasing the urgency to address extreme events like heatwaves and dust storms. This study examines the co-evolution and regional co-variability of heatwaves and atmospheric dust loading, represented by dust extinction aerosol optical thickness (AOT). Using a multi-model ensemble of CMIP6 General Circulation Models (GCMs) and high-resolution reanalysis datasets, we analyzed heatwave indices alongside AOT across six clusters from 1992 to 2100. Results show a substantial rise in heatwave activity, with increases in heatwave frequency and intensity projected across much of CA, particularly under future emission scenarios. AOT trends vary regionally, with both increasing and decreasing trends across clusters, periods, and emission scenarios. Spatial and temporal correlations, evaluated with Benjamini-Hochberg False Discovery Rate (BH-FDR) correction for multiple location-level tests, show regionally heterogeneous dust-heatwave co-variability, with both positive and negative associations across clusters and scenarios. The strongest FDR-supported relationships occur in selected cluster-index combinations, indicating localized and scenario-dependent co-variability rather than a uniform compound dust-heatwave signal across CA. These findings highlight the need for targeted adaptation strategies for CA, which faces intensifying heatwaves and spatially variable dust-related atmospheric conditions. This study supports early warning systems, risk assessments, and mitigation and resilience measures to safeguard vulnerable communities and ecosystems and strengthen resilience to these hazards in line with the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015-2030.

title: Comparative study of the load-bearing and deformation behaviors of metal mesh and polymer thin spray-on liner surface supports in mining roadways.
abstract: To investigate the differences in load-bearing capacity and deformation control between metal mesh and polymer thin spray-on liners (TSL) for roadway surface support, a study was conducted based on a mining roadway in Yulin, Shaanxi Province, China. Small-scale simulated roadway tests and engineering-scale numerical simulations were combined. Under the same geometric, boundary, and loading conditions, the peak load, strain response, surface displacement, and failure characteristics of the two support systems were compared. The effects of different surface supports on surrounding rock deformation and stress distribution were further analyzed under the same bolt-cable support conditions. The results show that the peak load of the metal mesh specimens was about 70 kN, with a maximum surface displacement of about 0.42 mm. The TSL specimens reached a peak load of about 85 kN, which was 21.4% higher than that of the metal mesh specimens, while the maximum surface displacement decreased by 23.8% to about 0.32 mm. Metal mesh mainly restrains loose rock blocks through tensile resistance, bending, and containment, whereas TSL provides earlier confinement to the shallow surrounding rock through continuous coverage, bonding, and membrane action. Numerical results indicate that, compared with metal mesh support, TSL support reduced the peak sidewall convergence, roof subsidence, and floor heave by 34.1%, 11.0%, and 6.3%, respectively, and slightly reduced the high-stress zone. The results suggest that, under the conditions investigated in this study, TSL has potential advantages in improving surface support performance and reducing shallow surrounding rock deformation. However, its long-term applicability and material safety require further verification through field monitoring and additional tests.

title: Comparing the impact of recess duration on motor coordination and psychological variables: An exploratory study.
abstract: Recess serves as a productive environment for children to play independently of adults, which promotes physiological and psychological development. However, current recess durations in schools across the United States (U.S.) are frequently insufficient in providing opportunities for physical activity (PA) to promote developmental improvements. One of the most well-studied evidence-based recess interventions, the LiiNK Project®, has demonstrated that when children receive 60 minutes of recess daily, motor coordination (MC) is significantly better than when children receive 30 minutes daily. However, child outcomes are lacking when schools modify the recess intervention duration in older grades to 30 minutes daily while continuing to practice the protocols and procedures from the full intervention. Therefore, the primary purpose of this study was to explore observed physiological (MC) and psychological (self-esteem and perceived physical ability) differences and associations between fourth and fifth grade children who received a modified version of the LiiNK intervention (n = 120) and children who did not receive the modified intervention (n = 98) at two-time points in one school year. The Körperkoordinationstest für Kinder (KTK) was used to assess MC, while the KID-KINDL self-esteem subscale and the Perceived Physical Ability Scale (PPASC) were used to assess the psychological variables. Grade, sex, race, and body fat percentages were collected to describe any group differences for a better interpretation of the groups. A mixed two-way repeated measures MANOVA analysis identified a between-group PPASC difference (p < 0.001), while the control group reported higher scores at both time points, suggesting a pre-existing group difference rather than a modified intervention change. Further, significant within-subjects time-related improvements were observed for single-leg hop (SH) and sideways stepping (SS), while a significant time-related decline was observed for self-esteem. Lastly, 2 x 2 Pearson chi-square analysis of "Normal-to-Great" and "Below Normal" MQ classifications was conducted separately at each time point. Although there were no significant findings, descriptively, both groups at Time 1 (85.8% of the modified intervention group and 90.8% of control group) were classified as "Normal-to-Great" MQ, improving to 88.3% and 95.9%, respectively, at Time 2. The "Below Normal" MQ classification decreased from 14.2% to 11.7% and 9.2% to 4.1% in the two groups respectively. Overall, these results provide preliminary insights into observed patterns of physiological and psychological outcomes for fourth and fifth grade children with similar recess minutes, but different protocols daily. However, these results provide no evidence that the modified intervention benefits the children any better than having 30 minutes of recess without the modified protocols. Future studies should compare the modified 30-minute intervention with a larger sample of children in the full LiiNK intervention (60 minutes) to assess these same variables, as well as collect the second data point in May instead of February.

title: Computational modelling of acetylcholine deficiency-mediated dysfunction in the basal ganglia-thalamocortical network related to Parkinson's disease dementia.
abstract: Parkinson's disease dementia (PDD) is a significant form of dementia. Its pathophysiology involves not only the dopaminergic system impairment but also the degeneration of cholinergic neurons in the pedunculopontine nucleus (PPN), which is considered a potential contributor to the cognitive decline in PDD. Therefore, this study develops a computational model of the PPN-modulated basal ganglia-thalamic-cortical network to investigate how acetylcholine deficiency affects cortical oscillations. Based on anatomical evidence, acetylcholine deficiency is modeled by modulating synaptic connections from the PPN to the thalamus and basal ganglia output nuclei. Power spectrum analysis shows that acetylcholine deficiency, whether in the PPN-thalamic nucleus pathway or in the PPN-basal ganglia output nucleus pathway, leads to a decrease in cortical power ratio between the high-frequency band and low-frequency band. These results qualitatively reproduce the characteristics of electrophysiological measurements recorded in PDD. Further dynamical analysis suggests that this reduction may be associated with weakened oscillatory activity, reflected by a shift in neuronal firing patterns from limit cycle to point attractor. Moreover, simulations of combined acetylcholine and dopamine deficiencies reveal that both neurotransmitters can reduce the cortical power ratio, with a synergistic interaction rather than a simple additive effect. These findings provide a systems-level perspective on how ACh deficiency may contribute to cortical dysfunction in PDD and may offer a potential direction for future therapeutic research.

title: Deep-learning side-channel analysis of embedded ML-KEM: Single-trace message recovery, cross-device generalization, and frequency-band leakage characterization.
abstract: Quantum computing undermines traditional public-key cryptosystems like RSA and ECC, prompting NIST to standardize Module Lattice Key Encapsulation Mechanism (ML-KEM) as a core Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) scheme in August 2024. Despite its theoretical security, ML-KEM's practical vulnerability in embedded systems remains underexplored. This study evaluates ML-KEM on an ARM Cortex-M4 microcontroller under deep learning(DL)-based side-channel attacks (DL-SCA), revealing that a single power trace enables 32-byte message recovery with 99.98% accuracy, while cross-device testing across three chips achieves over 99% accuracy, highlighting critical DL-driven threats. To better understand the spectral characteristics exploited by deep-learning-based side-channel attacks, we conduct a controlled frequency-band sensitivity study using Butterworth and Chebyshev low-pass filters applied to recorded traces. Across different cutoff frequencies and filter orders, the validation accuracy decreases substantially under aggressive attenuation, indicating that a significant fraction of exploitable leakage resides in higher-frequency components. Rather than claiming that offline digital filtering constrains a realistic adversary, we interpret these results as evidence for where leakage-sensitive information is concentrated, thereby providing guidance for implementable countermeasures such as masking, shuffling, desynchronization, and acquisition-path power/EM conditioning in embedded PQC systems. This cost-efficient solution requires no algorithm/hardware modifications, emphasizing the urgency of implementation-level protections for secure PQC deployment in resource-constrained systems.

title: Defining and predicting outcomes of a work-injuries rehabilitation program through multivariate baseline phenotypes and longitudinal modeling.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterize short-term pain and health-related quality-of-life (HRQoL) recovery trajectories in injured workers undergoing standardized musculoskeletal rehabilitation. We also examined whether multidimensional baseline phenotypes derived from brief self-report measures predicted these trajectories and subsequent recovery.
METHODS: Adults with work-related musculoskeletal injuries were enrolled at entry into a community-based rehabilitation program (N = 146), of whom 134 contributed to pain and 138 to HRQoL trajectory analyses. Participants were classified into one of 4 latent profiles at intake from a prior analysis: Localized/Resilient (57.0%), Mood-Dominant (21.8%), Neurosensory-Dominant (12.7%), and Complex/Central (8.5%). Pain (Numeric Pain Rating Scale, NPRS) and HRQoL (EQ-5D-5L index) were measured at baseline, 4, and 8 weeks; self-rated global recovery, self-reported return-to-work status, and administrative discharge/ongoing-care codes were collected at 8 weeks. Growth mixture modeling defined NPRS and EQ-5D-5L trajectories. Odds ratios (ORs) quantified associations between baseline classes and "No Recovery/No Improvement" trajectories, as well as point outcomes.
RESULTS: Three pain trajectories (Rapid Recovery 34.1%, Incomplete Recovery 42.2%, No Recovery 23.7%) and two QoL trajectories (Good QoL 86.2%, No Improvement 13.8%) were identified. Compared with the Localized/Resilient baseline class, odds of NPRS No Recovery were higher in the Mood-Dominant (OR 3.97, 95%CI 1.32-11.92), Neurosensory‑Dominant (OR 10.99, 3.20-37.38), and Complex, Central (OR 22.67, 4.76-107.90) classes, with similarly graded increases for EQ‑5D‑5L No Recovery (ORs 9.00, 7.50, and 150.00, respectively), although estimates for the small Complex/Central subgroup were imprecise. The Complex /Central class also had higher odds of self-reported "not fully returned to work" (OR 4.18, 1.05-16.64) and being coded as "requires ongoing care" (OR 5.74, 1.93-17.11) relative to Localized/Resilient, whereas self-rated global recovery showed no significant between-class differences.
CONCLUSIONS: Brief, fully self-reported, multivariate phenotypes obtained at program entry stratify acutely injured workers into likely rehabilitation outcomes in the short term. These findings support the potential value of integrating mechanism-informed phenotyping with trajectory modeling to inform stratified, risk-guided musculoskeletal rehabilitation.

title: Development and internal validation of machine learning models for predicting prediabetes in China.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetes imposes a growing health burden among Chinese adults, necessitating scalable tools for early identification of high-risk individuals. We aimed to develop and internally validate survival machine-learning models for prediabetes risk stratification using routinely available clinical indicators.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 77,478 Chinese adults from the Dryad repository (2010-2016). Candidate predictors were selected via LASSO regression and random survival forests (RSF). Six survival models, Cox proportional hazards (Cox-PH), CoxBoost, DeepSurv, gradient boosting machine (GBM), random survival forests (RSF), and survival tree, were developed and evaluated using the concordance index (C-index), time-dependent ROC curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). The best-performing model was deployed as a web-based application.
RESULTS: Eight predictors were consistently selected across methods: age, BMI, fasting plasma glucose, total cholesterol, triglycerides, HDL-C, LDL-C, and creatinine clearance rate. In the test set, DeepSurv and GBM achieved comparable discrimination (C-index: 0.756 vs. 0.751; adjusted P = 0.694). GBM was preferred due to better calibration and greater net benefit across clinically relevant thresholds, leading to its selection as the candidate model.
CONCLUSION: The GBM-based prediabetes risk model, built on eight inexpensive and routinely available clinical measures, showed promising internal discrimination and calibration in a large Chinese cohort. An interactive web tool was developed as a research prototype to facilitate future external validation and early risk identification. External validation in independent populations is warranted before clinical use.

title: Diabetes and all-cause mortality in hemodialysis: A comparative survival analysis with complementary machine-learning methods.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetes mellitus is the leading cause of end-stage renal disease and confers excess mortality in patients on hemodialysis. However, which diabetes-specific clinical parameters best predict survival remains insufficiently explored.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study followed 252 patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis (126 with diabetes, 126 without) from three centres in Ankara, Turkey, over 68 months (January 2020-September 2025; 66 deaths). Mortality predictors were assessed using Cox proportional hazards models, propensity score-weighted regression, and gradient-boosted machine-learning survival analysis. Eleven diabetes-specific parameters were examined within the diabetes subgroup.
RESULTS: Diabetes was associated with reduced survival (log-rank p = 0.038) and a 68% higher mortality hazard (HR 1.68, 95% CI 1.02-2.75). After multivariable adjustment, the association was attenuated but directionally consistent across all specifications (HR 1.52-1.66). Within the diabetes subgroup, HbA1c was the strongest modifiable predictor (adjusted HR 1.43 per 1%, 95% CI 1.17-1.76, p < 0.001), improving model discrimination (C-index 0.679 vs. 0.652). No other diabetes-specific parameter, including retinopathy, diabetic foot, and diabetes duration, independently predicted mortality.
CONCLUSION: In this Turkish hemodialysis cohort, diabetes showed a consistent adverse trend toward higher mortality. HbA1c was the dominant modifiable predictor, supporting the integration of structured glycaemic monitoring into routine hemodialysis care.

title: Differential and directional body coupling analysis in Parkinsonian gait.
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder primarily characterized by motor impairments and altered whole-body coordination. Objective and accessible approaches for quantifying inter-limb and cross-directional coupling during gait remain limited in clinical settings. Using a prospectively collected dataset of individuals with PD and healthy controls (HC), we propose a comprehensive analytical framework based on human pose estimation to extract time-series kinematic signals from key body landmarks. Coupling strengths between body segments were quantified to characterize whole-body coordination patterns. Statistical filtering identified discriminative body coupling factors that significantly differentiated PD from HC. The identified factors demonstrated clear and consistent alterations in coordination patterns across groups. Furthermore, multiple machine learning classifiers validated their discriminative capacity, achieving robust classification performance. Correlation analyses between the top 10 pre-specified directional body coupling factors and MDS-UPDRS III scores demonstrated modest but statistically significant associations in the full PD cohort (n = 121), with 8 of 10 factors surviving FDR correction (ρ=0.27-0.31). These associations suggest that directional body coupling metrics capture clinically relevant variation in motor impairment severity beyond binary PD versus HC discrimination and may serve as potential digital biomarkers of PD-related motor dysfunction. Subtype-stratified analyses were conducted only as exploratory supplementary analyses, and larger, more balanced subtype cohorts are required before subtype-specific conclusions can be drawn. Overall, body coupling metrics provide reliable biomechanical markers of PD-related gait impairment and support the clinical potential of this non-invasive and cost-effective pipeline for early diagnosis and longitudinal monitoring.

title: Distinguishing persistence from deviation in composite policy indices: A diagnostic framework for AI readiness trajectory screening and stratification.
abstract: Composite indices of national capability reduce dynamic trajectories to static rankings, offering no mechanism to distinguish expected persistence from departures that warrant diagnostic attention. This study asks when a year-to-year change in a national AI-readiness score warrants additional analytical attention. We develop a five-step diagnostic framework (Expect, Detect, Explain, Contextualise, Interpret & Investigate) and apply it to the Oxford Government AI Readiness Index (118 countries, 2021-2024) across two transition windows. An autoregressive baseline explains 97.9% of the variation in next-year scores (W1 in-sample R² = 0.9790, MAE = 1.6506), establishing persistence as the dominant structure and residuals as the primary analytical unit; under a common held-out protocol no flexible specification improves on that baseline, so pillar disaggregation is used for attribution rather than prediction. Government is the pillar most frequently selected by the attribution rule among flagged deviations, with wide uncertainty and a threshold-sensitive ranking (50.0% in W1, 45.8% in W2 after normalisation; Wilson 95% CI 31-69% in W1). Regime analysis defines three Level-dominated readiness strata (k-means, k = 3; W1 trajectory stability ratio, TSR = 0.9407); the W1 directional differentiation in ΔLevel (p = 0.0020) is consistent with mean reversion under the below-unity AR(1) slope (0.954), with the regime term non-significant once continuous prior score is controlled (ANCOVA p = 0.389), and the W2 non-recurrence (p = 0.3643) coincides with a slope near unity (1.007). The regime typology therefore serves as an interpretive stratification device rather than an independent source of trajectory differentiation. Zero skip-a-level movements occur in both windows, consistent with strong persistence rather than independent evidence of ordered mobility. By screening departures from expected persistence using a signed-decile rule with window-specific cut-points (24 of 118 observations flagged per window by construction), the framework reconceptualises composite indices as state-dependent diagnostic systems and supports targeted follow-up monitoring.

title: Distribution characteristics of fungi on surfaces in the hospital environment: What have we overlooked?
abstract: Hospital environmental fungal contamination is a significant cause of healthcare-associated fungal infections, which are associated with high mortality rates in immunocompromised populations. However, current understanding of the distribution characteristics and high-risk colonization sites of fungi on hospital inanimate surfaces remains limited, hindering the development of targeted infection control strategies. A cross-sectional study was conducted in December 2024 in a large tertiary care hospital in central China. Using two-stage stratified sampling, 100 environmental surface samples were collected from 10 clinical departments. All samples underwent fungal culture and quantification, and culture-positive samples were further analyzed by 18S rRNA sequencing to characterize fungal community composition. A total of 20% of samples were culture-positive for fungi, and 7% exceeded the ECDC-recommended threshold of 5 colony-forming units per square centimeter (CFU/cm²). Water-related surfaces showed the highest culture-positive rate (32.1%), with the highest individual count observed in an endocrinology department handwashing pool (15 CFU/cm2), followed by air disinfection machine vents and faucets. Aspergillus was the dominant genus (43.8% of isolates), and 70% of identified genera included WHO-listed priority pathogenic fungi. Water-related surfaces and ventilation equipment outlets are high-risk sites for fungal colonization. Current cleaning protocols are insufficient for these areas, requiring enhanced targeted surveillance and disinfection to reduce healthcare-associated fungal infection risk.

title: Double gravity-assist rendezvous trajectory to Halley's comet using deep-space low thrust.
abstract: The perihelion of comet 1P/Halley in 2061 is an excellent chance to revisit this object of outstanding scientific and cultural relevance. During its 1986 approach to the Sun, it was targeted by several flyby missions. Due to its retrograde, highly-inclined orbit, the relative velocities during the encounter were large, restricting the scientific return due to the short time spent inside the coma. A rendezvous trajectory would overcome this limitation, but the design is challenging due to the limitations of current propulsion technology. Given the lead times of spacecraft development and the long duration of the interplanetary transfer to the comet, it is imperative to start mission planning as soon as possible. We present a novel rendezvous strategy, combining unpowered Jupiter and Saturn gravity-assists with deep-space low-thrust arcs. It minimizes launch energy and propellant budget, constraining the arrival to occur before the onset of high activity. The double flyby strategy reduces the otherwise prohibitive cost of the plane change maneuver. Closed expressions for the optimal flyby geometry, together with an explicit low-thrust transcription technique, reduce the number of design parameter to three, improving computational efficiency. Crucially, this is the first rendezvous mission concept achievable with well-proven technology (standard radioisotope thermoelectric generators and an ion thruster) and compatible with several existing launchers. We describe the trajectory optimization strategy and perform a comprehensive exploration of the design space. Finally, we present two promising proof-of-concept trajectories in detail.

title: Early antenatal care initiation and associated factors in Hohoe Municipality, Ghana: A five-year multi-facility repeated cross-sectional record review study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early initiation of antenatal care (ANC) is a critical strategy for improving maternal and neonatal health outcomes, as it enables timely detection and management of pregnancy-related risks. However, women in low- and middle-income countries initiate ANC late. This study estimated the proportion of women initiating ANC within the first trimester in three health facilities in the Hohoe Municipality, Ghana, over a five-year period (2020-2024). It also assessed trends across years and examined factors associated with early ANC initiation.
METHODS: We conducted a multi-facility repeated cross-sectional record review of ANC records from three health facilities in Hohoe Municipality from January 2020 to December 2024. Of 7,660 records identified, 1,381 were excluded because the first ANC contact had occurred at another facility, leaving 6,279 for analysis. Background characteristics were summarised using frequencies and percentages, and the proportion of women initiating ANC within the first trimester was calculated overall and for each year. Multivariable binary logistic regression was used to examine the factors associated with early ANC initiation; age-by-parity interaction terms tested, and facility-by-predictor interaction models were fitted to assess effect heterogeneity. Results were presented as odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and statistical significance was set at p < 0.05.
RESULTS: Early ANC initiation increased slightly from 45.3% in 2020 to 46.4% in 2023 before declining to 44.3% in 2024, with an overall proportion of 45.1% across the study period. Patterns differed by facility between the COVID-19 (2020-2021) and post-COVID-19 (2022-2024) periods. Early initiation declined at Gbi-Wegbe Health Center (54.3% to 46.0%; p = 0.008) but increased at Adabraka Health Center (31.5% to 42.0%; p < 0.001) and at the Volta Regional Hospital (45.4% to 47.6%; p = 0.002). The odds of early ANC initiation was higher among women aged 31-40 years (aOR = 1.15; 95% CI: 1.01-1.31) than those aged 14-30, and among women with high-end of the acceptable range blood pressure (aOR = 1.44; 95% CI: 1.26-1.65), and those with above acceptable/Grade 1 hypertension (aOR = 1.95; 95% CI: 1.34-2.83) relative to those with acceptable hypertension status. Odds were lower with increasing parity, and lower at Adabraka Health Center and Volta Regional Hospital than at Gbi-Wedbe Health Center. The interaction analysis between maternal age and parity showed that multiparous women aged 31-40 had lower odds of early ANC initiation (OR = 0.61; 95% CI: 0.41-0.91), and lower among grand multiparous women of the same age (OR = 0.29; 95% CI: 0.11-0.77). In the facility-stratified analyses, grand multiparity was the only factor associated with early ANC initiation, which was consistent across all three facilities.
CONCLUSION: Fewer than half of women initiated ANC early in the Hohoe Municipality, with less variations across the study period and divergent trajectories between facilities. Early initiation was more likely among women aged 31-40 years and those with raised blood pressure, and less likely with increasing parity, with age and parity interacting. Facility-specific interventions prioritising women with high parity and reproductive education and needed to increase ANC initiation, whiles improving access to health facilities.

title: Effectiveness of ultraviolet-C robots in isolation room disinfection: Impact of dose, distance, and direct exposure on environmental surface decontamination.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: To minimize environmental services staff's exposure to pathogens, ultraviolet-C (UV-C) disinfection robots were applied before terminal manual environmental disinfection. This study aimed to evaluate the disinfection efficacy of the UV-C robot and to assess the effects of ultraviolet-C dose, distance, and direct exposure (line-of-sight irradiation) on disinfection outcomes.
METHODS: This before-after study was conducted in a negative-pressure isolation ward comprising 17 single-patient rooms at a medical center in Taiwan between August 24, 2024, and January 3, 2025, yielding a total of 270 paired samples. An ultraviolet-C-emitting robot with a wavelength of 254 nm was sequentially positioned on both sides of the patient bed and operated for 5 minutes on each side before routine manual environmental disinfection. Total aerobic colony counts (ACC) and bacterial culture positivity rates were obtained from high-touch environmental surfaces (e.g., bed rails, call bells and bedside chairs) before and after UV-C disinfection. The effects of UV-C dose, distance between the robot and surfaces, and the presence of direct exposure (line-of-sight irradiation) versus indirect exposure on disinfection efficacy were analyzed using multivariate binary logistic regression, performed using SPSS version 27.0. The results of the regression analysis were expressed as odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: The median ACC and bacterial culture positivity rates on surfaces significantly decreased after UV-C disinfection (0.76 vs. 0.08 CFU/cm²; 83% vs. 57.4%, P < 0.001). A weak negative correlation was observed between ACC and UV-C doses after disinfection (rs = -0.281, 95% CI: -0.390 to -0.164, P < 0.001), while no correlation (rs = 0.040, 95% CI: -0.083 to 0.162, P = 0.510) and weak correlation (rs = 0.317, 95% CI: 0.202 to 0.424, P <  0.001) were found between ACC at short and long irradiation distances. The ACC on environmental surfaces with direct UV-C exposure were significantly lower than those in shadowed areas [median: 0.00 (IQR: 0.00 to 0.44) vs. median: 0.16 (IQR: 0.00 to 0.80); P < 0.001]. Multivariate logistic regression identified direct exposure (line-of-sight irradiation) as the strongest predictor of negative bacterial culture results, reducing the odds of bacterial culture positivity by 79.5% compared to indirect exposure (OR = 0.205, 95% CI: 0.083 to 0.508, P < 0.001) in the layout of the negative pressure isolation room in this study.
CONCLUSIONS: Ultraviolet-C robots serve as an effective disinfection intervention for hospital environments. Their efficacy is most pronounced when direct exposure (line-of-sight irradiation) is achieved in the isolation rooms. Therefore, aligning movable items toward the UV-C robot prior to disinfection, alongside subsequent manual environmental disinfection and physical debris removal, remains essential, particularly in shadowed areas.
