title: Effects and mechanisms of exercise timing on cognitive function in older type 2 diabetes mellitus patients with mild cognitive impairment: A magnetic resonance imaging-based randomized controlled trial protocol.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is a prevalent complication of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Cognitive impairment progressively impairs self-care abilities, thereby triggering a vicious cycle of poor glycemic control and further cognitive decline. Exercise has been widely recognized as an effective strategy to improve both glycemic control and cognitive function; however, an optimal time of day for exercise to mitigate this neurodegenerative trajectory has not been determined. This trial aims to determine the most effective exercise timing to maximize cognitive benefits in older T2DM patients with MCI (T2DM-MCI) and to investigate the underlying neurobiological mechanisms using multimodal magnetic resonance imaging.
METHODS: In this randomized controlled trial, patients 60-75 years of age with T2DM-MCI will be assigned to a morning exercise group (09:00-10:10), an evening exercise group (19:00-20:10), or a health education group. The exercise groups will complete a 12-week, home-based, remotely supervised exercise program comprising aerobic and resistance exercises. The health education group will receive a 12-week health education program. Cognitive function will be evaluated at baseline and post-intervention using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment, Color-Word Stroop Test, N-back task, Trail making Test, Attention Network Test, and Digit Symbol Substitution Test. Additionally, brain structure and function based on imaging, blood biomarkers, and physical fitness will also be assessed.
DISCUSSION: In this study, we aim to identify the optimal time of day for exercise to maximize cognitive benefits in patients with T2DM-MCI and to elucidate underlying neurocognitive mechanisms. We will examine whether glycemic control mediates the relationship between exercise and cognitive function improvement. This research is expected to provide "time-specific" evidence for exercise prescription to maximize the neurocognitive benefits and mitigate dementia risk in this population.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry: [http://www.chictr.org.cn], identifier [ChiCTR2300073737].

title: Energy driven constitutive modeling of thermally damaged red sandstone under multilevel cyclic loading.
abstract: This study investigates the mechanical and energy responses of red sandstone subjected to high-temperature treatment and multilevel cyclic loading and develops an energy-driven constitutive model for its deformation behavior. Triaxial cyclic loading tests were conducted on red sandstone treated at different temperatures to examine the effects of thermal treatment and repeated loading on stress-strain response, residual deformation, and energy evolution. The results show that temperature significantly affects the mechanical properties and deformation characteristics of red sandstone. Under repeated loading at the same stress level, the hysteresis-loop area, residual-strain growth, and dissipated energy generally decrease with increasing cycle number, whereas an increase in stress level leads to renewed deformation and energy dissipation. Based on the experimental response, a staged constitutive framework is established for the initial loading, cyclic loading, and subsequent monotonic loading stages by considering compaction deformation, skeleton deformation, and damage evolution. Thermal and mechanical damage are incorporated through a load-carrying ratio, and energy density is introduced to characterize damage accumulation. The proposed model reproduces the main stress-strain characteristics observed in the tests and provides a constitutive description of the mechanical response of thermally treated red sandstone under multilevel cyclic loading.

title: Environmental enrichment is associated with changes in the gut microbiome and resistome of captive pythons.
abstract: Environmental enrichment is widely used to improve the welfare of captive animals, yet its effects on reptilian gut microbiota remain poorly understood. Here, we used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to investigate the gut microbiome and resistome of two captive python species: Burmese python (Python bivittatus) and reticulated python (Malayopython reticulatus), before and after environmental enrichment. We found that environmental enrichment was associated with increased α-diversity in Burmese pythons, as indicated by significantly higher ACE and observed species indices, while NMDS ordination revealed differences in the observed patterns of community composition between the two species. Pseudomonadota and Bacteroidota were dominant phyla in the gut microbiota of both python species, but their relative abundances responded differently to enrichment between hosts. Functional analyses suggested an enhanced metabolic potential in Burmese pythons, particularly in carbohydrate metabolism and environmental information processing, accompanied by increased abundance of carbohydrate-active enzymes. In addition, enrichment may influence the gut resistome, with Pseudomonadota contributing the majority of antibiotic resistance genes. Overall, our results demonstrate that environmental enrichment measures, such as dietary changes and improvements in water and air quality, are associated with changes in the gut microbiome and resistome of captive pythons in a host-dependent manner, highlighting the combined roles of diet and environmental conditions in the observed changes in the gut microbiota. These findings provide exploratory insights into the functional responses and host-microbiome evolution of reptile gut microbiota to captivity and have important implications for the management and welfare of captive animals.

title: Establishment of hairy root cultures of Lactuca serriola and enhancement of phenolic metabolites through methyl jasmonate elicitation.
abstract: Lactuca serriola is a wild lettuce species that synthesizes diverse phenolic compounds involved in plant defense and adaptation to environmental stress. Methyl jasmonate (MeJA), a key signaling molecule in plant defense, is known to regulate secondary metabolism by activating the phenylpropanoid pathway. In the present study, genetically stable hairy root cultures of L. serriola were established to investigate MeJA-induced metabolic reprogramming and its effects on phenolic accumulation and antioxidant defense responses. Hairy roots were induced using Agrobacterium rhizogenes strain ATCC 15834 and molecularly confirmed by PCR amplification of the rolC gene. The selected fast-growing hairy root line was treated with 0, 100, and 200 μM MeJA. MeJA significantly affected both growth and secondary metabolism. Although increasing MeJA concentrations reduced fresh and dry biomass, they promoted the accumulation of total phenolics and flavonoids. HPLC-DAD analysis further demonstrated significant increases in several phenolic metabolites, including caffeic acid, chlorogenic acid, p-coumaric acid, rosmarinic acid, and cinnamic acid. MeJA treatment also enhanced the activities of superoxide dismutase, catalase, ascorbate peroxidase, and guaiacol peroxidase, indicating activation of antioxidant defense systems associated with jasmonate-mediated stress responses and phenylpropanoid metabolism. This study provides the first comprehensive characterization of MeJA-induced phenolic metabolism in L. serriola hairy roots and demonstrates that MeJA effectively reprograms secondary metabolism toward enhanced phenolic biosynthesis. These findings advance our understanding of jasmonate-regulated defense metabolism in hairy roots while supporting the use of this in vitro system as a controlled platform for future studies and potential biotechnological production of specialized metabolites.

title: Experiences of individually tailored physical exercise in COVID-19-induced postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome: A qualitative content analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome (POTS) is a phenotype of post-COVID-19 Condition (PCC), characterised by orthostatic intolerance and a range of debilitating symptoms. Exercise is a frequently implemented intervention in the treatment of POTS and PCC. However, patients' experiences with exercise as a therapeutic modality remain largely unexplored. This study aimed to explore the experiences of individuals diagnosed with PCC and POTS who underwent an individually tailored physical exercise intervention.
METHODS: A qualitative study design with an inductive approach was applied. Twenty-three participants who completed a feasibility study, involving semi-supervised tailored exercise, were recruited for individual interviews. Data were collected using a semi-structured interview guide and analysed through qualitative content analysis.
RESULTS: Five main categories emerged, underscoring the importance of individualised design of exercise programs, flexible modalities, and continuous support from physiotherapists with expertise in PCC and POTS. Participants experienced improvements in physical, mental, and social functioning, although setbacks and symptom fluctuation were common. Strategies for energy management, alongside informal and formal support, were identified as facilitators and reduced barriers to exercise as a treatment. Psychological dimensions, including hope, motivation, goal setting, emotional adaptation, acceptance, and coping strategies, were central to participants' experiences. The combination of the intervention structure, therapeutic support, and effective strategies was perceived as contributing to the intervention's effectiveness, and many participants viewed exercise as a key pathway to recovery.
CONCLUSIONS: This study highlights the need for a flexible and individualised rehabilitation approach in COVID-19-induced POTS. Moreover, exercise should be closely monitored by a physiotherapist with condition-specific expertise, who not only adapts the exercise to symptom fluctuations but also addresses diverse psychosocial needs and individual resources. The participants' experiences indicate that a holistic, multidisciplinary, and person-centred rehabilitation model may support recovery and contribute to improved long-term wellbeing in individuals with PCC and POTS.

title: Explainable computational framework for subtype classification and biomarker identification in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma using machine learning.
abstract: The precise classification of basal, classical, atypical, and mesenchymal subtypes of Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma (HNSCC) is crucial for advancing precision oncology. Our research aims to develop an explainable subtype classification model for HNSCC.These molecular subtypes have been previously defined; reliable and meaningful computational methods for the classification of molecular subtypes and prioritization of molecular biomarkers for each subtype do not exist. We developed an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) model that classifies molecular subtypes based on combined transcriptomic profiles from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA-HNSC) and Gene Expression Omnibus (GSE65858). SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used to quantify the importance of genes for model predictions. Subsequently, genes with high predictive importance were analyzed in protein-protein interactions using STRING, and hub genes were identified by Maximum Clique Centrality (MCC) and used for the identification of candidate biomarkers for each of the subtypes. We employed machine learning methods such as Random Forest (RF), Logistic Regression (LR), Decision Tree (DT), AdaBoost (AB), Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN), Gaussian Naive Bayes (GNB), XGBoost (XGB), and Gradient Boosting (GB). The XGBoost model achieved an accuracy of 95% after hyperparameter tuning and cross-validation. Biologically relevant subtype-specific biomarkers associated with each molecular subtype were identified. To highlight the potential biological functions of these biomarkers, pathway analysis was performed. Further assessment of these genes, such as survival analysis and druggability, showed promise for the development of targeted therapies.

title: Exploration of complex shyness and the relationship between fear and approach behaviors in domestic cats (Felis catus).
abstract: Shyness in human psychology is recognized as a complex trait distinct from pure fear, often characterized by an approach-avoidance conflict. While shyness and fear are frequently conflated in animal behavior studies, this research investigated shyness in domestic cats (Felis catus), exploring whether they exhibit multifaceted personality structures similar to those of human infants. We conducted three sequential surveys with cat owners: Study 1 included 82 cats of both sexes, Study 2 included 114 male cats to follow up on the sex-specific pattern observed in Study 1, and Study 3 included 114 stray-born male cats to further examine the pattern identified among stray-born cats in Study 2. We used adapted versions of the Colorado Childhood Temperament Inventory (CCTI) and the Infant Behavior Questionnaire-Revised (IBQ-R) to assess shyness, fear, and approach tendencies. The predicted quadratic relationship between shyness and approach scores was not statistically significant, and thus the primary confirmatory hypothesis was not supported. Subsequent exploratory hierarchical cluster analyses suggested four candidate personality phenotypes in stray-born male cats: "Highly Sociable" (low fear/high approach), "Sociable" (low fear/moderate approach), "Fearful" (high fear/low approach), and a "Human infant-like shyness" type (high fear/high approach). These findings suggest that cat shyness is predominantly linked to fear, as supported by the strong positive correlations between shyness and fear. However, the cluster analyses identified a specific subset of cats exhibiting a complex personality involving high-approach tendencies despite high fear, mirroring human infant-like shyness. This study highlights the multifaceted nature of cat temperament and demonstrates that adapting human psychological frameworks can provide significant insights into animal personality, potentially improving welfare in domestic cats.

title: Filling the gaps in Australian angiosperm genomes.
abstract: The Genomics for Australian Plants Initiative (GAP) reference genome project aimed to provide high quality angiosperm genomes for previously underrepresented taxonomic groups with evolutionary significance, cultural value, biogeographic importance, and concerning conservation status in Australia. Here we present the results of long-read genomic sequencing and assembly for 29 selected angiosperm species, including analyses of genome completeness, contiguity, ploidy, gene annotations, and repeat content. Plastid and mitochondrion genomes were also assembled and annotated. The data provided a diverse selection of genome size, ploidy and complexity, which were compared. The long read sequencing methods, PacBio HiFi, and Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT), used in tandem and individually where appropriate, provided high quality near complete telomere to telomere assemblies. These genomes provide valuable genomic resources for Australian plants that will enable and extend research in evolution, conservation, functional adaptation, and comparative genomics.

title: Genetic analysis of 7,000 year old preserved goat leather from Cueva de los Murciélagos (Albuñol, Spain).
abstract: Advances in ancient DNA research have expanded the range of materials from which genetic information can be recovered, enabling the analysis of atypical materials. These often preserve both host and exogenous DNA, for example due to handling or native microbes, offering a window into past diversity. Here we report one such exceptional material: a well-preserved goat leather specimen from Cueva de los Murciélagos (Albuñol, Spain), associated with an Early Neolithic context. Archaeozoological analyses show clear evidence of tanning and anthropogenic modification of the skin, while radiocarbon dating confirms it to be ~ 7,250-7,000 years old. We generated genome-wide data from the leather (Murciélagos1) and demonstrated that it derives from a domestic goat of European ancestry. Comparisons with modern goats show highest affinity to the Bermeya breed from northern Spain, demonstrating genetic connectivity in goat herds from the Neolithic to present day Iberia. We additionally recover fragmented DNA from the leather deriving from human and canid sources, the former likely reflecting handling/wearing of the leather and the latter indicating post-depositional disturbance. Murciélagos1 represents one of the oldest nuclear genome data from organic remains outside of high altitude, high latitude regions, and demonstrates the value of ancient DNA analysis in exceptional cases of organic preservation.

title: Health visibility in electoral candidate programs: Insights from the ballot box in an Arab Gulf country.
abstract: Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries face substantial burdens from noncommunicable diseases along with high public expectations of health services, yet little is known about whether health is visibly represented in candidates' declared election programs in this region. This study examined publicly identifiable candidates' programs from the Kingdom of Bahrain's Council of Representatives 2022 elections and assessed among candidates with identifiable programs whether the presence of explicit visible health content and candidates' characteristics are associated with positive election outcomes. A cross-sectional study was undertaken using the complete cohort of candidates in Bahrain's 2022 elections (N = 336). Election programs were identified from publicly declared materials, and health visibility was coded as present when a program contained an explicit pledge, priority or proposal addressing health services, public health, prevention, health issues, or health related social support. Descriptive data analysis used full cohort of candidates (N = 336) where applicable, whereas analysis of health visibility was conditional on 108 candidates with identifiable programs. Of the 336 candidates, 262 (78.0%) were men and 40 (11.9%) were elected to the council. Among candidates with a publicly identifiable program (108), 88 (81.5%) candidates had visible health content in their identified programs. In Firth penalized-likelihood analysis, women had higher odds of visible health content than men (OR=3.826, 95% profile-likelihood CI 0.943-15.522, p = 0.060). Among program identified candidates (N = 108), the association between visible health content and electoral success was inconclusive (two-sided Fisher's exact test p = 0.188). This study has systematically quantified the health content visibility in a full candidate cohort from Bahrain's Council of Representatives 2022 elections. Although exploratory, these findings provide evidence on how health issues are represented in electoral discourse in this Arab Gulf setting and may inform future comparative studies across GCC countries.

title: Identification and validation of biomarkers associated with mitochondrial dynamics dysfunction in Parkinson's disease based on GEO datasets.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Parkinson's disease (PD), the second most prevalent neurodegenerative disorder, is characterized by an unclear etiology and a lack of specific early diagnostic biomarkers. This study investigated novel biomarkers associated with mitochondrial dynamics (MD) dysfunction in PD.
METHODS: Transcriptomic data from the Gene Expression Omnibus database (training set: GSE6613, n = 72; validation set: GSE99039, n = 438) and 23 MD-related genes (MDRGs) were integrated. Differentially expressed genes were screened using the limma package. Three machine learning algorithms (random forest, support vector machine, and generalized linear model) were employed to construct diagnostic models. Feature importance analysis identified key candidate biomarkers, which were preliminarily validated in clinical samples via reverse transcription quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR). Functional enrichment, immune infiltration, and compound prediction analyses were subsequently performed.
RESULTS: Cysteinyl leukotriene receptor 2 (CYSLTR2) and alpha‑tocopherol transfer protein‑like gene (TTPAL) were identified as MDRG score-correlated biomarkers. In the validation set, CYSLTR2 was significantly downregulated (log2FC = -1.25, P < 0.001) and participated in neuroactive ligand-receptor interactions. Conversely, TTPAL was significantly upregulated (log2FC = 1.52, P < 0.001) and associated with the pathogenic Escherichia coli infection pathway. Immune analysis revealed six differentially infiltrated immune cell types. Notably, TTPAL expression was positively correlated with keratinocytes (cor = 0.30, P = 0.031). Four potential therapeutic compounds were predicted. RT-qPCR suggested the downregulation of CYSLTR2 and upregulation of TTPAL in patients with PD (P < 0.0001).
CONCLUSION: This study identified CYSLTR2 and TTPAL as novel candidate biomarkers associated with MD dysfunction in PD, providing novel targets for mechanistic investigation and therapeutic exploration.

title: Impact of cardiometabolic and renal phenotypes on the prevalence of type 2 diabetes in the geriatric population of Añisok, Equatorial Guinea: A prospective cohort study (2024-2025).
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) represents a growing global health challenge, with management increasingly focused on organ protection and mitigating cardiometabolic-renal risk. In sub-Saharan African geriatric populations, the interplay between frailty, hypertension, and obesity presents critical diagnostic and management challenges. This prospective cohort study evaluated the baseline prevalence of T2D and the prospective risk of major adverse clinical outcomes associated with a concomitant high-risk cardiometabolic phenotype among older adults in Añisok, Equatorial Guinea.
METHODS: A total of 1,702 older adults (aged 60-100 years) were enrolled and followed prospectively from July 2024 to December 2025 (median follow-up: 18.6 months). Participants were stratified at baseline into a High Cardiometabolic Risk Cohort (n = 1,500; concomitant presence of obesity [BMI ≥ 30 kg/m2] AND hypertension [BP ≥ 140/90 mmHg or active antihypertensive treatment]) and a Low-Risk / Control Cohort (n = 202; normotensive and BMI < 30 kg/m2). Baseline prevalent T2D, prospective incident T2D (among baseline non-diabetics, n = 612), composite Major Adverse Cardiometabolic and Renal Events (MACRE), acute renal function decline, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), and peripheral vascular complications were evaluated using multivariable Poisson regression with robust variance and logistic regression models.
RESULTS: The overall baseline prevalence of T2D across the entire cohort was 64.0% (n = 1,090; 95% CI: 61.7%-66.3%). Among baseline non-diabetic participants (n = 612), the prospective 18-month incidence of T2D was 31.4% (n = 192). Over follow-up, composite MACRE occurred in 17.5% (263/1,500) of the high-risk cohort versus 4.5% (9/202) in the control cohort (adjusted Relative Risk [aRR] = 3.41, 95% CI: 1.75-6.66; p < 0.001). The high-risk phenotype was also independently associated with prospective peripheral vascular necrosis (aRR = 5.82, 95% CI: 1.44-23.51; p = 0.013) and baseline target-organ damage (aOR = 2.18, 95% CI: 1.84-2.58; p < 0.001). The prospective absolute risk difference (ARD) for composite MACRE between primary exposure cohorts was 13.0% (95% CI: 9.8%-16.2%), while the overall cumulative target-organ complication ARD was 18.8% (95% CI: 15.2%-22.4%). In secondary subgroup analysis stratified by baseline prevalent diabetes status, diabetic participants (n = 1,090) accumulated 263 composite MACRE events (24.1%) compared to 9 events (1.5%) in non-diabetic participants (n = 612; ARD = 22.6%, 95% CI: 19.8%-25.4%; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Concomitant obesity and hypertension are independently associated with a significantly higher prevalence of target-organ involvement and prospective risk of cardiorenal and vascular complications in older adults in rural Equatorial Guinea. These findings highlight the need for early multi-organ risk screening in primary care settings across resource-limited central African populations.

title: In vivo Nupr1 regulates oxidative stress-endoplasmic reticulum stress crosstalk and mitochondria-dependent apoptosis in varicocele-related testicular injury.
abstract: Varicocele (VCL) is a major cause of male infertility and is closely associated with oxidative stress (OS)-induced testicular injury. Increasing evidence suggests that endoplasmic reticulum stress (ERS) interacts with OS and mitochondrial dysfunction in the pathogenesis of spermatogenic impairment, but the molecular regulators linking these processes remain incompletely understood. In this study, we investigated the role of Nupr1 in VCL-related testicular stress responses. Re-analysis of transcriptomic data from VCL rat testes identified Nupr1 as a candidate gene associated with OS, ERS, and apoptosis. Nupr1 expression was significantly increased in VCL testes and was similarly upregulated in GC-2 and TM4 cells under H2O2-induced OS or tunicamycin-induced ERS. Stable knockdown of Nupr1 in GC-2 cells reduced viability under oxidative challenge, increased intracellular ROS accumulation, decreased mitochondrial membrane potential, and enhanced apoptosis, accompanied by increased cleaved caspase-3 expression and an elevated Bax/Bcl-2 ratio. Notably, Nupr1 deficiency attenuated the adaptive ERS response, as shown by reduced expression of GRP78, IRE1/p-IRE1, PERK/p-PERK, and ATF6. Pharmacological induction of ERS with tunicamycin further worsened cell injury in Nupr1-deficient cells, whereas 4-PBA failed to restore cell viability or GRP78 expression. Collectively, these findings indicate that Nupr1 is involved in the cellular stress response relevant to VCL and may help maintain adaptive UPR signaling and mitochondrial homeostasis in spermatogenic cells under oxidative stress.

title: Integrative analysis reveals shared biomarkers and pathways in osteoporosis and rheumatoid arthritis using machine learning and single-cell sequencing.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Osteoporosis (OP) and Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) are prevalent chronic diseases characterized by bone loss and immune dysregulation. Evidence suggests that patients with RA are at increased risk of developing OP; however, the shared molecular mechanisms linking these conditions remain incompletely understood.
METHODS: Publicly available bulk transcriptomic and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) datasets for OP and RA were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) was applied to identify shared gene modules associated with both diseases. Functional enrichment and protein-protein interaction analyses were performed to characterize common biological pathways. Machine learning algorithms, including Random Forest (RF) and Support Vector Machine (SVM), were used to identify and validate shared hub genes and to construct diagnostic models. Immune cell infiltration was evaluated using CIBERSORT, and the cellular localization of hub genes was further validated using scRNA-seq analysis.
RESULTS: WGCNA identified 329 genes shared between OP- and RA-associated modules, which were significantly enriched in muscle-related processes, cytokine signaling, and immune-inflammatory pathways. RF analysis identified three shared candidate genes: ANO5, IL27RA, and CNTN3. Among these, ANO5 and IL27RA demonstrated consistent expression evidence and literature support, whereas CNTN3 emerged as a computationally nominated candidate requiring cautious interpretation and experimental validation. An SVM-based model incorporating these genes demonstrated robust predictive accuracy in both OP and RA validation cohorts. Immune infiltration analysis revealed distinct yet coordinated immune landscapes, with hub genes showing significant correlations with T cells, macrophages, B cells, and plasma cells. ScRNA-seq analysis revealed that ANO5 was predominantly expressed in macrophages and fibroblasts, IL27RA was mainly enriched in T cells, whereas CNTN3 showed minimal enrichment at the single-cell level in both OP bone and RA synovial tissues.
CONCLUSION: This integrative bioinformatics and machine learning study identifies shared molecular signatures and immune-related mechanisms underlying OP and RA. ANO5 and IL27RA emerge as robust candidate regulators linking immune dysregulation and bone remodeling, whereas CNTN3-although identified by machine learning-requires cautious interpretation and further investigation due to limited supporting evidence. These findings provide novel insights into the pathogenesis of RA-associated OP and highlight potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets for their comorbidity.

title: Investigating GLP-1 sourcing preferences on social media and motivations for use: Survey with choice-based conjoint (CBC) exercise.
abstract: The growing use of glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) drugs such as Ozempic for weight loss interventions has led to increased concerns about inappropriate use, supply shortages, and high-risk sourcing. However, little is known about the influence of online marketing strategies on purchasing preferences for GLP-1 products. This study uses a survey with a Choice-Based Conjoint (CBC) exercise to assess features of social media posts that are most influential for intent to purchase GLP-1 products and identify motivations for use. Participants were recruited based on current use of GLP-1 drugs, previous use, or considering use (n = 242). Utility scores from the conjoint analysis quantified the influence of tested features. Conjoint findings showed greater preference for posts that feature branded semaglutide (e.g., Wegovy)(15.38, SD = 45.29), display products in packaging (47.49, SD = 46.72), have accredited digital pharmacies as the seller (25.16, SD = 47.31) (e.g., Amazon Pharmacy), include medical endorsements for diabetes treatment (13.16, SD = 49.04), and offer a free consultation (13.18, SD = 32.00). Analysis was conducted on survey questions measuring GLP-1 purchasing channels and motivations for use. Over half of participants (51.7%) reported that social media content influenced their perceptions of GLP-1 drugs and 45.8% (n = 65) of GLP-1 users reported purchasing product from high-risk sources (i.e., personal network or individual sellers online). Exploratory analysis shows a possible association between self-reported high-risk sourcing and reliance on GLP-1s for medical conditions. Overall, our findings identify influential attributes of GLP-1 social media ads (i.e., branding and visual display of products) and suggests greater support is needed for online moderation efforts to prevent high-risk purchasing activity and increase safe access to GLP-1s for those with medical needs.

title: Kin count: Social, physiological, and environmental correlates of annual survival in Belding's ground squirrels.
abstract: Long-term studies of free‑living animals provide opportunities to identify the traits and environmental conditions that predict survival under natural selection. Using over two decades of mark-recapture demographic data, we evaluated intrinsic, social and environmental predictors of annual survival in a population of Belding's ground squirrels (Urocitellus beldingi), obligate hibernators that exhibit female philopatry and kin-structured social groups. We assessed the effects of age, sex, body mass, glucocorticoid physiology, reproductive effort, kinship and snowfall using sex-specific generalized linear mixed models and logistic regressions. Adult females had higher survival than adult males, whereas juveniles-particularly males-experienced the highest mortality. As expected, survival was strongly associated with body condition: heavier individuals and those with lower fecal glucocorticoid metabolites were more likely to survive. For the first time, we demonstrate that the number of relatives predicted survival in this species. That is, adult females' probability of surviving to the next summer increased with the specific number of living female close kin, beyond the effect of kin presence alone. Male survival was unrelated to kinship. In contrast, juvenile females with more kin had lower survival, suggesting age‑specific trade‑offs associated with kin structure. Earlier emergence from hibernation improved juvenile survival and was also associated with successful adult female reproduction. Snowfall influenced survival through phenological pathways: lower snow before the active season was associated with earlier emergence and higher survival in adult females, while post‑season snow was not related to survival. Together, these results show that social structure, physiological state, and climate‑driven seasonal timing interact to shape annual survival in an obligate hibernator, with effects that vary by sex and life stage. Understanding these interactions will be increasingly important as snowfall declines across much of U. beldingi's range.

title: Lifestyle and dietary changes among cancer patients receiving active treatment: A cross-sectional study at a tertiary care center in Lebanon.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer diagnosis is often accompanied by changes in nutritional needs and lifestyle habits, which may ultimately be associated with patients' quality of life (QOL). Despite the high burden of cancer in Lebanon, limited data exist on how dietary intake and lifestyle behaviors change following diagnosis. This study aimed to assess self-reported retrospective changes in dietary and lifestyle behaviors following cancer diagnosis and examine factors associated with these changes and their relationship with QOL.
METHODS: This single-center, cross-sectional study was conducted at Al Zahraa Hospital University Medical Center in Beirut, Lebanon. Adult cancer patients receiving active treatment were assessed regarding self-reported dietary and lifestyle behaviors before and after cancer diagnosis. QOL was assessed using the validated Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy-General (FACT-G).
RESULTS: This study included 145 participants, the majority of whom were Lebanese (93.79%) and female (69.7%). Most lacked health insurance (84.8%), and 91.0% reported a financial burden related to treatment. Compared with recalled pre-diagnosis behaviors, 47.6% of participants reported favorable changes in smoking behavior, while 34.5% reported decreased physical activity. The most frequently reported favorable dietary changes according to the prespecified framework were reduced sugar (60.0%), reduced red meat (49.6%), and reduced fast-food consumption (34.5%). Younger age and employment were associated with the favorable dietary-change score in bivariate analyses, while age and marital status were associated with tobacco-habit change in multivariable analysis; medical insurance was associated with physical-activity change in bivariate analysis. The mean FACT-G total score was 70.48 ± 20.79. Favorable dietary changes were associated with FACT-G scores, including changes in fruit, milk, and fast-food intake.
CONCLUSIONS: Self-reported retrospective changes in dietary and lifestyle behaviors were observed among patients receiving active cancer treatment, with substantial variation across behavioral domains. The favorable dietary-change score was associated with QOL; however, the cross-sectional design and retrospective assessment preclude causal or directional interpretation. These findings may inform future longitudinal and interventional studies evaluating structured, individualized nutritional and lifestyle support during cancer treatment in Lebanon.

title: Metagenomic analysis of tomato rhizosphere microbiomes detects Ralstonia phage sequences in Kenyan agricultural soils.
abstract: Bacterial wilt caused by Ralstonia solanacearum species complex is a major constraint in tomato production in Kenya, resulting in yield losses of up to 100% in heavily infested fields. This study used high-throughput shotgun metagenomic sequencing approach to characterize the rhizosphere microbiomes of tomato plants in three of the major production areas in Kenya (Kirinyaga, Kiambu, and Laikipia counties) focusing on detecting Ralstonia phage sequences. Soil samples were collected from the rhizosphere of bacterial wilt-infected tomato plants, and microbial DNA was extracted using a modified phenol-chloroform protocol and sequenced using Illumina NovaSeq platform. Taxonomic profiling revealed diverse microbial communities dominated by Actinobacteria and Proteobacteria. Four Ralstonia species were confirmed (R. insidiosa, R. pickettii, R. mannitolilytica and R. wenshanensis). Sequences similar to the R. solanacearum species complex were also detected but were too short for species-level confirmation. Metagenomic analysis detected sequences matching four previously described Ralstonia phages (RSL1, RSIBR3, Anchaing, and Cimandef). Functional annotation demonstrated abundant metabolic pathways, energy production systems, and stress response mechanisms, indicating highly adaptive microbial communities in the tomato rhizosphere. This study provides baseline data on rhizosphere microbiome composition in Kenyan tomato production systems and identifies Ralstonia phage sequences that could guide future isolation and host-range studies. If future work shows that these phages are active against Ralstonia, they could contribute to locally adapted biocontrol approaches that reduce reliance on chemical pesticides.

title: Morphological adaptation of the root system of silver fir responding to changes of local environmental conditions.
abstract: The study aimed to verify allometric changes in the root system structure of nearly 100-year-old silver fir (Abies alba Mill.) growing in Białowieża Forest. Traditional views of this species as possessing a simple taproot with 4-5 strong diagonal roots required supplementation with evidence of significant modification under specific conditions. It was observed that it developed extensive lateral root networks reaching 41.8-44.2 m diameter in the upper soil profile, exceeding previously reported maxima (21.2 m). This resulted from reduced competition after Norway spruce (Picea abies (L.) H.Karst) mortality due to drought, low groundwater level, and bark beetle infestation. The allometric shift in favor of lateral roots shows significant plasticity despite advanced age. The results confirm the climax nature of the species and show that the studied species has significant morphological adaptation. Remarkable are the significant spatial parameters (especially horizontal) of the distribution of the thin roots in the horizon of soil parent rock: depth 1.95-2.40 m, distance from the tree 6.40-10.38 m.They belong to a flattened bundle of roots growing parallel to the soil surface from the tip of the taproot and diagonal roots. Root systems were examined using ground-penetrating radar and traditional excavation methods combined with soil coring. Root identification relied on distinctive visual characteristics and anatomical analysis.

title: Mothers' experiences of caring for a child with acute lymphoblastic leukemia in the West Bank, Palestine: A qualitative study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute lymphoblastic leukaemia (ALL) is the most common childhood cancer globally and requires prolonged, intensive treatment that places substantial demands on families. Mothers often assume primary caregiving roles; however, their experiences in conflict-affected settings remain underexplored.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to explore the experiences of Palestinian mothers caring for a child diagnosed with ALL in the West Bank.
METHODS: A qualitative descriptive study included fifteen mothers of children diagnosed with ALL and receiving treatment at Beit Jala Governmental Hospital, who were recruited using purposive sampling. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, transcribed verbatim and analyzed using qualitative content analysis following the approach of Graneheim and Lundman (2004).
RESULTS: The study identified five major themes and eighteen sub-themes reflecting mothers' experiences: emotional issues (shock and disbelief, negative emotions, denial and rejection); hindrances due to political situations (limited health care access, feeling isolated due to closures); impact of the child's illness (caregiver burden vs. protective bonding, financial strain, loss of previous life, sibling neglect, shift in the role of the mother, marital life impact, challenges in balancing home routine); resilience and endurance (leveraging social support networks, fatalism and religious faith as a framework, cultivating optimism and positive outlook); and mothers' needs to enhance resilience (emotional and psychological support, educational and informational needs, financial needs).
CONCLUSION: Mothers caring for children with ALL in the West Bank face profound emotional, social, and structural challenges shaped by both illness-related and political contextual factors. Despite these adversities, mothers demonstrate resilience through social support networks, religious faith, and optimism. Family-centered and context-sensitive interventions that address emotional, educational, and financial needs are essential for strengthening maternal resilience and improving care outcomes.

title: Nationwide trends in physical disability among rheumatoid arthritis patients in Korea (2010-2022): A retrospective cohort study based on national registry data.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether the burden of legally certified disability among patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) has decreased in the modern treatment era is uncertain, particularly in Asia. We investigated trends in registered and physical disability among Korean patients with RA.
METHODS: Using National Health Insurance Service data (patient-level 50% random sample), we identified patients aged ≥19 years with seropositive RA registered in the copayment assistance program for rare and intractable diseases in 2010-2022. Disability status, including physical disability (certified musculoskeletal impairment), came from the national disability registry. We estimated annual prevalence and, in newly diagnosed patients, incidence per 1,000 person-years, and compared the results with national disability statistics.
RESULTS: The number of patients with seropositive RA identified in the database and included in this study was 33,992 in 2010 and 67,844 in 2022. The prevalence of registered disability declined from 20.3% to 14.6% and that of physical disability from 17.4% to 10.9% (both p for trend <0.001) in both sexes. Among 61,086 newly diagnosed patients, the incidence of registered disability did not change (5.08 per 1,000 person-years; annual change -0.9%, p = 0.24), whereas that of physical disability declined by 6.7% per year (p < 0.001). Men had a higher incidence of registered disability than women (6.73 vs. 4.58 per 1,000 person-years), but not of physical disability. Older age (odds ratio [OR] 1.035 per year, 95% CI 1.032-1.039), male sex (OR 1.295, 95% CI 1.174-1.429), and lower income were associated with incident registered disability. In 2022, physical disability remained more prevalent in RA (10.9%) than in the general population (2.3%) and in those aged ≥65 years (7.1%).
CONCLUSIONS: Certified physical disability among Korean patients with RA declined substantially between 2010 and 2022, whereas the incidence of any registered disability remained stable. An excess burden of physical disability compared with the general population persisted.

title: Open access route and citation impact in orthopaedic research: A comparison of Gold/hybrid, Green, and Bronze open access within ten high-impact subscription-based journals.
abstract: Open access (OA) publishing has expanded access to research, but citation patterns may differ across OA routes. We examined the association between OA route and citation rate within ten high-impact, predominantly subscription-based orthopaedic journals, analysing 24,115 articles published from 2014 to 2019. Journals in which more than 95% of articles were OA were excluded by design; fully OA journals were therefore not represented, and every Gold OA article in this corpus was published as hybrid OA within a subscription journal (hereafter Gold/hybrid OA). Articles were classified as Gold/hybrid OA, Green OA, Bronze OA, or Closed Access using Web of Science OA indicators. Results are reported in three layers: unadjusted descriptive comparisons, a primary adjusted analysis, andsensitivity analyses. The primary analysis used an entropy-balanced negative binomial generalized linear mixed model adjusting for publication year, document type, author count, and journal influence, with journal-level random effects. Most articles were Closed Access (78.5%), followed by Green OA (9.1%), Bronze OA (8.7%), and Gold/hybrid OA (3.8%). In the primary analysis, Gold/hybrid OA and Green OA had higher citation rates than Closed Access (rate ratio 1.41, 95% CI 1.30-1.54; and 1.35, 95% CI 1.28-1.43), and did not differ from each other (1.04, 95% CI 0.95-1.15). Citation rates varied by publication year: Gold/hybrid OA had the highest predicted rate in recent cohorts and Green OA in older cohorts with longer follow-up. Bronze OA had the lowest unadjusted citation counts, largely because it was enriched for lower-cited document types. The higher citation rates for Gold/hybrid and Green OA persisted across all sensitivity analyses. Within subscription-based orthopaedic journals, OA routes are not interchangeable; these findings do not extend to fully OA journals.

title: Operationalizing independent oversight in large-scale public health cohorts: Monitoring protocol for the NIMHANS-NH-SKAN Stroke project.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: onitoring the implementation of observational studies are rare, unlike experimental studies. This article aims to describe the development and implementation of a monitoring plan and framework for a large-scale cohort and quasi-experimental study: the NIMHANS-NH-SKAN Stroke project.
METHODS: The monitoring framework was developed through a systematic, stepwise process involving expert consultation workshops conducted by an Independent Monitoring Team in collaboration with the study team. A logical framework approach was used to identify key processes throughout the study implementation. These processes were then disaggregated into critical activities (sub-processes) to generate an initial list of monitoring items. These items were prioritized using the Vital-Essential-Desirable (VED) strategy through consensus building. The shortlisted items were further refined using SMART criteria (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound) to finalize checklist components. Key Performance Indicators were subsequently derived from the finalized checklist items. The framework emphasized usability, feasibility, and relevance to implementation, enabling systematic monitoring of critical study processes.
RESULTS: A total of 89 activities were identified and consolidated into 10 checklists, from which 16 Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) were derived. The monitoring framework primarily emphasized indicator-based assessment of project outputs and outcomes while ensuring adherence to key processes and quality standards. KPIs were expressed as proportions to facilitate standardized performance assessment across sites and time periods. The checklists comprised a combination of in-person observations and record reviews. Monitoring findings were synthesized into periodic reports based on KPI proportions, enabling objective evaluation of implementation performance and identification of areas requiring corrective action.
CONCLUSIONS: Timely and systematic monitoring is critical to ensure rigor in large-scale projects, and the approach described in this study provides a replicable framework for the development of robust monitoring systems in similar community-based large-scale observational studies in India and similar countries.

title: Opportunities and challenges for introduction of balanced energy protein supplementation through routine antenatal care.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The World Health Organization (WHO) recommends balanced energy and protein (BEP) supplementation during pregnancy in contexts where prevalence of maternal underweight, defined as body mass index (BMI) < 18.5 kg/m2, is ≥ 20%. Evidence shows that BEP supplementation in underweight pregnant women reduces the risk of low birthweight, small for gestational age, and preterm birth. Yet little is known about how to introduce BEP through routine antenatal care (ANC). This paper explores challenges, opportunities, and recommendations for successful introduction of BEP supplementation through ANC service delivery.
METHODS: From August - December 2023, a mixed-methods landscape analysis was carried out, which comprised of a review of country antenatal care guidelines, as well as key informant interviews (KIIs) with thirteen global and country stakeholders. KIIs were recorded, transcribed, and analyzed by themes and subthemes using Dedoose qualitative software 10.0.
RESULTS: Findings revealed confusion around the definition of BEP, coupled with low awareness of the WHO ANC guideline on BEP supplementation among country stakeholders. Provider capacity for BEP provision is weak. Sharing, selling, and stockouts of BEP supplies are common. Data on the feasibility and cost-effectiveness of the introduction of BEP at country level is critical to inform implementation.
CONCLUSION: Successful introduction of BEP as part of ANC service delivery requires country program implementers to consider government commitments, health provider training, demand generation, compliance, supplies and logistics, local production, and routine monitoring of BEP indicators. Globally, standardized BEP guidance, indicators, and definitions are critical to support quality country implementation. For sustainability, emerging concerns around reductions in global health funding should be addressed in future program design and implementation.

title: Opportunities and challenges in training volunteer wildlife detection dog-handler teams for invasive plant monitoring.
abstract: Measures to combat invasive alien species (IAS) are costly and time-consuming, making effective and widely available detection methods essential. Wildlife detection dogs (WDD) are effectively used to detect hidden and cryptic species, offering enormous potential for early detection of IAS. While professional WDDs are rare, private dog owners are looking for meaningful activities. Therefore, we combined online dog training, practical seminars and field tests to train 31 companion dogs and their owners as volunteer WDD teams. We selected three IAS, the Fallopia spp. complex, Impatiens glandulifera and Ambrosia artemisiifolia, as target species due to their prevalence and strong impacts on biodiversity, economy and health. We used detailed video documentation and questionnaires to investigate the effects of inherent (social) parameters, training procedures and environmental conditions on performance and stamina of individual dog-handler teams during training in two cohorts. In total, 87.1% of the participants completed online training, 77.4% the practical seminar and 35.5% conducted the final field test. Both cohorts were comparably fast and accurate during online training, but cohort 1 performed better in the practical seminar. Performance during online training was mostly associated with social factors and reward types. In contrast, best results in the practical seminar were achieved for larger plant parts, when the participants had included all plant parts in their previous training and were able to adapt the training plan slightly. Spontaneous generalisation rate from thawed to fresh laid-out plant parts was 56%. Of the 12 teams conducting the field test, 11 teams passed. Neither the performance during online training nor during the practical seminar ultimately affected operational capability, but personal motivations determined whether a team finished the program. Finally, volunteer WDD teams can demonstrate high efficiency in monitoring, but the intensive training must be carefully monitored by professional ecologists and dog trainers.

title: Physiological and health-related effects of 5G-relevant radiofrequency fields: A systematic review of experimental studies in humans and mammals.
abstract: The introduction of the latest mobile communications standard of the fifth generation (5G) is accompanied by controversial discussions about potential health risks due to radiofrequency electromagnetic field exposure. Therefore, we conducted a systematic review of experimental and epidemiological studies investigating the physiological and health-related effects of 5G-relevant radiofrequency electromagnetic fields in humans and mammals. The review protocol has been registered in PROSPERO (CRD42022374434) and the review conforms to the PRISMA guidelines. The risk of bias and the quality of included studies were assessed using the recommended approach by the Office of Health Assessment and Translation of the National Toxicology Program. A total of 100 experimental animal and seven human controlled studies were included, analyzed, and evaluated. Narrative summaries were performed for a total of 23 topics (e.g., effects on cognition, male fertility, and thermoregulation). However, investigated species and outcomes in studies were very heterogeneous. Additionally, most studies had substantial methodological weaknesses. Only 11 studies showed a low risk of bias. In summary, for most topics, the current scientific data were inadequate to draw any conclusions about the physiological and health-related effects of radiofrequency electromagnetic fields in the investigated frequency range of 3-30 GHz. However, moderate evidence below the limit values was found for cytokine secretion in mice and low evidence was found for structural changes in the hippocampus of rats above the limit values, when taking the exposure limits presently recommended by the International Commission on Non-Ionizing Radiation Protection as the basis. Therefore, we strongly recommend high-quality systematic research. Particular attention should be paid to reasonable hypotheses, experimental studies on effects on the skin, eyes, and temperature increase, exposures to different frequencies and field strengths, as well as epidemiological studies with separate consideration of 5G (if possible).

title: Prediction models for venous thromboembolism in pediatric patients: A protocol for systematic review and critical appraisal.
abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) in children is a severe disease with high mortality rates. It is also gradually recognized as a major source of morbidity in hospitalized children, leading to increased length of hospital stay, higher mortality, and increased costs. The majority of pediatric subjects with VTE present inherited or acquired risk factors,such as the use of a central venous catheter (CVC), which accounts for more than more than 90% of neonatal VTE and 50% of pediatric VTE. Clinical studies on predictive models for VTE in children have shown inconsistent results. This systematic review aims to evaluate published prediction models for pediatric VTE, analyzing their characteristics, predictors, efficacy, and the methodological quality and applicability. The protocol has been prepared using the Preferred Items for Systematic Review and Meta-analysis Protocols (PRISMA-P) guidelines. The systematic review protocol for VTE prediction in pediatric patients has been registered on PROSPERO (PROSPERO 2025CRD420251231316. Available from https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/vi-ew/CRD420251231316.) A comprehensive search across five major databases (PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, CNKI, and Wanfang) will be conducted for studies on prediction models of VTE among pediatric patients. Two researchers will independently screen literature, extract data, and evaluate the bias risk and applicability of included studies using prediction modelling study tools. This systematic review will provide critical insights into the efficacy and quality of reporting of the VTE model in pediatric patients. This will guide clinical physicians in selecting the most appropriate VTE prediction model and inform future research endeavors in pediatric VTE prediction.

title: Psychometric evaluation of the Palliative Nursing Care Quality Scale (PNCQS) among ICU and oncology nurses in Iran.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Reliable and culturally adapted instruments are essential for assessing the quality of palliative nursing care. The Palliative Nursing Care Quality Scale (PNCQS) had not been psychometrically evaluated in Iran. This study aimed to translate the PNCQS into Persian and examine its validity and reliability among Iranian nurses.
METHODS: In this methodological study, the PNCQS was translated into Persian according to the World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines. A total of 620 nurses from oncology and intensive care units in teaching hospitals in Tehran, Tabriz, and Ardabil were recruited using a multi stage cluster sampling strategy with convenience sampling at the final stage. Face, content, and construct validity were evaluated. Construct validity was examined by first testing the original one-factor model using confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), followed by exploratory factor analysis (EFA) and cross-validation of the derived factor structure using CFA on an independent sample. CFA was conducted in AMOS using maximum likelihood estimation with bootstrapping (1,000 resamples). Reliability was assessed by internal consistency (Cronbach's α) and two-week test-retest reliability using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC).
RESULTS: The scale showed excellent content validity (S-CVI = 0.99). The initial CFA demonstrated that the original 20-item unidimensional model did not adequately fit the Iranian data. Subsequent EFA identified a four-factor structure-Family-Centered Care, Empathic and Spiritual Care, Hope and Life Review, and Physical Symptom Management-explaining 51.41% of the total variance. This structure was confirmed by CFA in an independent sample (n = 400), demonstrating good model fit (χ²/df = 2.84, CFI = 0.95, TLI = 0.95, RMSEA = 0.06). Composite reliability exceeded 0.70 for all factors. Although the AVE for Family-Centered Care was slightly below the recommended threshold (0.42), its composite reliability was acceptable (0.81), and discriminant validity was established for all constructs. Cronbach's α was 0.92 for the total scale (subscales: 0.76-0.83), and the two-week test-retest ICC was 0.76.
CONCLUSION: The Persian PNCQS demonstrated satisfactory psychometric properties and a culturally appropriate four-factor structure for assessing the quality of palliative nursing care among Iranian nurses. It provides a reliable multidimensional instrument for clinical practice, research, and quality improvement initiatives in palliative care.

title: SEQuential tUnneled Catheters and Infective Events in haemodiaLysis: A Five-Year Retrospective Cohort Study (SEQUEL Study).
authors: Wan Ahmad Hafiz Wan Md Adnan
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tunnelled-cuffed catheters (TCCs) are widely used for haemodialysis access when permanent vascular access is unavailable. Internal jugular vein (IJV) placement is guideline-preferred, but femoral vein (FV) catheters are frequently used when upper venous access is limited. Whether femoral access confers a higher infection risk than catheter sequence number remains unclear. This study evaluated these two competing determinants of catheter-related bloodstream infection (CRBSI).
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included all TCC insertions at a tertiary nephrology unit between January 2016 and December 2021. The primary analysis examined CRBSI incidence per 1000 catheter-days stratified by catheter sequence number (first, second, third+ insertion per patient). Secondary analyses compared femoral versus internal jugular TCCs overall and within sequence strata. A registry-index cohort (patients with no documented prior TCC before January 2016, n = 135) was used to reduce, though not eliminate, sequence-related confounding in the site comparison; given only 24 CRBSI events, this analysis is exploratory and a clinically meaningful site difference cannot be excluded. Kaplan-Meier methods with log-rank testing were used for time-to-event outcomes. A cluster-robust marginal Cox model was used to account for repeated catheter insertions within patients, adjusting for sequence number, insertion site, age, sex, insertion setting, and exchange from a non-tunnelled catheter.
RESULTS: Among 626 TCC insertions in 339 patients (389 FV, 237 IJV), contributing 98,727 catheter-days, CRBSI incidence escalated with catheter sequence: 1.17 per 1000 catheter-days for first insertions, rising to 1.98 for second and 2.49 for third-or-more insertions. Notably, by the second insertion, CRBSI rates were similar between FV and IJV access (31.7% each). In the index cohort (n = 135; FV = 95, IJV = 40), CRBSI-free survival did not differ significantly between sites (log-rank p = 0.340), nor did catheter survival (p = 0.950) or patient survival (p = 0.487). In the all-TCC cohort, after adjustment for catheter sequence number, age, sex, insertion setting, and exchange from a non-tunnelled catheter using a cluster-robust marginal Cox model, femoral access remained associated with a higher, though attenuated, CRBSI hazard after adjustment for the measured covariates (HR 1.43, 95% CI 1.02-2.01; p = 0.039), indicating a modest residual site hazard beyond the sequence effect.
CONCLUSIONS: Repeated catheterization was independently associated with increasing CRBSI risk, and catheter sequence number was the strongest predictor in the fully adjusted model. The femoral site effect was substantially attenuated after adjustment for sequence and was not statistically significant in the registry-index cohort analysis, though the wide confidence intervals preclude an equivalence interpretation. IJV access remains preferred; when IJV is unavailable, femoral TCC placement may be an acceptable alternative from an infection-risk perspective, but this must be weighed against thrombotic and limb complications, including deep vein thrombosis, which were not systematically ascertained in this study. Residual confounding cannot be excluded in this single-center retrospective study.

title: Saccadic suppression enhances saliency of ecologically relevant stimuli in the zebrafish optic tectum.
abstract: Saccadic suppression, a reduction in visual sensitivity around the time of rapid eye movements, is well-documented in primate psychophysics, but its mechanisms and functions remain debated. Here, we use zebrafish to trace the origins of saccadic suppression, and we demonstrate how saccadic suppression selectively enhances the visual salience of ecologically relevant stimuli. Saccadic suppression thus contributes to more than just compensation for rapid saccade-induced image shifts. We first established a behavioral correlate of saccadic suppression in larval zebrafish escape behavior. Then, using electrophysiology, we show that retinal ganglion cells jumpstart saccadic suppression in a spatial frequency-dependent manner. Calcium imaging, combined with 360° visual stimulation and behavioral tracking, revealed that motor signals enhance peri-saccadic suppression strength in the optic tectum, where suppression lasts for more than 3,000 ms. Notably, saccadic suppression is much weaker and more short-lived for stimuli related to hunting or escape behavior than for behaviorally less relevant global flashes. This unequal attenuation effectively increases the salience of the ecologically relevant stimuli in the optic tectum after saccades. Our results demonstrate that saccadic suppression integrates visual and motor signals to optimize sensory processing within neural constraints, and they provide insights into evolutionarily conserved visual strategies.

title: Shapley fields reveal mosaic chemotopic organization in the mouse Olfactory bulb across diverse chemical feature sets.
abstract: Neural representations in the olfactory bulb (OB) remain poorly understood compared to well-established coding principles in other sensory systems. This difficulty arises because a natural coordinate system for olfactory stimulus space has not yet been identified, complicating the characterization of neural receptive fields analogous to those in other sensory modalities. Moreover, the extent to which these tuning properties are spatially organized within the OB remains unclear. To advance our understanding of the olfactory coding, we introduce an interpretable method of Shapley fields, as an olfactory analog of retinotopic receptive fields. Shapley fields are spatial distributions of chemical feature importance for the tuning of OB glomeruli. We used this tool to investigate chemotopy in the OB with diverse sets of chemical features using widefield epifluorescence recordings of the mouse dorsal OB in response to stimuli across a wide range of the chemical space. We found that Shapley fields reveal a weak chemotopic organization of the chemical feature sensitivity of dorsal OB glomeruli. This organization was consistent across animals and mostly agreed across very different chemical feature sets: (i) the expert-curated PubChem database features and (ii) features derived from a Graph Neural Network trained on human olfactory perceptual tasks. This chemotopy involved at least three chemical feature dimensions, rather than one or two dominant properties. Moreover, we found that the principal components of the Shapley fields corresponded to single commonly accepted chemical classification groups. This implies that these chemical groups could have been identified purely from the mouse olfactory responses. Our findings suggest that Shapley fields may serve as a chemical feature-agnostic method for investigating olfactory perception.

title: Simple and multiplexed tracking of bacterial growth in double emulsion droplets.
abstract: Droplet-based microfluidics enable researchers to observe phenotypic heterogeneity within complex biological mixtures through parallel encapsulation of individual samples followed by imaging. Observing or quantifying dynamic heterogeneity remains challenging due to complexities associated with trapping and tracking many individual droplets. Current approaches for time-lapse imaging require specialized devices with droplet traps that limit accessibility and throughput. Here, using readily available materials and software, we demonstrate a simple method for stabilizing and monitoring many, individual droplets for up to 12 hours. We leveraged our method to track bacterial growth within droplets in a high-throughput manner for over 6 hours. Our method allows tracking the changes and variation in growth rate within and across droplets, revealing heterogeneity in growth patterns hidden in batch assays. Improving the affordability and throughput of time-dependent phenotyping assays helps to advance biological discovery and biotechnology innovation.

title: Spatial accessibility and equity of emergency medical services: Evidence from Ningbo.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Timely access to emergency medical services (EMS) is essential for improving survival outcomes and public health. In rapidly urbanizing Chinese cities, disparities in EMS accessibility are increasingly shaped by the spatial distribution of hospitals, population concentration, transport infrastructure, and built environment conditions. However, relatively few studies have simultaneously compared emergency and non-emergency medical accessibility and examined their spatial equity and influencing factors in medium-sized coastal cities. This study evaluates the spatial accessibility, equity, and clustering characteristics of EMS in Ningbo, China, and identifies the key built environment factors influencing these patterns.
METHODS: The shortest travel time model, based on API data, was employed to measure EMS accessibility for both emergency (ambulance) and non-emergency (public transport) scenarios across five core urban districts of Ningbo. The Lorenz curve and Gini coefficient were applied to assess healthcare equity. We used global Moran's I and local indicators of spatial association (LISA) to explore spatial clustering and a multiscale geographically weighted regression (MGWR) model to analyze spatial heterogeneity in influencing factors across built environment dimensions.
RESULTS: Both emergency and non-emergency medical services exhibited significant spatial disparities, decreasing gradually from the city center toward the periphery. The Gini coefficients for emergency and non-emergency models were 0.5156 and 0.4898, respectively, indicating substantial inequity. Strong spatial clustering was observed (global Moran's I = 0.846, p < 0.01), with high-value clusters concentrated in central districts and low-value clusters in mountainous outskirts. MGWR results revealed that accessibility was positively affected by the number of bus stops, road density, bus route density, and distance to the Central Business District (CBD), but negatively impacted by building density and development intensity. The MGWR model's explanatory power (R2 = 0.584) demonstrated significant spatial heterogeneity in these relationships. Building density and bus route density exerted the strongest local effects among the eleven built environment indicators.
CONCLUSION: EMS accessibility in Ningbo exhibits evident spatial inequality and clustering characteristics. Peripheral and mountainous areas remain disadvantaged, especially under non-emergency public transport conditions. Improving road connectivity, expanding public transit coverage, optimizing hospital and EMS resource allocation, and strengthening services in underserved areas can help reduce healthcare accessibility inequities. These findings provide an empirical foundation for optimizing EMS resource allocation for urban policymakers as well as offer practical insights for other rapidly urbanizing cities facing similar challenges.

title: Stability of eye movement-related eardrum oscillations to acoustic and gravitational/postural manipulations.
abstract: Recent studies describe Eye Movement-Related Eardrum Oscillations (EMREOs), low‑frequency signals recorded in the ear canal that arise from the tympanic membrane and are triggered by saccadic eye movements. Because EMREOs are thought to arise from motor elements in the peripheral auditory system, we examined how two known modulators of these elements affect the EMREO time course. First, the activity of outer hair cells (OHCs) can be suppressed by the medial olivocochlear reflex (MOCR). If OHCs contribute to the generation of EMREOs, activation of this reflex should reduce EMREO amplitude. To test this, we compared EMREO amplitudes elicited by saccades performed in silence and in the presence of contralateral noise. Second, postural (i.e., vestibular and proprioceptive) cues linked to head orientation may influence EMREOs via oculomotor control circuits that possibly modulate middle ear muscles. To test this, we recorded EMREOs while participants made saccades with their head upright (0° azimuth) and with their head tilted 30° in either direction. Across both experiments our data reveal no significant modulation of the EMREO by these experimental manipulations. Together with other recent studies these findings advocate for a stability of the EMREO towards multiple experimental modulations. We discuss how this fuels speculations that the signal may serve as a temporal reference frame, while also being compatible with the notion that the EMREO reflects a spatial coordinate transform for combining signals across the senses.

title: Statistical Parametric Mapping reveals sex-specific, phase-dependent differences in bilateral three-dimensional ground reaction force during Wushu Changbing PiJi in high-level athletes.
abstract: PiJi is a core attacking technique in Wushu Changbing competition, but continuous waveform evidence remains limited regarding the sex-specific phase characteristics of bilateral 3D ground reaction force (GRF) during PiJi performed with maximal voluntary effort (MVE). This study aimed to compare continuous changes in trailing-foot, lead-foot, and net bilateral GRF between high-level male and female athletes during PiJi performed with MVE. In this cross-sectional, laboratory-based observational study, 44 right-hand-dominant athletes, including 22 male athletes and 22 female athletes, performed PiJi with MVE, yielding 616 valid trials. Bilateral 3D GRF was recorded using two force plates. Each trial was time-normalized and linearly interpolated to 143 equally spaced nodes, and within-participant mean waveforms were calculated before between-group differences were analyzed using statistical parametric mapping. Primary analyses used random-field-theory inference, with sensitivity examined using 5,000 permutation tests. After Bonferroni correction, phase-specific sex differences were detected in trailing-foot, lead-foot, and net bilateral 3D GRF. Scalar localization showed that male athletes had higher trailing-foot Fy during the middle phase (33.98%-47.04%) and higher trailing-foot Fx (62.41%-71.99%) and net bilateral Fx (54.18%-70.41%) during the middle-to-late phase; female athletes showed only a brief period of higher trailing-foot vertical Fz during the middle phase (42.11%-44.61%). Although lead-foot 3D GRF differed overall, no confirmatory difference was localized to any single scalar component. These findings indicate that sex-related GRF differences in high-level PiJi were concentrated mainly in specific horizontal-plane phases of trailing-foot and net bilateral force, whereas the lead-foot difference was identified only at the overall 3D GRF level. These results provide kinetic evidence for phase-specific assessment of PiJi technique and suggest that training monitoring and mechanistic research should consider foot, direction, and movement phase rather than relying only on peak force or discrete variables. Future studies integrating multimodal measures and sport-specific performance may further clarify the functional significance of bilateral force-generation patterns.

title: Structural characteristics and policy differences of digital health management policies in China: A quantitative analysis based on the PMC index model.
abstract: Digital health governance increasingly relies on policy systems that coordinate data resources, information platforms, standards, service delivery, regulation, security, innovation, and implementation support. However, the structural composition and cross-policy heterogeneity of China's national digital health policy system remain insufficiently quantified. This study develops a domain-specific Policy Modeling Consistency (PMC) framework to evaluate the structural coverage of national-level digital health management policies in China. Using a source-locked corpus covering 2016-2025, 42 eligible policies were identified, of which 39 with complete and auditable texts were included in the quantitative analysis. The framework comprises nine dimensions and 48 binary indicators, generating 1,872 policy-by-indicator coding decisions. An independently coded 11-policy subset yielded 96.78% agreement and a Cohen's kappa of 0.914. The mean PMC score was 6.654 (SD = 1.456; median = 6.500; range = 3.467-9.000). Under the study's structural-coverage thresholds, nine policies were classified as perfect, 11 as good, 16 as acceptable, and three as poor. Regulatory governance, standards and institutional arrangements, and data resources showed the highest average coverage, whereas data protection and industrial innovation showed the lowest coverage and the greatest cross-policy variation. Leave-one-policy-out and policy-family sensitivity analyses confirmed the stability of the principal structural pattern. These findings reveal a policy architecture with relatively extensive governance, institutional, and data-related provisions but more uneven protection- and innovation-related coverage. The proposed framework provides a reproducible basis for comparing policy-text structure while avoiding the interpretation of textual completeness as evidence of implementation quality or policy effectiveness.

title: Technological adoption and innovation in OECD and BRICS countries: A two‑way fixed effects difference‑in‑differences analysis.
abstract: Understanding how technological progress unfolds across advanced and emerging economies remains central to both innovation research and development policy. This study compares the trajectories of technological adoption and innovation in OECD and BRICS countries using a two-way fixed effects difference-in-differences (DID) framework over the period 1995-2023. The analysis focuses on three core indicators: mobile cellular subscriptions, internet usage, and patent applications, and is supported by an extensive set of diagnostic checks, including partial R² contributions, residual normality and heteroskedasticity tests, and Ramsey RESET tests. Despite historically higher levels of connectivity and innovation in OECD countries, the estimated results indicate a relative slowdown in growth rates for mobile subscriptions, internet adoption, and patenting activity, with negative and statistically significant coefficients across specifications with and without control variables. On the other hand, BRICS countries show steady progress in all three outcomes, often rapid, catch‑up. These findings challenge conventional assumptions about the persistence of technological leadership in advanced economies and suggest that emerging economies are increasingly shaping global patterns of technology adoption and innovation. The results emphasize the necessity of policy frameworks that recognize heterogeneous pathways of technological progress and support both diffusion and innovation in a changing global economic landscape.
