title: The behaviour bends, the code holds: working-memory category information in the multiple-demand network across graded interruption
abstract: Protecting working memory (WM) from interference is essential for goal-directed behaviour, yet its neural mechanisms remain unclear. The multiple-demand (MD) network - a set of frontoparietal regions recruited by diverse cognitive demands - is a candidate system for maintaining WM content under interference. We examined how the MD network represents a memorandum when an unrelated task interrupts maintenance. Participants memorised an image of a tool or animal and, during the delay, performed a digit task whose difficulty was parametrically varied (passive, easy, hard), allowing us to test how task engagement and associated cognitive demands affected concurrently maintained information. Using fMRI and multivariate pattern analysis, we decoded the maintained category (tool vs. animal) from 13 MD regions and early visual cortex. Behaviourally, interruption reduced recall accuracy, while the most demanding interrupter slowed responses. Neurally, category information was present during the delay, most strongly in visual cortex and bilateral intraparietal sulcus. This information was unaffected by task engagement (active vs. passive), consistently across decoding accuracy and cross-validated Mahalanobis (crossnobis) distance, with Bayesian evidence supporting the null effect. Increasing the demand of the active interrupter, however, produced a modest, network-wide reduction in crossnobis distance that was not detectable in decoding accuracy. Together, these findings reveal a dissociation between the behavioural costs of interruption and the neural representation of maintained category information. Although interruption impaired recall, engaging in an interrupter did not measurably alter category-level information in the MD network or visual cortex. Increasing the demand of the interrupter produced only a modest, network-wide reduction in representational distance, without affecting decoding accuracy, suggesting that the behavioural costs of interruption may not be fully explained by changes in the categorical representation of the memorandum.

title: The ontogeny of hippocampal spatial memory is supported by postnatal Cajal-Retzius cells
abstract: The functional capabilities of the adult hippocampus depend on specialized circuits that are established during development. Cajal-Retzius (CR) cells persist in the hippocampus long after their disappearance from the neocortex and contribute to the postnatal maturation of hippocampal circuits, but how this developmental role shapes adult hippocampal function remains unknown. Here, we selectively ablated CR cells from the postnatal hippocampus and examined the consequences for spatial learning, navigation, and CA1 spatial representations. CR-cell ablated animals learned reward locations and adapted to changing task conditions, but learned more slowly and made more errors. Reinforcement-learning models suggest that these behavioral differences reflect less stable internal representations guiding behavior. Consistent with this, CA1 spatial representations remained present but were more unstable and showed reduced differentiation of reward locations, particularly when task conditions changed. Our findings identify postnatal CR cells as key developmental contributors to the stability of hippocampal spatial representations and the adaptive behavior they support.

title: Unilateral naris occlusion with custom-made plugs for reversible olfactory deprivation in juvenile and adult mice
abstract: Deprivation paradigms that reduce environmental input have been successfully applied across multiple species and sensory modalities, including vision, audition, somatosensation, and olfaction in order to understand how neurons and circuits respond to loss of sensory input. One notable advantage of studying sensory deprivation in the rodent olfactory system is the ease and control with which smell loss can be induced. Various methods of olfactory deprivation have long been available and rely on blocking a nostril, either through invasive and often non-reversible approaches such as chemical ablation or surgical procedures, or through reversible approaches such as unilateral naris occlusion using custom-made nose plugs. Here, we provide a systematic description of this well-established method, including its construction from commercially available materials, procedures, validation, and reliability in post-weaning mice, thereby providing a detailed and reproducible framework for controlled, reversible olfactory deprivation.

title: Vision-language representations link food perception to subjective valuation
abstract: Subjective values of foods guide dietary decisions. Yet, how the brain computes such values from visual input remains unclear. Here, we show that visual food valuation relies on higher-level conceptual representations captured by a multimodal vision-language deep neural network model. Using food images and human ratings (N = 194 and 200), we found that a vision-language model predicted subjective value more accurately than vision-only models. Representational analyses demonstrated that, compared with the vision-only model, the vision-language model preferentially encoded higher-level food attributes, including perceived healthiness, while encoding less image-level visual information. Multivariate analyses of fMRI data (N = 31) showed that embedding features from both models corresponded to activity patterns along the visual pathways. Critically, vision-language features showed greater correspondence than vision-only features in the fusiform gyrus, a downstream region of the ventral visual pathway. These findings suggest that higher-level conceptual representations link visual food processing to subjective valuation.

title: Cancer cells differentially modulate mitochondrial respiration to alter redox state and enable biomass synthesis in nutrient-limited environments.
abstract: The cell NAD+/NADH ratio can constrain biomass synthesis and influence proliferation in nutrient-limited environments. However, which cell processes regulate the NAD+/NADH ratio is not known. Here, we find that some cancer cells elevate the NAD+/NADH ratio in response to serine deprivation by increasing mitochondrial respiration. Cancer cells that elevate mitochondrial respiration have higher serine production and proliferation in serine-limiting conditions than cells with no mitochondrial respiration response, independent of serine synthesis enzyme expression. Increases in mitochondrial respiration and the NAD+/NADH ratio promote serine synthesis regardless of whether serine is environmentally limiting. Lipid deprivation can increase the NAD+/NADH ratio via mitochondrial respiration in some cells, including cells that do not increase respiration following serine deprivation. Thus, in cancer cells where lipid depletion raises the NAD+/NADH ratio, proliferation in serine-depleted environments improves when lipids are also depleted. Taken together, these data suggest that changes in mitochondrial respiration in response to nutrient deprivation can influence the NAD+/NADH ratio in a cell-specific manner to impact oxidative biomass synthesis and proliferation. Given the complexity of tumor microenvironments, this work provides a metabolic framework for understanding how levels of more than one environmental nutrient affect cancer cell proliferation.

title: Estimating bone marrow adiposity from head MRI and identifying its genetic architecture.
abstract: Bone marrow (BM) adiposity changes radically through the lifespan, but this phenomenon is poorly characterized and understood in humans. Large datasets of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans of the head have been collected to study the human brain, but also contain unexploited information about other organs. We developed an artificial neural network that localizes calvarial BM in T1-weighted MRI head scans, enabling us to study its composition in several large MRI datasets, and to model sex-dimorphic age trajectories, including the effect of menopause. We revealed high heritability in single-nucleotide polymorphism and twin data, and identified 41 genetic loci significantly associated with the trait, including six sex-specific loci. Integrating mapped genes with existing BM single-cell RNA-sequencing data revealed patterns of adipogenic lineage differentiation and lipid loading. Finally, we identified significant genetic correlations with several human traits, including cognitive ability and Parkinson's disease, which is intriguing in light of the recently discovered channels that link calvarial BM to the meninges.

title: Targeting tankyrase scaffolding in the β-catenin destruction complex by PROTAC overcomes the limitation of catalytic inhibitors in colorectal cancer.
abstract: Aberrant WNT/β-catenin signaling drives tumorigenesis and metastasis in cancer. Although enzymatic inhibitors of tankyrase (TNKS) effectively block AXIN degradation and stabilize the β-catenin destruction complex (DC), they have demonstrated limited efficacy in various colorectal cancer (CRC) models. Here, we demonstrate that, unexpectedly, the induction of AXIN puncta represents a major barrier to achieving therapeutic efficacy. Mechanistically, catalytic inhibition of TNKS prevents TNKS turnover and drives its accumulation in the DC, wherein the scaffolding function of TNKS induces AXIN puncta formation, rigidifies the DC, and impedes β-catenin turnover. Chemically induced degradation of TNKS overcomes this limitation by stabilizing AXIN without puncta formation, providing a deeper suppression of the WNT/β-catenin pathway activity and the proliferation of CRC cells harboring dysfunctional APC mutations. Collectively, these findings provide an explanation for the unsatisfactory outcomes of drugging the WNT/β-catenin signaling pathway by TNKS inhibitors and highlight TNKS degradation as a promising approach to treat WNT/β-catenin-driven CRC.

title: Dysregulated CSF T-cell responses and their evolution after intravenous immunoglobulin in Guillain-Barré syndrome.
abstract: Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) is an acute immune-mediated neuropathy that frequently results in long-term disability. The cellular mechanisms underlying GBS and the immunomodulatory effects of intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg) remain incompletely understood. In this prospective observational cohort study, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing with paired T cell receptor (TCR) sequencing on peripheral blood and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) collected before and after IVIg treatment from treatment-naïve patients with GBS. Pre-treatment blood and CSF were obtained from nine and eight patients, respectively; post-treatment samples were available from six patients for blood and three patients for CSF. Previously published healthy control (HC) blood and CSF single-cell datasets were analyzed for comparison. We characterized immune cell composition, transcriptional states, TCR clonality, and clonal dynamics across peripheral and CSF compartments as well as following treatment. Individuals with GBS exhibited enrichment of T helper 1 (Th1)-polarized CD4+ T cells, activated and resident-memory CD8+ T cells, and macrophages in CSF relative to paired peripheral blood. This CSF-to-blood enrichment was greater than in healthy controls (HCs) for Th1 cells, activated effector-memory CD8+ T cells, and inflammatory macrophages, although the overall degree of T-cell clonal expansion was similar between groups. In both GBS and HCs, expanded CSF CD4+ clonotypes were predominantly Th1-polarized and largely absent from blood, whereas expanded CD8+ clonotypes showed greater overlap between compartments. Among clonotypes detected in both blood and CSF, CD4+ and CD8+ T cells exhibited more activated transcriptional states in the CSF, a shift that was particularly pronounced in GBS. Following IVIg treatment, peripheral blood showed minimal changes, whereas CSF T-cell populations exhibited more substantial alterations, including reductions in Th1-associated and activated effector-memory states, increases in T helper 2 (Th2) and regulatory T cell populations, and changes in the clonal repertoire. Expanded T cell clonotypes with sequence-based predicted specificity for pathogens associated with GBS were identified in six patients, and convergent clonotype groups were detected both within and across patients. Demyelinating GBS is characterized by compartmentalized enrichment and activation of pro-inflammatory T-cell populations within the CSF rather than an overall increase in T-cell clonal expansion. Exploratory longitudinal findings further suggest that CSF T-cell populations are altered following IVIg treatment. Integrated single-cell transcriptomic and TCR analyses provide insight into the early immune response in GBS and identify candidate cellular pathways for biomarker development and therapeutic investigation.

title: A bivalent chromatin reader-WOX5 module maintains root stem cell niche in Arabidopsis.
abstract: Root stem cell niche maintenance requires precise control of quiescent center (QC) and columella stem cell (CSC) activity, yet how chromatin regulators interface with key transcription factors remains poorly understood. Here, we identify the bivalent chromatin reader EARLY BOLTING IN SHORT DAYS (EBS) as an essential regulator of root stem cell maintenance in Arabidopsis. A strong ebs-1 mutant shows CSC differentiation and QC activation, and EBS function requires its histone mark-recognizing BAH and PHD domains and a C-terminal SUMO-interacting motif. EBS physically interacts with the QC master regulator WUSCHEL-RELATED HOMEOBOX 5 (WOX5) and, together with WOX5, activates WOX5 transcription by promoting EBS enrichment at the WOX5 promoter. Consistently, wox5-1 is epistatic to ebs-1, and WOX5 overexpression rescues the ebs-1 stem cell defects. Together, this work uncovers a chromatin-based positive autoregulatory loop that integrates histone-state recognition and transcriptional feedback, providing a framework for epigenetic control of stem cell fate in plants.

title: A shared multi-feature population code for sensory reliability across mouse visual cortex.
abstract: Successful behavior depends on evaluating both what is present in the environment and how reliable that information is. Yet how neural populations represent reliability, and whether this representation is shared across cortical areas, remains unknown. Using two-photon calcium imaging of over 150,000 neurons in mouse visual cortices during presentations of coherent motion stimuli, we find that sensory reliability is encoded through coordinated changes in response amplitude, selectivity, and signal-to-noise ratio. These coherence-dependent response patterns are not fully accounted for by stimulus-based normalization models; rather, they track the distribution of motion energy across directions, while remaining relatively invariant to total motion energy. This multi-feature code is expressed at the single-neuron and population levels and is consistent across visual areas, suggesting a shared encoding scheme rather than area-specific computations. Together, these findings support a common population code for stimulus reliability across visual cortices.

title: ApoE-dependent lipid handling by median eminence microglia supports myelin remodeling and metabolic function.
abstract: Microglia regulate hypothalamic control of systemic metabolism, but the mechanisms underlying their contribution remain unclear. Here, we identify apolipoprotein E (ApoE)-associated microglial transcriptional states enriched in the median eminence (ME), a brain region involved in sensing peripheral cues and metabolic regulation. These transcriptional states are characterized by programs related to lipid handling, interferon-associated responses, and cellular stress. Consumption of a Western diet (WD) increased microglial lipid accumulation and altered myelin remodeling within the ME, while expression of the human APOE4 isoform exacerbated these changes. Deletion of Apoe altered microglial responses to nutritional stress, supporting a role for ApoE in microglial lipid handling. Finally, activation of liver X receptor using synthetic high-density lipoprotein (sHDL) nanoparticles enhanced microglial lipid-handling programs, improved hypothalamic leptin responsiveness, reduced food intake, and limited weight gain in WD-fed mice. Together, these findings identify ApoE-dependent lipid handling as a key component of adaptive microglial responses to metabolic stress.

title: Exercise trains the liver to save the heart.
abstract: Wang and colleagues1 demonstrate that exercise triggers the liver to release clusterin into the bloodstream, improving cardiac remodeling and myocyte proliferation post-myocardial infarction. Their findings add another mechanistic facet to the complexity and controversial role of clusterin in cardiac injury.

title: IDO1 methylation by EZH2 confers resistance to its targeted therapy in colorectal cancer through tryptophan-kynurenine metabolic rewiring.
abstract: Deciphering cancer metabolic reprogramming mechanisms can identify new targets to potentiate EZH2 inhibitor efficacy. Using an in vivo genome-wide CRISPR loss-of-function screen in a CRC mouse model, we pinpointed IDO1 as a key mediator of EZH2 inhibitor resistance. EZH2 blockade remodeled CRC cell metabolism by upregulating IDO1 protein and hyperactivating the tryptophan-kynurenine pathway. Both genetic and pharmacological inhibition of IDO1 suppressed tumor growth and rescued EZH2 inhibitor resistance in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, EZH2 directly binds and methylates IDO1. Methylation of IDO1 facilitates IDO1 ubiquitination and subsequent degradation. Accordingly, EZH2 inhibition stabilizes IDO1, augments tryptophan-kynurenine metabolic flux, and ultimately confers therapeutic resistance. In summary, our study identifies IDO1 as a non-histone substrate of EZH2 methyltransferase activity and validates that disrupting IDO1-mediated tryptophan metabolism is a viable strategy to overcome EZH2 targeted therapy resistance in cancers.

title: Theta-based organization of information in the frontal cortex.
abstract: Theta (4-10 Hz) oscillations seem to coordinate activity across long-range distances. It is less clear how theta coordinates activity more locally within frontal subareas. We examined activity in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC), ventrolateral prefrontal cortex (vlPFC), and frontal eye fields (FEFs) as non-human primates categorized dot patterns. We characterized how theta coordinates activity within frontal cortex. First, theta phase selectively couples to behaviorally relevant information in spiking. Second, theta influences move in a posterior direction during choices (i.e., dlPFC/vlPFC to FEF) and after correct outcomes (i.e., dlPFC to FEF), but not after errors. Instead, anterior-direction (i.e., FEF to vlPFC) theta influences are stronger after errors. Third, theta participates in behaviorally associated nested cross-frequency interactions. Theta couples to beta (15-30 Hz) oscillations during choices and after errors, whereas beta couples to gamma (40-90 Hz) oscillations after correct outcomes. Our results position theta as a critical mechanism that flexibly and dynamically coordinates activity in frontal cortex.

title: Non-triazole agricultural fungicides indirectly select for triazole resistance in the human pathogen Aspergillus fumigatus.
abstract: Agricultural intensification relies on chemical fungicides to manage crop disease,1,2 driving the evolution of resistance in plant pathogens.3 Fungicides persist in the environment, allowing activity beyond their intended targets, affecting downstream ecosystems and agricultural practices. The saprophytic and ubiquitous fungus Aspergillus fumigatus is an important human pathogen causing severe invasive fungal disease.4 Selection by agricultural triazoles, or demethylase inhibitors (DMIs), has led to cross-resistance to clinical triazoles, as both target the cyp51A gene.5,6 In the Netherlands,7,8 most triazole resistance arises from two cyp51A haplotypes, TR34 and TR46.9,10 Genomic surveys show that these resistance alleles often co-occur with resistance alleles to non-DMI fungicides, including quinone outside inhibitors (QoIs) and succinate dehydrogenase inhibitors (SDHIs).11 We hypothesize that agricultural environments with non-DMI fungicides can indirectly select for triazole resistance. Using grass mesocosms to compete A. fumigatus isolates, we found that low concentrations of DMI, SDHI, and QoI fungicides, comparable to agricultural residues, independently increased the proportions of triazole-resistant alleles. Resistance alleles for each class are not intrinsically cross-resistant, indicating that their co-occurrences result from linked resistance alleles. Consistent to these findings, environmental samples from heaps with only non-DMI fungicides contained high phenotypic triazole resistance (>20%). This work provides experimental and field evidence that triazole and non-DMI resistance can increase in parallel, consistent with genomic hitchhiking. We thus predict that novel resistance alleles are likely selected in isolates that have already accumulated resistance alleles to other fungicide classes. Therefore, managing selection and spread of environmental triazole resistance will require consideration of all fungicide classes.

title: Serotonin signaling in the central nervous system is required for correct spine morphogenesis in zebrafish.
abstract: Although adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) affects over 1% of children and teenagers worldwide, its causes are not fully understood. While defects in serotonergic system have been associated with certain familial cases of AIS, the underlying causes remain elusive. Over the last decade, zebrafish have emerged as a valuable model to study the mechanisms driving deformations of the spine by uncovering roles for cilia, sensory feedback, and the Reissner fiber (RF). In tryptophan hydroxylase 2 (tph2) mutant zebrafish, we demonstrate that serotonin (5HT) depletion causes progressive 3D spinal misalignment mimicking human AIS. Mutant larvae develop normally up to 21 days post-fertilization (dpf) when spine curvatures emerge. As in AIS, deformities of zebrafish tph2 mutant worsen with age both in sagittal and coronal planes, without vertebral malformations. Remarkably, the RF is intact, yet 5HT is absent from the spinal cord. Intraspinal serotonergic neurons are gradually depleted up to scoliosis onset, together with supraspinal projections from the inferior raphe, eliminating all sources of 5HT to the spinal cord by 21 dpf. Our findings indicate that spinal 5HT signaling plays an essential role for proper spine alignment during post-embryonic morphogenesis.

abstract: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change recommended 1.5°C carbon reduction target, requiring powerful enforcement from major economies. China, the largest CO 2 emitter, is facing severe difficulties for both variable renewable accommodation and decarbonization of hard-to-abate sectors. Hydrogen, as a critical green energy carrier bridging renewable to end-users, faces significant obstacles in real-world deployment such as costly transportation, storage and fuel-cell adoption. Affordable and coordinated hydrogen deployment plan to accelerate the carbon-neutral transition remains ambiguous. Here, we present cost-effective carbon-neutral transition pathways for entire energy economy of China emphasizing the significant role of hydrogen and derivatives as green energy carriers, considering high-resolution renewable deployments, hourly power system operations in 29 provincial regions, over 46,000 rail/road/marine/pipeline transfer routing of hydrogen derivatives, process-level fuel adoption strategies in all end-use sectors. Results show that incorporating hydrogen and derivatives can reduce the overall transition cost by $ 10.7 trillion compared with renewable and electrification pathways, achieving negative carbon abatement costs ($-6.15/ton), eliminating external oil import expenses, equivalent to over 50% of China trade surplus (2023 level) 1 , significantly boosting employment and economic growth. Hydrogen derivative based transition pathway offers a vital direction for affordable and secure decarbonization for China and beyond under volatile international energy markets.

abstract: Hypertension is a silent killer, with over half of affected adults unaware of their condition 1,2 . This lack of awareness is a major concern, as early intervention is critical for preventing major adverse cardiovascular events 3,4 . Here we show that applying artificial intelligence (AI) to multimodal waveforms (photoplethysmography and accelerometry) recorded using a widely available consumer smartwatch (AI-PPG-ACC-HTN), without any cuff calibration, can detect hypertension with accuracy levels comparable to traditional cuffed blood pressure (BP) devices in the existing clinical framework. We validated AI-PPG-ACC-HTN in a prospective, multicenter study of 196 diverse participants free from known cardiovascular disease and antihypertensive medication against gold-standard 24-hour ambulatory BP monitoring. Over seven days of real-world monitoring, AI-PPG-ACC-HTN detected hypertension with a sensitivity of 65.8% (95% CI, 54.0%-76.3%), specificity of 90.0% (95% CI, 83.2%-94.7%), and positive predictive value (PPV) of 80.6% (95% CI, 68.6%-89.6%). In comparison, initial office BP screening achieved a sensitivity of 55.3% (95% CI, 43.4%-66.7%), specificity of 90.0% (95% CI, 83.2%-94.7%) and PPV of 77.8% (95% CI, 64.4%-88.0%). These results highlight an opportunity for consumer smartwatches to facilitate population-level opportunistic hypertension screening by prompting at-risk individuals toward clinical assessment and confirmatory diagnosis using established cuff-based methodologies, offering an accessible tool to address this major public health challenge.

abstract: Atypical chemokine receptors (ACKRs) are non-signaling GPCRs that regulate ligand availability, with ACKR3 functioning as a dual scavenger of chemokines and opioid peptides. Here, we demonstrate that following ligand stimulation, besides the canonical internalization, ACKR3 is released on extracellular vesicles (EVs). ACKR3 was also found on EVs released under basal conditions, although to a lesser extent. These observations were confirmed across multiple cellular contexts, including endogenous systems. Mechanistically, basal and ligand-induced EV release are independent of GRKs and β-arrestin but each relies on different trafficking routes and C-terminal determinants. Ligand-induced EV release is associated with plasma membrane localization and receptor recycling pathways. In contrast, basal EV release is governed by intracellular sorting processes and influenced by receptor ubiquitination and RAMP3. Functionally, EV-associated ACKR3 retains high-affinity ligand binding, enabling sequestration of CXCL12 and opioid peptides and thereby attenuating their signaling through CXCR4 and MOR. We also show that the release on EVs, in particular under basal conditions, is observed for other receptors such as KOR, CXCR4 and several ACKRs. Collectively, these findings establish EVs as regulators in chemokine and opioid systems and as a distinct dimension of ACKR3 and more broadly GPCR biology.

abstract: Lipid metabolism is fundamental to cellular homeostasis, supporting energy storage, membrane architecture, and cellular signaling. Beyond these canonical roles, lipids have emerged as critical regulators of host immunity. Here, we define a lipid-driven mechanism that governs host–pathogen interactions by impacting pathogen clearance and thus infection outcomes. Exploiting Drosophila , we show that enteric infection triggers robust accumulation of neutral lipids, and specifically 1,2-diacylglycerols (DAGs), in the midgut. Disruption of DAG biosynthesis or lipid transport in midgut enterocytes (ECs) impairs lipid accumulation and reduces host survival. Conversely, dietary lipid supplementation enhances lipid storage and improves survival. Mechanistically, these lipid-dependent responses regulate defecation, thereby controlling bacterial clearance from the midgut. DAGs can act as signaling lipids that activate protein kinase C (PKC), and DAG accumulation in ECs correlates with elevated PKC activity and calcium signaling in midgut visceral muscle (VM), promoting VM contraction, midgut motility, and expulsion of pathogens via defecation. Together, our findings reveal a previously unrecognized role for DAG metabolism in shaping host defenses.

abstract: Semantic processing relies on flexible interactions between specialized lexico-semantic regions and domain-general control networks, particularly under challenging conditions. Using transcranial magnetic stimulation interleaved with functional magnetic resonance imaging, we investigated acute network adaptation when the left posterior middle temporal gyrus—a core lexico-semantic region—was perturbed during lexico-semantic decisions in 25 healthy participants. High-intensity transcranial magnetic stimulation over the posterior middle temporal gyrus induced task-specific activity increases across semantic control and lexical retrieval areas, as well as remote domain-general regions. Critically, increased local activity at the stimulation site correlated with slower reaction times, whereas greater upregulation in domain-general frontal regions was associated with less disrupted semantic performance. These findings indicate that acute semantic disruption triggers immediate, flexible recruitment of domain-general control areas consistent with the maintenance of task performance, highlighting the brain’s capacity to dynamically adapt to interference. Our findings contribute to the current understanding of putative compensatory network-level mechanisms supporting lexico-semantic cognition.

abstract: The brain’s representations are encoded in the collective activity of neural populations whose non-monotonic tuning properties define the population code. Adaptive behavior calls for flexible retuning of this code as stimulus statistics change across contexts. Yet how such adaptation occurs is unknown. Using fMRI during a numerosity-estimation task with variable number ranges, we show that number representations in human parietal cortex dynamically recalibrate to context, enabling context-sensitive behavioral accuracy. The tuning properties of neural populations collectively shift and rescale with the range. This distributed range adaptation achieves efficient coding in real time: neural precision scales with the range and predicts corresponding changes in behavioral precision. Individuals with stronger neural adaptation show larger behavioral adjustments. These findings extend static sensory efficient coding to adaptive representations of abstract magnitudes. Such flexible population tuning may constitute a canonical mechanism of encoding networks that enables the brain to sustain precise, adaptive behavior.

abstract: Quantifying enzyme kinetic parameter changes upon mutations is essential for accelerating enzyme evolution. Current methods focus on predicting absolute values of kinetic parameters (turnover numbers k cat and Michaelis constants K m ), yet they fail to accurately capture mutation effects. To our knowledge, no method directly models mutation effects (Δ k cat and Δ K m ) due to the scarcity of such training data. Moreover, these methods haven’t fully exploited protein structural geometry. Here, we establish a high-quality enzyme mutation effect dataset by pairing wild-type and mutant kinetic parameters measured under identical experimental conditions via a semi-automatic procedure combining language model-assisted parsing and manual verification. Leveraging this dataset, we develop DeltaCata, a Siamese geometric graph neural network to directly predict the changes in kinetic parameters induced by residue substitutions. DeltaCata demonstrates substantial performance improvements over existing methods, especially for enzymes unseen in the training sets. Its utility is further validated through in silico beneficial mutation screening experiments using deep mutational scanning datasets. Finally, we apply DeltaCata to engineer the methyltransferase sGmOMT2, achieving up to a 7.0-fold improvement in catalytic efficiency for in vitro icaritin synthesis. These results suggest the high potential of DeltaCata for industrial enzyme engineering.

abstract: Affinity maturation is an essential process in antibody engineering. Although powerful, it is iterative, time-consuming, and can result in trade-offs, where affinity is gained at the cost of important properties, such as specificity and stability. We present a scalable strategy, called LAffAb, that starts from a crystallographic structure of the antibody-antigen complex and introduces combinations of mutations to the antibody to optimize the energy of the complex. A combinatorial library comprising 7000 variants with up to nine mutations results in gains of up to 30-fold in affinity while co-optimizing stability. Surprisingly, the library does not converge on a single solution, instead favoring diverse variants with a high mutational load. Small-scale screening of 10 designs against a potential drug target improves affinity by an order-of-magnitude while maintaining high developability. We also apply LAffAb to improve the developability of a therapeutic antibody while maintaining affinity. We envision that LAffAb can be used to design stable, specific, and high-affinity binders and to improve our understanding of sequence, structure, and function relationships in antibodies.

abstract: Understanding the behaviors of contractile actomyosin systems requires precise spatiotemporal control of filamentous myosin activity. Here, we develop a tool for optical control of contractility by extending the MyLOV family of gearshifting motors to create engineered filamentous myosins that change velocity in response to blue light. We characterize these minifilaments using in vitro single-molecule tracking assays, contractility assays in reconstituted actin networks, and imaging of contractile phenotypes in live cells. In vitro, gearshifting minifilaments change speed and/or direction when illuminated, and contraction rates of minifilaments in actin networks can be modulated using blue light. In cells, gearshifting minifilaments enable optical control of protrusion retraction, cortical flow, and cell migration. Finally, we develop an alternative design for minifilaments that only interact processively with actin in blue light. Engineered minifilaments could be used to dissect behaviors such as self-organization and mechanotransduction in contractile systems both in vitro and in cells and tissues.

abstract: Bidirectional promoters (BDPs), intergenic regions that coordinate transcription of oppositely oriented genes, pervade eukaryotic genomes, yet sequence signatures remain poorly defined. Existing approaches to BDP identification rely on distance thresholds and cannot infer activity from DNA. Here, we use Evo2, a genomic language model, to predict BDP activity and uncover sequence-encoded regulatory principles across four plant species ( Arabidopsis , maize, rice, and wheat). We stratify BDPs by co-expression strength and compare Evo2-derived embeddings against k -mer profiles, transcription factor binding site matrices, and convolutional neural networks trained on sequence. Evo2 embeddings outperform all baselines, demonstrating that genomic language models capture regulatory information underlying BDP activity. Models trained on one or multiple species transfer to held-out species, and in planta validation in Spartina alterniflora confirms predicted high-activity BDPs. Sparse autoencoder analysis links Evo2 embeddings to nucleosome positioning and species-specific transcription factor landscapes, providing insight into sequence determinants underlying BDP activity . This work establishes how genomic language models can extract bidirectional promoter logic from sequence and identify conserved regulatory rules across plants.

abstract: Differentiating arginine vasopressin (AVP) deficiency from primary polydipsia is challenging. The most accurate test, hypertonic saline–stimulated copeptin, requires intensive monitoring. Intravenous mannitol stimulates AVP release and may provide a simpler alternative. In a randomized double-blind crossover trial, 22 healthy adults received mannitol and placebo in random order, of whom 21 were included in the primary analysis. In a pilot study, 10 patients with AVP deficiency and 10 with primary polydipsia received mannitol. The primary outcome was copeptin after mannitol infusion. Mannitol resulted in a 2.29-fold higher copeptin at 90 minutes (+6.4 pmol/L (95% CI: +5.2, +7.7; p <0.001)) than after placebo at mean baseline copeptin levels in healthy adults. In patients, copeptin after 30 minutes was 11.7 pmol/L (95% CI: 6.5, 17.0) higher in primary polydipsia than in AVP deficiency. Mannitol infusion shows promise as a new diagnostic approach. Larger confirmatory studies are required to validate both the optimal diagnostic cut-off and patient safety. Trial Registration number: NCT06542198 .

abstract: Effective stress coping relies on neural and endocrine coordination, with the mesostriatal system serving as a central substrate. However, how striatal subregions contribute to stress vulnerability versus resilience remains unclear. Here, we show dissociable roles of the nucleus accumbens (NAC) and dorsal caudate (dCA) and their associated brain networks in shaping stress responses. We identify neural stability (NS)—capturing stress-induced changes in state-switching frequency over the course of stress responses—as a marker: task-state NS correlates positively with stress-related NAC activity, whereas resting-state NS correlates inversely with stress-related dCA activity. NAC-mediated networks and associated NS further predict faster cortisol recovery. Intriguingly, NAC-related functional connectivity patterns spatially covary with dopamine D 2 receptor distributions and gene expression in inhibitory neurons and glia, whereas dCA-related patterns covary with μ-opioid receptor distributions. Together, these findings reveal striatal subregional heterogeneity in stress coping and characterize resilience as a multisystem homeostatic process integrating neural, endocrine, and molecular layers.

abstract: Glucocorticoid-induced bone loss (GIBL) remains a major clinical challenge, manifested by both systemic osteopenia and osteonecrosis of the femoral head under chronic glucocorticoid exposure, yet current therapies are limited in coordinately addressing bone deterioration and vascular impairment. With advances in precision medicine, oligonucleotide therapeutics offer opportunities for pathophysiology-informed intervention. Here, we report a pathology-adapted peptide-oligonucleotide nanohybrid (PON) developed for targeted miR-26a-5p delivery to glucocorticoid-injured bone. By integrating self-assembly, bone targeting, enzyme responsiveness, cell penetration, and lysosomal escape, PONs were designed to incorporate pathology-responsive delivery features and address key barriers to oligonucleotide delivery. Mechanistically, PON-mediated miR-26a-5p delivery reduced GSK-3β expression and promoted HIF-1α stabilization, thereby preserving osteogenesis-angiogenesis coupling and attenuating apoptosis. In a rat model of GIBL, systemic PON administration protects against early skeletal and vascular injury and limits progression after disease establishment. These findings identify the therapeutic relevance of miR-26a-5p in GIBL, and support the potential of PON system for bone-targeted oligonucleotide therapy.

abstract: Musculoskeletal infections (MSIs), including fracture-related infections (FRIs) and periprosthetic joint infections (PJIs), remain difficult to treat because of biofilm formation and increasing antimicrobial resistance. Bacteriophage therapy (PT) has re-emerged as a promising adjunctive strategy, although prospective clinical evidence remains scarce. Here, we prospectively evaluated adjunctive local PT in 13 patients with refractory MSIs treated within the multidisciplinary PHAGEFORCE framework at University Hospitals Leuven (BE). Following surgery, personalized phage preparations were administered through a closed drain system for 8–10 days alongside systemic antibiotics. Clinical, microbiological, immunological, and genomic data were collected. Four patients with refractory MSIs lacking suitable phages served as a control cohort. Clinical remission was observed in nine of eleven evaluable phage-treated patients (82%), whereas all control patients experienced infection recurrence during follow-up. PT was well tolerated, with no serious adverse reactions or clinically meaningful toxicity. Local phage titers remained detectable throughout therapy despite interpatient variability. Serum-mediated phage neutralization was observed during and after PT, and longitudinal genomic monitoring revealed patient-specific phage dynamics, neither of which was clearly associated with clinical outcome. These findings demonstrate the feasibility and safety of standardized local PT and support further evaluation of this approach in controlled clinical trials.

abstract: Resident cardiac macrophages (RCM) are essential for myocardial repair following acute myocardial infarction (AMI); however, their therapeutic application is hindered by limited availability. Here, we show that RCM transplantation from healthy mice markedly attenuates cardiac injury in mice. Importantly, we identify a pro-reparative CD301b⁺ RCM population profoundly depleted after AMI and show that adoptive transfer of this subset alone mitigates cardiac injury following myocardial infarction. To overcome the scarcity of native RCMs and favour their replenishment, we expand ex vivo a CD301b + macrophage-like population (RCML) by polarizing bone marrow-derived macrophages with an ILC2-derived cytokine cocktail, and show that RCML transplantation confers robust post-AMI cardioprotection. Mechanistically, CD301b promotes efferocytosis by enhancing TFEB-mediated lysosomal function via a GATM-AMPK-mTOR axis, a pathway conserved in human macrophages. Thus, our findings identify a key pro-reparative macrophage subset and establish a feasible cell-based strategy for cardiac repair.

abstract: Non-human primates like rhesus macaques are pivotal models for decoding human visual cortex physiology and disorders. However, there is a lack of high-resolution transcriptomic atlases comparing distinct areas of the visual cortex in macaque. Here, we developed BrainSPACE, an innovative pipeline for rapid and precise brain tissue banking, to sample visual cortex areas: V1, V2, V4, MT, and TEO. We applied single-nucleus RNA-sequencing (snRNA-seq) to unravel neuronal diversity in BrainSPACE-banked V1 and V4 areas ( ~ 100,000 nuclei). We uncovered conserved GABAergic neuron profiles but stark area-specific diversity in principal neurons, featuring seven unique layer 4 subtypes in V1 and one in V4. Complementary smFISH validated transcriptional gradients across these areas, aligning with ventral and dorsal stream hierarchies. Gene ontology analyses highlighted plasticity-related pathways in unique layer 4 subtypes, with genes like NTNG1 and NLGN1 linked to neurodevelopmental disorders such as autism and schizophrenia. Our insights bridge molecular architecture to visual processing, offering an interactive atlas for community use. By revealing how layer 4 heterogeneity drives hierarchical specialization, our work advances primate brain mapping and informs therapeutic strategies for vision-related pathologies.

abstract: The modular architecture of multi-domain enzymes is a key source of functional diversity. GH18 chitinases exemplify this, possessing a variety of auxiliary domains that have been postulated to underpin their role as essential global nutrient cyclers. However, there is no evolutionary framework that accounts for the vast assortment of domain compositions observed across the protein family. Here, we map the sequence space of prokaryotic chitinases, integrating phylogenetics with a quantitative analysis of domain promiscuity to decode their evolutionary history. We reveal that diversification follows distinct trajectories: enzymes necessary for environmental chitin scavenging evolve via high modular plasticity and structural elaboration of the catalytic core, whereas sequences required for specialized, essential developmental roles fix their domain architecture to fulfil lineage-specific physiological roles. By resolving how domain accretion co-evolves with catalytic scaffolds, this work provides a framework for understanding how multi-domain enzymes adapt to complex environments.

abstract: Equine rhinitis A virus (ERAV), a picornavirus closely related to foot-and-mouth disease virus, causes respiratory infections in horses. We performed a HEK293T CRISPRi screen and identified integrin α2β1 as a protein receptor for ERAV. Using knock-out cells and pretreating cells with an antibody or soluble receptor, we confirmed the importance of this integrin for infection of multiple cell types, including equine fibroblasts. Cryo-EM and glycoproteomics analyses revealed that ERAV binds integrin α2β1 in its closed conformation by attaching to the β-propeller of the α2 chain, independent of divalent cations, as well as to a high-mannose glycan on α2 N112 and a sialylated glycan on β1 N269. Using glycan knockout and knock-in cells and by reconstituting integrin α2β1-depleted cells with mutant receptors, we demonstrated the importance of these glycans for virus entry. Our results identify a hitherto unseen combination of protein and glycan interactions between a virus and its receptor.

abstract: Autonomous sensors and machine learning are transforming ecology by enabling large-scale observation of organisms and ecosystems. However, camera traps, audio recorders and other sensors currently produce species-level detections. Tracking individuals continues to require invasive, high-effort capture–mark–recapture. Here we introduce an automated, general approach that identifies individual animals in passive acoustic recordings based on individually distinctive vocalizations. We train a convolutional neural network to extract salient features from audio recordings using a location-prediction task, then apply dimensionality reduction and clustering on features to achieve song-based individual identification. We identify individuals not included in the training data with 96% accuracy. We apply this approach to track 405 male ovenbirds ( Seiurus aurocapilla ) from 126 locations across 4 years, then model abundance and apparent survival. We provide open-source code to facilitate applications of our approach to other species. Performing automated individual identification on passive acoustic datasets will support the study of population trajectories and inform proactive ecosystem management to prevent biodiversity loss.

abstract: Spatial multi-omic technologies measure multiple molecular layers within intact tissues. Two central challenges are vertical integration, which combines different molecular modalities, and horizontal integration, which aligns cell types across studies. Here we show domain invariant representation through adaptive calibration (DIRAC), a geometric deep learning model that unifies these tasks in a generalized domain adaptation framework. DIRAC learns task-discriminative features that are insensitive to domain shifts caused by batch effects, omic modalities or study sites, enabling a shared embedding space and automated cell-type annotation through label transfer from reference datasets. Across sequencing-based and imaging-based datasets, DIRAC identified a new microvascular proliferation domain in glioblastoma, corrected cortical-layer annotations in severe Alzheimer’s disease, resolved subtle structures in mouse embryos and remained robust to missing data and unseen cell types. We generated mouse spleen and thymus Stereo-CITE-seq data and used DIRAC to reveal thymic T cell migration and splenic immune cell interactions. DIRAC is fast and scales to millions of cells.

abstract: Advances in single-cell sequencing and spatial omics technologies have enhanced our understanding of diverse cellular identities, compositions, architectures and functions. However, the single-cell three-dimensional (3D) organization of the epigenome is still not well understood, due to an absence of spatial single-cell methods that allow high-resolution, locus-specific detection of combinations of epigenetic marks while maintaining 3D genome organization. Here we develop epigenetic proximity hybridization reaction (Epi-PHR), a nondisruptive image-based single-cell spatial epigenetic profiling technology. Epi-PHR detects combinations of epigenetic marks in situ at hundreds of gene targets within single cells while preserving 3D genome organization. Phased Epi-PHR combined with chromatin tracing reveals unexpected associations between epigenetic mark enrichment and chromatin folding of an imprinted gene cluster at the single-chromatin-copy level for the distinct alleles from different parental origins. We expect Epi-PHR will be broadly applicable in research requiring single-cell spatial epigenetic information, advancing our understanding of the combinatorial epigenetic code and its relationship with chromatin organization.

abstract: Understanding the subcellular localization of RNAs is critical for their functions, but visualizing circular RNAs (circRNAs) has been hindered by their sequence overlap with linear counterparts. Here we developed amplicon-based circRNA fluorescence in situ hybridization (abcFISH), which uses an optimized rolling-circle amplification strategy targeting back-splicing junction sites for robust, high specificity, single-molecule circRNA imaging. abcFISH enables quantitative, multiplexed imaging in cells and tissues, allowing us to reveal alternative circularization patterns from the single locus, uncover cell-type-specific circRNA expression linked to combinatorial effects of RNA-binding proteins, map distinct spatial distribution patterns of circRNAs in neurons and brain tissues, and show functional colocalization of circRNA Cdr1as and long noncoding RNA Cyrano. We further applied abcFISH to validate therapeutic double-stranded circRNA aptamers, simultaneously visualizing AAV-delivered double-stranded circRNA aptamers and the resulting reduction in astrocyte infiltration around transduced cells. Collectively, abcFISH provides a robust, user-friendly toolkit for deciphering circRNA localization and function in vivo.

title: Opposing excitatory and inhibitory synaptic pathologies drive ZC4H2-associated intellectual disability.
abstract: Understanding genotype-phenotype correlations is critical for precision medicine, yet patients carrying mutations in the same gene are often classified under one disorder and treated alike, despite potentially opposite responses to therapy. ZC4H2-associated rare disorder (ZARD) is an X-linked neurodevelopmental condition caused by diverse mutations across ZC4H2. Here, we show that distinct ZC4H2 mutations drive intellectual disability through opposing synaptic mechanisms. The gain-of-function mutation ZC4H2L66H enhances GABAA receptor (GABAAR) degradation, impairing inhibitory synaptic transmission and plasticity. By contrast, the loss-of-function mutation ZC4H2R213W increases AMPA receptor (AMPAR) stability and dysregulates excitatory synaptic activity. Despite these diametrically opposed synaptic pathologies, ZC4H2L66H/y and ZC4H2R213W/y knockin mice exhibit comparable cognitive deficits. Importantly, muscimol, a GABAAR agonist, specifically rescues deficits in ZC4H2L66H/y mice, whereas the AMPAR antagonist perampanel rescues ZC4H2R213W/y mice. These findings demonstrate that opposing synaptic etiologies can underlie a single genetic disorder and highlight pathomechanism-based stratification for targeted therapeutic strategies.

title: A computational framework to model cartilage degeneration induced by mechanoinflammation and cytokine-driven inflammation in post-traumatic osteoarthritis.
abstract: Knee joint injury is a major risk factor for post-traumatic osteoarthritis (PTOA), often associated with early cartilage degeneration. Mechanical overloading and cytokine-driven inflammation are key drivers of this process, yet the underlying mechanisms and their distinct temporal and spatial contributions to cartilage degradation remain unclear. Here, we present a mechanobiological finite element framework that simulates cartilage degradation through cell-mediated proteolytic activity triggered by injurious loading-driven mechanoinflammation and cytokine-driven inflammation. The model reproduces experimentally observed depth-dependent loss of collagen and aggrecan, with mechanoinflammation inducing a transient response and cytokine-driven inflammation sustaining prolonged matrix degradation. Sensitivity analysis further shows that mechanoinflammation-driven degradation is governed mainly by protease production per cell, whereas cytokine-driven degradation is more sensitive to the rate of cellular stimulation. Together, this framework provides a mechanistic basis to study proteolytic cartilage degeneration and supports future in silico evaluation of therapeutic strategies aimed at mitigating cartilage degradation in PTOA.

title: A lightweight vision-based framework for automated aero-engine blade damage inspection.
abstract: Automated visual inspection of aero-engine blades is central to aviation safety, yet it is challenged by damage that is small and low-contrast against a strongly textured metal surface, and by the need for models that are light enough for edge deployment. This paper presents a lightweight vision-based framework for automated blade damage inspection. Rather than assembling independent detection modules, the framework is organized as a three-stage inspection pipeline: (1) a multi-scale feature-discrimination stage (MSBlock) captures defects across a wide size range at negligible computational cost; (2) a texture-suppression stage (TSA) filters high-frequency machining-background noise through product-based channel-spatial attention, exposing genuine defects; and (3) an efficient-prediction stage (Detect_Efficient) fuses cross-scale features and recalibrates confidence with roughly half the parameters of a standard head. On a self-built engine-blade dataset, the framework improves recall, F1-score, and mAP@0.5 by 4.8, 1.9, and 0.8 percentage points over YOLOv11n (reaching 92.0%, 91.6%, and 94.2%), while cutting parameters and computation by 50.0% and 58.7% and reaching 527 FPS. It also outperforms YOLOv8n, YOLOv9t, and YOLOv10n in recall and F1-score, confirming its suitability for real-time edge-based blade inspection.

title: A pretreatment ECM-high/immune-low transcriptomic score is associated with pathological complete response after neoadjuvant therapy in breast cancer.
abstract: In this retrospective public-cohort observational study, we evaluated a biologically motivated extracellular matrix (ECM)-high/immune-low transcriptomic score for association with pathological complete response (pCR) after neoadjuvant therapy in breast cancer. The score contrasted standardized ECM/fibroblast and immune-response components. Cohort-specific logistic models adjusted for available clinical covariates; their performance was evaluated separately and was not validation of a locked transported model. In I-SPY2/GSE194040 (n = 987; 319 pCR events), a one-standard-deviation higher score was associated with lower pCR odds (odds ratio [OR] 0.687, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.588-0.803). Inverse adjusted estimates were also observed in GSE25066 (OR 0.744, 95% CI 0.568-0.975) and GSE20271 (OR 0.407, 95% CI 0.232-0.715). Apparent areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) for these multivariable models were 0.750, 0.732 and 0.798; corresponding 500-bootstrap optimism-corrected estimates were 0.731, 0.713 and 0.765, conditional on processed scores. GSE20194 estimates were nonsignificant, and substantial record overlap with GSE25066 prevented interpretation as additional independent confirmation. A GSE25066 sensitivity restricted to deposited human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-negative status retained direction but had a confidence interval crossing unity. Higher scores correlated with lower immune-related reverse-phase protein array signals in matched I-SPY2 samples. The findings support a hypothesis-generating bulk-transcriptomic response association, with limited cross-cohort robustness. Heterogeneous treatment, sampling, assay and endpoint annotations, together with absent spatial and prospective validation, preclude claims of causality or clinical treatment-selection utility.

title: Amplified MS2 labeling reveals heterogeneous dynamics of RNA granules in the live murine brain ex vivo.
abstract: Dynamics of messenger ribonucleic acids (mRNAs) and the complexes with associated proteins (RNPs), also known as RNA granules, provide post-transcriptional control of gene expression. This regulation is crucial for cell-type diversity and activity-dependent plasticity of the mammalian central nervous system (CNS). However, elucidating the physiological significance of RNA granules has been hampered by technical difficulties to probe them in live brain. Here, we describe a novel method to visualize RNA granules in native CNS tissues of mouse. To amplify the fluorescence signal from single mRNAs incorporating MS2 stem loops, MS2 capsid protein (MCP) was conjugated with 4 tandem superfolder green fluorescent proteins (sfGFPs). Using MCP-4 × sfGFP, significantly more RNPs could be detected in the fresh acute brain slices than with MCP-GFP. Amplified MS2 signal could visualize Actb mRNAs in specific cells, either driven by promoter or via Cre-dependent expression, revealing remarkably distinct localization and movements of RNPs across different CNS cell types, including neurons and glial cells. The highly sensitive live-tissue RNA imaging could be useful for investigating the regulation of the dynamics of RNA granules in the native niche, ultimately in naive and diseased animal models.

title: An adaptive energy management and control framework for long-endurance UAV missions in dynamic environments: A reproducible simulation study.
abstract: Long-endurance uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) missions are limited by onboard energy, and hybrid battery/fuel-cell systems increasingly extend flight time. Prior work largely treats power-source allocation and flight-path planning as separate problems, which can strand one energy source while the other is still available. This paper proposes an Adaptive Energy Management and Control Framework (AEMCF): a nonlinear, wind-compensating guidance law that sets heading and airspeed, coupled to a receding-horizon quadratic program (QP), solved every control step, that allocates power between a battery and a fuel cell using an equivalent-consumption principle so that neither energy source is exhausted while the other still has capacity. We implement the full model in an open, reproducible simulation (UAV point-mass dynamics, a stochastic wind-gust process, a battery state-of-charge model, a load-dependent fuel-cell efficiency curve) and evaluate it against two baselines: a fixed 50/50 power split, and a static equivalent-consumption split computed once before flight. Across 50 Monte Carlo wind realisations, AEMCF achieves a mean endurance of 124.6 minutes, versus 108.0 for the fixed-split baseline and 123.4 for the static offline split; AEMCF and the static split both consume close to 100% of the true onboard energy budget, whereas the fixed split strands roughly 16% unused. This resource-balancing advantage is robust, holding under harsher wind (30 seeds) and realistic sensor bias and noise (20 seeds). The online controller's further, smaller advantage over the static split is less robust: it does not grow under harsher wind, and does not survive the sensor imperfections tested, indicating AEMCF's principal contribution is the power-balancing objective itself rather than wind-aware guidance specifically. We report this honestly, including where it complicates the original motivation for the wind-compensating layer, and identify state estimation as a concrete next step for recovering it. All simulation code and results are openly available and run end-to-end without modification.

title: An explainable machine learning framework for cross-dataset chronic kidney disease risk prediction using hybrid data balancing.
abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a major global health problem, and early detection is important for reducing complications and improving treatment. Machine learning has shown strong potential for CKD prediction, but many existing studies rely on single datasets, face severe class imbalance, and provide limited interpretability. These challenges reduce model reliability and make cross-dataset use in real clinical settings more difficult. Therefore, this study aimed to develop an interpretable and adaptable machine learning framework for CKD risk prediction across different datasets. The proposed hybrid explainable machine learning (HXAI-ML) framework used two public CKD datasets: the UCI CKD Risk Factor Prediction dataset as the source dataset and the Kaggle CKD dataset as the target dataset. After preprocessing, label binarization, imputation, and standard scaling, seven balancing methods and six classifiers were evaluated. A target adaptation setting was applied by using 10% of the target dataset for calibration and 90% for blind testing. SHAP, LIME, and Permutation Importance Analysis were used to explain the model predictions. Among all tested combinations, RO + TL + ETC achieved the highest overall accuracy among the evaluated target-domain adaptation configurations and was therefore selected as the primary model under the accuracy-based selection criterion. On the 1,494-sample blind holdout it obtained 91.97% accuracy, 92.24% precision, 99.64% recall, 95.80% F1-score, and 67.52% ROC-AUC. However, its specificity of 5.74% and balanced accuracy of 52.69% indicate substantial class-wise imbalance in predictive performance. The findings demonstrate the methodological feasibility of cross-dataset target-domain adaptation and explainable machine learning under limited target-domain data. However, the relatively low ROC-AUC values and low specificity for the non-CKD class indicate limited discriminative ability. Therefore, the proposed framework should be regarded as an exploratory cross-dataset evaluation rather than a clinically deployable screening or decision-support system.

title: Antimicrobial-resistant Salmonella and Escherichia coli in fresh vegetables from Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso: Prevalence, β-lactamase genes, and food safety implications.
abstract: Fresh vegetables consumed raw are a recognized but underappreciated vehicle for foodborne pathogens and antimicrobial-resistant (AMR) bacteria, yet data on AMR determinants in fresh produce remain scarce for West Africa. This cross-sectional study characterized the prevalence of Escherichia coli and Salmonella spp. in 300 fresh vegetable samples from farms, markets, restaurants, and supermarkets in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso, along with their antimicrobial resistance profiles, selected β-lactamase genes, and associated food-handling risk factors. E. coli was detected in 63.0% of samples (95% CI: 57.4-68.3%) and Salmonella spp. in 10.0% (95% CI: 6.9-13.9%). Prevalence did not differ significantly by season for either species (E. coli: 61.3% dry season vs 64.7% rainy season, χ²(1) = 0.36, p = 0.55; Salmonella: 8.0% vs 12.0%, χ²(1) = 1.33, p = 0.25). Per-agent resistance rates were likewise broadly similar between seasons for both species (e.g., Salmonella tetracycline resistance 23.3% dry vs 26.7% rainy). Salmonella isolates showed higher resistance for several individual agents than E. coli isolates, most notably tetracycline (25.0% vs 15.3%) and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (21.7% vs 12.8%; see Table 1). Multidrug resistance (non-susceptibility to ≥ 3 antimicrobial classes) was observed in 60% of resistant Salmonella isolates. Among eight resistant isolates screened by multiplex polymerase chain reaction (four E. coli and four Salmonella, selected to represent the range of resistance phenotypes observed), blaTEM was detected in 100% (8/8), blaOXA in 50.0% (4/8), and blaCTX-M in 50.0% (4/8), with co-occurrence of all three genes in 37.5% (3/8) of isolates. The detection of the extended-spectrum β-lactamase-associated blaCTX-M gene provides new surveillance data on vegetable-associated bacteria in Burkina Faso, an environmental compartment not previously included in national AMR monitoring. Risky food-handling practices were widespread: 98% of vendors stored vegetables at ambient temperature, 85% applied no disinfection, and 80% of settings presented cross-contamination risk with raw meat. A screening-level model yielded an indicative 2.0% exposure-risk estimate for antibiotic-resistant Salmonella per raw salad serving; this is a screening-level indicator rather than a confirmed infection probability (see Methods). A HACCP-based control framework with five critical control points is proposed as a preliminary, field-validation-pending tool. These findings support the integration of fresh produce into One Health antimicrobial resistance surveillance strategies in West Africa.

title: Antiviral activity of Rumex crispus extract and its bioactive constituent emodin against human coronavirus OC43.
abstract: Coronaviruses are responsible for diseases ranging from mild respiratory symptoms to severe infections such as COVID-19. Despite the availability of vaccines and therapeutic agents, the emergence of new variants and drug-resistant strains highlights the need for additional antiviral strategies. In this study, Rumex crispus was investigated as a potential source of antiviral compounds. The ethanol (EtOH) extract of R. crispus roots was prepared and subsequently fractionated into n-hexane (n-hex), ethyl acetate (EA), and aqueous fractions. Among these, the n-hexane and EA fractions exhibited significant antiviral activity against human coronavirus OC43, as demonstrated by Western blot, qRT-PCR, and plaque assays. Chemical analysis of the extract by HPLC led to the identification of epicatechin, naphthalene derivatives, and anthraquinones. Notably, emodin, an anthraquinone, showed pronounced antiviral activity, and was found to be enriched in the active n-hexane and EA fractions. These findings suggest that emodin may contribute to the antiviral activity of R. crispus extract, although the potential involvement of other bioactive constituents cannot be excluded.

title: Assessment of algorithmic performance in PET-CT segmentation of solitary lung tumors.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: PET-CT (Positron emission tomography-computed tomography), a nuclear medicine imaging technique is preferably used for lung tumor detection. However, manual image analysis may be time-consuming. To enhance efficiency, many automated segmentation algorithms have been developed. This study aims to develop a radiomics agreement-based method to evaluate segmentation algorithms and to compare the performance of two deep learning-based algorithms nnU-Net (No-new-net Convolutional Neural Network) and RECOMIA (Research Consortium for Medical Image Analysis Lung Cancer "Lung Cancer FDG-PET/CT v1.5") for PET-CT solitary lung tumor segmentation.
METHODS AND RESULTS: PET-CT images of 221 patients at the University of Debrecen's Hospital were collected and anonymized. The predictions of segmented lung tumors done by nnU-Net and RECOMIA were compared with the manual segmented masks via Wilcoxon signed-rank test and Pearson correlation values, based on eight groups of radiomics parameters calculated by PyRadiomics software. The combined p-values were calculated using Brown's method, which were 0.481 and < 0.001 for nnU-Net and RECOMIA, respectively. The absolute values of correlation were summed, which were 37.259 and 16.358 for nnU-Net and RECOMIA, respectively. Altogether, RECOMIA shows statistically greater differences, therefore, it performs worse than nnU-Net does. Statistical analyses with Intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), Multivariate analysis of variance (MANOVA) and follow up pairwise t-test further confirmed stronger agreement between extracted radiomics features from nnU-Net predicted masks and manual masks than RECOMIA and manual masks, which validated the proposed comparison method.
CONCLUSION: The superior performance of nnU-Net highlights the importance of training data alignment and model adaptability in achieving accurate and reliable segmentation in medical imaging. However, nnU-Net requirements for training and extra computational demands may limit its application in some clinical environments. Despite lower accuracy, RECOMIA remains valuable because of its efficiency and intuitiveness. These findings provide valuable guidance for selecting segmentation algorithms in real-world clinical and research settings.

title: Can the exposome help solve the alcohol and cancer mystery?
abstract: Alcohol consumption is a preventable driver of many cancers, yet a central biological question remains unresolved: by what mechanisms does ethanol promote malignancy? We propose that alcohol in the context of the exposome (i.e., the network of chemical, biological, and social determinants that interact with ethanol across the life span) provides a unifying framework for understanding alcohol-related carcinogenesis. Viewed through the lens of the exposome, alcohol is not only as a direct carcinogen but also as a systemic amplifier of environmental risk acting across multiple levels of biological organization, from molecular damage to whole-body physiology. This reframing has important implications for mechanistic research, precision prevention, and public-health policy.

title: Clinical outcomes in various coronary artery bypass grafting techniques: A systematic review and network meta-analysis.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: There are different coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) techniques, conventional (C-CABG), minimally invasive (MI-CABG), and robotic (R-CABG), each with its respective advantages and drawbacks. This study aimed to compare all three techniques and their nine sub-technique variations to provide a reference for the clinical selection of the most suitable surgical approach.
METHODS: A systematic search was applied to seven databases to find observational studies or randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that compared outcomes between CABG techniques in patients. Critical appraisal of observational studies (Newcastle-Ottawa Scale) and RCTs (Cochrane Risk of Bias 2.0) was performed. We used frequentist network meta-analysis to rank and analyze the pooled odds ratios and mean differences of each intervention. Primary outcomes were mortality and complete revascularization, while the rest were secondary outcomes. The protocol was registered with the ID CRD42023480325.
RESULTS: A total of 132 studies with 779,773 patients were included. All three techniques were associated with comparable revascularization rates. However, in the comparison of the nine sub-techniques port access (PA)-CABG was associated with a significantly higher rate compared to C-ONCAB. R-CABG demonstrated the most favorable outcomes in terms of ICU stay, overall hospital stay, mortality, and ventilation time compared to MI-CABG and C-CABG. Additionally, R-CABG was associated with lower rates of wound infection, cerebrovascular accident, and renal failure. Both R-CABG and MI-CABG were associated with lower rates of non-sinus rhythm compared to C-CABG. While MI-CABG was associated with the highest reoperation rate.
CONCLUSION: R-CABG suggested promising outcomes over MI-CABG and C-CABG. However, as this exploratory NMA was predominantly based on observational data, these findings should be regarded as a hypothesis-generating framework for future research. Clinicians should interpret results cautiously, prioritizing patient-specific factors and institutional experience until higher-level evidence emerges.

title: Clinical supervision in public hospitals in Lesotho: Nurse managers' support for registered nurses.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clinical supervision is regarded as essential for nurse managers in diverse healthcare settings to enhance nurse satisfaction, competence, and retention, leading to improved nursing care quality. The study aimed to explore and describe nurse managers' support provided to registered nurses during clinical supervision at public hospitals in Lesotho.
METHODS: The study employed an exploratory descriptive qualitative research design to explore and describe the support provided to registered nurses during clinical supervision. Data was gathered through eight in-depth individual face-to-face interviews with participants purposefully selected from the public hospitals in Lesotho. Face-to-face interviews were recorded and transcribed verbatim for analysis. Data was analyzed by the researcher and the co-coder using thematic analysis as proposed by Braun and Clarke.
RESULTS: Three themes emerged from the data; namely: nurse managers' supervisory dimensions to facilitate healthcare quality, nurse managers' supervisory practices to capacitate and support registered nurses and nurse managers' challenges with clinical supervision. The findings indicate that nurse managers provide structural support to registered nurses, apply various supervisory methods and processes, and supervise nursing practices in ways that relate to patient care outcomes during clinical supervision.
CONCLUSION: Nurse managers guide registered nurses through performance monitoring, quality assurance, and resource supervision to uphold standards and policies. Supervision of registered nurses also support skill development, conflict management, and psycho-social well-being. However, challenges include addressing registered nurses' attitudes, managing skill gaps, and overcoming nurse managers' own knowledge limitations.

title: Clinicopathologic characteristics and survival outcomes of gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms in Peru: A 15-year retrospective cohort study.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Incidence of gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms (GEP-NENs) has increased globally; however, data from Latin America remain scarce. This study aimed to describe the sociodemographic and clinicopathologic characteristics, treatment modalities, survival outcomes, and prognostic factors of GEP-NENs in a 15-year single-center cohort at a national referral cancer center in Lima, Peru.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, hospital-based cohort study. Patients diagnosed with GEP-NENs at the Instituto Nacional de Enfermedades Neoplásicas (INEN) were included from 2009 to 2024, and tumors were classified according to the 2019 WHO Classification of GEP-NENs. Overall survival (OS) was estimated using Kaplan-Meier curves and compared using the log-rank test. Prognostic factors were identified through Cox proportional hazards models.
RESULTS: Three hundred sixty-eight patients were included. The median age at diagnosis was 57 years, with a female predominance (56.2%). Most patients presented with an ECOG performance status of 0-1 (96.5%), and among patients with available disease-extent information, 64.7% had non-metastatic disease. The majority of tumors were well-differentiated (neuroendocrine tumors [NETs]) (84.2%), while 15.8% were poorly differentiated (neuroendocrine carcinomas [NECs]). The most common primary tumor sites included the rectum (39.1%), stomach (19.8%), and pancreas (18.8%). With a median follow-up of 61.9 months, the 5-year OS rate was 52%. NETs exhibited longer OS than NECs, with 5-year OS rates of 65% and 8%, respectively (log-rank p < 0.001). In the multivariable analysis, metastatic disease (aHR = 2.61, 95% CI: 1.63-4.20; p < 0.001) and poorly differentiated histology (aHR: 4.36, 95% CI: 2.59-7.31; p < 0.001) were independently associated with worse overall survival, whereas surgery (aHR: 0.25, 95% CI: 0.15-0.41; p < 0.001) and systemic treatment (aHR: 0.53, 95% CI: 0.31-0.92; p = 0.024) were associated with improved overall survival.
CONCLUSION: Our findings demonstrate that GEP-NENs represent a highly heterogeneous group of neoplasms with substantial variability in clinicopathological characteristics and survival outcomes. Most patients in our cohort had well-differentiated NETs and favorable long-term survival. These findings support the need for comprehensive national registries and multicenter collaborative studies to validate our results and better characterize GEP-NENs in underrepresented Latin American populations.

title: Co-designing physical activity intervention in Danish kindergartens: A design-based research approach.
abstract: Physical activity in early childhood supports health, psychosocial development, and motor competence, yet many Danish kindergarten children do not meet recommended activity levels. Early childhood settings are therefore key health promotion environments where routines, pedagogical practices, and staff competencies shape children's access to daily physical activity. This study examines how a kindergarten-based intervention can be co-designed to strengthen physical activity by equipping pedagogical staff and supporting enabling environments through participatory, practice-embedded processes using a design-based research approach. Five Danish kindergartens participated in a one-year development phase guided by a complex intervention framework. The process included four iterative domains: context analysis, laboratory work, design experiments, and reflection. Data from observations, interviews, workshops, and prototype testing were analyzed thematically. The co-design process resulted in six elements: active group time with PA prompts; a play catalog with pedagogical cues; a key ring with pedagogical prompts; structured playground activities; designated PA Agents; and a competence development program. Six themes informed the design: Physical activity as an overlooked pedagogical resource; variation in children's physical activity competences; the role of leadership in cultural change; pedagogical staff's bodily engagement; pedagogical judgment as a driving force, and; competence development as an adoption strategy. The process produced a contextually grounded and professionally owned intervention. By strengthening local capacity, ownership, and equitable access to physical activity, the co-design approach supports health promotion embedded in every day kindergarten practice and informs future feasibility testing.
