title: Community-based delivery of lifesaving maternal and newborn health interventions in vulnerable Ethiopian communities: Lessons from implementation research.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: In Ethiopia, women in remote agrarian and pastoralist regions face major barriers to accessing timely, quality maternal and newborn health (MNH) services, leading to high rates of home births and preventable mortality. This study assessed the implementation of the Village Health Leader (VHL)-led community-based MNH package in vulnerable agrarian and pastoralist communities in Ethiopia.
METHODS: Implementation research deploying a mixed-methods process evaluation across seven health centers and 38 vulnerable communities in the Afar, Somali, and Oromia regions was carried out from December 2023 to July 2025. VHLs were trained to deliver community-based MNH interventions that included misoprostol for the prevention of postpartum hemorrhage, chlorhexidine for umbilical cord care, iron-folic acid for the prevention of anemia, and postpartum family planning counseling and services. Quantitative program monitoring data were collected from 3,980 pregnant women and analyzed descriptively. Qualitative data were collected through 90 in-depth interviews and 14 focus group discussions with VHLs, health workers, postpartum women, community members, and supervisors. Qualitative data were coded in ATLAS.ti using both deductive and inductive approaches. Findings from the quantitative and qualitative components were integrated to provide a comprehensive assessment of implementation.
RESULTS: The intervention reached about 4,000 pregnant women, with high rates of uptake for lifesaving MNH services. Among women who gave birth, 35% delivered at home, 92% used misoprostol, and almost all applied chlorhexidine to the umbilical cord stump. Qualitative findings indicated generally positive perceptions of the intervention and highlighted its acceptability and feasibility. VHLs demonstrated strong adherence to protocols and timely referrals to health facilities. Challenges included supply shortages, lack of incentives for VHLs, and weak referral feedback systems. Despite these constraints, the intervention improved access, enhanced equity, and did not disincentivize facility-based deliveries.
CONCLUSIONS: Community-based delivery of lifesaving MNH interventions by VHLs is both feasible and acceptable in most underserved communities. The model strengthens the primary health care system by extending its reach, improving the continuum of care, and addressing persistent access barriers. However, sustainability requires reliable supply chains and tailored approaches for pastoralist populations. The findings support the integration of trained community volunteers into national MNH service delivery strategies to reduce preventable maternal and newborn deaths.

title: Comparative outcomes of endovascular versus synthetic bypass for isolated superficial femoral artery lesions: A 3-year single-center cohort study.
abstract: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) ranges from intermittent claudication to critical limb‑threatening ischemia (CLTI), with <3% of intermittent claudication cases progressing to CLTI. This study aimed to compare the outcomes of percutaneous transluminal angioplasty with stenting (PTAS) and synthetic graft femoropopliteal bypass (FPB) in a homogeneous PAD cohort. A subgroup analysis of TransAtlantic Inter-Society Consensus (TASC) B and C lesions, which lack standardized treatment algorithms, was also performed. We retrospectively analyzed 88 patients with no prior history of vascular interventions in the same limb who were treated for isolated superficial femoral artery lesions between 2016 and 2020 (29 underwent PTAS and 59 underwent FPB). Primary outcomes were reintervention, limb amputation, mortality, and vessel patency (primary, assisted primary, and secondary) over a 3‑year follow‑up. Subgroup analysis was performed to assess differences in treatment outcomes. No statistically significant differences were detected in reintervention, limb amputation, mortality, or patency between the two treatments. For loss of primary patency, the hazard ratio (HR) for FPB versus PTAS was 1.89 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.76-4.69; log-rank p = 0.146) and 1.23 (95% CI, 0.45-3.38) after adjustment for lesion length and TASC grade. In the TASC B and C subgroup, no significant differences were observed in primary, assisted primary, or secondary patency (log-rank p = 0.809, 0.302, and 0.135, respectively). The study was underpowered to detect modest effects (post-hoc power for primary patency, 34.4%). In this small single-center cohort, no statistically significant difference in 3-year outcomes was detected between PTAS and FPB for isolated superficial femoral artery lesions; clinically meaningful differences cannot be excluded, and the findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating.

title: Comparing attenuation parameter and liver stiffness measurement using Hepatus and Fibroscan for the evaluation of steatosis and fibrosis in patients with chronic liver disease: A prospective study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: There are limited studies comparing Hepatus (HP), a novel visual transient elastography device with Fibroscan (FS), one of the most studied and validated non-invasive tests in the field of hepatology.
METHODOLOGY: HP and FS examinations were performed on patients with chronic liver disease by two operators, healthcare providers from different background, twice on each patient, at two different time points, independent of each other.
RESULTS: The data for 158 patients with 1264 examinations was analysed. There was moderate to strong correlation for attenuation parameter (Spearman's rho 0.67, p < 0.001) and liver stiffness measurement (LSM) (Spearman's rho 0.74, p < 0.001) obtained using the two devices. The mean difference (95% limits of agreement) in measurements was 15 (-69-99) dB/m for attenuation parameter and 1.2 (-5.0-7.2) kPa for LSM. There was fair to moderate agreement for diagnosis of steatosis grade >S0, > S1 and >S2 and substantial agreement for diagnosis of unlikely and likely compensated advanced chronic liver disease. The interquartile range (IQR) for attenuation parameter and IQR/median for LSM were lower for HP compared with FS (12 dB/m vs 33 dB/m, p < 0.001, and 13% vs 14%, p < 0.001, respectively). The intra- and inter-observer reliability using both devices were good to excellent with intraclass correlation coefficients of 0.86-0.97. Subgroup analyses demonstrated that agreement between HP and FS was maintained across obese and non-obese patients as well as patients with viral hepatitis and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. HP had shorter examination time (43 s vs 62 s, p < 0.001) and fewer invalid measurements (0 vs 1, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: HP demonstrated good comparability and reproducibility with FS for the assessment of hepatic steatosis and fibrosis, with shorter examination time and fewer invalid measurements.

title: Cost-effectiveness of atosiban versus placebo for threatened preterm birth (APOSTEL 8 trial).
abstract:
BACKGROUND: To assess the cost-effectiveness of treatment with atosiban compared to placebo for threatened preterm birth from 30+0 to 33+6 weeks of gestation.
METHODS: We performed an economic evaluation from a societal perspective alongside the multicentre randomised controlled APOSTEL 8 trial, including 755 participants with threatened preterm birth from 30+0 to 33+6 weeks of gestation who were randomised to atosiban or placebo, of whom 752 (884 infants) were included in the intention-to-treat analysis. Costs, collected between randomisation and three months corrected child age, were measured using a combination of hospital records and the self-reported iMTA Medical and Productivity Cost Questionnaires and estimated at infant level. The main outcome measure was cost-effectiveness expressed in terms of incremental cost per severe adverse neonatal outcome prevented. Multiple imputation by chained equations was used to handle missing data. Non-parametric bootstrapping was used to estimate statistical uncertainty surrounding incremental cost-effectiveness outcomes.
FINDINGS: The difference in mean costs between the atosiban group (€40,743.1) and the placebo group (€40,793.6) was not statistically significant (mean difference: -€50.5; 95% confidence interval (CI) -4037.6 to 3936.7). The incremental cost per severe adverse neonatal outcome prevented was dominant (-€5286.6), falling in the south-east quadrant of the cost-effectiveness plane, indicating cost-savings and reduced severe adverse neonatal outcomes by atosiban. However, the bootstrapped cost-effect pairs were distributed across all four quadrants of the cost-effectiveness plane, indicating high uncertainty surrounding cost-effectiveness estimates. The probability of cost-effectiveness of atosiban reached 50% at a willingness to pay threshold of €33,023.3 per severe adverse neonatal outcome prevented.
INTERPRETATION: This economic evaluation did not demonstrate that atosiban is a cost-effective treatment for threatened PTB from 30+0 to 33+6 weeks gestation. In addition to the absence of clinical benefit, our findings show no economic advantage, further discouraging its routine use at this gestational age. These results contribute to optimizing evidence-based management of threatened preterm birth.

title: Crack identification and detection in mine boreholes using deep learning: A case study of hexi coal mine.
abstract: The internal cracks in deep rock masses are an important factor determining the safety of coal mining. The borehole peeping technology is an important method for obtaining the distribution of coal and rock fractures in deep geological engineering. However, there are often problems such as strong background interference and complex joints in real mines, which bring greater challenges to obtaining the distribution of cracks. Therefore, this study proposes a deep learning-based method for identifying internal cracks, which is used for the intelligent identification and analysis of cracks in drilled rock masses. The experimental verification was carried out based on the real borehole peeping images of the tunnels in Hexi Coal Mine as the data set. By embedding the ResCBAM attention mechanism into the YOLOv8 head network, the reliability and accuracy of identifying internal cracks in rock were further enhanced. The test results show that, the proposed Res-YOLOv8 algorithm can more accurately suppress the interference of complex backgrounds and present the morphological characteristics of rock cracks to compare with the fusion of typical attention mechanisms SE and CBAM with YOLOv8. The ResCBAM-YOLOv8 algorithm demonstrates strong performance in the evaluation indicators of confusion matrix, loss rate, precision, recall and MPA. The proposal of method has improved the efficiency of detecting and identifying cracks in coal and rock masses in real mines, and provided more reliable technical support for the stability evaluation of coal mine roof.

title: Crafting of physical exhibits by undergraduate medical students: A mixed method study to assess the acquisition of higher-order cognitive skills and student perceptions.
abstract: Active learning engages students in some activity that induces them to reflect upon ideas and how they are using these ideas. It also involves the process of keeping students mentally, and often physically, active in their learning through activities that engage them in gathering information, thinking, and solving problems. This study was conducted to determine if creating physical exhibits fosters higher-order cognitive skills like problem solving and critical thinking (application and analysis, respectively). In this study, carried out in the Department of Physiology, 50 medical undergraduate students were divided into four batches of 12-13 students each. Each batch was supervised by a faculty mentor and assigned a topic for the preparation of a physical exhibit. Multiple-choice questions (MCQ) testing higher-order cognitive skills were used to assess the gain in knowledge post-intervention. The qualitative component of the study consisted of open-ended questions and a Focus Group Discussion to ascertain students' perceptions regarding the creation of physical exhibits. The students created physical exhibits related to the sensory pathway, the light reflex & the conjunctival reflex, the micturition reflex mechanism, and the automatic bladder. Median post-test scores showed significant improvement compared to pretest scores (16 vs 12, p < 0.01). Students reported that the active learning strategy promoted deep learning, enhanced memory, and helped them apply theory to practice. Secondly, it cultivated teamwork skills. The learning experience was enjoyable and led them to score higher on the post-test exams. Students also suggested that tightening the nuts and bolts, as in prior meticulous planning, would make the experience more enjoyable.

title: Depressive symptoms among people living with HIV in Northern Tanzania: The role of family history, social support, and maladaptive coping.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Depression is a common mental disorder among people living with HIV (PLWH) and is driven by both neuroimmunological and psychosocial pathways. In turn, depressive symptoms worsen HIV outcomes through reduced adherence, risk behaviors, and impaired immune function. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of depressive symptoms and identify associated factors among PLWH attending health facilities in northern Tanzania.
METHODOLOGY: We conducted a cross-sectional study (September-October 2023) in four Care and Treatment Clinics (CTCs) across three health system levels in Moshi Municipality. Study sites were selected purposively to represent tertiary, secondary, and primary care. Within each site, adult (≥18 years) clients on ART for ≥6 months were sampled using systematic random sampling. Standardized instruments included a sociodemographic questionnaire, the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9), the Duke-UNC Functional Social Support Questionnaire (FSSQ), the Brief COPE, and a 12-item HIV-related stigma scale. Data were entered and analyzed using STATA version 16. Logistic regression analysis was performed to identify associations between depressive symptoms and various independent variables.
RESULTS: A total of 598 clients participated, just above half (56%) from the secondary health facility level, and nearly three-quarters (70.9%) of participants were female. The prevalence of depressive symptoms was 14%. Participants reported having a family history of mental illness, good social support and predominantly use maladaptive coping strategies were more likely to report having depressive symptoms (AOR 2.15, 95%CI: 1.12-4.13; P 0.022), (AOR 8.19, 95%CI: 1.29-51.92; P 0.026), (AOR 3.98, 95%CI: 2.62-6.05; P < 0.001) respectively.
CONCLUSION: Depressive symptoms are common among PLWH receiving HIV care and treatment in northern Tanzania, and are associated with a reported family history of mental illness, predominant use of maladaptive coping, and even good social support. Thus, more studies need to be done on the relationship between depressive symptoms and social support among PLWH. Integrating mental health intervention into HIV services and providing personalized interventions focused on addressing maladaptive coping and social support are key to reducing depression among people living with HIV.

title: Development of a SCGP-CGAN framework for bidirectional H&E-Masson's Trichrome Virtual Staining.
abstract: In virtual staining of histopathological sections, deep learning-based methods continue to face challenges arising from the irreversible nature of chemical staining, morphological variations between consecutive tissue sections, and the limited availability of multi-staining paired data from the same tissue region. While existing unsupervised approaches partially alleviate the reliance on paired datasets, they often struggle to maintain consistent color reproduction and preserve fine tissue structures. To address this issue, we develop a task-oriented framework for unsupervised virtual staining, referred to as SCGP-CGAN, where "S," "C," "G," and "P" denote skip connections, CBAM-based attention, WGAN-GP-based adversarial optimization, and perceptual constraints, respectively, while "CGAN" refers to the underlying CycleGAN framework. Here, perceptual constraints refer to the complementary SSIM, LPIPS, style, and color consistency constraints used to promote structural, perceptual, stylistic, and color consistency in the generated images. This framework systematically integrates and evaluates existing components to enhance structural fidelity and perceptual quality in virtual staining. Experimental results on real histopathological datasets indicate that SCGP-CGAN exhibits favorable performance compared with CycleGAN and conventional staining normalization approaches under the evaluated dataset setting, showing improvements in perceptual quality and multiple quantitative evaluation metrics. All experiments are conducted on a publicly available patch-level dataset, and no independent WSI-level or multi-center validation is included. Within this experimental setting, the study demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed framework for bidirectional H&E-Masson's trichrome virtual staining and provides a methodological reference for further research in digital pathology image analysis.

title: Development of a variable ground pressure tracked chassis for soil compaction mitigation.
abstract: Traditional tracked agricultural machinery with a fixed contact geometry struggles to balance high maneuverability on hard pavements and low soil compaction in soft paddies. To solve this problem, this paper proposes an active variable ground pressure tracked chassis system. The effective ground contact length of the track is adjusted by distributed electric cylinders and a multi-stage linkage mechanism. To evaluate its performance, we conducted kinematic modeling, finite element analysis (FEA), and field tests. First, a planar kinematic model was established to describe the relationship between the cylinder stroke and the track geometry. Second, an internal load transfer path method was used in the FEA post-processing to reduce numerical errors from the track lugs, showing that the low-pressure mode reduces the mean compressive stress from 0.03 MPa to 0.008 MPa. Finally, soil bin tests with a physical prototype were carried out. The results indicate that the low-pressure mode decreases the peak subsoil stress from 93 kPa to 63 kPa at low speeds. In contrast, the regular mode with a shorter track length on hard surfaces reduces steering resistance. This study provides a practical design method for adaptable agricultural tracked vehicles.

title: Development of shelf-stable reagents and assay kits for bioluminescence applications using the capillary-assisted vitrification platform stabilization technology.
abstract: Luminescence is a powerful method for detecting trace analytes and monitoring biological processes. However, most bioluminescence reagents, including luciferase and its substrates, are sensitive to temperature, limiting their usable shelf lives, and resulting in inconsistent performance. Enhancing the stability of these reagents could reduce signal variability between experiments, simplify workflows, and address cold chain storage issues. In this study, we demonstrate the application of the platform stabilization technology, capillary-assisted vitrification (CAV), as a tool to stabilize different luciferases and their substrates, and the application of the stabilized reagents in both in vitro and in vivo bioluminescent assays. We demonstrate that CAV-stabilized reagents can be stored and shipped ambiently, maintain consistent performance over time, and are suitable for use in cell viability quantification, tumor monitoring, in vivo imaging, microbial detection, and immunoassays. Additionally, different reagents can be co-formulated to make ready-to-use assay kits that can also be shipped and stored ambiently. Our results demonstrate that CAV stabilization is a viable alternative to traditional storage methods, with broad potential to improve bioluminescence workflows.

title: Differential changes in cervical proprioception and motor imagery following structured imagery training in chronic neck pain.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic neck pain (CNP) is associated with altered sensorimotor function, including impairments in cervical proprioception and changes in body-related perception. While implicit motor imagery (IMI)-based interventions have shown clinical benefits, their effects on cervical proprioceptive performance and motor imagery-related outcomes in individuals with CNP remain unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the effects of lateralization and IMI training on cervical proprioception (CP), neck awareness (NA), IMI performance, pain, disability, kinesiophobia, and range of motion (ROM) in individuals with CNP.
METHODS: In this clinical trial, 34 participants (17 CNP, 17 healthy controls) completed a 4-week structured imagery training (SIT) program combining lateralization and IMI training delivered via telerehabilitation. Primary outcome was cervical joint position error (JPE). Secondary outcomes included IMI performance (left/right judgment task), pain, disability, kinesiophobia, NA, ROM, and cognitive interference (Stroop).
RESULTS: Following SIT, the CNP group showed statistically significant within-group reductions in pain intensity (Holm-adjusted p = 0.012, d = 0.76), kinesiophobia (Holm-adjusted p = 0.034, d = 0.50), neck-related disability (Holm-adjusted p = 0.034, d = 0.37), and FreNAQ-T scores (Holm-adjusted p = 0.012, d = 0.09). However, baseline-adjusted models revealed no statistically significant between-group post-training differences for extension JPE (p > 0.05, partial η2 = 0.009), flexion JPE (where post-training values remained persistently elevated in CNP; partial η2 = 0.310), and IMI accuracy/reaction times for neck and hand tasks (all Holm-adjusted p = 1.000, partial η2 ≤ 0.068).
CONCLUSIONS: A 4-week SIT program was associated with short-term improvements in subjective clinical symptoms in individuals with CNP; however, no differential group effects were observed for objective cervical proprioception or motor imagery performance.

title: Ecological traits predict extinction risk of the world's traded carnivores.
abstract: Wildlife trade is a major driver of biodiversity loss, yet how trade interacts with species' ecological traits and extinction risk remains underexplored. Carnivores warrant special attention because they are disproportionately exploited and vulnerable to extinction compared to other taxa. We analyzed 171,637 international trade records spanning 50 years (1975-2024) for 129 carnivore species listed under the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES). We analyzed trade volumes across the globe and then used logistic regression to evaluate associations between ecological traits and extinction risk, as well as family-level differences in extinction risk. Trade volumes were dominated by exports from North America and Europe and imports concentrated in East Asia, highlighting persistent transcontinental trade. Logistic regression identified longer generation length and greater dispersal distance as positively associated with higher extinction risk, whereas broader habitat breadth was associated with lower extinction risk. Among carnivore families, only Ursidae (bears) exhibited significantly greater odds of being threatened relative to the Canidae (canids) reference family. Our findings demonstrate that ecological traits are associated with extinction risk within CITES-listed carnivores, supporting the use of trait-based approaches as a complementary tool for conservation assessment and monitoring of internationally traded species.

title: Effectiveness of nurse-led hypertension interventions on retention, adherence, and blood pressure control among adults in low- and middle-income countries: A systematic review.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension affects more than 1.28 billion adults globally and remains the leading modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular disease, stroke, renal failure, and premature death. This burden is inconsistently distributed across Low- and Middle-Income Countries (LMICs), where nearly three-quarters of adults live with hypertension. This gap is largely driven by poor adherence and low retention. This systematic review aims to assess the effectiveness of nurse-led interventions on retention in care, medication adherence, and blood pressure among adult patients with hypertension in primary health care settings in LMICs.
METHODS: The protocol was registered (PROSPERO CRD420251136515) following the PRISMA guidelines. We searched PubMed, Scopus, and Cochrane for articles published between 2000 and 2026. Eligibility criteria included: adults (≥18 years) with hypertension receiving care from primary care clinics; nurse-led interventions; usual care as comparator; primary outcome: retention rates; secondary outcomes: medication adherence, blood pressure (BP) control. Inclusion: experimental, quasi-experimental, and prospective cohort studies. Dual independent screening and data extraction were performed. Quality assessment was performed using Cochrane Risk of Bias 2(RoB2) for randomized controlled trials and Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) tools for quasi-experimental and observational studies. Due to heterogeneity in intervention duration, outcome measures, and follow-up periods, a narrative synthesis was employed.
RESULTS: Eleven unique studies (n = 19,005) were identified: 63.6% RCTs, 18.2% quasi-experimental, and 18.2% observational. Seven studies were conducted in Africa and four in Asia. The mean age range was 52.0-67.4 years; 51.3%-76.0% were female. Risk-of-bias assessment revealed high or unclear risk in the missing outcomes data domain for most RCTs. Ten studies used multicomponent interventions. Retention rates varied with appointment attendance (12.6-96.5%), routine clinical retention (27.0-62.8%), and study completion of follow-up (83.8% to 97.2%). Four studies reported medication adherence with varying effects in the intervention group compared to the control or baseline. Ten studies reported systolic blood pressure (SBP) outcomes; 9 reported mean SBP after intervention; the majority reported the mean reduction of SBP was greater than 10 mmHg. Nine studies reported diastolic blood pressure (DBP) outcomes; all studies reported a reduction in DBP after the intervention, with a range of -1.8 mmHg to -20.6 mmHg. Reported SBP and DBP reductions included both within-group controlled estimates; these should not be interpreted as a pooled effect.
CONCLUSION: This systematic review included 11 studies that showed nurse-led interventions improved blood pressure control in primary health care facilities of LMICs. But retention in care showed substantial variability in nurse-led interventions in primary health care facilities of LMICs. Nurse-led interventions in LMICs are a promising strategy for improving blood pressure control. However, retention in care was substantially and variably due to heterogeneous definitions and evidence on medication adherence was limited. Future research should prioritize standardized outcome measures and robust study designs to strengthen the evidence base and inform sustainable scale-up of these models in LMICs.

title: Enjoy Life LocallY (ELLY): A qualitative study of a co-designed healthy weight and wellbeing intervention in two disadvantaged Scottish communities.
abstract: People who are unable to achieve a healthy lifestyle are at greater risk of type II diabetes, some cancers, heart disease, stroke, mobility problems and poor outcomes from disease. For individuals living in disadvantaged areas, life circumstances such as low income, unemployment, working anti-social hours and limited local services present barriers to the challenge of living healthy lives. Working with two disadvantaged communities in Forth Valley, Scotland, we co-designed and implemented an evidence-informed, incentive-based intervention, Enjoy Life LocallY (ELLY), to support citizens with healthy weight and wellbeing. The intervention comprised free soup twice weekly (café/delivery/pickup); a loyalty card (stamped upon engagement in community assets such as local activities, groups and clubs) exchanged for a £25 shopping card when a minimum of 9 assets over 12 weeks were attended; goal setting; information resources; and self-monitoring of weight and wellbeing. ELLY was delivered by volunteers over a 12-week period, from September 2023 to November 2023, to 75 residents. Qualitative interviews were conducted at 12-weeks with 10 participants per community, to assess study feasibility and conceptualise pathways to how ELLY led to healthy weight and wellbeing outcomes. Data were analysed using framework analysis. The ELLY intervention demonstrated strong acceptability and feasibility and was positively received by participants. In-depth interview data informed the construction of a conceptual framework identifying pathways through which the intervention supports healthy weight and wellbeing, including positive changes in behaviour, strengthened social connectedness, improved dietary habits, measurable participant-reported health improvements and the acquisition of new skills and knowledge. Collectively, findings support the hypothesis that engagement in the ELLY intervention was associated with a range of important health outcomes for participants, making a valuable contribution to the evidence base on community-based interventions and highlighting the important role of co-designed community interventions in supporting underserved, disadvantaged communities in health improvement.

title: Ensemble frequency ratio-maximum entropy landslide susceptibility modelling for climate‑resilient road corridors in Bocas del Toro and Chiriquí, Panama.
abstract: Landslides are a major rainfall-triggered hazard affecting road infrastructure across the mountainous terrain of western Panama. This study develops an ensemble Frequency Ratio (FR)-Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt) modelling framework to assess landslide susceptibility, identify critical management zones, and determine key drivers of slope failure along road corridors in the mainland districts of Bocas del Toro and along the Rambala-Hornito-David route. Within a 1,000 m corridor buffer, 87 mapped landslides (63 for training and 24 for validation) and 15 environmental conditioning factors were used to develop and validate the FR and MaxEnt models. An AUC-weighted linear combination of the independently calibrated FR and MaxEnt models was used to generate the ensemble susceptibility map. The ensemble delineated 9.67% and 3.99% of the corridor as high and very high susceptibility, respectively, achieving the highest predictive performance (AUC = 0.945) and outperforming the FR (0.873) and MaxEnt (0.943) models. Sensitivity analyses based on alternative training-validation partitions (57:30 and 70:17) produced consistently good performance (prediction-rate AUC > 0.88), indicating that the principal findings were not strongly influenced by the inventory allocation. Hotspot analysis identified three major clusters of elevated susceptibility and confirmed statistically significant spatial clustering at the 95% and 99% confidence levels. More than 71 km of primary roads intersect high-susceptibility zones, with Hornito, Bajo Cedro, and Valle de Agua Arriba exhibiting the greatest exposure. Slope gradient and NDVI were identified as the most influential predictors. These findings provide a practical basis for prioritising monitoring, slope stabilisation, drainage improvement, and ecosystem-based interventions to strengthen the resilience of road infrastructure in tropical mountain environments. Future work should incorporate larger landslide inventories, event-based rainfall information, and climate-change scenarios to improve the representation of landslide dynamics and support risk-informed infrastructure planning.

title: Equid population dynamics in Mexico over five decades: Divergence between national census records and FAOSTAT estimates.
abstract: Equid populations are widely used to inform animal health, welfare, and rural development strategies, yet their interpretation depends on how animals are counted, classified, and reported. Using a repeated cross-sectional analysis of national census records, this study examined long-term changes in Mexico's equid population and evaluated the consistency between national Agricultural Census records and FAOSTAT livestock statistics. Data for horses, donkeys, and mules were obtained from the Mexican Agricultural Censuses of 1970, 1991, 2007, and 2022, accounting for changes in how equids and their working functions were recorded over time. The total equid population recorded within Mexican Agricultural Production Units - which does not represent Mexico's overall equid population - declined from 6.82 million animals in 1970 to 1.60 million in 2022, a reduction of 76.5%. Donkeys showed the greatest decline (90.1%), followed by mules (84.1%) and horses (62.0%). In contrast, the census-recorded working-equid population increased by 37.1% between 2007 and 2022, driven predominantly by a 73.0% increase in working horses. Comparison with FAOSTAT revealed a progressively widening discrepancy: the FAOSTAT-to-census ratio increased from 1.82 in 1970 to 8.11 in 2022, with FAOSTAT indicating a 4.5% increase over the same period and observations shifting from official (1970) to estimated (1991, 2007) and imputed (2022). These findings demonstrate a major long-term transformation of Mexico's equid population while also showing that equids remain functionally important within contemporary agricultural systems, particularly through the increasing contribution of working horses. The marked divergence between national census records and FAOSTAT further highlights the importance of considering census definitions, functional classifications, statistical status, and data provenance when equid population estimates are used for research, veterinary planning, animal-welfare interventions, or public policy.

title: Evaluating nursing performance during heatwave simulations: Protocol for a repeated measures cross-over study.
abstract: This study protocol combines clinical simulations with climatic chamber experiments, to evaluate 1) the impact of heat stress on hospital nurses' physiological strain, physical and mental fatigue, vigilance, and clinical performance; and 2) the efficacy of a practical cooling intervention (i.e., electric fan) in mitigating the negative impact of heat stress. UK-based, registered adult nurses working in hospital settings will be recruited to partake in a repeated-measures cross-over design study, consisting of five separate 3-hour experimental sessions simulating clinical work, and taking place within a climatic chamber at Southampton General Hospital (UK). Sessions will differ by ambient temperature and cooling intervention as follows: 1) control (CTR; 18°C, 50% relative humidity [RH]); 2) warm (WARM; 26°C, 50%RH); 3) warm with electric fan (WARM+FAN; 26°C, 50%RH); 4) hot (HOT; 34°C, 50%RH); 5) hot with electric fan (HOT + FAN; 34°C, 50%RH). This study has been registered on a publicly accessible clinical trial registry (ISRCTN45793399). During each session, participants will first complete a standardised fatigue-induction protocol simulating shift work (i.e., low-intensity cycling with cognitive tasks); followed by a simulated hospital ward round involving six simulated patients and two simulated cardiac arrest scenarios. Nursing cognitive and physical performance will be assessed using a standardised observational assessment battery, along with objective cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) performance metrics. Physiological responses will be assessed by monitoring changes in core temperature (Tcore), skin temperature (Tskin), heart rate, and whole-body sweat loss (WBSL). Fatigue and vigilance will be measured using the Swedish Occupational Fatigue Inventory (SOFI) and Brief Psychomotor Vigilance Task (PVT-B), respectively. Baseline (i.e., prior to fatiguing protocol) to post simulation changes in 1) vigilance assessed via the PVT-B (i.e., a determinant of role-specific cognitive performance); 2) CPR quality score (i.e., a determinant of role-specific physical performance); and 3) Tcore (i.e., a determinant of thermo-physiological state); will be analysed using linear mixed models to determine the effects of ambient temperature and cooling intervention on nurses' clinical and physiological performance. By providing a controlled methodological framework for assessing the effects of heat exposure on hospital nurses' physiological, perceptual, and clinical performance, this study will provide empirical evidence on air temperature-related changes in nursing performance and physiological strain and the role of cooling interventions in modifying these responses. This will support the development of evidence-based climate adaptation strategies to protect healthcare staff wellbeing and maintain patient safety during periods of extreme heat.

title: Fabrication and evaluation of a sulfacetamide-loaded niosomal gel for the treatment of ocular bacterial infections.
abstract: Topical ocular drug delivery is often restricted by rapid precorneal clearance, which can decrease drug residence time and bioavailability at the ocular surface. The purpose of the study was to develop a sulfacetamide-loaded niosomal gel (SA-Nio-Gel) to enhance ocular drug delivery. Thin film hydration method was used for the preparation of SA niosomes, employing nonionic surfactants (Span 60 and Span 80) and cholesterol. The optimized niosomal formulation was then incorporated into a Carbopol 934 gel base to prepare the final SA-Nio-Gel formulation. The optimized niosomes exhibited encapsulation efficiency of 76% ± 1.5 and a mean particle size of 129.7 ± 2.52 nm. Rheological analysis of the SA-Nio-Gel demonstrated pseudoplastic behavior, characterized by a reduction in viscosity with increasing shear rate. Biocompatibility evaluation indicated that the formulation was non-toxic. In vitro release profiles showed a slow and sustained SA release from the developed formulation. Furthermore, microbiological assays confirmed the potent antibacterial activity of the SA-Nio-Gel against S. aureus. Compared to the SA solution and SA-Nio, the SA-Nio-Gel formulation significantly minimized precorneal drainage and improved drug penetration. These results indicate that the niosomal gel-based system could be a promising platform for the ocular delivery of SA, which provides sustained release and enhanced drug permeability.

title: Factor structure and psychometric properties of the Arabic version of the 9-item Trier Inventory for Chronic Stress (TICS-9).
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic stress is a major determinant of physical and psychological health, yet validated instruments for assessing long-term psychosocial stress remain limited in Arabic-speaking populations.
OBJECTIVE: The present study aimed to translate and culturally adapt the 9-item Trier Inventory for Chronic Stress (TICS-9) into Arabic and to evaluate its psychometric properties in an adult sample.
METHODS: The English 9-item short version of the TICS was translated following International Test Commission guidelines, including independent forward translations, back-translation, and expert committee review to ensure conceptual and linguistic equivalence. A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among 291 Arabic-speaking adults in Saudi Arabia. Internal consistency was assessed using Cronbach's alpha and McDonald's omega. Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) was performed using robust weighted least squares estimation (WLSMV) appropriate for ordinal data. Construct-related evidence was explored using hierarchical regression analyses with demographic and medical variables.
RESULTS: The Arabic TICS-9 demonstrated excellent internal consistency (α = 0.876; ω = 0.904). CFA provided preliminary support for a unidimensional structure with moderate to strong standardized loadings (0.583-0.819). Model fit showed a mixed pattern in the initially specified model but improved after theoretically justified post hoc residual correlations were added between item pairs with overlapping content. Income was inversely associated with chronic stress scores after adjustment for education, work status, and marital status. Depression was associated with higher stress scores after controlling for other chronic conditions.
CONCLUSION: These findings provide initial evidence of internal consistency and preliminary structural support for the Arabic TICS-9 in Saudi Arabic-speaking adults. Further studies are needed to evaluate test-retest reliability, convergent validity, and measurement invariance across populations.

title: Formulation and biological evaluation of a bacterial nanocellulose-based nanoemulsion hydrogel loaded with Persea americana Mill. seed extract: An anti-aging assessment.
abstract: Avocado (Persea americana Mill.) seed is an underutilized by-product rich in catechins and fatty acids, with potential anti-aging properties. However, the utilization of avocado seed in topical formulations is limited by its poor solubility, physicochemical instability, and minimal skin penetration. Therefore, this study aimed to develop and evaluate a bacterial nanocellulose (BNC)-based nanoemulsion hydrogel incorporating avocado seed extract as a topical anti-aging delivery system. Nanoemulsions were prepared using avocado seed oil, Cremophor® RH40, and PEG 400, followed by incorporation into a BNC matrix to obtain a hydrogel-like formulation. Physicochemical characteristics were evaluated by globule size, polydispersity index (PDI), transmittance, pH, viscosity, morphology (TEM), FT-IR profile, and freeze-thaw stability. Skin permeation study was conducted using Franz diffusion cells, while anti-aging activities were assessed using the pinch test, skin hydration, and collagen density assessment in UVB-induced photoaging rat model.The optimized nanoemulsion exhibited a globule size of 20.3 ± 0.10 nm, PDI of 0.109 ± 0.029, transmittance of 99.62 ± 0.27%, and pH of 4.92 ± 0.01 with 1:6:3 ratio of oil, surfactant, and co-surfactant subsequently. The formulation was stable in globule size, PDI, or pH after three freeze-thaw cycles. Incorporation of avocado seed extract up to 5% did not adversely affect nanoemulsion characteristics. The cumulative permeation of BNC-based nanoemulsion was significantly higher than BNC-based conventional emulsion, reaching 198.28 ± 0.54 µg/cm2 after 120 min compared with 121.35 ± 0.54 µg/cm2. In vivo studies showed that the formulation significantly improved skin elasticity, hydration, and collagen density while reducing UVB-induced wrinkle formation (p < 0.05). In conclusion, the developed BNC-based nanoemulsion hydrogel successfully enhanced the delivery of avocado seed extract and provides a stable and effective platform for topical delivery of natural bioactive compound in anti-aging cosmetic applications.

title: From data neglect to data respect: A framework for institutionalising a sustainable research data management culture in Kenyan universities.
abstract: Research Data Management (RDM) is increasingly recognised as critical for enhancing research integrity, efficiency, and data reuse globally; however, in Kenya, institutionalised RDM frameworks remain underdeveloped, resulting in fragmented practices, data loss risks, and limited data sharing and reuse. This study, drawn from a PhD investigation, proposes a comprehensive RDM framework informed by empirical evidence on current practices, enablers, and challenges in selected Kenyan universities. The study is anchored on the Australian Research Data Commons (ARDC) Capability Maturity Model for RDM and the UK Data Archive Research Data Lifecycle model. The framework was developed through a multi-stage mixed-methods study comprising a systematic review, a bibliometric analysis, and surveys examining the RDM landscape in Kenyan universities. A multiple-case study design involving six public and private universities, purposively selected based on the June 2023 Webometrics rankings, was adopted. Data was collected through interviews with six head librarians and five heads of research units, as well as questionnaires administered to 306 respondents from a targeted sample of 355. Quantitative data was analysed using IBM SPSS (Version 28), while qualitative data were thematically analysed using NVivo (Version 14). Triangulation and pretesting were used to enhance validity and reliability. All necessary ethical considerations were addressed before data collection. Findings indicate a growing awareness of RDM among researchers; however, practices remain largely ad hoc, poorly coordinated, and weakly supported institutionally. Notably, none of the universities studied had dedicated RDM policies, structured RDM support services, or dedicated RDM Information and Communication Technology (ICT) infrastructure, revealing gaps across personal, institutional, and national levels. This study proposes a multi-level, stakeholder-driven RDM framework that integrates researchers, librarians, ICT personnel, research offices, and key national agencies such as the National Commission for Science, Technology and Innovation (NACOSTI), the Commission for University Education (CUE), and the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner (ODPC) to support coordinated, policy-driven data stewardship aligned with international best practices for sustainable RDM in Kenyan universities.

title: Gender differences in pre-surgical motivations, expectations, and patient-reported outcomes in Class III orthognathic surgery patients: An item-level analysis.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate gender differences in pre-surgical motivations, expectations, functional and psychosocial evaluations, and treatment process perceptions among adult patients with skeletal Class III malocclusion undergoing orthodontic preparation for orthognathic surgery.
METHODS: In this single-center, cross-sectional study, 81 adults (37 females, 44 males) with skeletal Class III malocclusion completed a 27-item investigator-developed questionnaire during pre-surgical orthodontic preparation, covering demographics, problem awareness, functional and psychosocial evaluations, motivation and expectations, treatment process, and patient engagement. Gender differences were analyzed item by item with Mann-Whitney U, chi-square, or Fisher's exact tests. P-values for the 37 comparisons were adjusted with the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) procedure within questionnaire domains, and effect sizes with 95% confidence intervals were estimated. Because the a priori sample size calculation did not address between-gender comparisons, these were treated as exploratory.
RESULTS: Seven differences met the unadjusted threshold (p < 0.05), of which three remained significant after within-domain FDR correction: females reported greater lack of self-confidence in social environments (q = 0.044), and males reported more adequate information from their orthodontist (q = 0.018) and higher pre-operative treatment satisfaction (q = 0.019), with moderate effect sizes (rank-biserial |r| = 0.30-0.35). The other four, all reported more often by females (eating difficulty, food avoidance, temporomandibular joint problems, and lack of confidence when photographed), were nominally significant only (unadjusted p = 0.013-0.043). No difference survived correction across all 37 comparisons. For the other items no significant differences were detected, but confidence intervals did not exclude small-to-moderate differences.
CONCLUSIONS: Gender differences in social self-confidence, perceived information adequacy, and pre-operative satisfaction were the strongest exploratory findings. Because the study was not powered for gender comparisons, non-significant results do not indicate that the genders are similar. These exploratory findings warrant confirmation in adequately powered multi-center, longitudinal studies.

title: Genotype-derived interpretive categories of drug response in 908 pharmacogenomic reports from Chinese patients with type 2 diabetes: A retrospective single-centre study.
abstract: Pharmacogenomic testing is increasingly ordered in routine diabetes care, but the reports it generates are heterogeneous and are not in a form that can be analysed systematically. We examined how genotype is translated into interpretive categories of drug response in a real-world Chinese cohort, and how consistently that translation is applied. We analysed 908 de-identified pharmacogenomic reports issued for patients with type 2 diabetes at a single centre between July 2022 and April 2024. An interpretation rulebook, taken from the standing appendix that the testing laboratory attached to every report and completed by reconstructing the rules that appendix does not state, mapped six single-nucleotide polymorphisms onto eight genotype-derived interpretive categories. These are classifications, not measured outcomes: no glycaemic response, hypoglycaemia, adverse event, treatment discontinuation or dose modification was recorded, so no category could be checked against outcome. Allele frequencies matched gnomAD East Asian data except at the risk loci, where the risk alleles were enriched, as expected in a case-only cohort. Each pre-defined variant was the statistical driver of its corresponding category, with odds ratios inflated by quasi-complete separation because the coding rules are deterministic. Across 5,983 category assignments the rulebook reproduced 5,940 (99.3%), leaving 43 discordant assignments in 28 reports; a structured audit makes most of them consistent with a mismatch between the genotype printed on a report and the genotype its interpretation was generated from. The sulfonylurea efficacy category was assigned by two different rules over the study period, and the "increased efficacy" level appeared only in reports from the later, six-locus panel, where it tracked reduced-function CYP2C9 genotypes. Nothing in the report indicated which rule had been applied. Interpretation drifts as assays are revised, and writing the rulebook down and versioning it is what makes that drift visible.

title: Harpagide alleviates neuroinflammation and cognitive dysfunction in sepsis-associated encephalopathy: Association with the MMP9/NF-κB signaling pathway.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE) is a severe neurological complication of sepsis, characterized by uncontrolled neuroinflammation and cognitive decline, yet no specific therapy is currently available. Harpagide, a naturally occurring iridoid glycoside, has been reported to possess anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective activities; however, its therapeutic potential in SAE remains unexplored. This study aimed to investigate whether Harpagide exerts neuroprotective effects in SAE and to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms.
METHODS: A mouse model of SAE was established by intraperitoneal injection of lipopolysaccharide (LPS, 18 mg/kg). Cognitive performance was assessed using behavioral assays. Brain tissue morphology and neuronal survival were evaluated through histopathological examination. Glial cell activation and the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6) were measured. Network pharmacology was employed to predict potential targets, followed by molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations to predict binding interactions with core targets. Western blotting was performed to determine the expression levels of key proteins involved in the MMP9/NF-κB signaling pathway.
RESULTS: Treatment with Harpagide significantly improved behavioral performance, ameliorated brain pathological changes, preserved hippocampal neurons, suppressed glial activation, and reduced the levels of TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 in SAE mice. Network pharmacology analysis predicted four core targets: GAPDH, CASP3, MMP9, and ICAM1. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations suggested stable binding between Harpagide and MMP9. Western blot analysis further showed that Harpagide treatment was associated with reduced expression of MMP9 and phosphorylated NF-κB p65 in both hippocampal and cortical tissues.
CONCLUSIONS: The present study demonstrates that Harpagide exerts neuroprotective effects in SAE, which are associated with mitigated neuroinflammation and reduced MMP9/NF-κB signaling, supporting its potential as a promising therapeutic candidate for this devastating condition.

title: Identification of Plasmodium sporozoites using angle-resolved scattered light pulse shapes.
abstract: Flow cytometry is widely used to identify and sort rare cells, but conventional approaches rely on fluorescent labels. Label-free discrimination of rare targets in complex, heterogeneous samples remains challenging. Here, we introduce a label-free strategy that combines multi-angle pulse shape flow cytometry (MAPS-FC), which exploits the full temporal structure of the signal pulses during cell or particles transit through the laser spot, with a deep learning-based analysis. As a biologically relevant test case, we focus on Plasmodium falciparum sporozoites, the infectious stage of the malaria parasite, which need to be isolated from mosquito salivary glands and are embedded in a heterogeneous mosquito-derived background. Using a GFP-expressing reporter line for validation, we trained a long short-term memory (LSTM) neural network to classify sporozoites solely from their scattering pulse shapes captured through MAPS-FC. Using training data from multiple days and setting a threshold on the classification confidence, the network can distinguish sporozoites from mosquito debris without fluorescent labels. This work establishes MAPS-FC with deep learning as a platform for label-free identification of rare parasites in complex biological samples.

title: Immediate gastrocnemius responses to intermittent cold compression at different pressure levels in soccer players.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intermittent cold compression (ICC) is widely used for post-exercise recovery, but the optimal pressure for gastrocnemius recovery in soccer players remains unclear. This study investigated the immediate effects of different ICC pressure levels on gastrocnemius recovery after fatigue.
METHODS: Seven male collegiate soccer players (national Level 2 or above) participated in a randomized crossover trial. Following a 90-minute soccer-specific fatigue protocol, participants received a single 20-minute, 1°C ICC intervention at either low pressure (LP, 5-15 mmHg) or moderate pressure (MP, 5-50 mmHg), with a 48-hour washout. Outcomes included subjective perceptions (VAS pain, Borg CR10 fatigue), motor function (countermovement jump [CMJ] height, peak force, peak power, concentric work, rate of force development [RFD]), muscle mechanical properties (tone, stiffness, elasticity), and muscle architecture (thickness, pennation angle), assessed pre-and post-intervention.
RESULTS: Pain and RPE scores decreased significantly from pre- to post-intervention (p < 0.05), with no significant pressure or pressure × time effects. Significant time effects were found for CMJ height (F = 25.94, p = 0.002, η2ₚ = 0.812), peak force (F = 11.07, p = 0.016, η2ₚ = 0.649), and peak power (F = 13.17, p = 0.011, η2ₚ = 0.687), all declining post-intervention. Significant pressure × time interactions emerged for RFD (F = 6.07, p = 0.049, η2ₚ = 0.503) and lateral gastrocnemius logarithmic decrement (F = 9.21, p = 0.023, η2ₚ = 0.606).
CONCLUSIONS: While both regimens alleviated subjective symptoms, significant pressure × time interactions were observed for RFD and lateral gastrocnemius logarithmic decrement, suggesting that compression pressure may influence the acute neuromuscular and mechanical responses to ICC. These findings should be interpreted cautiously given the small sample size and the absence of significant within-condition changes in RFD.

title: Inactivation of microorganisms in the complex regions of transvaginal ultrasound probes by a UVC-LED light based disinfection system.
abstract: Endocavity ultrasound transducers, particularly transvaginal ultrasound (TVUS) probes, contain intricate structures such as notches, grooves, lens surfaces, and handle edges that are highly susceptible to microbial contamination yet difficult to disinfect using conventional high-level disinfection (HLD) methods. This study evaluated the efficacy of a novel ultraviolet C light emitting diode (UVC-LED) HLD system in eliminating microbial contamination from these complex probe surfaces. Two TVUS probes were sampled from predefined high-risk regions before and after disinfection following clinical use. Probe A was sampled at the top and bottom notches and both sides of the handle, while Probe B was assessed at the lens, edges, and bent groove regions. Microbial contamination was quantified using swab sampling, culture on agar plates, and identification via Matrix-Assisted Laser Desorption/Ionization Time-of-Flight (MALDI-TOF). Environmental sampling of examination and disinfection rooms was also performed. To assess this system robustness, probe sites were repeatedly inoculated with Bacillus subtilis spores and evaluated following UVC treatment. Before UVC treatment, contamination rates ranged from 25% to 57% across sampled regions, with microbial loads reaching up to 3.9 log10 colony forming units (CFU). Identified organisms included Staphylococcus epidermidis, Pseudomonas koreensis, Bacillus cereus, and Propionibacterium spp. Probe sheaths were also predominantly contaminated with Staphylococcus epidermidis., with counts reaching up to 4.3 log10 CFU, Environmental sampling revealed diverse microbiota, with higher contamination levels in examination rooms compared to disinfection areas. Following 90 seconds of UV-C exposure, no microbial growth was detected on any sampled site, indicating 100% decontamination. Additionally, UVC treatment achieved > 6.5 log10 reduction of B. subtilis spores across all tested regions. These findings demonstrate that UVC-LED technology provides rapid, effective, and consistent high-level disinfection of complex TVUS probe surfaces, supporting its potential as a rapid and reliable disinfection modality in clinical setting.

title: Initial failure morphology of shallow loess containing millimeter-scale cracks: Insights from CT 3d imaging.
abstract: Frequent shallow loess slope failures in loess regions pose significant threats to both linear infrastructure and local communities. Millimeter-scale initial cracks induced by water, temperature, and weathering are key factors controlling such loess failures. Early diagnosis and prevention remain challenging, largely because the disaster chain triggered by millimeter-scale initial cracks is not fully understood, and the early failure behavior of these cracks is poorly characterized. In this study, laboratory experiments were conducted on loess specimens containing artificial millimeter-scale initial cracks to simulate natural cracks. Uniaxial compression tests combined with CT scanning were performed on specimens with initial cracks of varying characteristics. Three-dimensional structural models of the specimens at initial failure were reconstructed using machine learning methods, and the morphology and structural characteristics of the cracks were analyzed qualitatively and quantitatively. The test results show that the cracks generated in the initial failure state mainly involve wing cracks and extension cracks from the initial crack edges as well as wing cracks extending from both sides, initial cracks of varying characteristics produce different types of secondary cracks. Compared to intact specimens, samples with shallow, 45°-inclined, or shallow-surface compound cracks reached initial failure at substantially lower axial stresses-reduced by 78%, 65%, and 81%, respectively. This reduction is attributed to the development of larger-volume failure cracks in specimens with initial cracks. The distribution, inclination, and combination of millimeter-scale initial cracks exacerbate initial failure. Specifically, deeper initial cracks promote more large-volume failure cracks; 45° inclined initial cracks generate more large-volume failure cracks than horizontal or vertical ones; and two initial cracks produce more large-volume, large-diameter failure cracks than a single crack.

title: Integrated nutrition-sensitive interventions are associated with improvements in household food security and dietary diversity among vulnerable women in the host communities of Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh: Findings from a pre-post comparison study.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Nutrition-sensitive interventions aim to improve or at least safeguard the underlying causes of malnutrition, especially among the most vulnerable populations. Integrated nutrition-sensitive interventions are effective strategies for improving household food security and dietary diversity in low-income settings. In 2021, the European Union (EU) and UNICEF, in collaboration with the Government of Bangladesh and partners, implemented nutrition-sensitive interventions combining two income-generating activities (IGAs): backyard poultry rearing and tailoring with asset transfers, direct cash support, and nutrition education for vulnerable women in the host communities of Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh. We evaluated the association of these interventions with household food security and dietary diversity among vulnerable women.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We analyzed data from two rounds (2022 and 2024) of repeated cross-sectional surveys involving 1,255 vulnerable women (638 in 2022 and 617 in 2024) across four upazilas in Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh. Covariates were initially imbalanced across groups because the interventions were not randomly assigned; therefore, we employed propensity score weighting to balance the covariates between the two groups. We used modified Poisson regression and binomial regression models to estimate the association between exposure and outcomes from the pseudo-population obtained by propensity score weighting. All the inferences in this manuscript were based on a 5% significance level.
RESULTS: In 2024, vulnerable women had a 53% higher likelihood of household food security (RR = 1.53, 95% CI: 1.27-1.85, p < 0.001) than in 2022. Similarly, dietary diversity of vulnerable women increased markedly, showing over two and a half-fold higher likelihood of adequate dietary diversity in 2024 (RR = 2.78, 95% CI: 2.36-3.27, p < 0.001). The E-values corresponding to the associations of food security and dietary diversity with survey year were 2.44 and 5.00, respectively, on the risk ratio scale, which shows that the findings were less sensitive to unmeasured confounders.
CONCLUSION: Household food security and dietary diversity substantially increased over time among vulnerable women in the study areas. As the study was a two-repeated cross-sectional survey, residual confounding and other time-varying contextual factors cannot be excluded, so the observed differences should not be interpreted as definitive causal effects of the intervention. Future controlled or longitudinal evaluations are needed to establish the causal effectiveness and long-term sustainability of integrated nutrition-sensitive interventions.

title: Land degradation neutrality state and progress in the Central Region, Malawi.
abstract: Achieving Land Degradation Neutrality (LDN) is vital for the long-term sustainability of human well-being and the realisation of Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 15.3.1. We estimated the overall indicator of SDG 15.3.1, the proportion of land that is degraded over the total land area in the Central Region, Malawi, from 2001 to 2022, using the Trends.Earth tool in QGIS. The study applied the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD) Good Practice Guidance methodology for SDG Indicator 15.3.1 assessment, integrating land cover, land productivity, and soil organic carbon (SOC) sub-indicators. The default datasets in the Trends.Earth plugin were adopted for all sub-indicators. The study has revealed that: (i) The proportion of degraded land increased from 26.8% in the baseline period (2001-2015) to 41.2% in the monitoring period (2016-2022). Stable land area decreased from 62.2% to 55.7%, while improved land area declined from 10.0% to 2.0%. Overall, during the entire study period (2001-2022), 27.1% of the land remained degraded, 62.4% was stable, and 9.4% improved. (ii) Land with degraded productivity significantly declined from 74.5% to 29.3%. In contrast, land with stable productivity slightly increased from 1.1% to 1.9%. (iii) SOC levels remained largely stable (>97%), although slight losses occurred in cropland, grassland, and wetland areas. (iv) Land cover remained predominantly stable (96.7%) throughout the study period. The overall SDG 15.3.1 indicator indicates continued degradation trends exceeding the rate of land recovery and restoration. This study has highlighted key spatial patterns and identified insights into the priority areas for targeted LDN interventions in the Central Region of Malawi. The findings provide critical evidence for guiding sustainable land management strategies and accelerating progress toward achieving land degradation neutrality in Malawi.

title: Lean MAFLD as an independent risk factor for carotid plaque: The value of FIB-4 index in subgroup analysis.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the associations between different subtypes of Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) and carotid plaque, and to evaluate the independent association of the Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index with carotid plaque risk.
METHODS: Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess associations of MAFLD subtypes and the FIB-4 index with carotid plaque. Two covariate‑selection strategies were adopted: confounders for MAFLD‑subtype analyses were chosen based on clinical considerations, while subgroup‑analysis confounders were screened using a univariable p < 0.10 threshold. Separate adjusted models were constructed disentangle the independent association of the composite FIB-4 score from its individual components.
RESULTS: A total of 15,544 participants were included. After multivariable adjustment, lean MAFLD demonstrated an independent association with carotid plaque (OR=1.444), and its point estimate was numerically higher than those for diabetes-related MAFLD (OR = 1.354) and overweight/obesity-related MAFLD (OR = 1.172), although the confidence intervals overlapped. The FIB-4 index demonstrated a significant association with carotid plaque across all MAFLD subtypes (all p < 0.05) in models excluding its individual constituent components (OR range: 1.401-2.227).
CONCLUSION: Lean MAFLD is independently associated with carotid plaque. The FIB-4 index, a readily accessible noninvasive marker, shows consistent associations with carotid plaque across all MAFLD subtypes.

title: Limited capital? Explaining transatlantic divergences in artificial intelligence startup financing.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is a global general-purpose technology (GPT), yet the financial systems that scale AI ventures differ markedly across regions. This paper compares AI-focused venture capital (VC) dynamics in Europe and the United States from 2000 to 2025 using approximately 8,000 AI-related VC rounds from PitchBook and macroeconomic and institutional data from the World Bank. Exploiting the 2021 generative-AI inflection point as a common technological shock that triggered a structural reallocation of venture capital toward AI ventures, we apply a difference-in-differences (DiD) design to distinguish between startup formation and scale-up financing. Descriptive evidence shows that Europe keeps pace with the US in AI deal counts, suggesting no major pipeline gap in startup formation. However, Europe lags substantially in AI investment volumes and in AI's share of total VC funding. In the Post-period, AI accounts for around 60% of VC investment volume in the US, compared to roughly 31% in Europe. Difference-in-differences estimates are consistent with parallel trajectories in AI deal activity but point to large and statistically significant transatlantic gaps in AI investment volume and investment intensity. These results are robust to macroeconomic and governance controls, a formal event-study test of pre-treatment trends, and a sensitivity analysis that excludes the United Kingdom (which alone accounts for roughly 31% of European VC volume), a placebo test using a false treatment year, and the exclusion of the COVID-19 period. Interpreting the findings through GPT diffusion and the Varieties of Capitalism framework, we interpret the pattern as being consistent with the US liberal market economy having a structural advantage in mobilizing large-scale risk capital. The results inform current debates on European technological sovereignty, the Capital Markets Union, and AI-related policy initiatives.

title: Membrane tension and cell-nucleus mechanical coupling regulate confined cell migration.
abstract: Cell migration is a fundamental physiological process essential from embryogenesis to cancer metastasis. It is primarily governed by the coupled mechanics of the plasma membrane (PM) and the nucleus, together with cytoskeletal dynamics. Being the largest and stiffest organelle, the nucleus is considered a rate-limiting factor in confined migration. However, nuclear positioning varies across cell types and migration modes, and the forces orchestrating its mechanical coupling with the PM are not completely understood. In recent decades, mathematical modelling has gained relevance to support cell migration research, yet models face the fundamental challenge of balancing mechanistic detail with computational efficiency. Here, we develop a dimensionless, biophysically grounded model based on geometric surface partial differential equations (GS-PDEs) for cell migration. This approach benefits from dimensional reduction-the PM and the nuclear envelope (NE) are modelled as energetic geometric membranes-and is solved using the evolving surface finite element method (ESFEM), balancing mechanistic detail with computational feasibility. The model reproduces experimentally observed migration patterns: exhaustion of lipid reservoirs and nuclear-lamina unfolding limit PM and NE surface area, blocking cell passage through constrictions; nuclear velocity peaks upon pore exit; and nuclear movement alternates between pulling and pushing regimes. Moreover, the modelling approach makes key predictions: the velocity peak upon nuclear pore exit is driven by the release of the curvature-elastic energy stored as membrane tension at the NE rear, and PM-NE mechanical coupling can hinder cell translocation, since part of the locomotion energy is invested in nuclear positioning. The model quantifies forces that are not easily experimentally accessible, including membrane tension, bending energy, osmotic pressure, PM-NE elasticity, and contact forces, offering an interpretable platform to test and propose mechanistic hypotheses on confined cell migration.

title: Microclimatic regulation effects of landscape elements on university campus in a temperate monsoon climate zone: A case study during extreme summer heat.
abstract: Although temperate monsoon climate regions are traditionally known for their harsh winter climates, the combined effects of rapid urbanization and global climate change have significantly intensified summer urban heat island effects in these areas, making them a neglected yet increasingly severe challenge in high-latitude urban climate adaptation planning. This study takes a typical campus in Shenyang, a temperate monsoon climate region in Northeast China, as the experimental subject. It quantitatively dissects the non-linear statistical associations and regulatory mechanisms of biotic and abiotic landscape elements and their spatial configurations on microclimate parameters and human thermal comfort (Physiologically Equivalent Temperature, PET) by combining microclimate field observations with validated ENVI-met numerical simulations. Field measurement results show that the vertical structural characteristics of vegetation dominate cooling efficiency: evergreen trees and shrubs, with their dense radiation-blocking structures, exhibit optimal regulatory potential, with mean Physiological Equivalent Temperature (ΔPET) values reaching 10.6°C and 10.4°C, respectively, significantly outperforming deciduous trees (8.1°C). In contrast, abiotic elements play an auxiliary role, with dynamic water bodies and enclosed pavilions providing PET improvement values of 3.1°C and 2.9°C, respectively, while paving materials have limited direct regulatory capacity (< 2.0°C). Simulation optimization further reveals a significant "blue-green synergy" effect: the composite configuration of high-canopy evergreen trees and large-area dynamic water bodies forms the optimal spatial solution, reducing daily average PET to 48.7°C, a decrease of 7.3°C compared to the vegetation-free baseline scenario. Addressing the unique "humid-heat" challenge that distinguishes temperate monsoon climates from arid or semi-arid regions where summer thermal stress is often attributed solely to high temperatures, this study goes beyond merely documenting cooling effects to elucidate the "structural-thermal decoupling" mechanism in temperate monsoon climates. It challenges the conventional "deciduous-first" design paradigm by quantifying the superior radiative-blocking efficiency of evergreen species during extreme heatwaves, providing a physically-grounded framework for campus microclimate resilience.

title: Microscopic risk assessment of highway weaving sections based on large-scale UAV trajectory data: What kinematic and interaction measures each detect.
abstract: Microscopic risk assessment of highway weaving sections relies largely on single-vehicle kinematic indicators, yet what such indicators actually detect is rarely tested against a measure of vehicle-to-vehicle interaction. This study analyses 12,256 complete vehicle trajectories collected by UAV at seven highway weaving sections, and evaluates every trajectory along two independent dimensions: a kinematics-based composite indicator combining longitudinal acceleration, lateral acceleration and longitudinal jerk with entropy-derived weights, and an interaction-based measure derived from time-to-collision with the leading vehicle. Because only seven sections are available, all section-level results are assessed by exact permutation as well as by parametric tests. Three findings follow. First, cumulative risk, the time integral of instantaneous risk, is mechanically dominated by traversal time (r = 0.989 with duration, r = 0.948 with weaving length at section level) and is unsuitable for comparing sections of differing length; time-averaged risk intensity is used instead. Second, individual behaviour dominates risk variation and both dimensions agree about it: merging and diverging movements carry higher risk and more conflicts than through movements, and heavy vehicles fewer conflicts than passenger cars (1.1% against 2.7% of trajectories below TTC = 3 s). Higher entry speed shortens exposure by 30.9% and lowers cumulative risk by 25.4% while raising risk intensity by 12.7%, so it reduces exposure rather than severity. Third, and centrally, the two dimensions respond differently to section configuration: task complexity is more strongly associated with interaction-based conflict rate than with kinematic risk intensity (permutation p = 0.028), although with seven sections neither association is significant on its own (p = 0.052 and p = 0.915), and the negative association between weaving length and risk intensity is directionally consistent across three methods but does not reach significance under permutation (p = 0.083). Kinematic indicators therefore characterise the demand placed on the individual driver, and no association between them and the interaction burden a section imposes was detected in these data; the two families of measure must be reported together. Risk tiers built on either kinematic feature are nonetheless externally valid, with conflict rate rising monotonically from 1.2% to 8.3% across intensity tiers.

title: Modeling and controlling a half-car model suspension system using an ANFIS controller.
abstract: Passive suspension systems (PSS) use fixed spring and damping characteristics and cannot adapt to changing road disturbances and operating conditions. Active suspension systems (ASS) address this limitation by generating additional control forces, but controller design must balance ride comfort, road holding, model uncertainty, and control effort. This study develops a four-degree-of-freedom (4-DOF) longitudinal half-car model and evaluates an Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) controller against PSS and PID-controlled ASS under double-bump and ISO-classified random Type A and Type C Road profiles at 10 and 20 m/s. The ANFIS controller is trained using PID-generated input-output data with two inputs, five Gaussian membership functions per input, 25 Takagi-Sugeno rules, and 150 training epochs. For the double-bump case at 10 m/s, ANFIS reduces body vertical displacement from 0.0435 to 0.0084 m (80.6%), vertical acceleration from 2.40 to 0.77 m/s2 (67.9%), and front suspension travel from 0.0652 to 0.0090 m (86.2%) relative to PSS. Compared with PID, the corresponding reductions are 53.6%, 49.3%, and 43.8%, respectively. Settling time is reduced by 38.8% for body vertical displacement and 38.6% for pitch acceleration relative to PSS. The result meets all the qualifications for riding comfort of the ISO 2631 standard. The study identifies limitations related to PID-supervised training, linear modeling, and actuator-energy assessment by employing simulation. Experimental evaluation is required to establish robustness to parameter uncertainty, sensor noise, actuator delay, and implementation energy requirements.
