title: Nephroprotective and Gastroprotective potential of Aerva javanica (L.) green synthesized nanoparticles, supported by Molecular Networking.
abstract: NSAIDs pose a significant risk to the stomach and kidneys, with oxidative stress being a key driver in the development of indomethacin-induced gastric ulcers and acute kidney injury by disrupting the balance between oxidation and antioxidation. Effective management of oxidative stress and bolstering antioxidant defenses are crucial strategies for preventing and treating these conditions. This study explored the potential of Aerva javanica, a plant abundant in Saudi Arabia and used in traditional medicine, to mitigate these adverse effects. Researchers identified 27 phytochemicals in its leaf extract using LC-MS and synthesized silver nanoparticles (SNPs), characterizing them with TEM and UV-visible spectrophotometry. Network analysis suggested a link between procyanidin dimer and kaempferol 4'-O-methyl ether with genes protecting the kidneys and stomach, possibly involving the AGE-RAGE and HIF-1 signaling pathways. In vivo experiments using an indomethacin-induced injury model demonstrated that administering A. javanica resulted in a dose-dependent decrease in gastric ulcer severity and a return of elevated serum renal markers to normal levels. Furthermore, the treatment reduced oxidative stress markers (MDA) and increased antioxidant levels (GSH) in both the stomach and kidneys. A. javanica also suppressed the expression of pro-inflammatory markers and inhibited the NF-κB p65 and STAT-3 signaling pathways. Histological examination corroborated these protective effects. The observed scavenging activity of A. javanica is attributed to its rich content of flavonoids and phenolic compounds. These findings suggest that A. javanica offers promising gastroprotective and nephroprotective properties against NSAID-induced complications by reducing oxidative stress and inflammation through the coordinated regulation of key signaling pathways.

title: PIP5K isoforms and phosphoinositide molecular species in EGF-stimulated PIP3 synthesis: A multi-method approach using enzyme genetic suppression and chemical inhibition in MCF10A cells.
abstract: The membrane phospholipid PI(4,5)P2 has structural functions and is a substrate for PLC and PI3K enzymes to generate Ins(1,4,5)P3, DAG and PI(3,4,5)P3 signals. PIP5Ks, that 5-phosphorylate PI4P, are the major source of PI(4,5)P2 in mammalian cells. Current thinking suggests distinct pools of PI(4,5)P2 may be differentially generated by PIP5Kα, β and γ isoforms and involved in different physiological functions. Phosphoinositides are comprised of families of acyl-chain variants but are uniquely enriched in C38:4 species. There is evidence that PIP5Ks are selective for certain acyl chain species of PI(4)P. We aimed to understand how inhibition of PIP5Ks impacts PIP3 production and whether they differentially support synthesis of a pool of PI(4,5)P2, that may be marked by a distinct profile of molecular species variants, which supply class I PI3Ks in a non-transformed human cell line (MCF10A cells). Using a combination of siRNA, Cas9/CRISPR-mediated gene knockout (k/o), recently derived selective, small-molecule inhibitors of PIP5Ks and mass-spectrometry-based lipidomic techniques, we attempted to address these questions. We found that MCF10A cells only express PIP5Kα and γ and that neither siRNA-mediated reduction nor k/o of either protein changed the levels or acyl chain profiles of any of the phosphoinositides in Epidermal Growth Factor- (EGF) stimulated MCF10A cells. We found that selective PIP5K inhibition reduced levels of PIP2 and EGF-stimulated PIP3 and increased levels of PIP, however, the acyl-chain-profiles of none of these lipids were significantly altered in MCF10A cells. We found EGF-stimulated Akt, EGF Receptor (EGFR) and MAPK phosphorylation were also reduced by PIP5K inhibitors in this cell line. To deconvolute these results, we tested the impact of a selective PI3Kα inhibitor (A66) and found it inhibited PIP3 accumulation and Akt phosphorylation and reduced MAPK phosphorylation but was without effect on total EGFR or its phosphorylation, suggesting some cross-talk between EGF-stimulated activation of class I PI3K and MAPKs in MCF10A cells.

title: Perceived importance, self-rated performance satisfaction, learning stress, and practicum experiences among nursing students: A cross-sectional study with supplementary open-ended responses.
abstract: This cross-sectional study examined nursing students' perceived importance and self-rated performance satisfaction regarding fundamental nursing practicum competencies, explored learning-stress scores across academic-achievement categories and psychological-counseling history, and descriptively summarized written practicum experiences. All 730 eligible third-year nursing students were invited; 28 did not participate, 702 returned signed consent forms and questionnaires, and 3 incomplete questionnaires were excluded, leaving 699 participants. Importance-performance analysis (IPA) used sample grand means (importance, 4.679; performance satisfaction, 4.503) as crosshairs. Paired importance-performance gaps and 95% confidence intervals were calculated, and 5,000 bootstrap samples assessed coordinate uncertainty and quadrant stability. Exploratory grade-group and counseling-history comparisons used analysis of variance and independent-samples t tests, respectively, with Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction. Exploratory adjusted linear models used heteroskedasticity-consistent (HC3) standard errors. The Core Competence in Fundamental Nursing Practicum Scale importance and satisfaction scores showed very high internal consistency (alpha/omega = .987/.987 and .985/.986, respectively), potentially indicating item redundancy. The nursing-process domain received high absolute ratings but fell below both sample grand means; its importance-performance gap was 0.229 (95% CI, 0.179-0.280). Communication and biomedical-science quadrant classifications were unstable across bootstrap samples, indicating sensitivity to the selected crosshairs. Exploratory analyses using the adapted learning-stress questionnaire showed higher reported stress scores among students in the lowest academic-achievement category. However, maximum-likelihood and ordinal diagonally weighted least-squares confirmatory factor analyses did not support the prespecified two-factor structure, and within-cluster dependence could not be modeled. Counseling-history comparisons were descriptive and did not evaluate counseling effectiveness. All 699 participants answered both open-ended questions; after non-substantive entries were excluded from thematic assignment, 217 non-mutually-exclusive segment-to-theme assignments remained. These findings describe students' perceptions and exploratory associations rather than observed competence, validated stress constructs, or causal effects.

title: Performance and carcass traits of nursery, growing, and finishing pigs fed fourth-generation phytase superdoses in diets severely restricted in calcium and phosphorus.
abstract: This study evaluated the effects of increasing inclusion levels of a bacterial phytase in diets with reduced calcium (Ca) and phosphorus (P) on growth performance and carcass traits of pigs across nursery, growing, and finishing phases. A total of 250 pigs (21 days of age; 6.079 ± 0.744 kg) were assigned to a randomized complete block design with five treatments: a positive control (PC), a negative control (NC; -0.18% available P and -0.16% Ca), and NC diets supplemented with 600, 1,200, or 1,800 FYT/kg. During the nursery phase, pigs fed the NC diet showed reduced average daily gain (ADG) and poorer feed conversion ratio (FCR) compared with PC (p < 0.05), whereas phytase supplementation restored performance to levels comparable to PC. Average daily feed intake was not affected (p > 0.05). In the growing and finishing phases, performance variables were affected by treatment (p < 0.05), with NC pigs showing lower ADG and worst FCR, while phytase-supplemented pigs performed similarly to PC. Across periods, quadratic responses to phytase inclusion were observed for FCR (p < 0.001), with estimated optimal levels of 1,320 and 1,404 FYT/kg during nursery and growing-finishing phases, respectively. Carcass traits were also affected by dietary treatments (p < 0.05). Pigs fed the NC diet showed lower final body weight (FBW), hot carcass weight (HCW), carcass yield (CY), and lean meat percentage (LMP) compared with PC, whereas phytase supplementation restored these variables to values comparable to PC. Quadratic responses to phytase inclusion were observed for FBW (p = 0.004), HCW (p < 0.001), CY (p = 0.028), and LMP (p < 0.001), with estimated optimal inclusion levels of 1,377, 1,324, 1,416, and 1,246 FYT/kg, respectively. In conclusion, phytase supplementation effectively mitigated the negative effects of dietary Ca and P restriction, maintaining growth performance and carcass characteristics comparable to a nutritionally adequate diet across all production phases.

title: Phylogenetic evidence that migratory behavior increases ungulate extinction rates.
abstract: Widespread instances of migratory collapse have been documented within the past several decades, indicating that migration may be a fragile strategy in the Anthropocene. Yet the fragility of migration as a strategy for navigating seasonally variable resource availability may extend deeper into evolutionary time. We used phylogenetic imputation to infer the migratory habits of 51 ungulate species that went extinct during the late Quaternary and evaluated whether migration enhances extinction rates on macroevolutionary timescales. We found that ~80% (41 of 51) of recently extinct species were migratory, whereas only 46% (95 of 207) of extant ungulates are migratory. Furthermore, Hidden State Speciation and Extinction modeling indicated that migratory species likely experienced higher speciation and extinction rates compared to nonmigratory species, resulting in elevated lineage turnover for migratory ungulates, though diversification parameter estimates depended strongly upon whether extinct species were included in analyses. The extinctions of these ungulates led to negligible declines in global ungulate functional richness (0.8%) but more substantial declines (2.7%) across Africa. Altogether, our findings indicate that migration has complex macroevolutionary consequences, enhancing both speciation and extinction rates, which may render migration an evolutionarily fragile strategy, particularly as increasingly widespread and intensive anthropogenic activity cause gradients of resource availability to become severed (e.g., via human infrastructure) and more unpredictable (e.g., via climate change).

title: Polysomnography harmonization schemes: A multi-institutional sleep research resource.
abstract: Sleep disorders are associated with cardiovascular diseases and cognitive decline worldwide, highlighting the need for effective therapeutic strategies. Polysomnography (PSG) is the gold standard diagnostic tool for sleep disorders. However, long examination times, high costs, specialized biosignal equipment and controlled settings requirements hinder large-scale data collection. As artificial intelligence applications in sleep research expand, structural heterogeneity in PSG data across institutions complicates multi-center integration, increases preprocessing burden, and limits reproducible large-scale algorithm validation. We investigated biosignals, sleep parameters, and demographic features from eight publicly available PSG datasets. A set of schemas for PSG harmonization is proposed to formalize unified structural specifications aligned with established clinical guidelines. These schemas systematically integrate heterogeneous biosignals, derived sleep parameters, and demographic features to achieve consistent attribute selection and uniform preprocessing across datasets. When applied to construct an integrated dataset, the schemas demonstrated stable demographic and clinical distributions through repeated sampling. By addressing schema-level interoperability, the proposed framework facilitates consistent algorithm evaluation and comparison and provides a structured reference for reproducible, large-scale sleep research.

title: Potential antimicrobial activity, antioxidant, and anti-wrinkle effects of Linum usitatissimum oil nanoemulgel.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Linum usitatissimum (L. usitatissimum) seeds have been reported to have several biological efficacies, such as antioxidant, anti-aging, sun protection, and antimicrobial actions. The present study aimed to develop L. usitatissimum oil nanoemulgel and evaluate its cosmeceutical and antimicrobial characteristics for use in topical applications.
METHOD: L. usitatissimum oil nanoemulgel formulations were prepared by optimizing the non-ionic surfactant (Tween® 20, Tween® 80, and Span® 80) using a self-nanoemulsifying technique, followed by the addition of Carbopol®. The droplet size, polydispersity index, zeta potential, and rheological behavior of the emulgel formulations were measured. In addition, the antioxidant activity, elastase inhibition activity, sun protection factor (SPF), and antimicrobial properties were evaluated.
RESULTS: The prepared nanoemulgel had a homogenous appearance and a smooth, creamy texture and was found to have good spreadability and an acceptable adhesion to the skin. Tween® 80 gave the optimum nanoemulgel formulation, which had a droplet size of less than 200 nm. The crude L. usitatissimum seed oil was found to possess strong intrinsic antioxidant activity (IC50: 3.15 ± 0.46 µg/ml) when compared to trolox (IC50: 2.21 ± 0.23 µg/ml) and elastase inhibition activity (IC50: 17.3 ± 0.5 µg/ml) when compared with oleanolic acid (IC50: 10.2 ± 0.3 µg/ml), and a sun protection factor (SPF) of 5.87, suggesting significant potential anti-wrinkle and photoprotective properties. When incorporated into the optimized nanoemulgel formulation, the system showed considerably higher antimicrobial activity against S. aureus, MRSA, and C. albicans than the crude oil (p < 0.05). No antibacterial activity was found against E. coli, E. faecium, or S. sonnei.
CONCLUSION: In conclusion, a novel L. usitatissimum oil nanoemulgel was prepared that shows promise for pharmaceutical and cosmeceutical applications.

title: Prevalence and determinants of diarrhoea among children under five years: A pooled facility-based cross-sectional study across three ecological zones in Ghana.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diarrhoea remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality among children under five years in sub-Saharan Africa. Although national estimates are available in Ghana, district-level evidence across different ecological settings is limited. This study estimated the prevalence and determinants of diarrhoea among children under five across three geographically diverse districts in Ghana.
METHODS: A pooled analysis of three facility-based cross-sectional studies was conducted in the Ga West Municipality, Gomoa East District, and Jirapa Municipal District of Ghana. A total of 1,266 caregiver-child pairs (422 per district) were selected using stratified random sampling. Data were collected through structured interviewer-administered questionnaires. The primary outcome was caregiver-reported diarrhoea within six months preceding the survey. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify independent determinants of diarrhoea at both district and pooled levels using STATA version 17.
RESULTS: The pooled prevalence of diarrhoea was 66.4% (95% CI: 63.7-69.0), with marked district variations: 91.7% in Ga West, 72.3% in Gomoa East, and 34.8% in Jirapa.In the pooled multivariable model, children in Gomoa East (AOR = 0.24; 95% CI: 0.12-0.45) and Jirapa (AOR = 0.07; 95% CI: 0.03-0.13) had significantly lower odds of diarrhoea than those in Ga West. Children aged 9-16 months (AOR = 3.47; 95% CI: 1.69-5.47), 17-25 months (AOR = 5.07; 95% CI: 3.05-8.44), and 26-59 months (AOR = 3.63; 95% CI: 2.14-6.14) had higher odds of diarrhoea than infants aged 1-8 months, and unimproved water source was independently associated with increased odds (AOR = 1.99; 95% CI: 1.19-3.36). Protective factors included tertiary education (AOR = 0.33; 95% CI: 0.19-0.57), health insurance enrolment (AOR = 0.60; 95% CI: 0.37-0.95), and availability of handwashing facilities (AOR = 0.53; 95% CI: 0.38-0.74), while caregiver knowledge that handwashing prevents diarrhoea (AOR = 3.44; 95% CI: 1.81-6.54) and rotavirus vaccination (AOR = 3.04; 95% CI: 1.69-5.47) were paradoxically associated with higher odds.
CONCLUSIONS: Diarrhoea burden among children under five remains high and varies considerably across districts in Ghana. Strengthening water, sanitation, and hygiene interventions and targeting vulnerable age groups, and addressing underlying district-level drivers may help reduce the burden of childhood diarrhoea.

title: Research on magnetotelluric signal noise separation based on improved SVD.
abstract: As the impact of cultural noise on magnetotelluric impedance estimation becomes increasingly severe, we propose a magnetotelluric signal-to-noise separation method based on improved Singular Value Decomposition (SVD). Compared to cultural noise, the amplitude of the useful electromagnetic signal is weaker. Based on the difference in amplitude between the noise and the useful signal, the SVD method can separate the noisy components from the original signal. However, traditional SVD struggles to completely extract and remove noise when separating different components, and residual noise often exists at the boundary of noise waveforms. Therefore, by combining the Complementary Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition (CEEMD) to improve the SVD method, the goal of effectively separating useful magnetotelluric signals and cultural noise is achieved. The proposed method is applied to synthetic cases and actual data processing. Compared with traditional SVD and CEEMD, the results showed that the proposed method improved the problem of incomplete noise suppression in the SVD method. It achieved good processing results for large-scale noise and impulse noise in low signal-to-noise ratio data, and can reduce the distortion of the apparent resistivity phase curve. Furthermore, compared with the processing results of traditional robust methods, the proposed method exhibits superior noise resistance and restores smoother response curves.

title: SHOCKING! College professor reveals hidden secrets of news headlines. Can you guess? Examining the efficacy of clickbait detection training and news literacy.
abstract: This study used a survey and an experiment to examine how news literacy and personal locus, which is a competency adjacent to news literacy, affected clickbait detection and engagement with clickbait via clicking, reading, and sharing clickbait headlines and stories. The survey measured the effect of news literacy and the four psychometric personal locus variables (reflective thinking, the tolerance for ambiguity, signal detection, and the drive for information) on detection and engagement with clickbait. The pre- and post-test experiment with a control group measured the effect of clickbait detection training on detection and engagement. Overall, news literacy improved detection and reduced engagement, as did signal detection. Reflective thinking performed likewise via correlation but showed marginal main effects. The tolerance for ambiguity was inversely correlated with engagement, but not with detection, and it only reduced clicking marginally among the individual engagement variables. While the drive for information was not correlated with detection, it increased engagement, thus contradicting extant research. The experiment showed that while clickbait detection training reduced engagement with clickbait, it improved detection only when clickbait headlines were considered, and not when both clickbait and non-clickbait headlines were considered. The author recommends that news literacy training incorporate aspects of personal locus improvement and clickbait detection training.

title: Social jetlag and DXA-derived adiposity in Korean adults: A nationwide study using the 2024 Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Social jetlag, the discrepancy between weekday and weekend sleep timing, is a behavioral marker of circadian timing mismatch and has been linked to obesity, mainly through conventional anthropometric measures. We examined its association with dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA)-derived adiposity using the nationally representative 2024 Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (KNHANES).
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included adults aged ≥40 years reporting usual weekday and weekend bedtimes and wake times. Social jetlag, the absolute difference between weekday and weekend sleep midpoints, was categorized as <1 h, 1- < 2 h, and ≥2 h, with ≥2 h as the primary exposure. The primary outcome was DXA-derived total body fat percentage; subtotal and trunk fat percentages were key secondary outcomes. Height, weight, and waist circumference were obtained by standardized KNHANES examination. Survey-weighted linear regression was adjusted for age, sex, height, average sleep duration, income, education, smoking, alcohol use, physical activity, hypertension, and diabetes.
RESULTS: Among 4,483 participants, 267 (6.0%) had social jetlag ≥2 h. In fully adjusted models, this group had higher total body fat percentage (β = 0.81 percentage points; P = 0.025), subtotal fat percentage (β = 0.86; P = 0.025), and trunk fat percentage (β = 1.01; P = 0.036), but not higher BMI or waist circumference. Associations persisted after adjustment for depressive symptoms, but were attenuated and no longer significant after adjustment for a chronotype-related proxy, and were not reproduced when social jetlag was corrected for sleep debt. Sleep duration variability showed no association.
CONCLUSIONS: Social jetlag ≥2 h was associated with modestly higher DXA-derived total and trunk body fat percentage, differences not captured by BMI or waist circumference. Because the associations did not persist in chronotype-adjusted or sleep-corrected analyses, conventional social jetlag may partly reflect compensatory weekend sleep. These findings are hypothesis-generating and need longitudinal confirmation.

title: Social manipulations trigger shifts in group-level dominance patterns.
abstract: Within dominance hierarchies, individuals often direct aggression based on their own rank and the rank of others. When many group members make the same rank-informed aggression decisions, a broader group-level "dominance pattern" can emerge which further structures aggression within the framework of the dominance hierarchy. However, whether groups can change their group-level dominance patterns over time, and what factors might drive these changes, are not well understood. We investigated aggression dynamics by experimentally manipulating captive groups of monk parakeets (Myiopsitta monachus) using targeted rank-based removals and reintroductions of group members to induce social instability. Dominance patterns often shifted after experimental perturbations but remained stable in their absence. The rank of the perturbed individual affected both individual aggression decisions and the shifts in dominance patterns observed. In particular, reintroductions of top-ranked birds led to marked changes in aggression and shifts in dominance patterns. Understanding the factors that shape these dynamics can help explain how animal societies respond to social disturbance.

title: Spatial variability of soil fertility parameters in Kaski District, Nepal: A geostatistical approach.
abstract: Mapping of soils and depicting spatial variability across agro-ecological regions remains underexplored, especially in Nepal's hilly areas. The current study aimed to assess spatial variability and map key soil properties such as pH, soil organic matter, total nitrogen, available phosphorus, and available potassium across the Kaski district, Nepal. A total of 263 composite, geo-referenced samples from 0-20 cm depth were collected using a proportional random sampling design across different land- use types. Fertility maps were generated using Inverse Distance Weighting (IDW) interpolation in ArcGIS 10.8. Descriptive statistics revealed significant spatial variability among soil parameters, with a coefficient of variation from 15.2% (low) for pH to 137.93% (high) for available phosphorus. Most soils were moderately to strongly acidic with a mean of 5.48 ± 0.004. Soil organic matter, total nitrogen, and available phosphorus showed medium fertility levels (SNI = 1.91, 2.19 & 1.95), whereas available potassium reflected a low soil nutrient index (SNI = 1.61), indicating potassium deficiency. Spatial autocorrelation analysis confirmed significant positive clustering for SOM and potassium, while nitrogen exhibited a random distribution pattern (I = 0.25, z = 1.46, p = 0.14). Trend analysis revealed directional gradients with saddle-shaped curves in pH, SOM, and total nitrogen, influenced by topography, elevation, and fertilizer management practices. This study provides a comprehensive characterization of soil fertility, highlighting fertility constraints and offering insights for precision agriculture and land-use planning aimed at sustainable soil management in the Kaski district of Nepal.

title: Stakeholder perspectives on implementing geographic information systems for leprosy elimination in Pakistan: A qualitative study.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Leprosy remains a pressing global health concern, with Pakistan among countries still facing missed and delayed diagnosis. By highlighting elevated risk areas, Geographic Information Systems (GIS) are a cost-effective solution to improve leprosy case detection by guiding targeted interventions to high-risk areas. This study's purpose was to investigate the perceived GIS implementation facilitators and barriers, to support targeted interventions and advance the Zero Leprosy strategy.
METHODS: Semi-structured interviews were conducted with twelve stakeholders, including local field staff, program managers, and international experts. Thematic analysis was guided by the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) and the Diffusion of Innovation Theory (DOI) to identify facilitators and barriers concerned with GIS implementation for leprosy.
RESULTS: Key facilitators included an integrated multi-disease and pilot-based rollout approach, capacity building activities, offline-capable tools, and improved visibility to drive motivation. Barriers included the limited local capacity in complex GIS data analysis, hybrid digital-manual workflows, historical data lacking GPS, and ensuring feedback and ownership for staff members.
CONCLUSION: GIS implementation is not only dependent on individual readiness, but also on broader external and organizational facilitators and constraints. This necessitates holistic implementation strategies that recognize the interconnectedness of different parts of the system. Internal capacity building is paramount to address statistical complexity and to build trust, ownership, and independence. As the world moves closer to achieving Zero Leprosy, integrating GIS within a multi-disease approach will be critical to making sustainable progress in combatting neglected tropical diseases.

title: Study on hydration cementation and enhancement mechanism of grout-rock interface of PVA modified grouting material.
abstract: The weakly cemented sandstone aquifer in coal mine is prone to particle softening under mining disturbance and water-rock interaction, which induces the decrease of rock integrity and the development of water conducting channel, leading to the instability and failure of aquifer. To address the low early-age hydration activity of grouts containing a high proportion of coal gangue, discontinuous grout-rock interfacial bonding, and limited adaptability to weakly cemented sandstone, this paper uses cement and coal gangue(CG) as raw materials to prepare modified grouting materials with different polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) content. The uniaxial compression, XRD, FTIR and SEM test methods were used to systematically study the influence of PVA content on the performance of solid waste based slurry, the bearing characteristics of slurry-rock composite, the evolution of hydration products and the interface micro structure. The synergistic enhancement mechanism of PVA induced hydration cementation film coating and slurry-rock interface was revealed. The results show that: (1) High content of CG weakens the early hydration activity of cement slurry system. After PVA is added, the fluidity of slurry increases, the initial and final setting time is further prolonged, and the bleeding rate decreases, indicating that PVA can improve the flow stability and water retention performance of coal-based solid waste slurry. (2) PVA content has obvious dosage dependence on the bearing capacity of the grout rock complex. The peak stresses of the 0%, 0.3%, 0.6% and 1.0% PVA groups are 4.87 ± 0.14 MPa, 5.35 ± 0.06 MPa, 6.04 ± 0.09 MPa and 5.12 ± 0.09 MPa, respectively. The 0.6% PVA group shows relatively better mechanical properties within the test range of this paper. (3) Appropriate amount of PVA can promote the filling of C-S-H gel, AFt rod crystals and C-H flake crystals on the surface of sandstone particles and in the pores and fracture, and adsorb and coordinate through hydroxyl groups to form hydration products and flexible polymer film. The hydration products provide a rigid skeleton, and the PVA flexible film plays a buffering role in the interface bonding and deformation, and synergistically realizes the densification, continuity and toughness enhancement of the weakly cemented sandstone-grout interface. The experimental results show that 0.6% PVA content can achieve a better balance between slurry performance, water retention stability, interface hydration cementation and mechanical bearing capacity, which can provide material design basis for grouting reinforcement of weakly cemented aquifer, thickening of aquiclude and prevention and control of mining-induced water disasters.

title: Summer seasonal precipitation prediction in the middle and lower reaches of the Yangtze River using neural network approaches.
abstract: Accurate prediction of summer precipitation is essential for agricultural planning and flood prevention. However, precipitation is strongly nonlinear. In the middle and lower reaches of the Yangtze River (MLYR), many interacting factors and large interannual variability make conventional forecasting methods unreliable. This study proposes neural network approaches to address this challenge. We select independent predictors from 130 circulation indices of the National Climate Center (NCC) and from the ERA5 monthly dataset, including sea surface temperature (SST), 500 hPa geopotential height, and land surface variables. Predictors are chosen through correlation, partial correlation, and autocorrelation analyses. They are then processed with detrended fluctuation analysis (DFA), standardization, and normalization. Four models are trained: a back propagation (BP) network, a gated recurrent unit (GRU) network, a coupled BP-GRU network, and a particle swarm optimization (PSO)-optimized coupled BP-GRU network. A strict chronological split is used (training: 1980-2000; validation: 2001-2010; testing: 2011-2024). Results are reported as the mean ± standard deviation over ten independent runs. The PSO-optimized coupled network performs best (test MSE = 0.0177 ± 0.0106; spatial correlation r = 0.44). It outperforms the standalone GRU (MSE = 0.0207 ± 0.0003), the coupled BP-GRU (MSE = 0.0357 ± 0.0175), and the standalone BP model (MSE = 0.0447 ± 0.0212). It is also the only network to beat the climatological baseline (MSE = 0.0181). The GRU is the most stable across runs but reproduces spatial patterns poorly. Overall, combining recurrent architectures with physical predictors through evolutionary optimization improves seasonal prediction. However, all models show limited skill (R2 near zero), reflecting the difficulty of this task. The approach offers a reference for flood-season forecasting in the MLYR, with potential use in agriculture and flood prevention.

title: Ten simple rules for a successful global health roundtable.
abstract: Qualitative approaches play a critical role in global health research by capturing the social, political, and contextual dimensions that shape health outcomes. While interviews and focus groups are widely used, these methods are often time‑limited and project‑specific. Global health roundtables offer a complementary approach, providing a flexible and long-term platform for engaging diverse stakeholders-including researchers, practitioners, policymakers, and community representatives-in collective dialogue, knowledge exchange, and collaboration. When designed well, roundtables can support co‑production of knowledge, address complex system‑level challenges, and generate insights with relevance beyond a single event. Despite their growing use, practical guidance on how to design and run roundtables specifically for global health remains limited. In this article, we present ten simple rules for organising successful global health roundtables, drawing on existing literature, practice‑based experience, and examples from different geopolitical and health‑system contexts. The rules address key stages of the roundtable lifecycle, including topic selection, objective setting, inclusive participation, management of power dynamics, optimisation of engagement and commitment, ethical recognition of contributions, and translation of dialogue into meaningful outputs and sustained collaboration. Together, these rules provide an accessible framework to support researchers, practitioners, and policy actors in using roundtables as ethical, inclusive, and impactful tools for global health research, policy development, and practice.

title: The effects on investor sentiment and business cycles on the systematic risk of an ESG portfolio.
abstract: In this study, we analyze the time varying nature of the systematic risk of an ESG portfolio to common sources of systematic risk. We model the conditional covariances and variances of different sources of systematic risk such as the world stock index, risk aversion as a proxy for investment sentiment (fear), and changes in interest rates. Afterwards, we test for sources of transmission of volatility to ESG systematic risk by controlling for different stages of the business cycle and rising interest rates. Our main finding is that investment sentiment (fear) is not a statistically significant source of systematic risk to the ESG portfolio in the expansion phases of the business cycle but becomes highly relevant in the trough and recession phases and during periods of rising interest rates.

title: The form of density-dependence in host growth impacts parasitoid-driven host suppression.
abstract: Leveraging the discrete-time formalism of the Nicholson-Bailey model, we investigate the ecological population dynamics of host-parasitoid interactions with an arbitrary form of density-dependence in the host growth rate, and map out regimes allowing stable coexistence of the consumer (parasitoid) and the resource (host). If the parasitoid-free host population dynamics is stable, we provide sufficient conditions that ensure stability is maintained with the inclusion of the parasitoid irrespective of the level of parasitism. When parasitoids parasitize hosts at a constant rate, high parasitism levels are shown to always destabilize the population dynamics. This results in a limit of host suppression that we quantify using the ratio of host density (just before stability is lost for high parasitism levels) and the host's parasitoid-free carrying capacity. We systematically examine this limit for different types of intrinsic self-limitations in host growth. Our analysis shows that for both Ricker and Beverton-Holt-type host population dynamics, this parasitoid-driven host suppression limit is 33% for slow-growing hosts and 10-20% for fast-growing hosts. Moreover, our results reveal that these limits can be much higher for Hill-type density-dependence in host growth rate. In summary, this contribution characterizes the impact of coupling different forms of intrinsic host population dynamics with and without additional stabilizing factors (such as a fraction of hosts protected from parasitism). These results have important implications for using parasitoids as natural enemies against arthropod pest populations, and the success of such biological control is inherently tied to the form of self-limitation in host growth.

title: The impact of robot-assisted frameless brain biopsy on performance differences between junior and senior neurosurgeons.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Frameless stereotactic brain biopsy is a standardized and routinely performed neurosurgical procedure, frequently carried out by residents under supervision in academic centers. Robot-assisted (RA) guidance has been introduced to standardize workflow and reduce operator-dependent variability. This study investigates whether RA frameless biopsy reduces experience-related performance differences between residents and attending neurosurgeons compared with a manually operated frameless system (MFS).
METHODS: We performed a retrospective, non-randomized cohort study of consecutive patients undergoing RA frameless stereotactic brain biopsy for intracranial lesions at a tertiary academic center between 2021 and 2025. Outcomes included perioperative complications, diagnostic yield, and operative time, stratified by surgeon experience level (residents vs. attendings). Results were compared with those of a cohort operated with a MFS.
RESULTS: A total of 98 procedures were analyzed (49 RA, 49 MFS). Across the entire cohort, total operative time was longer with RA than with MFS (115.6 ± 34.1 vs. 97.9 ± 27.2 minutes; p = 0.0036), primarily due to longer setup times. Diagnostic yield and complication rates were comparable between systems. Importantly, subgroup analysis demonstrated that residents using RA achieved operative times, diagnostic yield, and complication rates comparable to attending surgeons. In the MFS cohort, total operative time did not differ significantly between residents and attendings.
CONCLUSIONS: RA-assisted biopsy was associated with comparable diagnostic accuracy and safety relative to MFS. Robotic assistance was associated with smaller observed differences in operative efficiency between residents and attending surgeons, suggesting a potential role in bridging experience-related performance differences during neurosurgical training.

title: The influence of arm swing constraint on thigh kinematics, heart rate response, and perceived exertion during the two-minute step test.
abstract: Holding a smartphone against the thigh provides a simple means of instrumenting the Two-Minute Step Test (2MST), but it constrains arm swing and may affect movement, cardiovascular responses, and perceived exertion. This study examined whether holding a smartphone against the thigh during the 2MST alters thigh kinematics, heart rate response, or perceived exertion in healthy young adults. Forty-five participants (27 men and 18 women; 19.5 ± 2.6 years) performed the 2MST under two counterbalanced conditions: unrestricted arm swing, with the smartphone secured to the right thigh using an elastic pouch, and constrained arm swing, with the smartphone held against the right thigh and the opposite hand placed on the contralateral thigh. Smartphone gyroscope data were used to determine step cycles, mean thigh peak angular velocity, cycle duration, variability, and the rate of change in thigh peak angular velocity. Heart rate response and perceived exertion were also recorded. Paired comparisons were performed using appropriate tests with Bonferroni correction. Step cycle counts were similar between constrained and unrestricted conditions (131 ± 20 vs 127 ± 19 cycles; p = 0.091). Mean thigh peak angular velocity, cycle duration, rate of change in thigh peak angular velocity, cycle duration variability, and heart rate response did not differ between conditions. Thigh peak angular velocity variability was higher in the constrained condition (p < 0.01; effect size = 0.68). Perceived exertion was also slightly higher in the constrained condition (12.6 ± 1.8 vs 11.9 ± 2.1; p = 0.024), but the difference was below the minimal detectable change threshold. These findings indicate that holding a smartphone against the thigh does not meaningfully alter overall 2MST performance, most thigh kinematic outcomes, or heart rate response, supporting this practical smartphone-based protocol.

title: The surgical outcome among children with congenital pseudoarthrosis of Tibia: Our 12 years of experience.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Congenital Pseudoarthrosis of the Tibia (CPT) is a rare condition characterized by poorly perfused, invasive hamartomatous fibrous tissue that leads to fracture and pseudoarthrosis of the tibia. Management challenges include achieving union and preventing refractures. This study aims to evaluate surgical interventions and their outcomes in managing congenital pseudoarthrosis of the tibia in children.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study reviewed 70 CPT cases treated between 2010 and 2022 at Nepal's only specialized center for children with physical disabilities. It assessed demographics, surgical procedures, and outcomes, with techniques including periosteal grafting and the Masquelet method. Union was defined radiologically, and analyses were conducted using MS Excel and SPSS.
RESULTS: This study included 70 CPT patients; 40 male (57.1%) and 30 female (42.9%). The mean age at presentation was 3.84 years, with the first surgery at 5.38 years. Most cases were Boyd type 5 (71.43%) and Crawford type 4 (71.43%). Of 35 patients who underwent surgery, the union rate was 41.93% (13/31), with a refracture rate of 23.08% among unions. Periosteal grafting had a 50% union rate, while the Masquelet technique achieved 41.67%.
CONCLUSIONS: This study highlights the challenges in managing Congenital Pseudoarthrosis of the Tibia (CPT), emphasizing the need for personalized surgical approaches based on patient age, limb length discrepancy, and classification. Effective patient counseling on risks and benefits is crucial for informed decisions.

title: Three-dimensional characteristics analysis of maglev train with rotating operation conditions.
abstract: Traction, suspension and guidance are characteristics of core electromagnetic performance of high-speed maglev. When the vehicle passes through curves or uneven ground, it is prone to generating significant three-dimensional (3-D) force fluctuations, which have a significant impact on the safety and stability of the maglev. This paper will discuss the effects of transient motion states on the suspension force, traction force and guidance force of maglev. First, general topology and 3-D distribution of electromagnetic forces of system is described. Then, force expressions in 3-D state are developed analytically taking into account the body translation and rotation. Lastly, the variation of force during the roll, pitch and lateral deviation under conditions are tested. The relevant conclusions indicate that the multi-degree-of-freedom motion of the vehicle will change the fluctuation values of 3-D electromagnetic forces, necessitating a magnetic levitation power device with a relatively large electromagnetic stiffness value, the design of a magnetic levitation power device requires a relatively large electromagnetic stiffness value.

title: TriTower-m6Am: A triple-tower heterogeneous deep learning architecture integrating semantic, sequential, and structural information for mRNA N6,2'-O-dimethyladenosine site prediction.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: N6,2'-O-dimethyladenosine (m6Am) is a cap-proximal mRNA modification deposited by PCIF1 (phosphorylated C-terminal domain (CTD)-interacting factor 1) at the first transcribed nucleotide of eukaryotic mRNAs. Knowing where m6Am sites sit would help explain how cells tune mRNA stability and translation, but current predictors typically depend on a single representation and do not jointly model multiple views of the same RNA sequence.
RESULTS: We present TriTower-m6Am, combining semantic (RNA-FM, a pretrained RNA foundation model, with BellPooling), sequential (One-Hot BiLSTM, bidirectional long short-term memory), and structural (RGCN, a relational graph convolutional network, over the 41-nt window) representations of each RNA window. On an independent test set of 640 sequences, TriTower-m6Am reaches an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.776 and a Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of 0.425, against DTC-m6Am's AUC = 0.765 and MCC = 0.411, using 4.4 times fewer trainable parameters; at every matched specificity between 0.40 and 0.70 it recovers 1-7 more true sites out of 320 than DTC-m6Am. The AUC-weighted voting keeps every tower's contribution readable for any individual prediction. Analyses of the graph tower delimit its benefit to the relational aggregation of local backbone adjacency over sequence-derived node features: the edge-type ablation, the node-feature ablation, and a structure-permutation control agree that the specific RNAfold-predicted fold carries no attributable signal, and a probing analysis shows that per-base base-pairing status is largely recoverable from the sequence-derived RNA-FM embeddings (AUC = 0.72 vs. 0.65 from the raw sequence), so the fold annotation is substantially redundant with the semantic representation the ensemble already receives.
CONCLUSIONS: Combining semantic, sequential, and structural views of the same RNA sequence improves m6Am prediction beyond any single representation, and the ensemble's voting weights make each prediction auditable without a post-hoc explainer. Whether the triple-tower pattern transfers to other RNA modification prediction tasks remains to be tested in future work.

title: Two parallel lateral hypothalamic GABAergic projections differentially modulate pain and anxiety in mice.
abstract: The lateral hypothalamus (LH) is fundamentally involved in motivated behaviors, yet the precise functional segregation of its GABAergic projections in modulating pain and its affective dimensions remains poorly understood. Here, using male and female mice, we revealed that LH GABAergic neurons sent parallel projections to two pivotal pain and affect processing centers: the lateral parabrachial nucleus (LPB) and the paraventricular nucleus of the thalamus (PVT). In vivo fiber photometry revealed that LH GABAergic terminals in both the PVT and LPB are robustly activated by noxious, aversive, and rewarding stimuli, indicating their roles in encoding salient and affective information. Critically, we uncovered a remarkable functional segregation of these LH GABAergic pathways. Optogenetic activation of the LH-PVT projection exerted anxiogenic effects without altering pain sensitivity in both naïve and neuropathic pain mice; whereas optogenetic inhibition of this pathway exerted significant analgesic and anxiolytic effects specifically in neuropathic pain, highlighting a context-dependent modulation of pain and affect. In contrast, optogenetic activation of the LH-LPB projection induced contralateral pronociception without impacting affective behaviors, conversely, inhibition of this pathway significantly elevated contralateral pain thresholds in both physiological and neuropathic pain conditions. We also demonstrated that stimulation of the LH-LPB projection acted via a disinhibitory mechanism involving local LPB GABAergic interneurons to enhance activity of LPB glutamatergic neurons. Collectively, our findings delineate two parallel and functionally segregated LH GABAergic output pathways that differentially control distinct aspects of pain experience, thereby offering novel circuit-specific targets for the treatment of chronic pain and its debilitating emotional comorbidities.

title: Unveiling Molecular Basis of Terminalia chebula in Modulating the AGE-RAGE-PRKCB Axis in Diabetic Nephropathy: Integrative Network Pharmacology and Computational Study.
abstract: AbstractDiabetic nephropathy (DN), a progressive microvascular complication of diabetes, remains a principal cause of renal failure worldwide, yet its multifaceted molecular complexity continues to challenge effective therapeutic intervention. In this study, an integrative network pharmacology and computational modeling framework was employed to unravel the mechanistic basis of Terminalia chebula in mitigating DN pathology. A total of 357 phytoconstituents were retrieved from the IMPPAT 2.0 and PubChem databases and screened through SwissADME and pkCSM, yielding 14 bioactive, drug-like, and non-toxic compounds. Target prediction integrated data from SwissTargetPrediction, BindingDB, and CTD, while DN-related genes were compiled from GeneCards, OMIM, and transcriptomic datasets (GSE154561, GSE154881, GSE217709, and GSE30528). Overlapping targets were analyzed using STRING and Cytoscape to identify key hub proteins, followed by Gene Ontology (GO) and KEGG enrichment analysis. Integration of compound- and disease-associated targets identified 173 overlapping genes. Enrichment analyses revealed significant involvement in the AGE-RAGE signaling pathway, implicating PRKCB as a key regulatory node linking hyperglycemia to oxidative stress, inflammation, and apoptosis. The Random Forest-based QSAR model (R2 = 0.91, RMSE = 0.41) denoted Luteolin and Quercetin as potent PRKCB inhibitors (predicted pIC₅₀ ≥ 6). Docking and molecular dynamics simulations confirmed stable PRKCB binding (RMSD ≤ 3.0 Å; ΔG_bind ≈ -122 kcal/mol), supported by DFT analysis indicating high chemical softness and strong charge-transfer potential. This integrative computational analysis suggests that T. chebula may exert renoprotective effects through modulation of the PRKCB-driven AGE-RAGE axis, with luteolin and quercetin emerging as promising natural inhibitors. Therefore, these computational findings provide potential molecular insight into the traditional therapeutic efficacy of T. chebula and a foundation for further experimental validation in DN.

title: Women's experiences of emergency post-abortion care at Kawempe National Referral Hospital, Uganda: A qualitative descriptive study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-abortion care (PAC) encompasses emergency treatment, counselling, contraceptive services, and referral linkages. Emergency post-abortion care (EPAC), the life-saving component of PAC, addresses acute abortion-related complications, including haemorrhage, sepsis, retained products of conception, and severe pain. In Uganda, where abortion is legally restricted and socially stigmatised, women's care experiences are shaped by clinical urgency, fear, moral vulnerability, provider interactions, and structural health system constraints. Despite EPAC's centrality to maternal survival, qualitative evidence on how women interpret and evaluate their care experiences in referral hospital settings in Uganda remains limited. This study explored women's experiences of EPAC at Kawempe National Referral Hospital (KNRH) and identified the factors that shaped those experiences.
METHODS: A qualitative descriptive design employing inductive thematic analysis was used. Sixteen in-depth interview transcripts from women who received EPAC at KNRH in March-April 2026 were analysed. The Socio-Ecological Model (SEM) was subsequently applied as a post-hoc organising framework to situate findings across individual, interpersonal, facility, and community levels.
RESULTS: Six themes were identified: (1) survival and physical relief as the immediate measure of good care; (2) pain, fear, and emotional distress during treatment; (3) reassurance and support as buffers against vulnerability; (4) dignity under pressure: communication and privacy in EPAC; (5) structural barriers across the pathway of care; and (6) experiences beyond discharge: incomplete recovery and uncertainty. Care was frequently evaluated through the lens of survival, yet these accounts co-existed with intense procedural pain, compromised privacy, delays, financial burden, and inadequate post-discharge support. EPAC at KNRH was experienced as a complex encounter shaped by bodily vulnerability, interpersonal dynamics, and system-level constraints.
CONCLUSIONS: Strengthening EPAC requires patient-centred approaches that integrate clinical effectiveness with respectful communication, pain management, improved triage, and structured post-discharge support.

title: Atypical phenylalanine ammonia-lyases that enhance phenylpropanoid production in plants.
abstract: Plants synthesize diverse phenylpropanoids, which provide us essential medicine, nutrients, and biomaterials while also acting as a major global carbon sink. Phenylpropanoids are primarily derived from L-phenylalanine (Phe) via Phe ammonia-lyase (PAL), a highly regulated enzymatic activity that limits phenylpropanoid production. However, it remains poorly understood how different plant species regulate PAL enzymes. Phylogeny-guided biochemical screening uncovered complex and diverse feedback regulation of PAL enzymes from 14 different plant species. This screening found a previously uncharacterized PAL clade, namely PALnc (from noncanonical), with some members exhibiting feedback activation by p-coumaric acid, caffeic acid, and 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvic acid in vitro. Transient expression of two PALnc genes, from Elaeis guineensis (EgPALnc) and Piper methysticum (PmPALnc2), in Nicotiana benthamiana leaves elevated phenylpropanoid content, supported by the high in planta stability of PALnc proteins compared to canonical PALs. Whereas overexpression of Arabidopsis thaliana PAL1 (AtPAL1) in stable Arabidopsis transgenic lines resulted in very low accumulation of AtPAL1 protein and minor metabolic effects, introduction of EgPALnc rendered high content of EgPALnc protein and hyperaccumulation of hydroxycinnamates derivatives. Our findings uncover a previously overlooked diversity in the regulation of the entry step of phenylpropanoid biosynthesis across various plants and identify atypical PALs within the PALnc clade as valuable tools to debottleneck and enhance phenylpropanoid production in planta.

title: Dysregulation of mechanosensing signaling in monocytes of patients with systemic sclerosis is associated with skin inflammation.
abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a severe autoimmune connective tissue disease characterized by immune dysregulation and progressive fibrosis of the skin and internal organs, resulting in substantial organ dysfunction and increased mortality. Fibrosis is driven in part by infiltration of immune cells, including monocytes that become activated within fibrotic tissue. However, how the mechanical properties of fibrotic skin regulate their function remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that increased stiffness activates human monocytes through mechanosensing. Reanalysis of single cell RNA sequencing datasets revealed that skin infiltrating monocytes exhibit heightened inflammatory signatures as compared to circulating counterparts, with further amplification in SSc. Using collagen-coated hydrogels modeling physiological and fibrotic stiffness, we show that increased stiffness enhances CD86 expression, and broadly upregulates inflammatory transcriptional programs in human monocytes. Mechanistically, stiffness-driven activation was associated with chromatin remodeling and epigenetic reprogramming, identifying the transcription factor Specificity Protein 1 (SP1) as a central regulator. CRISPR-Cas9-mediated disruption or pharmacologic inhibition of SP1 significantly attenuated stiffness- induced inflammatory gene expression, whereas we found no evidence for involvement of the canonical YAP/TAZ-TEAD axis, and pharmacological modulation of PIEZO1 neither reproduced nor blocked the response. Further, monocytes from patients with SSc displayed altered transcriptional trajectories and an exaggerated inflammatory response to high stiffness, accompanied by reduced expression of wound healing and antifibrotic programs. Together, these findings identify SP1-dependent mechanosensing as a previously unrecognized pathway controlling human monocyte activation in the skin and provide mechanistic insight into how tissue stiffness sustains inflammation in SSc.

title: In-group neural alignment serves as a biomarker of social identity.
abstract: In this study, we propose a perspective on neural synchronization. Beyond reflecting shared understanding between individuals, we suggest it serves as a biological marker of social homogeneity. We examined fMRI neural responses of 42 participants (21 religious, 21 secular) watching neutral and religion-relevant video narratives. While explicit measures of emotional response, agreement, and engagement showed no significant differences in within-group variance, religious participants-representing a tighter social structure-exhibited significantly higher in-group neural synchrony across all content types and brain networks. Remarkably, synchrony values predicted religious orientation with an accuracy of up to 92%. We conclude that a community's homogeneous social structure drives pervasive neural alignment, positioning neural synchrony as a potential signature of group cohesion beyond explicit behavioral measures.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Intermittent gas-liquid rearrangement controls the mixing of gases in porous media.
abstract: Gas mixing in porous media governs important environmental and industrial applications in which multiple gas components share the available pore space with liquid water, simultaneously undergoing gas mixing and gas-liquid redistribution. Currently, this process is represented by macroscopic models that ignore pore scale dynamics. We demonstrate that this is not generally valid, and can lead to large errors in the mixing rate. We use 4D X-ray imaging to investigate nitrogen injection into a porous sandstone saturated with krypton and water, jointly imaging the gas mixture composition evolution and multiphase flow of gas and water. In contrast to the smooth, continuous representation of the conventional advection-diffusion model, our results show that gas mixing evolves through a sequence of distinct regimes controlled by gas connectivity. Initially, immiscible gas-water displacement generates gas composition variance as the different gases occupy neighboring pores separated by water. As gas connectivity increases, intermittent gas-liquid interfacial rearrangements rapidly connect regions of contrasting gas composition, driving a fast decay in composition variance. Once connectivity stabilizes, mixing is controlled by a confined diffusion process within the quasi-static gas network. At later times, further mixing is driven slowly by multicomponent Ostwald ripening, whereby trapped gas ganglia exchange solutes through the surrounding liquid phase. These findings provide insights into gas mixing in porous media, suggesting concepts for upscaling the role of pore scale multiphase flow in gas mixing in the subsurface.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Majorana edge reconstruction and the ν = 5/2 non-Abelian thermal Hall puzzle.
abstract: Pioneering thermal transport measurements on two-dimensional electron gases in high magnetic fields have demonstrated that the quantized Hall state at filling factor ν = 5/2 has a thermal Hall conductance κ quantized in half-integer multiples of [Formula: see text]. Half-integer [Formula: see text] is a signature of neutral Majorana edge modes, in turn linked to the presence of non-Abelian anyon excitations in the bulk. However, the experimentally observed value of κ corresponds to the "PH-Pfaffian" state, in tension with numerical studies which instead favor either the Pfaffian or the AntiPfaffian. A variety of mechanisms have been invoked to explain this discrepancy, but have been either ruled out by further experiments or else involve fine-tuning. Building on density-matrix-renormalization group studies of physically realistic edges and analytic calculations of edge structure, we propose an alternative resolution of this puzzle involving an "edge reconstruction" solely involving the neutral Majorana sector of the theory. Such a Majorana edge reconstruction can "screen" a Pfaffian or AntiPfaffian bulk, so that transport signatures become indistinguishable from those of the PH-Pfaffian. We argue that this physically natural scenario is consistent with experiment.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Normalized Raman imaging for studies of tissue physiology of the kidney.
abstract: Conventional histology relies on fixation, embedding, sectioning, and staining methods that distort cellular architecture, extract lipids, and introduce variability, limiting reproducibility. We present a pipeline for automated histopathology in the mouse kidney using normalized stimulated Raman imaging (NoRI) that enables quantitative, label-free protein and lipid measurements at high spatial resolution. NoRI computationally corrects protein, lipid, and water Raman signals, allowing quantitative biomass measurements while preserving tissue architecture, facilitating analysis by convolutional neural networks (CNN) for quantitative, morphological feature extraction. Applied to mouse kidney, CNN analysis of NoRI images was able to accurately classify tubule types (F1=0.93; harmonic mean of precision and recall against immunofluorescence-defined labels), anatomical regions (F1 = 0.91), and biological sex (F1 = 0.97), revealing greater cytoplasmic lipid (+6.5 to 7.3 mg/mL; P ≤ 0.028) and nuclear protein (+26.3 mg/mL; P ≤ 0.001) in female tubules. Using acute kidney injury (AKI) in mice as a disease model to test our histopathology pipeline combining NoRI and CNNs, we captured dynamic lipid and protein organization and quantified brush border remodeling and lipid droplet changes over 25 d postinjury. Spatial lipid quantification was central for feature classification in AKI (F1 = 0.99). Quantitative NoRI images also significantly outperformed equivalent raw stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) images in distinguishing early time points (24 to 48 h) of ischemia-reperfusion injury [F1 = 0.99 (NoRI) vs. 0.84 (SRS); P < 0.0001], demonstrating the improvement of NoRI over conventional SRS imaging. These results establish our pipeline, which combines NoRI imaging with advanced CNN analyses, as a reproducible, quantitative method for histopathology and feature discovery.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Polarized twin walls in a halide perovskite.
abstract: Halide perovskites have emerged as promising materials for next-generation photovoltaics, laser sources, and X-ray detectors. There is intense debate as to whether some photoactive halide perovskites exhibit ferroelectric behavior and whether it might be possible to utilize the bulk photovoltaic effect to enhance the performance of halide perovskite solar cells. Here, using low-dose scanning transmission electron microscopy, we identify ferroelastic twin walls in vapor-deposited CsPbI3 thin films, parallel to {110} and {112}. Remarkably, despite CsPbI3 being centrosymmetric and nonpolar, we observe directly that Pb atoms shift at {110} twin walls driving a local ferroelectric-like polarization. These polar twin walls form an intrinsic array of nanoscale interfaces, spaced ~30 to 50 nm apart, embedded within the nonpolar perovskite lattice. In contrast, {112} twin walls do not show a polar displacement of Pb but strongly suppress octahedral tilt and off-center Cs atom displacements, revealing a different untapped structural degree of freedom. These findings reveal previously hidden nanoscale polarization in halide perovskite semiconductors, opening opportunities for enhanced conductivity and photovoltaic behavior through domain wall engineering.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Some theoretical limitations of t-SNE.
abstract: t-distributed Stochastic Neighborhood Embedding (t-SNE) has gained popularity as a dimension reduction technique, especially for visualizing data. It is well-known that dimension reduction may lose important data features. We provide a mathematical framework for understanding this loss for t-SNE, establishing several quantitative results across different scenarios that demonstrate how important structural information is lost.

title: Trust as a hidden driver of epidemic-relevant behavior: Institution- and behavior-specific associations across 20 national survey waves.
abstract: Compartmental models of infectious disease transmission make assumptions about human behaviors. Specifically, they parameterize interactions across population groups, assumed to have distinct epidemiologically relevant behavioral patterns, primarily through contact matrices stratified by demographic variables such as age, gender, or socioeconomic status. Although such demographic characteristics are readily measurable, they may inadequately capture the social and psychological forces that govern protective behaviors. Drawing on 20 waves of a national survey conducted throughout the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States, we show that institutional trust-particularly trust in public health agencies, physicians, and hospitals-is a dominant predictor of protective behavior adoption. For mask wearing during periods of strongest pandemic activity, institutional trust explains more behavioral difference across population groups than age, income, education, and partisan affiliation combined. In unadjusted analyses, the difference in protective behavior adoption between individuals with the highest and lowest trust in the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) was four- to six-fold larger than the corresponding differences by age, income, or education, and exceeded the difference between Democratic and Republican respondents. This association was institutionally specific (the relationship attenuates for trust in banks), and behaviorally specific (trust in the CDC is associated with protective behaviors but not visiting a doctor). The latter suggests that trust modifies voluntary compliance with public health recommendations rather than healthcare access or use. These findings identify institutional trust as a candidate stratifying variable for models of behavior-coupled transmission dynamics, and as a measurable target for public health surveillance.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Denoising the US Census: Succinct block hierarchical regression.
abstract: The 2020 United States Census adopted differential privacy to protect individual confidentiality, adding calibrated noise to summary demographic measurements that are then reconciled into population tables. We developed BlueDown, a postprocessing algorithm that combines techniques from linear regression and constrained optimization while exploiting measurement structure for efficiency. On 2020 Census data, BlueDown reduced the error of groupings by race at the county level by 21 to 36% and of all county-level groupings by 9 to 58%; at the tract level, it reduced error of groupings by housing type by 38 to 61%. These gains came at no cost to confidentiality or computational efficiency and would improve the validity of research relying on this definitive dataset and analyses used to guide the distribution of more than $1.5 trillion in annual federal spending.

title: Direct evidence for psychoactive cannabis use 2800 years ago.
abstract: Cannabis is the world's most-used illicit psychoactive plant, yet direct prehistoric evidence for its consumption is rare. In this study, we present the earliest direct evidence of cannabis use: offerings of plant parts and chemical compounds in ancient human hair recovered from a monumental tomb in Siberia. The findings suggest that the plant was used for its psychoactive qualities across Eurasia, where specific wild populations might have had naturally higher active compound levels. We show that the practice of cannabis consumption dates back at least 2800 years, anchoring debates around contemporary usage and informing discussions on cannabis in medicine, public health, law, and industry.

title: Discovering molecular modulators with nanoswitch screening.
abstract: Molecules that modulate protein-protein interactions, including through ternary complex formation, have been established as key therapeutics. Yet they can be challenging to discover, as standard screening approaches often lack throughput or fail to directly assay multibody interactions. We addressed this by combining DNA nanoswitch-based selection of nucleotide-encoded libraries with next-generation sequencing to create FIND (Functional Interaction-based Nanoswitch Discovery), which enables ultrahigh-throughput discovery of compounds that induce or increase protein-protein interactions. We demonstrate FIND by discovering nanobodies that stabilize the interaction between angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 and the receptor-binding domain of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 and by discovering agonists of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma from a DNA-barcoded small-molecule library. By enabling rapid discovery of molecular modulators, FIND could lead to new therapeutics across many conditions.

title: Echoes of the Anthropocene: Noise pollution as a global threat.
abstract: Anthropogenic noise is a rapidly expanding global pollutant, but its effects across biological levels from individuals to ecosystems remain unquantified. We conducted phylogenetically controlled meta-analyses of 214 experimental studies on 177 aquatic and terrestrial species with ranges that span six continents. Noise altered at least one physiological, developmental, or behavioral trait in 80% of species studied, with declines in fitness and abundance and disruptions of predator-prey interactions. Effects occurred in every habitat, although response mechanisms varied for some traits and species, creating winners and losers. Only multispecies analyses can reveal such species- and ecosystem-level impacts of anthropogenic stressors. Our results establish noise as a novel selection pressure reshaping ecosystem dynamics and as a pervasive stressor requiring soundscape protection alongside habitat conservation.

title: Equivalence of pseudogap and pairing energy in a cuprate high-temperature superconductor.
abstract: The pseudogap stands out in the phase diagram of the cuprate high-temperature superconductors because its origin and relationship to superconductivity remain elusive. The origin of the pseudogap has been debated, with competing hypotheses attributing it to preformed electron pairs or local order, such as charge density waves. We present unambiguous evidence supporting the pairing scenario, using local shot-noise spectroscopy measurements in Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+δ. Our data demonstrate that the pseudogap energy coincides with the onset of electron pairing and is spatially heterogeneous with values reaching up to 70 milli-electron volts. Our results exclude a pure local order origin of the pseudogap, link the pseudogap to Cooper pair formation, and suggest that the limiting factor for higher critical temperature in cuprates is phase coherence.

title: Glacial abrupt transitions in ocean circulation were much slower than ice-core records imply.
abstract: Dansgaard-Oeschger (DO) events during the last ice age are thought to reflect rapid shifts in the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC). Greenland ice cores suggest warming transitions within only a few decades-or even just over 10 years. Using precisely dated speleothem oxygen-isotope records from the Asian monsoon region, we have shown that the same DO warmings unfolded over more than a century. Isotope modeling revealed that Greenland records primarily capture a rapid atmospheric reorganization triggered by the initial sea-ice retreat in the northeastern North Atlantic, whereas the parallel AMOC recovery and hemispheric thermal adjustment proceeded much more slowly. These findings reveal that natural AMOC transitions evolved more slowly than the rapid North Greenland oxygen-isotope shifts would imply, thereby refining our understanding of "abruptness" during DO events.

title: Obesity management medications: The way forward.
abstract: Obesity is now widely recognized as a chronic progressive condition. The altered biological mechanisms that cause obesity frequently require long-term treatment, including pharmacotherapies or bariatric surgery. In recent decades, the pathophysiology of obesity has been understood to an extent that obesity management medication (OMM) discovery could be rationally pursued. Advances in defining the regulation of food intake and energy expenditure by molecular communication from peripheral organs to the brain led to the development of OMMs that appear capable of safely achieving scalable and sustained body weight loss. However, side effects, heterogeneous treatment responses, long-term metabolic adaptations, adherence, and other factors may limit the use of existing OMMs and justify the development of additional medications to improve the health of people living with obesity.

title: Obesity pharmacotherapies and cognition.
abstract: Pharmacotherapies for obesity and type 2 diabetes are increasingly being evaluated for their effects on cognition and brain health. Evidence from preclinical models, observational cohorts, and clinical trials has intensified interest, but findings remain mixed. A central challenge is to determine whether potential cognitive effects arise from direct actions on neural circuits, indirect consequences of improved cardiometabolic health, or both. This Review examines the evidence across cardiometabolic disease, aging, and Alzheimer's disease, focusing on glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)-based therapies and combination approaches that engage glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, glucagon, and amylin pathways. We assess how receptor pharmacology, brain exposure, metabolic context, and disease stage shape cognitive outcomes and discuss how mechanistic clarity could guide therapies aimed at preserving or improving cognition.

title: Quantum gas microscopy of three-flavor Hubbard systems.
abstract: Hubbard systems are paradigmatic realizations of strongly correlated many-body systems. Introducing additional species breaks the SU(2) symmetry of the Hubbard model and leads to a wide variety of new exotic quantum phases. Here, we extended quantum gas microscopy to three-flavor Fermi lattice gases in the Hubbard regime. Relying on site- and flavor-resolved detection, we studied the phase diagram of the three-flavor Hubbard model and found signatures of flavor-selective localization and selective pairing at temperatures down to the tunneling energy scale. Our measurements were then compared with numerical linked-cluster expansion calculations. Further increase of phase space density may enable the observation of a distinct pair Mott phase at half filling and shows a path toward the study of color superfluidity and other aspects of quantum chromodynamics.

title: Quantum gases below 10 picokelvin in space.
abstract: Ultracold atom platforms enable low temperatures and long free evolution times, which are crucial for fundamental physics tests and atom interferometry. The lowest equivalent temperature reported in such a system is 38 pK with a free expansion time of 2 s, achieved in atom-chip-based magnetic traps in microgravity. Optical dipole trap (ODT) systems offer better optical access and the flexibility to condense both magnetic and non-magnetic atoms, but have not been used to prepare quantum degenerate gases under microgravity conditions. Here we report an ODT-based Bose-Einstein condensate created aboard the China Space Station, containing 2.0 × 104 atoms, reaching an equivalent temperature of [Formula: see text] pK with a free expansion time of 7.0 s. This record-low temperature could stimulate a new generation of ODT-based experiments in quantum simulation and precision measurements in space.

title: Seafloor geodesy delineates fast megathrust relocking after the giant 2011 Tohoku earthquake.
abstract: How and when the subduction megathrust recovers its locking state after a great earthquake is important to understanding earthquake-cycle physics and future hazards. Here we report the delineation of the relocking process after the 2011 magnitude 9 Tohoku earthquake with 14 years of postseismic seafloor geodetic observations. These data, combined with onshore geodetic observations, analyses of repeating earthquakes, and numerical modeling, reveal how the recovery of locking is interrupted by afterslip on the megathrust and accompanied by stress relaxation in the viscoelastic upper mantle. The results indicate that the megathrust has already arrived at a locking state today similar to that before the earthquake despite the ongoing stress relaxation. The acquired knowledge aids understanding of megathrust earthquake cycles at other subduction zones.

title: Stacked porous NiTi structure with low cost and ultrahigh fatigue life for elastocaloric cooling.
abstract: Elastocaloric cooling (eC) uses shape memory alloys (SMAs) as energy-efficient, eco-friendly refrigerants. However, cost-effectively fabricating SMAs into fatigue-resistant, heat transfer-enhanced structures remains a key obstacle to commercialization of the eC technology. We introduce a "stamping and stacking" (S-S) method for producing porous, fatigue-resistant SMA structures. Honeycomb-like chips are stamped from nitinol (NiTi) thin sheets and then stacked into a layered tubular structure to increase heat exchange surface and at the same time avoid buckling and splitting failures encountered in existing SMA structures. The stacked structure endures >108 compression cycles and can deliver high specific cooling power of 3850 watts per kilogram. Our S-S method reduces fabrication costs by one order of magnitude compared with existing approaches, enabling mass production of eC refrigerant structures for commercial deployment.
