abstract: Similarity of body-plan features across distant phyla provides striking testimony to the Darwinian concept of common descent throughout Metazoa. In both the cnidarian Nematostella and chordates, gastrula organizers direct the initial establishment of embryonic axes. Whether these domains share a common evolutionary origin is a fundamental question for understanding the origin of the chordate body plan. To address this question, we combine trans-species transgenesis, perturbations of signaling pathways, cross-phylum single-cell transcriptomic comparisons, and transplantation assays. We show that cis-regulatory elements that recapitulate NvBmp2/4 and NvChordin expression in Nematostella —and therefore report the endogenous cnidarian organizer regulatory environment—also drive organizer-restricted activity in chordate embryos, consistent with chordate organizer gene-regulatory logic. Moreover, we show that, as in chordates, Smad2/3-mediated signaling is active in the Nematostella organizer and is required for organizer-specific expression of NvBmp2/4 and NvChordin . Together, our data support remarkable homology between cnidarian and chordate gastrula organizers and are consistent with the idea that the cnidarian–bilaterian ancestor possessed a blastopore organizer with the potential to generate dorsal–anterior chordate fates. On this basis, we propose a scenario in which asymmetric positioning of the ancestral blastopore organizer and skewed body-axis elongation contributed to the emergence of the chordate body plan.

abstract: Associative memory, traditionally modeled by Hopfield networks, enables the retrieval of previously stored patterns from partial or noisy cues. Yet, the local computational principles which are required to enable this function remain incompletely understood. To formally characterize the local information processing in such systems, we employ a recent extension of information theory—Partial Information Decomposition. It decomposes the contribution of different inputs to an output into unique information from each input, redundant information across inputs, and synergistic information that emerges from combining different inputs. Applying this framework to individual neurons in classical Hopfield networks we find that below the memory capacity, the information in a neuron’s activity is characterized by high redundancy between the external pattern input and the internal recurrent input, while synergy and unique information are close to zero until the memory capacity is surpassed and performance drops steeply. Inspired by this observation, we use redundancy maximization at each neuron as an information-theoretic learning goal. This increases the network’s memory capacity to 1.59, a more than tenfold improvement over the 0.14 capacity of classical Hopfield networks, and also outperforming recent state-of-the-art implementations of Hopfield networks. Overall, this work establishes redundancy maximization as a design principle for associative memories and opens pathways for new associative memory models based on information-theoretic goals.

abstract: In patients with acute ischemic stroke caused by medium vessel occlusion (MeVO), intra-arterial tenecteplase may offer a targeted strategy to improve recanalization; we hypothesized that intra-arterial tenecteplase would increase successful reperfusion compared with standard care with a comparable safety profile. This phase 2, prospective, randomised, open-label, blinded-endpoint, multicentre study aims to assess the efficacy and safety of intra-arterial tenecteplase for patients with acute ischemic stroke caused by MeVO. Patients with MeVO were randomly (1:1) assigned to receive intra-arterial tenecteplase or standard care. The primary outcome was successful reperfusion of medium vessel occlusion. A total of 80 patients were randomized to either the tenecteplase group ( n = 41) or control group ( n = 39). Successful reperfusion reached 61.0% (25/41) in the tenecteplase group versus 28.2% (11/39) in the control group (unadjusted odds ratio 3.98, 95% CI 1.56-10.16; P = 0.004). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage within 24 h was similar between the tenecteplase and control groups. This work suggests that intra-arterial tenecteplase significantly increased the probability of successful reperfusion compared with standard care, with a comparable safety profile in this stroke population. abstract: Accurate visualization of glioblastoma is essential for guiding biopsy, resection and radiotherapy. Contrast-enhanced MRI is routine in clinical practice, yet it can miss metabolically active tumor outside areas of blood-brain barrier disruption. In a histopathology-validated cohort with 472 tissue samples of 61 patients with IDH-wildtype glioblastoma, we show that O-(2-[¹⁸F]fluoroethyl)-L-tyrosine PET ([ 18 F]FET PET) depicts tumor tissue significantly better than contrast-enhanced MRI (CE-MRI), especially in regions that show no enhancement on MRI. [ 18 F]FET PET achieves substantially higher sensitivity for tumor detection (91.2% vs 52.6%) and maintains high reliability in non-enhancing tissue (positive predictive value 98.3%), findings that are consistent across newly diagnosed and recurrent disease and in both cohorts undergoing either resection or biopsy. These results indicate that [ 18 F]FET PET complements MRI by revealing MRI-occult tumor burden. Incorporating amino acid PET into routine planning may therefore improve the accuracy of tumor visualization and, ultimately, patient management.

title: A Kampo medicine, kamishoyosan, ameliorates menstruation-associated symptoms in patients with premenstrual syndrome: An exploratory open-label, randomized controlled trial.
abstract: Premenstrual syndrome (PMS) is a psychological or physical symptom. We conducted an open-label, randomized, exploratory trial with the aim of evaluating the efficacy and safety of kamishoyosan (KSS) for PMS. KSS was administered orally during three menstrual cycles. The primary endpoint was the change in the premenstrual Menstrual Distress Questionnaire (MDQ) total score. The secondary endpoints included MDQ total and subscale scores, a daily symptom questionnaire, the Work Productivity and Activity Impairment (WPAI) Questionnaire, overall impressions, sleep status, and heart rate. A total of 50 patients were enrolled. The primary endpoint, the premenstrual MDQ total score, was significantly ameliorated after KSS treatment. Furthermore, KSS reduced MDQ scores during the menstrual cycle. Among the MDQ subscales, KSS decreased score of pain, concentration, behavioral change, and negative feelings during the premenstrual cycle. In addition, hyperthymia reduced during the menstrual cycle. The results of the daily symptom questionnaire indicated that KSS treatment alleviated irritability, easy anger, anxiety, emotional instability, abdominal distension, coldness, and stiff shoulders.The WPAI activity impairment score was lower in the KSS group, and overall impression favoured in KSS treatment.. The only adverse event related to KSS was headache in one case. These exploratory findings suggest that KSS may improve menstrual-related symptoms in PMS.

title: A pre-post single-arm pilot trial of a digital multicomponent intervention for self-efficacy enhancement among online support groups of primary caregivers of children with neuro-muscular disorders: SEE-NMD protocol.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA) and Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) are progressive genetic neuromuscular disorders that impose substantial caregiving demands on families. In Pakistan, where disease-modifying therapies remain largely inaccessible, care is predominantly supportive, frequently resulting in psychological distress and diminished caregiver confidence. An individual's belief in their capacity to execute required behaviours, self-efficacy, is a recognised determinant of caregiving quality, yet evidence on caregiver self-efficacy in SMA and DMD within low-resource settings remains sparse. This protocol describes the methods for an exploratory, single-arm, pre-post trial. The trial aims to generate preliminary evidence on changes in self-efficacy following a multicomponent, digitally delivered intervention and its implementation feasibility among primary caregivers of children with SMA and DMD in Pakistan.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: A single-arm, pre-post study design will recruit primary caregivers of children with SMA and DMD enrolled in the Treat-NMD Registry of Pakistan, with 40 caregivers per condition (80 total) analyzed as separate disease-specific cohorts. An eight-week intervention will be delivered via online support groups, comprising educational video clips, expert-led live sessions, pictorial guides, and progressively tapering audio reminders. The primary outcome, self-efficacy, will be measured using a culturally adapted, content-validated Urdu version of the DMD Caregiver Self-Efficacy Scale (DMD-CSES), assessed at baseline (T0) and eight weeks post-intervention (T1). Pre- and post-intervention scores will be compared using a paired t-test or Wilcoxon signed-rank test, depending on the data distribution, with analyses conducted in STATA Version 17.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: Ethical approval has been granted by the Ethics Review Committee of Aga Khan University (2025-11875-37040). Verbal informed consent will be obtained from all participants, and confidentiality will be maintained throughout the trial. The findings will be disseminated via peer-reviewed publications, conference presentations, and shared with the Treat-NMD registry network.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NAME AND NUMBER: NCT07356063, Date of registration: 11/January/2026.

title: A psychological perspective on peer tutoring in EFL collaborative writing in Chinese higher education contexts.
abstract: In Chinese higher learning institutions, students learning English as a foreign language (EFL) often demonstrate low writing self-efficacy (WSE) and poor writing competence. The present study examined the associations between the integration of peer tutoring with collaborative writing and students' WSE and writing outcomes from a psychological perspective. A quasi-experiment was implemented for 11 weeks for 100 Chinese university students studying EFL. Changes in WSE were examined, and writing competence was assessed using tests. The results showed a notable rise in students' WSE after the instructional intervention. The multiple linear regression analysis indicated that gains in WSE were positively associated with the writing outcome after controlling for pretest writing competence and group membership, explaining 20.2% of the total variance. These results suggest that peer-supported collaborative writing was associated with higher EFL writing competence alongside increased WSE. These findings align with theoretical justifications based on peer scaffolding and the Zone of Proximal Development, although these processes were not directly measured in the present study. These findings imply that incorporating peer tutoring into collaborative writing might be associated with the development of WSE and improved writing competence among EFL students at Chinese universities. Increased WSE appeared to be a significant, albeit partial, predictor of writing competence, highlighting the potential relevance of WSE development in peer-supported collaborative writing contexts.

title: A stepwise fresh porcine head model for three-dimensional dissection of ventricular, limbic, and deep venous anatomy.
abstract: Deep ventricular, limbic, cisternal, and deep venous structures form a compact three-dimensional anatomical system that is difficult to understand from two-dimensional resources alone. We evaluated the technical feasibility of organizing fresh ex vivo porcine heads into a four-module, stepwise dissection model for demonstrating these relationships. Five porcine heads obtained from a regulated food supply chain were prepared without formalin fixation, vascular injection, or specialized laboratory equipment. A neurosurgery resident performed the dissections under faculty supervision. Anatomical feasibility was assessed by the successful identification of prespecified targets within transcallosal, transchoroidal, interforniceal, posterior deep venous, and atrial-inferior horn dissections. The complete four-module sequence was achieved, and all prespecified anatomical targets were identified during dissection in all five specimens. In an independent image-based assessment of three specimens with complete unannotated photographic sets, 26 of 31 targets were identifiable in all three specimens, whereas five deep ventricular or venous targets were identifiable in two of three specimens. The dissection demonstrated the spatial continuity of the caudate nucleus, fornix, foramen of Monro, choroid plexus, thalamostriate vein, velum interpositum, internal cerebral veins, Galenic venous system, hippocampal formation, choroidal fissure, and adjacent cisternal spaces. Natural vascular coloration remained visible without injection and supported orientation during sequential dissection. This low-infrastructure preparation may serve as an accessible physical reference for understanding the three-dimensional continuity of deep ventricular, limbic, cisternal, and venous anatomy, particularly where access to human cadaveric dissection is limited.

title: A systematic review of Moringa oleifera seed toxicity and safety: Comparative analysis of toxicology methodologies and results.
abstract: This systematic review aims to assess the reliability of contemporary toxicological research on Moringa oleifera seeds. Academic databases were browsed on a yearly basis (2014-2024); identification and screening were conducted between July 17th 2023 and January 13th 2025. Primary research reports on M. oleifera seed toxicology were included for data collection. Fifty-three fields were used to collect data. Data was synthesised by comparing methodological data points to contemporary toxicity testing guidelines; results were presented as a narrative synthesis. Conflict of interest, research quality and risk of bias were assessed using Cochrane tools modified for non-human laboratory studies. Thirty-seven non-duplicate publications were identified, of which 14 were included for data collection. In total, 395 data points were collected and synthesised. Financial conflicts of interest were declared in one report. Nine reports received "lower quality" or "lowest quality" research quality judgements. Six reports received "high risk of bias" judgements. Bias risk was commonly associated with selective reporting of data. M. oleifera seed toxicity was commonly tested via rodent study. Seven rodent studies included an acute toxicity test and nine included a sub-acute toxicity test. Two acute oral toxicity tests returned LD50 values of 14,000-15,000 mg/kg bw. Three sub-acute oral toxicity tests returned NOAEL values of 100-257 mg/kg bw/d. Oral LD50 and NOAEL data could only be derived from reports with "lowest quality" research and/or "high risk of bias" judgements, so these safety limits are unreliable. Inadequate dosing schemes were the primary cause of limited LD50 and NOAEL data. Dose range non-compliance also caused unnecessary animal suffering. To facilitate standardisation in future research, several guideline-based methodological recommendations are made. Determining reliable safety limits for M. oleifera seed consumption may reduce incidence of acute kidney injury, thereby supporting Targets 3.4 and 3.d of the United Nations sustainable development goals.

title: ACMNet: An attention-convolution mixed neural network for semantic segmentation of high-resolution remote sensing images.
abstract: Semantic segmentation of remote sensing imagery, which is widely used in land cover classification, urban planning, and environmental monitoring, has become a research hotspot in the fields of remote sensing and computer vision. As its applications continue to expand, improving the segmentation accuracy and generalization have become pressing challenges. However, most existing semantic segmentation models rely solely on either attention mechanisms or convolutional neural networks (CNNs), thus leaving room for performance improvement. In this study, we propose ACMNet (Attention-Convolution Mixed Network), which adopts a hybrid attention-convolution architecture. The decoder of ACMNet employs an innovative mixed design, where two branches are used to extract and integrate different types of contextual information and achieve hierarchical aggregation of contextual features, thereby enhancing its performance. To evaluate the performance of ACMNet, we conducted ablation experiments and comparative experiments on the Potsdam, Vaihingen, and WHU Building datasets. The results show that ACMNet achieved the best overall performance across all three datasets, with mF1 scores of 91.79%, 88.70%, and 96.56% on the Potsdam, Vaihingen, and WHU Building datasets, respectively. These findings indicate that ACMNet delivers superior performance in the semantic segmentation of high-resolution remote sensing images in urban areas, which provides valuable support for diverse tasks related to fine-grained urban management and dynamic monitoring.

title: Adaptive-based cascaded PI-PID controller for load frequency regulation with real time verification.
abstract: In order to address Load Frequency Control (LFC) problems in single-area and interconnected two-area power systems, this work proposes a cascaded control scheme that combines PI-PID control with the Set-Membership Affine Projection Algorithm (SMAPA). The proposed approach is evaluated under various practical operating conditions, including step load disturbances, random load variations, wind power fluctuations, and parameter uncertainty. In addition, frequency-domain stability analysis is performed to further assess the robustness of the proposed controller, while real-time validation is conducted for the two-area system to demonstrate its practical effectiveness. The proposed controller is compared with conventional PI controllers tuned using five optimization methods for the single-area system. For the two-area system, its performance is benchmarked against PID controllers designed using three optimization methods and the recently reported SPPI-based approach. The simulation results show that the proposed controller achieves lower overshoot and faster settling time in both configurations. These improvements are attributed to the integration of real-time adaptive parameter updating provided by SMAPA with the favorable dynamic characteristics of the PI-PID control structure. The results demonstrate that the proposed cascaded SMAPA-based PI-PID controller provides robust frequency regulation under different operating conditions and offers promising potential for practical interconnected power system applications.

title: Aligning entity of knowledge graph based on graph convolutional network with maximum translated similarity.
abstract: Entity alignment is a pivotal technology for integrating heterogeneous knowledge graphs, yet most embedding-based alignment methods destroy the inherent structural embedding information of knowledge graphs when unifying cross-graph embedding spaces, resulting in limited alignment accuracy and stability. To tackle this issue, this paper proposes a novel model for entity alignment tasks, which named as Graph Convolutional Network with Maximum Translated Similarity (GCN-MTS). GCN-MTS innovatively leverages a maximum translated similarity mechanism to optimize the adjacency matrix, degree matrix and loss function. This core design effectively maintains the original relative embedding structure of cross-graph entities during embedding space unification, which is the key improvement over existing approaches. Comprehensive experiments on 3 pairs of real-world knowledge graph dataset demonstrate the superior performance of GCN-MTS against advanced baseline methods. It achieves average performance gains of 5%-15% in Hits@1 and 4%-16% in Hits@10. Ablation results confirm that the optimized module brings a nearly 22% improvement in alignment metrics compared with the vanilla GCN. Furthermore, GCN-MTS presents excellent robustness and stability across different seed alignment quantities and seed combinations.

title: Antibiotic stewardship challenges in Madagascar's poultry sector: informality, knowledge gaps, and market constraints.
abstract: Antibiotic resistance (ABR) is a major global public health threat, largely driven by the overuse and misuse of antibiotics. Tackling its animal health component is particularly difficult in low- and middle-income countries, where data and resources are limited. This qualitative study aims to explore antibiotic use (ABU) and its underlying drivers in poultry farms in Analamanga, Madagascar's region with the highest poultry density. In April 2023, we conducted semi-structured interviews with 79 poultry farmers (13 backyard and 66 semi-intensive), 10 animal health professionals, and 10 agrovet shop sellers. Thematic analysis was used to examine farm characteristics, poultry health management, veterinary medicine supply and use, and interactions with poultry production stakeholders, in order to identify antibiotic stewardship challenges in Madagascar's poultry sector. Backyard and semi-intensive farmers shared several features: informality (absence of farm registration, rare cooperative membership, limited training), irregular profitability, easy access to antibiotics, recurrent antibiotic misuse (for example use in poultry viral infection treatment, first-line fluoroquinolone treatments), and limited veterinary inspection by competent authorities. However, the two farmer groups differed, as semi-intensive farmers had slightly greater knowledge of ABU and ABR than backyard farmers; they primarily consulted chick and feed suppliers for health advice and medicine purchase; and they widely perceived antibiotics as essential to maintaining poultry health and productivity. Practical roadblocks to invest in preventive measures or adopt effective antibiotic stewardship (ABS) were their narrow profit margins, limited access to credit, and weak bargaining power towards poultry product buyers. Tailored approaches such as supporting professionalization of poultry sector, building capacity of chick and feed suppliers to provide training in appropriate ABU and management of flocks, flock vaccination, deworming schedules, treatment record keeping and ABS principles may enhance antibiotic usage in the Madagascar poultry sector. Future research should build on this exploratory study, which used a convenience sample of stakeholders, by examining ABU trends and drivers in Analamanga with representative sampling and rigorous quantitative validation across Madagascar's poultry sector.

title: Arabic translation, cross-cultural adaptation, and testing measurement properties of the European heart failure self-care behaviour (EHFScBS-12 and EHFScBS-9).
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Enhanced self-care is the primary objective of many heart failure (HF) management programs. The European Heart Failure Self-care Behaviour Scale (EHFScBS), available in 12-item and 9-item versions, is widely used to assess self-care in patients with HF. However, the EHFScBS has not been translated or evaluated its measurement properties in Arabic-speaking populations with HF.
OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study was to translate, culturally adapt and evaluate the measurement properties of the Arabic version of EHFScBS-12 and EHFScBS-9 followed the COSMIN (COnsensus-based Standards for the selection of health Measurement Instruments) guidelines and to compare both versions regarding structural validity, reliability, and model fit among Arabic-speaking patients with HF.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A cross-sectional study conducted at a governmental hospital in Riyadh used purposive sampling to recruit participants who met the predefined inclusion criteria relevant to the study objectives:137 patients with HF (mean age = 59 years; 61.3% male). The researchers evaluated the comprehensive measurement properties of the 12- and 9-item (EHFScBS) included forward-backward translation, confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), and reliability testing. In addition, convergent and divergent validity were assessed using the Self-Care Heart Failure Index version 6.2 and the Perceived Stress Scale10-Item.
RESULTS: The scale demonstrated excellent content validity as evidenced by I-CVI of .85 to 1 and S-CVI of .95, and the CFA of the 12-item scale yielded ambiguous fit indices: root mean square error of approximation (RMSEA) =0.084, (90% CI: .059-.108), comparative fit index (CFI) =0.824, and normed fit index (NFI) =0.706 which is low/suboptimal. The CFA of the 9-item scale showed good fit indices (RMSEA = 0.042, (90%CI: .000-.084), CFI = 0.969). The internal consistency was acceptable for both scales at 0.75 and 0.72, respectively. Both the versions demonstrated convergent and discriminant validity.
CONCLUSIONS: The EHFScBS as unidimensional showed satisfactory measurement properties in Arabic-speaking HF patients. The 9-item one-factor has demonstrated better fit in the present sample compared to the 12-item version achieved after post-hoc modification, support its use in practice and research. However, future studies should conduct independent cross-validation in separate samples from Saudi Arabia and other Arabic-speaking countries to confirm the generalizability, and cross-cultural validity of the instrument.

title: Artificial intelligence (AI) adoption and Chinese art teachers' career exploration behavior: The roles of job substitution risks, job insecurity, and organizational AI readiness.
abstract: The increasing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in art education raises questions about teachers' professional security and career development. Drawing primarily on Conservation of Resources (COR) theory and, in a complementary manner, on Career Construction Theory (CCT), this cross-sectional study examined associations among AI adoption, perceived job substitution risk, job insecurity, career exploration behavior, and organizational AI readiness. Survey data from 381 Chinese art teachers were analyzed using Mplus 7.4. AI adoption was positively associated with career exploration behavior. Statistically significant indirect associations were observed through job substitution risk, job insecurity, and their hypothesized sequential combination. Organizational AI readiness positively moderated the AI adoption-career exploration relationship: the association was stronger at higher readiness. COR theory offers a resource-threat interpretation of the indirect associations, while CCT highlights that career exploration may reflect threat-related coping, growth-oriented development, or both. The data did not separately measure these motivations or establish causal ordering. The findings provide context-specific insights into career exploration among art teachers during AI-related technological change.

title: Assessment of the appropriateness of stress ulcer prophylaxis practice among hospitalized patients across Lebanese hospitals: A multicenter prospective study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stress ulcer prophylaxis (SUP) is recommended for critically ill patients at high risk of stress-related gastrointestinal bleeding. Despite established guideline recommendations, inappropriate use of acid suppressant medications (ASMs), particularly proton pump inhibitors (PPIs), remains common worldwide and may expose patients to unnecessary adverse effects and increased healthcare costs. This study aimed to assess the appropriateness of SUP prescribing practices among hospitalized patients across Lebanese hospitals, focusing on indication, choice of pharmacologic agent, dosing regimen, route of administration, duration of therapy, discharge prescribing, and factors associated with inappropriate SUP practice.
METHODS: A multicenter prospective study was conducted between April 20 and May 22, 2026, across ten tertiary-care hospitals in different regions of Lebanon. Adult patients (≥18 years) admitted to Internal Medicine Unit, Intensive Care Unit (ICU), or Coronary Care Unit wards were assessed for the appropriateness of SUP, regardless of whether ASMs were prescribed. The appropriateness of SUP practice was evaluated according to the Society of Critical Care Medicine and American Society of Health-System Pharmacists (SCCM/ASHP) 2024 and ASHP 1999 guidelines. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors associated with inappropriate SUP practice.
RESULTS: A total of 552 patients were enrolled, with a mean age of 64.3 ± 18.5 years, and 58.7% were male. According to the SCCM/ASHP 2024 and ASHP 1999 guidelines, 90.8% and 77.2% of patients, respectively, were not eligible for SUP. Omeprazole was the most frequently prescribed agent (75.4%), and PPIs were used in all SUP prescriptions. Among patients admitted to ICU, 11.2% continued receiving ASMs after the SUP indication had resolved or following ICU transfer without a persisting indication. Overall, SUP practice was inappropriate in 77.9% of patients. Multivariable analysis demonstrated that anticoagulant therapy was associated with higher odds of inappropriate SUP practice (AOR = 2.78, 95% CI = 1.35-5.74, P = 0.006).
CONCLUSIONS: Inappropriate SUP practice is highly prevalent among hospitalized patients in Lebanon, largely due to prescribing without guideline-based indications. Inappropriate continuation after resolution of the SUP indication or ICU transfer was also observed. Strengthening adherence to evidence-based recommendations through stewardship programs, prescribing audits, standardized protocols, and updated national guidance may help optimize SUP use and improve patient care.

title: Association of unmet discharge needs on readmission or mortality among acute respiratory failure survivors during the COVID-19 pandemic: The Addressing Post-Intensive Care Syndrome (APICS-COVID) multicenter prospective cohort study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Survivors of acute respiratory failure (ARF) often face long-term impairments known as Post-Intensive Care Syndrome. These impairments, coupled with fragmented healthcare, contribute to high rates of readmission and mortality. The COVID-19 pandemic challenged healthcare systems, providing an important opportunity to evaluate healthcare fragmentation before and during the pandemic.
METHODS: From December 2020 to July 2022, this prospective multicenter study (APICS-COVID) enrolled ARF survivors discharged home from acute care hospitalization. The primary exposure was unmet healthcare needs within 1-4 weeks post-discharge and the primary composite outcome was 3-month readmission and mortality. We additionally compared unmet healthcare needs in this study versus a predominately pre-pandemic cohort from an identical study protocol (APICS-01).
RESULTS: Of 201 patients enrolled, 94% had at least one unmet healthcare need. The median (IQR) number of healthcare needs upon discharge was 18 (11-25) and the median proportion of unmet healthcare needs was 26% (17-36%). Follow-up appointments were the most frequent unmet need. Higher vs. lower unmet healthcare needs were not significantly associated with 3-month readmission or mortality (aRR 0.61, p = 0.22). Compared to the APICS-01 cohort, the frequency of 3-month readmission/mortality was lower (14% vs. 29%, p = 0.26), despite higher unmet needs in the APICS-COVID cohort (26% vs. 16%, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Across six US academic hospitals during the COVID-19 pandemic, we did not detect a significant association between higher and lower unmet healthcare needs and 3-month readmission or mortality. Compared to APICS-01, unmet follow-up appointments increased but readmission and mortality decreased. Home health services, durable medical equipment, and medications remained robust during pandemic conditions.

title: Bridging the gap: A qualitative study on veterans' experiences with systemic barriers and support during transition.
abstract: Many veterans face complex challenges during the transition from military to civilian life, particularly when navigating healthcare and benefits systems. This qualitative study examines how recently separated veterans with service‑connected musculoskeletal disorders perceive and navigate systemic barriers within Department of Defense and Veterans Affairs transition and healthcare systems. Semi‑structured interviews were conducted with 20 veterans within one year of separation who had filed a musculoskeletal service‑connection claim. Using a rapid qualitative analytic approach, interviews captured experiences with the discharge process, transition programming, and efforts to access healthcare and benefits. Analysis identified four major themes: the interaction of physical, psychological, and bureaucratic stressors during discharge, particularly salient for those managing musculoskeletal conditions; varied and often critical views of transition programming, which many perceived as generic and misaligned with individual needs; systemic barriers to care and benefits, including delays, fragmented processes, and cultural norms that discourage disclosure; and recommendations emphasizing continuity of care, case management, and emotional support to address identity disruption and loss of purpose. Overall, the findings highlight persistent structural and cultural obstacles that complicate transition and hinder early engagement with services. Improved coordination, continuity‑oriented supports, and psychologically responsive programming may reduce these barriers. Further research is needed to evaluate scalable models that enhance early post‑separation outcomes.

title: Calibration of a fully closed-loop lumped-parameter cardiovascular model with baroreflex in response to induced central hypovolemia.
abstract: Calibration of cardiovascular models is essential to their clinical utility. We provide a full description of the calibration of a non-linear, dynamic model using global optimisation methods. Specifically, we consider an experimental cohort response in a closed-loop, baro-regulated cardiovascular model, in the setting of induced central hypovolemia.We propose a framework for simplifying calibration of dynamic, regulated models. We perform global sensitivity analysis and orthogonality analysis of a 58-parameter non-linear cardiovascular model including the baroreflex, to select an optimal subset of parameters for model calibration. We fit the model to relative Lower Body Negative Pressure data, using global optimisation (Differential Evolution method), searching a reduced input parameter space. Global sensitivity analysis and orthogonality analysis revealed multiple higher-order interactions within the model, as well as areas of similar influence of input parameters, on the components of the objective function. The model was fitted using only baroreflex parameters. Relative errors in the estimation of heart rate, mean arterial pressure, and stroke volume were reduced from -15.03%, 1.60% and 42.06% before calibration to 0.42%, -1.37% and 0.61% after the fitting, respectively.

title: Cardiovascular disease risk prediction models for people living with HIV in Sub-Saharan Africa: A scoping review protocol.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The landscape of Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) care has dramatically shifted with the advent of effective antiretroviral therapy (ART), transforming HIV from a rapidly fatal illness into a chronic, manageable disease. This success, however, has unveiled new challenges, primarily the increased prevalence of non-AIDS-related comorbidities, with non-communicable diseases (NCDs) such as cardiovascular disease (CVD) emerging as a critical concern for people living with HIV (PLWH). CVD has now become a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in this population, and its risk assessment is imperative. However, there is scanty data on CVD risk prediction models developed and/or applied among PLWH in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). Therefore, this planned scoping review aims to systematically map existing literature on CVD risk prediction models developed and/or used among PLWH in SSA. The review will identify the models that have been developed, used, and validated in the region.
METHODS: The scoping review protocol will follow an established framework for conducting scoping reviews. The study will employ the methodological approaches by Arksey and O'Malley and its recent advances, the Joanna Briggs Institute, and the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis Protocols. The objective of the scoping review will be achieved through a comprehensive published literature search from 01 January 2000 to 03 June 2026 across five selected databases: PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and CINAHL, based on a predefined strategy. Inclusion criteria will focus on studies written in English that develop, validate, or apply CVD risk prediction models among PLWH in SSA. The screening of search results and data extraction will be conducted by two independent reviewers.
EXPECTED OUTCOMES AND CONCLUSIONS: The review will synthesize and summarize the existing literature on CVD risk prediction developed and used among PLWH in SSA, identify knowledge gaps, and provide insights to inform the development of a novel CVD risk prediction model specific to PLWH in SSA. Registration: Open Science Framework https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/XVFUA.

title: Clinical and epidemiological characteristics of invasive non-typhoidal Salmonella disease in Ghana.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Invasive non-typhoidal Salmonella (iNTS) disease remains a significant public health threat in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). Although the disease is important, its clinical characteristics are not well described in literature. This study describes the clinico-epidemiological profile of iNTS disease in Ghana aiming to bridge important knowledge gaps and inform more effective management strategies.
METHODS: The study spanned 8 years and utilized selected fever surveillance sites in Ghana. Patients with fever and/or history of fever for ≥ 3 consecutive days within the week prior to visit were approached and blood sample taken after consenting for investigations including blood culture. iNTS isolates were recovered using BACTEC blood culture, identified by Analytical Profile Index (API), sero-grouped using the Kauffmann-White scheme and confirmed by Illumina whole genome sequencing. Conditional logistic regression was used to assess associations between clinical and laboratory features and iNTS blood culture positivity in a 1:3 age-, sex-, and residence-matched case-control analysis.
RESULTS: Of 271 blood-culture-derived bacterial pathogens, 15.5% (42/271) were identified as iNTS making it the second most common cause of bacteremia. iNTS disease exhibited seasonality with peak detections coinciding with the rainy seasons in Ghana. 23.7% (9/38) of iNTS isolates were multidrug-resistant (MDR), of which 5.3% (2/38) were extensively drug-resistant including resistance to ceftriaxone and ciprofloxacin. Several factors showed crude associations with iNTS disease; however, only anaemia retained its association after adjustment of other factors (aOR=2.41 p = 0.030).
CONCLUSION: iNTS is a major cause of bloodstream infections with the highest burden in children under 5 years of age with susceptibility to the infection amplified by anaemia. The Salmonella serovars involved are increasingly becoming multidrug-resistant, including resistance to critical antibiotics.

title: Commonly expressed key driver genes in the pathogenesis of viral and non-viral liver cancer.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a common and lethal liver cancer primarily associated with viral infections like hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV), as well as non-viral causes. Understanding the molecular mechanisms of these subtypes is essential for identifying potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets.
METHODS: In this study, an integrated bioinformatics approach was used to analyze publicly available datasets related to HBV-associated, HCV-associated, and non-viral HCC. Functional enrichment analyses and protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks were constructed to identify key hub genes.
RESULTS: Our analysis identified dysregulated genes across all HCC subtypes. Among these, GPC3 and SPARCL1 were significantly upregulated, while ALB and HNF4α were downregulated, and are involved in critical cancer pathways such as Wnt, PI3K/Akt, and p53 signaling. Functional analysis linked these DEGs to essential processes in tumorigenesis, including cell cycle regulation and immune modulation. Notably, SPARCL1 has been identified as a potential inhibitor of SPP1, a key driver of HCC. Validation using databases such as GEPIA and TNMplot confirmed the dysregulation of these genes in numerous HCC tissue samples and their significant association with patient prognosis.
CONCLUSION: This study provides a comprehensive overview of HCC pathogenesis by suggesting a shared gene profile between viral and non-viral forms, paving the way for universal diagnostic markers and targeted therapies while highlighting the need for further experimental validation to advance precision medicine in HCC.

title: Completing upper secondary school: Results from a ten-year longitudinal study in Norway.
abstract: The completion of education is important both for the individual and society. High dropout rates from upper secondary school have been a national problem in Norway, and especially in northern Norway. Academic aptitude or grades (GPA) are important, but given the multifaceted nature of dropout, we conducted a longitudinal analysis to examine predictors of school completion after ten years. The study included 1676 students in Troms County (latitude 69 degrees north) starting in upper secondary education in 2010. We included a broad set of predictors related to school performance, psychological factors such as vulnerability, resilience, personality, and mental health, alongside demographic data. The mixture modeling revealed three completion trajectories: normal progression (40.1%), delayed completion (36.6%), and non-completion (23.3%). Correlation analyses showed significant relationships between completion and several of these predictors; however, in multinomial regression analyses, no variables beyond GPA significantly predicted the normal progression trajectory, whereas delayed completion was additionally accounted for by study track choice and self-perceived health, with GPA playing an even stronger role. This underscores the importance of prior school performance, but we also discuss the implications of the findings for the delayed-completion group.

title: Data-driven risk assessment framework for railway operation accidents based on an improved Bayesian network.
abstract: As a cornerstone national infrastructure, railway systems have faced increasingly intensive operational demands, escalating accident risks that threat socio-economic stability and public welfare. Therefore, ensuring operational safety is of paramount importance. This study develops an effective framework for assessing railway operational accident risks by integrating an improved Bayesian network. Firstly, to mitigate data imbalance, the Adaptive Synthetic Sampling algorithm is introduced to establish a reliable and representative dataset. Subsequently, the AcciMap theory is introduced to form a multi-level risk assessment system. Secondly, to address the epistemic uncertainty within unstructured data, the Bayesian network is combined with hesitant cloud model. Finally, the performance of the proposed model is validated through different methods. The results demonstrate that the proposed model scientifically identifies the critical risk influencing factors of railway operation and can provide reliable and accurate risk assessment results. This study provides valuable insights for railway operation decision-makers to develop reasonable accident prevention measures and valuable support for railway operation risk management.

title: Deep learning optimisation for cardiology: Neural Architecture Search-driven arrhythmia classification with electrocardiograms.
abstract: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death worldwide. Sudden cardiac death (SCD) accounts for roughly 50% of all cardiac deaths. The electrocardiogram (ECG) is widely used for diagnosing cardiac disease. However, the complexity of interpretation limits the ECG's efficacy. Modern deep learning methods can assist clinicians in diagnosis. We applied Neural Architecture Search (NAS) to identify optimal deep learning architectures for classifying cardiac arrhythmias with ECGs. We applied the Differentiable Architecture Search strategy to an AutoFormer search and trained, validated, and tested the resulting model on the PhysioNet Challenge 2021 (PC21) dataset (n = 88,253 from three continents). We optimised hyperparameters on the NAS output, exploring input patch size, class weighting, and loss function. The PC21 metric and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) are the performance metrics. The NAS converged towards minimal architectural configurations (embedding dimension: 384, depth: 4, self-attention heads: 4, MLP ratio: 1) with a validation and test PC21 metric of 0.66 (PC21 winner: 0.63). The NAS-created network achieved an AUROC of 0.97 and a PC21 metric of 0.72 during testing (PC21 winner: 0.69). We tested the PC21 winner architecture (1D-convolutional neural network with attention mechanism) without the attention mechanism and with the NAS-suggested architecture of 4 self-attention heads (instead of 8). The architecture without the attention mechanism performed similarly to the one with 8 self-attention heads (AUROC: 0.90, PC21 metric: 0.69). The architecture with 4 self-attention heads scored an AUROC of 0.91 and improved the PC21 metric to 0.71. The attention mechanism visualisation for two SCD-related arrhythmias (premature ventricular contractions and prolonged QT-interval) showed more clinically relevant attention for the 4-self-attention-head architectures. We interpret architectural simplicity as driving performance in arrhythmia classification. The self-attention mechanism can autonomously abstract clinical representations, simplifying clinical deployment by eliminating the need for an explicit feature-extraction pipeline.

title: Development, validation, and testing of an agriculture support exoskeleton in adjunct to conventional physiotherapy for farm labourers with chronic low back pain: A two-phase, mixed-methods, quasi-experimental pilot study protocol.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Low back pain (LBP) affects 619 million people globally, with projections reaching 843 million by 2050. Farm labourers exhibit markedly higher prevalence than the general population, with lifetime (70-85%), 12-month (15-45%), and point (approximately 30%) prevalences driven by sustained trunk flexion, repetitive manual handling, and limited access to ergonomic or rehabilitative interventions. While conventional physiotherapy is the cornerstone of chronic LBP (CLBP) management, its effectiveness may be limited by ongoing mechanical loading during agricultural work. Back support exoskeletons (BSEs) have shown promise in reducing lumbar loading. However, no study has integrated exoskeleton development, validation, and clinical testing within a physiotherapy framework for farm labourers. The objective of the two-phase protocol is to design, develop, and laboratory-validate an agriculture support exoskeleton (AgSuEx), followed by examining the effects of AgSuEx-assisted physiotherapy compared with conventional physiotherapy alone on pain intensity, work productivity, disability, physical function, and quality of life (QOL) among farm labourers with CLBP.
METHODS: The two-phase, mixed-methods, quasi-experimental pilot study will be conducted in Wardha district, Maharashtra, India. Phase I will involve participatory co-design, iterative engineering development, and laboratory validation of an AgSuEx using finite element analysis (FEA), multibody dynamics (MBD) simulation, surface electromyography (sEMG), inertial measurement units (IMUs), interface pressure mapping, and validated usability instruments, integrated with focus group discussions (FGDs) from farm labourers. Phase II will employ a quasi-experimental, non-equivalent control group pretest-posttest design with repeated measures. Farm labourers aged 25-49 years with CLBP will be assigned (1:1) to AgSuEx-assisted conventional physiotherapy or conventional physiotherapy alone for 6 weeks, with follow-up at 3 and 6 months.
OUTCOMES: Phase I primary outcome: lumbar extensor sEMG activation. Phase II primary outcomes: pain intensity (Quadruple VAS) and work productivity. Secondary outcomes: functional disability (RODI), physical function (RMDQ), and QOL (SF-12). Device-specific outcomes (SUS, QUEAD and LPP) will be assessed across both phases. Outcome assessors and data analysts will be blinded to group assignment.
CONCLUSION: This protocol will generate preliminary evidence on the feasibility, usability, and preliminary clinical effects of integrating a Make in India AgSuEx with conventional physiotherapy for farm laborers with CLBP. Findings will guide future larger-scale controlled trials and inform ergonomic and rehabilitative strategies for agrarian populations.
TRIAL REGISTERED PROSPECTIVELY: Clinical Trial Registry- India CTRI/2025/11/097725 [Registered on: 20/11/2025]. Acknowledgement Number: REF/2025/11/116856. URL: https://ctri.nic.in/Clinicaltrials/pmaindet2.php?EncHid=MTQ1NzE3&Enc=&userName=Protocolversion4.0,4/09/2026.

title: E-Service quality and customer satisfaction in online shopping: Implications for sustainable digital commerce.
abstract: The rapid growth of e-commerce has intensified competition among online retailers, making e-service quality increasingly important for building customer trust, satisfaction, and sustainable customer-platform relationships. This study examines the relationships among e-service quality, customer trust, customer satisfaction, and customer loyalty using a second-order Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) framework. The five SERVQUAL dimensions such as empathy, responsiveness, reliability, assurance, and tangibles were modeled as first-order constructs reflecting the higher-order construct of service quality. Data were collected through an online questionnaire from 402 respondents with prior online-shopping experience. Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) and SEM were employed to assess the measurement and structural models. The measurement model demonstrated satisfactory reliability, convergent validity, discriminant validity, and overall model fit. The structural results showed that service quality significantly and positively influenced customer trust and customer satisfaction, while customer trust significantly enhanced satisfaction. Trust also partially mediated the relationship between service quality and satisfaction, indicating that e-service quality improves satisfaction both directly and through increased customer confidence. The SERVQUAL dimensions contributed positively to overall service quality, with responsiveness and assurance showing particularly strong contributions, while empathy exhibited a comparatively moderate contribution. In contrast, customer loyalty had no significant direct effect on trust or satisfaction, and its indirect effect on satisfaction through trust was also nonsignificant. These findings demonstrate that reliable, responsive, secure, and well-designed digital services are important for strengthening trust and satisfaction in competitive e-commerce environments. By identifying trust as a key mechanism linking multidimensional e-service quality with customer satisfaction, the study contributes to SERVQUAL and digital-commerce literature and provides implications for the economic and relational sustainability of e-commerce platforms through more resilient and durable customer relationships.

title: Effectiveness of childhood pneumonia awareness program among pregnant women: A hospital based quasi experimental study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pneumonia poses a substantial threat to the lives of the under five children in Nepal, underscoring the crucial role of maternal awareness in preventing this condition. The objective of the program was to assess the effectiveness of the Pneumonia awareness program designed to educate the expectant mothers, enrich their understanding, and empower them to take timely preventive measures against the Pneumonia.
METHODS: The study utilized an intervention-based concurrent mixed methods design, employing a quasi-experimental study to evaluate awareness and an exploratory design to assess perception of the pregnant women attending the hospital. A structured questionnaire was used for quantitative data, and interview guideline for qualitative study to conduct face-to-face interviews. The data analysis was performed by using STATA software. The knowledge of pneumonia before and after the awareness campaign was compared using a paired t test. The structured questionnaire covered a number of areas pertaining to pneumonia, including an overview of the disease, its symptoms, its mode of transmission, vaccination, and risk factors. The STROBE guideline was used to ensure standard reporting of the results.
RESULTS: The findings revealed the enhancement in the participant's knowledge. Their skill in identifying symptoms and immunizing their children against pneumonia improved. Notably, there was significant change in the knowledge level from pretest score to post test score indicating the effectiveness of the educational intervention. The participants in qualitative findings showed improved health -seeking behaviour, increased awareness of pneumonia and their commitment to preventive measures. The proactive intentions of early health seeking practice through identification of danger signs and adopting the preventive measures as complete dose of vaccination and controlling other risk factors were conveyed by the participants. Also, they perceived the program as effective in enhancing their knowledge and promoting their healthy behaviour.
CONCLUSION: The findings highlight the program's effectiveness and emphasize the importance of regularly promoting similar awareness campaigns as a strategy to improve maternal and child health. Educational programs play a crucial role in empowering mothers to take timely preventive measures, thereby reducing pneumonia-related risks in children under five. Regular promotion of such campaigns is recommended to maintain and enhance maternal and child health.

title: Effectiveness of dose-matched immersive virtual reality-stationary cycling combined with neurological physiotherapy versus neurological physiotherapy alone in individuals with chronic stroke (CIVIS): A single-blind, randomized crossover trial protocol.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stroke is a leading cause of long-term disability worldwide and frequently results in persistent motor and functional impairments, particularly affecting gait and balance. Given the high prevalence and impact of these limitations on independence and quality of life, innovative rehabilitation strategies are needed. Immersive virtual reality combined with stationary cycling (IVR-SC) has emerged as an innovative rehabilitation approach with the potential to improve mobility and functional outcomes after stroke.
AIM: To analyze the comparative effectiveness of two dose-matched programs, one combining IVR-SC plus neurological physiotherapy (NP), versus the other consisting of NP alone, in individuals with chronic stroke.
METHODS: A randomized, single-blind, crossover clinical trial will be conducted. After calculating the sample size, a minimum of 8 participants with chronic stroke (≥6 months), hemiparesis, and gait and balance impairments will be randomly assigned to one of two sequences of intervention. Each participant will receive both neurological physiotherapy and IVR-SC across two 4-week intervention periods separated by a washout period (4 weeks). Each intervention period consists of 8 sessions delivered over a 4-week period, with each session lasting 60 minutes. The primary outcome will be gait quality, assessed using Wisconsin Gait Scale (WGS), while secondary outcomes will include walking endurance, balance, motor function, and muscle tone. Clinical outcomes will be assessed at baseline and after each intervention period. Satisfaction with using the IVR-SC intervention will also be evaluated. Statistical analyses will follow an intention-to-treat approach using a linear mixed-effects model (LMM) with treatment, period, sequence, baseline, and center as fixed effects, and participant as a random effect. Statistical significance will be set at p < 0.05. An individual responder analysis will be performed to determine if participants exceeded the minimal clinically important difference (MCID) of 2.25 points on the WGS.
DISCUSSION: This study will contribute to understanding the potential comparative effects of IVR-SC in stroke rehabilitation. Given the heterogeneity of individuals with stroke, which may limit the conclusiveness of findings in parallel-group studies, the crossover design allows each participant to serve as their own control, reducing inter-individual variability and strengthening the interpretation of the results. If effective, IVR-SC could represent a feasible and scalable option for partially replacing NP within standard neurorehabilitation, with potential for implementation in both clinical and home-based settings.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT07529665. Effectiveness of dose-matched rehabilitation with immersive virtual reality-stationary cycling combined with neurological physiotherapy versus neurological physiotherapy alone in individuals with chronic stroke (CIVIS): study protocol for a single-blind, randomized crossover trial. URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07529665. Date of registration: 2026-04-14. Version 1.

title: Effects of laser processing parameters and scanning angle on damage morphology and residual tensile properties of CFRP laminates with a continuum damage mechanics model.
abstract: Laser processing of carbon fiber-reinforced polymer (CFRP) composites offers significant advantages in precision and efficiency, yet the thermal damage it induces remains a critical concern for structural integrity. This study investigates the effects of laser drilling and cutting on the damage morphology and residual tensile properties of T300-3K/epoxy CFRP laminates, with systematic variation of laser power, irradiation duration, scanning angle, and scanning distance across 21 processing conditions. White-light interferometric microscopy characterized three-dimensional ablation topography, and uniaxial tensile testing quantified mechanical degradation. For drilled specimens, increasing power from 250 W to 1000 W enlarged the ablation crater diameter by approximately 200% (1007-3021 μm), while extending irradiation duration from 0.5 s to 1.0 s produced a further 37% increase. For cut specimens, perpendicular scanning induced a broader heat-affected zone and more severe interfacial disruption than fiber-parallel scanning due to anisotropic thermal conductivity, with the maximum surface height difference reaching 4259 μm at 500 W and 90°. Residual tensile strength decreased monotonically with increasing energy input: drilled specimen strength declined from 735 MPa to 293 MPa (a reduction of over 60% to the pristine strength of 954 MPa); cut specimen strength at 500 W decreased from 466 MPa at 0° to 233 MPa at 90° due to progressive fiber severance, with cut specimens consistently weaker than drilled counterparts owing to kerf-induced stress concentration. A CDM-based empirical model integrating all four parameters was developed; nonlinear regression yielded A = 0.0266187, m = 0.464431, n = 0.645373, α = 0.0745099, β = 0.22664, and R2 = 0.9151, providing a validated quantitative tool for structural integrity assessment of laser-processed CFRP components.

title: Effects of vitamin D supplementation on vitamin D status and physical performance in football players: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Low vitamin D status is frequently reported among athletes, but whether vitamin D supplementation improves physical performance in football players remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the effects of vitamin D supplementation on serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] concentration, jump performance, sprint performance, aerobic capacity, and muscular performance in association football and futsal players.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from database inception to 31 May 2026. Controlled intervention studies comparing vitamin D supplementation with control conditions were eligible. Standardized mean differences were calculated as Hedges' g and pooled using random-effects meta-analyses. Two reviewers independently extracted data and assessed risk of bias using RoB 2 or ROBINS-I. The certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE. The protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261430873).
RESULTS: Eleven reports representing nine independent studies and 312 players were included. In RCT-only primary analyses, vitamin D supplementation was associated with higher circulating 25(OH)D concentrations (g = 1.41, 95% CI 0.90 to 1.92; I² = 58.0%). Pooled effects were not statistically significant for jump performance (g = 0.21, 95% CI -0.10 to 0.53), sprint performance (g = -0.03, 95% CI -0.40 to 0.34), aerobic capacity (g = 0.00, 95% CI -0.45 to 0.45), or muscular performance (g = 0.19, 95% CI -0.14 to 0.51). The certainty of evidence was low for circulating 25(OH)D, jump performance, and muscular performance, and very low for sprint performance and aerobic capacity.
CONCLUSIONS: Vitamin D supplementation was associated with increased circulating 25(OH)D concentrations, whereas current evidence is insufficient to support a consistent improvement in physical performance. Given the low to very low certainty of evidence, these findings should be interpreted cautiously. Larger, well-designed randomized controlled trials using standardized, football-relevant performance tests are warranted.

title: Efficacy of diadynamic currents versus transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation for transcutaneous tibial nerve stimulation in subjects with overactive bladder syndrome: A double-blind randomized controlled trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: In the traditional treatment of overactive bladder (OAB) with transcutaneous posterior tibial nerve stimulation (TTNS), physical therapists currently use only transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS). However, the literature has commonly replaced TENS with diadynamic currents for various musculoskeletal pain syndromes. Moreover, no literature describes the use of diadynamic currents in the TTNS procedure. Therefore, our study aimed to determine the efficacy of diadynamic currents (DDC) versus TENS for TTNS in OAB Treatment.
METHODOLOGY: A randomized controlled trial was conducted among female patients with OAB aged 18-80 years. Subjects were randomly allocated to control and experimental groups. Participants in the control group received TTNS with TENS, and those in the experimental group underwent TTNS using DDC. Both groups received 8 TTNS sessions, two per week for 4 weeks. We measured pre- and post-intervention improvements using the International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire (ICIQ) for OAB and the ICIQ OAB Quality of Life (QOL). The study is registered with the Clinical Trials Registry of India under registration number CTRI/2025/12/099269.
RESULTS: The mean age of the included sample was 59.75 years. Pre- and post-intervention ICIQ-OAB and ICIQ-OAB QOL scores showed significant improvements in disease symptoms and quality of life among patients with OAB in both the control and experimental groups. Comparison of improvements between the two groups on the ICIQ questionnaires showed no significant difference (p-values of 0.87 and 0.95). Correlations between patient-related characteristics and improvements in outcome measures were also not significant.
CONCLUSION: Eight sessions of TENS and DDC, combined with conventional physical therapy, including Kegel and breathing exercises, can reduce OAB symptoms and improve QOL in subjects with OAB syndrome. Diadynamic current can be used as an adjunct to conventional TENS in TTNS for treating OAB syndrome.

title: Enhancing medical education with AI: A comparative study of various large language models in radiology.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare how various Large Language Models (LLMs) perform when solving text- and image-based medical student-level radiology multiple-choice questions (MCQs).
METHODS: We evaluated the accuracy of seven LLMs (i.e., ChatGPT-4o, ChatGPT-5, ChatGPT-5 Plus, DeepSeek-V3.1-Terminus, Microsoft Copilot, Claude 4, and Gemini 2.5 Flash) in solving 60 text-based and 60 image-based MCQs. We compared the seven LLMs' accuracy across question types, domains, and topics.
RESULTS: The mean accuracy across the seven evaluated LLMs was 79.9% (671/840 correct responses). Claude 4 achieved the highest observed accuracy at 86.7%, whereas Gemini 2.5 Flash and Microsoft Copilot recorded the lowest accuracy at 75.0% each. Accuracy was substantially lower for image-based questions than for text-based questions (64.5% vs. 95.2%). In the generalized estimating equations analysis, question type was significantly associated with response accuracy (Wald χ2(1) = 64.53, p < 0.001), as were question domain (Wald χ2(1) = 6.86, p = 0.009) and the question type × domain interaction (Wald χ2(3) = 80.26, p < 0.001). The omnibus effect of model was not statistically significant after accounting for these factors (Wald χ2(6) = 6.59, p = 0.361). Although Claude 4 achieved the highest observed accuracy, no pairwise model comparison remained statistically significant after Bonferroni correction.
CONCLUSIONS: Large Language Models are less accurate at solving image-based than text-based radiology questions, supporting their role as adjunctive educational tools that require faculty oversight rather than independent replacements for radiology instruction.

title: Epidemiological surveillance of bacterial pathogens in cultured European sea bass (Dicentrarchus labrax) along the Aegean coast of Türkiye.
abstract: Intensive aquaculture of European sea bass (Dicentrarchus labrax) along the Aegean coast of Türkiye faces continuous production challenges from infectious diseases, yet comprehensive multi-year baseline data remain limited. This study presents a multi-year retrospective surveillance program (2020-2025) monitoring bacterial pathogens associated with 748 distinct cage-level disease outbreaks in fish across 19 discrete offshore commercial sea farms. To maintain industry confidentiality, diagnostic data from these separate facilities were fully aggregated and evaluated across three broad macro-regional surveillance zones. A total of 5,235 fish displaying clinical signs underwent diagnostic necropsy. Presumptive bacterial identification was conducted using phenotypic profiling through the API 20E system, and organ touch-imprint cytology. Six distinct bacterial species were isolated from positive clinical individuals, recovering a total of 2,490 isolates. Across the recorded outbreak events, etiological agents were ranked as primary drivers as follows: Photobacterium damselae subsp. piscicida (48.80%; N = 365), Tenacibaculum maritimum (35.83%; N = 268), Vibrio (Listonella) anguillarum (9.49%; N = 71), V. harveyi (3.74%; N = 28), V. ordalii (1.20%; N = 9), and V. alginolyticus (0.94%; N = 7). This hierarchy directly mirrored the overall bacterial isolation frequency, where P. damselae subsp. piscicida showed the highest relative distribution rate (46.18%; n = 1,150), followed by T. maritimum (34.10%; n = 849). Significantly lower isolation rates were recorded for V. (Listonella) anguillarum (11.41%; n = 284), V. harveyi (5.26%; n = 131), V. ordalii (1.77%; n = 44), and V. alginolyticus (1.29%; n = 32). Descriptive tracking of the purified laboratory isolates revealed localized variations in diagnostic recovery frequencies among the three sectors, while establishing a highly stable baseline dominated by P. damselae subsp. piscicida and T. maritimum across the Eastern Aegean Turkish mariculture network.

title: Estimation of aerobic and anaerobic performance using a novel intermittent reactive agility test - An exploratory correlation study.
abstract: Separate tests are usually used to assess an athlete's ability to meet the aerobic and anaerobic demands of ball sports. These tests often compromise ecological validity by relying on linear runs and sprints rather than multidirectional reactive agility. This study investigated the correlations between a novel motor-cognitive reactive agility (RA) test and aerobic and anaerobic performance indices. Twenty-two trained participants (V˙O2max: 56 ± 6.4 ml ∙ kg-1 ∙ min-1) performed a treadmill ramp test to determine maximum oxygen uptake (V˙O2max), a running-based anaerobic sprint test (RAST) to determine peak power output (PPO), average power putput (POAV), fatigue index (FI) and anaerobic capacity (AC) and a motor-cognitive RA test on the SKILLCOURT. The RA test required participants to perform four 150 m maximal multidirectional change of directions runs with a break of 30 s. Running time, heart rate and power output were determined for all runs and correlated to V˙O2max and anaerobic performance indicators. Running time of the 4th SKILLCOURT run was correlated to V˙O2max (r20 = -0.80, p < 0.001) and a strong relation was found between PPO determined in the RAST and SKILLCOURT test (r20 = 0.72, p < 0.001). The SKILLCOURT RA test provides a promising tool for sport coaches to monitor aerobic and anaerobic performance indices, considering reactive agility. This needs to be validated in future studies.

title: Ethnic disparities in outcomes of coronary artery bypass grafting in Israel.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Ethnic disparities after cardiac surgery are well reported. Israeli Arabs have lower life expectancy and greater frequency of cardiovascular risk factors. We sought to compare long-term outcomes following coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) between Arab and Jewish patients in Israel.
METHODS: Retrospective study of adult patients with multivessel disease undergoing isolated CABG in three centers between January 1st, 2009, and December 31st, 2023. The primary outcome was a composite of major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE). The cumulative incidence of MACCE was plotted using KM curves. The hazard ratio (HR) for Arabs vs. Jewish were calculated using multivariate Cox models.
RESULTS: Our cohort included 6,330 patients, 1,819 (28.74%) and 4,511 (71.26%) patients were Arabs and Jewish, respectively. Median follow-up time was 78.32 months. Arab patients had higher rate of the primary outcome at median follow-up (46.26% vs 40.90%, HR 1.184, 95%CI: 1.09-1.286, P < 0.001) and there was no difference in mortality between the two groups (26.44% vs 26.45%, HR 1.004, 95%CI: 0.901-1.118, P = 0.82). After multivariable adjustment, the risk of MACCE was similar between the groups (adjusted HR 1.073, 95%CI: 0.965-1.193, P = 0.19).
CONCLUSIONS: After multivariable adjustment for baseline and socioeconomic factors, ethnicity was not independently associated with worse long-term clinical outcomes in patients undergoing CABG in Israel, while unadjusted disparities remained evident.

title: Evaluating a candidate predictor beyond statistical significance: Atmospheric pressure and psychiatric day-care attendance as a worked example.
abstract: In observational research, statistical detectability, robustness to adjustment, and predictive utility are distinct properties of a candidate predictor, yet they are often conflated. A statistically significant association may weaken after accounting for co-varying factors and may add little to out-of-sample prediction. We illustrate this distinction using atmospheric pressure and daily attendance at a Japanese psychiatric day-care as a worked example. Using four consecutive fiscal years of facility-level daily attendance, we evaluated same-day atmospheric pressure as a pre-specified candidate predictor in three stages: statistical detectability, robustness to adjustment for co-varying meteorological factors and seasonality, and incremental out-of-sample predictive utility beyond institutional scheduling variables and recent attendance history. Same-day pressure was positively associated with attendance in all four years (incidence rate ratios 1.003-1.007 per hPa). However, effect-estimate stability varied across years, with marked attenuation in FY2022, moderate attenuation after precipitation adjustment in FY2023, and specification-sensitive precision in FY2024, whereas FY2025 was comparatively stable. In contrast, the structural baseline incorporating scheduling variables and recent attendance history provided strong out-of-sample prediction, explaining 55%-69% of the variance across years. Adding atmospheric pressure produced only small and unstable changes in the primary expanding-window cross-validated performance (mean ΔR2 ≈ +0.005), with increments varying in sign across years. Thus, a candidate predictor that was repeatedly statistically detectable showed limited stability of effect magnitude or precision under reasonable adjustment and little incremental predictive utility beyond a strong structural baseline. In this highly schedule-driven, single-facility setting, the weather signal examined contributed little incremental information for out-of-sample prediction of aggregate attendance. More broadly, this worked example illustrates why candidate predictors should be evaluated separately for detectability, robustness of effect estimates, and out-of-sample predictive utility before statistically significant associations are interpreted as meaningful or actionable.

title: Evaluating the effectiveness of open-weight LLMs for multi-domain Bengali text classification with zero-shot and few-shot prompting.
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have advanced multilingual NLP significantly, yet their effectiveness for Bengali, a globally important but low-resource language, remains understudied due to limited linguistic resources and the absence of a standardized evaluation benchmark. This is due to the unavailability of large linguistic resources and the lack of a standard benchmarking framework, which has yet to be established. This study aims to address the underrepresentation of Bengali text classification by leading a systematic evaluation. It involves assessing multiple open-weight LLMs on Bengali text classification tasks and observing their limitations and regular error patterns. The procedure consists of six open-weight LLMs, which include LLaMA-3.2-3B, Mistral-V3-7B, DeepSeek-R1-8B, Phi-4-14B, Gemma-2-27B, and Qwen-2.5-72B, and are evaluated using four critical text classification tasks in Bengali, namely sentiment analysis, emotion recognition, hate-speech detection, and fake-news classification. Furthermore, two prompting methods are compared in the context of zero-shot and few-shot prompting using both the vLLM inference engine and Hugging Face Transformers pipelines to investigate the adaptability of the models in resource-limited settings. Across all four tasks, the two largest models (Qwen-2.5-72B and Gemma-2-27B) obtained the highest scores, although the ranking was not strictly monotonic in parameter count and, because each scale is represented by a single model family, the design cannot attribute these differences to model size alone. When training in zero-shot, Qwen-2.5-72B showed the best performance at 79.90% accuracy and 79.88% Macro-F1 score, showing amazing accuracy on hate-speech detection. In the case of fake news, Gemma-2-27B performed best at 84.45% accuracy and 84.33% Macro-F1 score. With a few-shot set-up, Gemma-2-27B and Qwen-2.5-72B demonstrated a high level of performance in terms of Macro-F1 score, reaching 84.17% for fake-news detection and 66.80% for emotion recognition, respectively. Paired multi-model tests (Cochran's Q with Holm-corrected McNemar post-hoc comparisons) confirmed significant differences among the six models across all tasks and prompting settings, whereas the effect of five-shot prompting, obtained with a single fixed demonstration set, was significant for only 4 of 24 model-task combinations after correction and never for the three largest models. The findings characterise benchmark classification performance under the evaluated settings rather than real-world effectiveness, and indicate that model scale, multilingual pre-training, and in-context demonstrations are jointly associated with, but cannot be causally isolated as drivers of, performance on Bengali text classification.

title: Evaluation of the efficacy of Si-based agent in Rheumatoid Arthritis with complicating vestibular impairment.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by persistent joint inflammation and progressive disability. Although current therapies have improved clinical outcomes, safer and more effective therapeutic approaches remain needed. Silicon (Si)-based agents have antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties and have shown beneficial effects in several inflammatory disease models.
METHODS: We evaluated the effects of oral administration of a Si-based agent in a type II collagen-induced arthritis mouse model. Arthritis severity was assessed using an arthritis index, hindlimb oedema, and the hindlimb extension reflex test. Serum type II collagen-specific autoantibody levels were also measured. Vestibular function was evaluated using the vestibulo-ocular reflex (VOR), and inner-ear structural changes were assessed by magnetic resonance imaging and histological analysis.
RESULTS: The Si-based agent reduced arthritis-related outcomes, including the arthritis index, hindlimb oedema, and joint movement restriction, and reduced serum type II collagen-specific autoantibody levels. In contrast, no significant differences between the Si-based agent and control groups were detected in VOR-related outcomes, endolymphatic space measurements, or inner-ear histological findings.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that the Si-based agent may have beneficial effects on arthritis-related manifestations. However, its effects on the vestibular function-related outcomes examined in this study were not evident. Further studies are needed to clarify the relationship between RA and vestibular dysfunction and to determine the potential therapeutic effects of Si-based agent on these complications.
