title: Experimental and theoretical investigation of parameter-driven stability and chaos in a non-linear neuron circuit model.
abstract: In this study, a neural-inspired electronic circuit consisting of a pressure-sensitive FitzHugh-Nagumo model with the addition of a piezoelectric bi-membrane and two capacitors is explored. The governing equations are obtained analytically from Kirchhoff's laws, which represent the nonlinear interactions, oscillatory response, and stability of the circuit. A perturbation term is added to investigate the deviations from the system potential, and the transitions in the system are studied under the assumption of the model. By applying statistical methods and eigenvalue analysis, the parameter space is systematically subdivided and examined, and the results show that the behavior of the system is dominated by divergent behavior, although some periodic oscillatory behavior is seen in certain regions. This highlights the importance of initial conditions and parameter selection on the behavior of the system, which are essential to obtaining stable behavior and developing an efficient control design. Furthermore, an ensemble-size sensitivity analysis is performed to verify the robustness and convergence of the statistical characterization across different numbers of initial conditions. Phase disturbance plots, power spectrum density plots, attractor reconstruction plots, return maps, and noise detection maps are used to analyze the system dynamics. In addition, a multi-sum (multi-parameter interaction) diagram is created to depict the interactions between circuit variables and the overall system behavior.

title: Exploratory cluster analysis of noninvasive vascular measures reveals heterogeneous vascular profiles after stroke.
abstract: Vascular dysfunction is prevalent after stroke and contributes to elevated cardiovascular risk; however, the extent to which vascular heterogeneity exists in this population remains unclear. This study examined whether distinct multi-domain cluster-derived vascular profiles are present in individuals with chronic stroke and whether these profiles are associated with functional performance. Vascular structure and function were assessed using flow-mediated dilation, carotid intima-media thickness, pulse wave velocity, and augmentation index, with age included in vascular clustering to account for vascular aging. Unsupervised k-means clustering was applied to identify vascular profiles. Functional performance was assessed using gait speed and predicted peak oxygen consumption (VO2peak) derived from a submaximal exercise test. Between-cluster differences were characterized using analysis of variance. Forty-five individuals with chronic stroke (62 ± 12 years; 29 ± 30 months post-stroke) were included. Three vascular profiles were identified (cluster 1: n = 13; cluster 2: n = 11; cluster 3: n = 21), with significant differences across clusters for all vascular measures (p < 0.01). Although age increased across clusters, vascular structure and function did not change uniformly. One profile exhibited elevated arterial wave reflection despite relatively preserved endothelial function and arterial structure, whereas another demonstrated impairment in all vascular variables. Vascular profile was not associated with predicted VO2peak (p = 0.31) or gait speed (p = 0.65). Three exploratory cluster-derived vascular profiles emerged among participants with chronic stroke, and age did not fully account for the observed vascular heterogeneity. Multi-domain cluster-derived vascular profiling revealed heterogeneous vascular profiles in individuals with chronic stroke, providing a basis for future studies to evaluate their relevance to cardiovascular risk stratification and long-term health management. title: Finite-time robust motion control of intelligent vehicles based on neural approximation and disturbance estimation.
abstract: This paper addresses the inherent trade off between rapid convergence and high‑precision disturbance rejection in intelligent vehicle motion control under severe nonlinearities, parametric uncertainties, and time varying external perturbations. A composite finite‑time robust control strategy is proposed by synergistically integrating a nonsingular fast terminal sliding mode (NFTSM) surface, radial basis function neural networks (RBFNN), and a finite time disturbance observer (FTDO). The NFTSM guarantees singularity free finite time convergence of the tracking errors. The RBFNN approximates the slowly varying unknown dynamics, while the FTDO compensates online for the neural approximation residual and fast varying disturbances in a cascaded "coarse to fine" manner. Lyapunov-based Extensive co‑simulations with MATLAB/Simulink, conducted under double lane change and sinusoidal path scenarios with simultaneous road friction drops and stochastic lateral wind gusts, demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly outperforms conventional nonsingular terminal sliding mode control and disturbance observer based sliding mode control in terms of tracking accuracy, convergence speed, and chattering suppression.

title: Fruit and vegetable consumption among people living with HIV at a large Urban HIV Clinic in Central Uganda: A cross-sectional study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fruit and vegetable consumption has been shown to effectively reduce the risk of developing non-communicable diseases such as hypertension. This study assessed the prevalence, perceptions and factors associated with fruit and vegetable consumption among people living with HIV (PLHIV) at an Urban HIV clinic in central Uganda.
METHODS: This was a cross-sectional study conducted at the Infectious Diseases Institute (IDI) HIV clinic located in Kampala, Uganda. An adapted World Health Organisation STEPwise questionnaire was administered with Open Data Kit (ODK) to a random sample of 431 PLHIV clients aged 18 years and older to obtain data on levels and perceptions of fruit and vegetable consumption. Adequate intake of fruits and vegetables was defined as consumption of five or more servings of fruits and/ or vegetables per day in a typical week. We conducted multivariable robust Poisson regression to determine the independent factors associated with adequate fruit and vegetable consumption. Data were analyzed in Stata version 17.0.
RESULTS: A total of 44 out of 417 (10.6%) respondents met the WHO recommendations of fruit and vegetable consumption. Overall, the perceptions of respondents about consumption of a fruits and vegetables were favourable (mean = 3.7, SD = 0.5), with the construct of perceived barriers to eating fruits and vegetables (mean = 3.2, SD = 1.6) having the least favourable perceptions. Being unemployed (APR: 0.1, 95% CI:0.0-0.8, p = 0.027), having a higher household income (APR:0.99, 95% CI: 0.900-0.998, p = 0.039) and having a longer duration on Antiretroviral Therapy (ART) (APR:0.9, 95% CI:0.89-0.996, p = 0.046) were significantly associated with inadequate consumption of fruits and vegetables.
CONCLUSIONS: Fruit and vegetable consumption among PLHIV was low. Our findings underscore the need for targeted strategies and interventions to promote healthy dietary practices, reduce perceived barriers, and improve awareness of hypertension risk among PLHIV.

title: Fuzzy-clustering-based multi-scale intrusion detection for the industrial internet of things.
abstract: The Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) faces severe intrusion-detection challenges under multi-protocol, multi-device, and massive heterogeneous traffic, especially extreme class imbalance and poor minority-class detection. To address this, we propose a fuzzy-clustering-based multi-scale intrusion detection model (FPBW-IDS). At the data level, we introduce boundary-prioritized FCM-SMOTE: fuzzy memberships distinguish core vs. border samples, interpolation is prioritized in high-membership regions, and sampling weights are adjusted by membership, thereby significantly enhancing minority-class representation and suppressing noise diffusion while keeping the majority class fixed at a multiplier of 1.0. At the feature-learning level, we build three parallel branches across the spatial, temporal, and frequency domains: parallel Pyramid Depthwise Separable Convolutions (PDSC) to capture spatial (cross-feature) dependencies, BiGRU to model temporal dependencies, and wavelet transforms to extract multi-scale spectral statistics; their outputs are fused with learned weighting to form a complementary tri-domain representation. Experiments on the CICIDS2017 dataset show that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance under both unsampled and sampled settings: Accuracy 99.39%, Precision 98.22%, Recall 93.69%, F1 95.56% in the comprehensive comparison; and Accuracy 98.97%, Recall 99.09%, F1 96.69% in a recall-oriented setting, markedly reducing missed detections while maintaining stable training/validation curves and a small generalization gap. These results show the effectiveness and reliability of clustering-guided oversampling combined with tri-domain multi-scale representation for IIoT intrusion detection.

title: GT-PNID: A lightweight graph-temporal network integrating GCN and transformer for power network intrusion detection.
abstract: Driven by the advancement of information technology, the transformation of traditional power grids toward intelligence has rendered power systems more vulnerable to cybersecurity risks arising from greater openness and connectivity. Smart grid communication networks exhibit high heterogeneity, diverse protocols, and strict real-time constraints. Existing intrusion detection systems suffer from two key limitations: neglect of spatiotemporal dependencies in network traffic, which hinders the modeling of complex attack evolution, and absence of a unified detection framework with cross-scenario generalization capability. To overcome these limitations, this study develops GT-PNID, a graph-temporal network-based intrusion detection model designed for grid communication networks. The model utilizes a sliding-window dynamic graph construction mechanism to transform heterogeneous traffic into spatiotemporal graph structures. Subsequently, graph convolutional layers are applied to extract local spatial features, while a multilayer Transformer is introduced to model long-range temporal dependencies, followed by graph-level feature fusion for joint spatiotemporal representation. Experiments on CICIDS2017 and NSL-KDD datasets demonstrate that accuracy and F1-scores exceed 99.98%, while the model's parameter count (424,478) and per-sample inference time (0.09 ms) are substantially lower than mainstream methods, confirming its superior detection capability, lightweight efficiency, and cross-dataset generalization potential for smart grid security.

title: HIF-1α/PPAR-γ/SIRT1 axis drives astrocyte senescence and regulates endothelial function via GDNF/NRTN in diabetic retinopathy.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a leading cause of blindness in working-age populations. Astrocyte senescence is highly prevalent in DR, but the underlying regulatory mechanism remains unclear. This study aims to investigate the role of the HIF-1α/PPAR-γ/SIRT1 axis in regulating retinal astrocyte senescence and endothelial function in DR.
METHODS: Mouse retinal astrocytes were exposed to high glucose (30 mM) to mimic diabetic conditions. Senescence was evaluated by β-galactosidase staining. Signaling pathways were manipulated using HIF-1α inhibitor (PX-478), PPAR-γ inhibitor (T0070907), SIRT1 agonist (SRT2104), and autophagy inhibitor (3-MA). Protein and mRNA levels of key factors were detected by Western blot and RT-qPCR. Astrocytes and retinal microvascular endothelial cells were co-cultured in Transwell systems to assess paracrine regulation on endothelial migration, proliferation, and apoptosis.
RESULTS: High glucose induced astrocyte senescence, inflammatory activation, and downregulation of GDNF and NRTN, accompanied by elevated HIF-1α and PPAR-γ, and reduced SIRT1 expression and autophagy activity. Inhibiting HIF-1α or activating SIRT1 attenuated senescence, apoptosis, and inflammation, restored autophagy, and upregulated GDNF/NRTN secretion. HIF-1α negatively regulated SIRT1 expression via PPAR-γ. Senescent astrocytes impaired endothelial function through reduced GDNF/NRTN; overexpression of GDNF or NRTN in astrocytes preserved endothelial migration and proliferation, and inhibited apoptosis.
CONCLUSION: HIF-1α/PPAR-γ/SIRT1 axis mediates high glucose-induced astrocyte senescence via autophagy dysfunction. Senescent astrocytes disrupt retinal endothelial homeostasis by reducing GDNF/NRTN secretion. Targeting this axis may represent a novel neurovascular protective therapeutic strategy for DR.

title: HIV/AIDS knowledge and stigmatizing attitudes among adult residents of the United Arab Emirates: A cross-sectional study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: HIV-related stigma remains a significant barrier to prevention and treatment efforts in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region. This study assessed HIV knowledge and stigmatizing attitudes among United Arab Emirates (UAE) residents.
METHODS: A cross-sectional survey was conducted across the UAE between January and March 2025. A total of 1,211 eligible adult residents were recruited through convenience sampling. Demographic analyses included all 1,211 participants, while HIV knowledge and stigma analyses included 1,171 participants with analyzable outcome data. The questionnaire assessed demographics, HIV transmission knowledge, and stigmatizing attitudes using the Stigmatizing Attitudes Towards People Living with HIV/AIDS Scale (SAT-PLWHA-S). Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, bivariate analyses, and multiple linear regression.
RESULTS: Among the 1,211 participants included in the study, 1,171 contributed analyzable data to the HIV knowledge and stigma analyses. While 96.4% had heard of HIV/AIDS and demonstrated moderately high transmission knowledge (mean score: 75.5%), significant misconceptions persisted, particularly regarding condom effectiveness (60.5% overestimated risk). Strong stigmatizing attitudes emerged, especially regarding criminalization of transmission (79.6% support) and moralistic views. Higher knowledge correlated with less stigma (r = 0.347, p < 0.001), though nationality, language preference, and knowing someone with HIV were stronger predictors. Only 6.2% knew someone with HIV.
CONCLUSIONS: Despite adequate basic knowledge, significant HIV-related stigma persists in the UAE, driven by cultural and moral perspectives. Comprehensive interventions combining education, contact-based strategies, and policy reform are needed to reduce stigma and improve HIV prevention outcomes.

title: Harrowing experiences of vagina fistula victims in the Kpandai District of Ghana: A qualitative study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vaginal fistula (VF), particularly vesicovaginal fistula (VVF), remains a significant reproductive health challenge in many low-resource settings, including the Kpandai District of Ghana. Despite its profound physical and psychosocial impact, the lived experiences of affected women in rural districts remain under-documented.
AIM: This study explored the lived experiences of women diagnosed with vesicovaginal fistula in the Kpandai District of Ghana, focusing on their physical, emotional, and social challenges, as well as coping strategies.
METHODS: A qualitative descriptive study was conducted using in-depth interviews with ten women with clinically confirmed VVF. Participants were initially identified through a district health facility and subsequently recruited using a combination of purposive and snowball sampling techniques. Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analysed thematically.
RESULTS: Prolonged and obstructed labour-often occurring at home-emerged as the primary reported cause of VVF. Cultural beliefs, gender-based decision-making dynamics, limited access to healthcare, and financial constraints were key barriers to timely medical intervention. Consequences included persistent urinary incontinence, social stigma, emotional trauma, marital dissolution (reported by eight participants), loss of livelihood, and social isolation. Coping strategies included frequent washing, use of absorbent materials, and reliance on perfumes or herbal remedies.
CONCLUSIONS: Vesicovaginal fistula remains a devastating yet largely preventable condition in rural Ghana. The findings highlight the need to strengthen maternal health services, improve timely referral systems, and integrate psychosocial support within community-based care frameworks.

title: Intravenous midazolam alters short-interval paired-pulse TMS responses differently in younger and older adults.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Aging is associated with changes in cortical excitability and altered responsiveness to benzodiazepines, but the effects of benzodiazepine challenge on motor cortical paired-pulse physiology in older adults remain incompletely understood. We examined whether intravenous midazolam differentially modulates corticospinal excitability and short-interval paired-pulse transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) responses in younger and older adults.
METHODS: Sixteen younger adults (18-35 years) and sixteen older adults (50-69 years) underwent single-pulse and paired-pulse (conditioning stimulus: 110% motor threshold; test stimulus: 143% motor threshold) TMS of the left primary motor cortex at baseline and during intravenous midazolam administration. Single-pulse motor evoked potential (MEP) amplitude was used to assess corticospinal excitability. Short-interval paired-pulse responses were quantified as the ratio of conditioned to unconditioned MEP amplitude.
RESULTS: At baseline, younger adults showed greater corticospinal excitability than older adults, reflected by larger single-pulse MEP amplitudes (adjusted p = 0.04). Younger adults demonstrated paired-pulse inhibition at baseline, reflected by a conditioned/unconditioned MEP ratio below 1.0 (ratio = 0.73; adjusted p < 0.01), whereas older adults did not show inhibition and instead had a mean ratio above 1.0 (ratio = 1.25). Midazolam reduced single-pulse MEP amplitudes in both groups. During midazolam administration, paired-pulse inhibition was no longer observed in younger adults, and older adults continued to show no evidence of inhibition.
CONCLUSIONS: Younger and older adults differed in baseline corticospinal excitability and in short-interval paired-pulse TMS responses. Intravenous midazolam reduced corticospinal excitability and altered paired-pulse response patterns, eliminating baseline paired-pulse inhibition in younger adults while producing little measurable change in older adults. These findings suggest that aging may modify the net motor cortical response to benzodiazepine challenge. The results should be interpreted in relation to the paired-pulse stimulation parameters used and support further studies using complementary approaches to characterize age-related differences in inhibitory and facilitatory motor cortical circuits.

title: Introduction of contraceptive implants as a family planning strategy in Honduras and Chiapas: Results from the Salud Mesoamerica Initiative (SMI).
abstract: Expanding access to a broad range of contraceptive methods is critical for reducing unintended pregnancies and improving reproductive health. This study evaluates the introduction of subdermal contraceptive implants in the selected areas of Honduras and Chiapas, Mexico, in the context of the Salud Mesoamérica Initiative, a results-based financing program focused on disadvantaged populations. Data were obtained from household surveys conducted between 2012 and 2022 among women aged 15-49 years in selected intervention and comparison municipalities in Chiapas, Mexico, and Honduras, using a two-stage sampling design. Indicators included contraceptive prevalence rates, reasons for method switching, and adoption by sociodemographic characteristics. Findings show a substantial increase in implant use in both settings over time. In the selected areas of Honduras, implant uptake increased gradually, reaching 7.9% in the 2022 SMI household survey, while in the selected areas of Chiapas use rose to 7.2%. Younger women aged 20-29 years and those with full literacy exhibited the highest adoption rates. In the selected areas of Chiapas and Honduras, implants most often replaced non-modern and short-acting hormonal methods, suggesting successful integration into the existing method mix. Variations in adoption across sociodemographic subgroups highlight persistent inequities. The results underscore the potential of subdermal implants to expand access to long-acting reversible contraception in resource-limited settings. To sustain and enhance this progress, strategies must address sociocultural and structural barriers, ensuring equitable access across all population groups and mitigating service disruptions. These findings may inform future strategies to expand informed contraceptive choice in similar resource-limited settings; their effects on reproductive health outcomes require further evaluation.

title: Male breast cancer in Northern Tanzania: Clinicopathology and predictors of two-year survival (2016-2022).
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Male breast cancer (BC) is rare, accounting to approximately 1% of all breast cancers worldwide. Patients often present with advanced disease, contributing to poor outcomes. This study aimed to estimate two-year overall survival (OS) and identify clinicopathological and health-system-related predictors of survival among men with breast cancer treated at Kilimanjaro Christian Medical Centre (KCMC).
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted among 55 histologically confirmed male BC patients managed at KCMC between 2016 and 2022. The primary outcome was two-year overall survival, defined as time from histological diagnosis to death from any cause or censoring at two years. The dependent variables were clinical and pathological factors and the key independent variable was overall survival (OS). Descriptive statistics summarized participants characteristics. Kaplan-Meier curves, log-rank and Cox proportional hazards regression were used to estimate the OS and the factors associated. A p-value <0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: The mean age at diagnosis was 62.2 ± 14.3 years, with most patients (54.6%) aged between 50-70 years. Over half (52.7%) presented with stage III or IV disease, and 21.8% had distant metastasis. Invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC) was the predominant histological subtype (85.5%), and luminal B was the most common molecular profile (23.6%). Surgery was performed in 60% of patients, chemotherapy in 47.3%, hormonal therapy in 30.9%, and radiotherapy in only 9.1%. The overall two-year survival rate was 67.3%. Independent predictors of poor survival included age > 70 years (p = 0.009), stage IV disease (p = 0.005), delayed receipt of histopathological results (> 2 weeks), delayed surgery (>6 weeks), and non-receipt of hormonal therapy or radiotherapy.
CONCLUSION: Male BC in Northern Tanzania remains a disease for older who frequently present with advanced-stages. Two-year overall survival remains suboptimal and is strongly influenced by advanced disease stage, older age, diagnostic and treatment delays, and limited access to adjuvant therapies. Strengthening early diagnosis, timely pathology reporting, and access to radiotherapy and hormonal therapy may substantially improve outcomes.

title: Multi-feature fusion for grassland information extraction and temporal change monitoring.
abstract: Grasslands play a vital role in maintaining ecological security and supporting sustainable development, yet accurate extraction and dynamic monitoring remain challenging in complex mountainous regions. This study takes Chengbu Miao Autonomous County, Hunan Province, as the study area and develops a multi-feature fusion framework on the Google Earth Engine platform by integrating optical imagery, Sentinel-1 SAR data, vegetation indices, texture features, topographic factors, and time-series characteristics. A Random Forest model was employed for high-accuracy grassland extraction, while multi-temporal remote sensing observations from selected cloud-free years between 2000 and 2025 were used to analyze long-term spatial distribution and temporal dynamics. Fractional vegetation cover (FVC) was introduced to assess grassland ecological conditions, and Nanshan Pasture was selected to investigate the impacts of topography, human activities, and climatic factors on grassland variation. The results show that multi-feature fusion significantly improves classification accuracy, achieving an overall accuracy (OA) of 93.79% and a Kappa coefficient of 0.7165 in the optimal feature combination scheme, with optical and SAR data exhibiting strong complementarity under complex terrain conditions. Grassland area in Chengbu County remained relatively stable from 2000 to 2025, with annual variations ranging from 47.32 to 52.15 km² and no significant long-term change trend. The mean FVC exhibited relatively stable interannual fluctuations, with values generally ranging from 0.59 to 0.72 during most years. However, spatial analysis of FVC trends revealed considerable heterogeneity, with significant decreasing trends observed in localized areas, particularly in the southwestern part of Nanshan Pasture, indicating potential vegetation degradation risks. In Nanshan Pasture, FVC showed a significant negative correlation with DEM (r = -0.2839) and precipitation (r = -0.589), while correlations with human activities and land surface temperature were relatively weak. Overall, grassland dynamics in the study area may reflect the combined effects of environmental conditions and human activities, although the relationships identified in this study mainly represent statistical associations rather than causal mechanisms. The proposed framework provides an effective methodological reference for grassland monitoring, ecological assessment, and sustainable management in subtropical mountainous grassland environments.

title: Mutation-induced structural and dynamic perturbations at the IL-17A-IL-17RA interface: Therapeutic insights from multi-replicate molecular dynamics simulations.
abstract: The interaction between Interleukin-17A (IL-17A) and its receptor IL-17RA plays a key role in pro-inflammatory signal transduction and is implicated in the pathogenesis of inflammatory autoimmune diseases. Blocking this protein-protein interaction is a major approach to developing therapeutic agents to inhibit IL-17A-induced signaling. Predicting the consequences of mutations on structure and function in proteins can be accomplished by using computational methods, which are relatively inexpensive and rapid compared with experimental methods. Here, we used a multidimensional in silico approach to gain insight into the functional and thermodynamic consequences of targeted mutation of hotspot residues of IL-17A. The focus of our analysis was on the residues in the two chains that are equivalent to hotspot residues of the related cytokine, IL-17F, at positions 55 and 67 of chain B and 85 and 86 of chain A. Comprehensive analysis of the conformational dynamics, interaction profiles, and structural transitions of the four mutant variant systems (R55V, W67V, Y85I, and H86S) and the wild-type system was performed based on molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and Molecular Mechanics/Generalized Born Surface Area (MM/GBSA) calculations. A total of 3 μs simulations were performed: three 200 ns replicates for each of the wild-type and mutant complexes. Results from principal component analysis (PCA) and free energy landscape (FEL) analyses indicate conformational destabilization of the mutant systems. These findings help to elucidate the mechanisms of molecular interactions involved in the dynamics of cytokine-receptor interaction. Changes in these important PSN network parameters resulted in differences in hub connectivity and distribution of the links between the systems, which suggests allosteric perturbations and remodeling of the system in the interaction between IL-17A and IL-17RA when compared to the wild-type systems. The multiple-replica MD simulation protocol provided insight into how mutations affected the structure, contact networks, dynamics, and binding affinity of the IL-17A/IL-17RA complex, shedding light on the IL-17A downstream signaling cascades. Overall, this study provides a fundamental framework for designing therapeutic strategies to regulate IL-17A-mediated inflammatory diseases.

title: Neuromodulatory effects of audio-proprio-phonatory reinforcement training on subjective tinnitus, a HD-EEG study protocol.
abstract: Tinnitus affects 14% of the global population, with 2% experiencing a severe form of the condition. Sound therapy using white noise emitted by hearing aids is a common intervention, supported by the phenomenon of residual inhibition observed during tinnitus assessment. This study aims to investigate whether audio-proprio-phonatory reinforcement training can improve the quality of life of patients with chronic subjective tinnitus by enabling them to listen to their own phonation, which may mask the tinnitus or induce residual inhibition. We will conduct a prospective, controlled, monocentric, 2-arm block-randomized study, stratified by the Tinnitus Handicap Inventory (THI) score, involving two groups for two sequential phases (Phase 1 and Phase 2). Fifty-six patients with tinnitus, recruited from the Ear Nose Throat (ENT) Department of Orléans University Hospital, will undergo a five-week training program, randomized into weekly remote group workshops, and daily individual sessions using specially developed videos. Training efficacy will be assessed through self-report questionnaires. The primary endpoint, the Tinnitus Handicap Inventory, will be assessed at three ENT medical visits: at inclusion, end of phase 1 and end of phase 2. Additionally, patients in both groups will regularly complete Visual Analog Scales for Tinnitus and five related questions (noise, cervical, jaw, sleep, stress-anxiety) via a secure digital platform throughout the study. High-density electroencephalograms (HD-EEG) will be performed in a blinded manner before and after Phase 1 at the Neurology Department of Orléans University Hospital. This pilot study aims to evaluate the clinical efficacy of audio-proprio-phonatory training in patients with chronic subjective tinnitus and to objectively measure its effects using HD-EEG. We will explore potential correlations between changes brain activity (such as functional brain connectivity) and clinical responses to the intervention.

title: PINN-based functional inference in size-structured population models: Application to fish oogenesis.
abstract: Early oogenesis in juvenile fish establishes the ovarian reserve, which conditions lifelong reproductive capacity. This process is regulated by local hormonal feedback mechanisms, mainly involving Anti-Müllerian Hormone (AMH). In this work, we develop a mechanistic size-structured population model describing an unstructured germ-cell compartment and a population of growing oocytes, with AMH feedback on the renewal of the precursor cells compartment. Using repeated cross-sectional observations of oocyte size distributions in fish ovaries, we formulate and solve a nonlinear inverse problem with Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) to infer three demographic functions: the size-dependent oocyte growth rate, the AMH-regulated net renewal rate of the precursor cells compartment, and the recruitment rate of new oocytes. We introduce an auxiliary PINN formulation to handle the nonlocal interaction term and jointly infer unobserved state variables and demographic functions. Our inference strategy combines non-parametric PINNs with a data-guided model-selection step: demographic functions are first inferred without prescribing their functional forms, and the learned profiles are then used to select parsimonious parametric laws, whose parameters are subsequently estimated within a parametric PINN. We investigate identifiability at both the functional and parametric levels, combining structural identifiability analysis with synthetic-data experiments assessing the practical recovery of functions and parameters. The inference procedure is embedded within an individual-level bootstrap framework to assess sensitivity to repeated-cross-sectional sampling and stochastic training. Applied to juvenile fish oogenesis, the framework recovers interpretable growth and renewal dynamics, provides access to unobserved quantities, and enables conditional in silico investigation. More broadly, this work provides a framework for functional and parametric inference in size-structured population models with nonlocal interactions from sparse cross-sectional data.

title: Parameter calibration of the simulation model for coated rice seeds in UAV seeding based on discrete element methodology.
abstract: The discrete element method (DEM) is widely used in agricultural mechanization, but accurate parameter calibration for UAV seeding simulation of coated rice seeds remains challenging due to empirical parameter selection and single-stage optimization in existing studies. This study combined physical and simulation experiments to calibrate DEM parameters for coated rice seeds (CRS). Physical tests measured the intrinsic parameters and actual repose angle (18.84°). A three-stage progressive optimization strategy was then adopted: Plackett-Burman test to screen significant parameters, steepest ascent test to narrow the optimal range, and quadratic rotation orthogonal combination test to establish a regression model. Four significant parameters were identified: the CRS-CRS coefficient of restitution (C), the CRS-CRS coefficient of static friction (D), the CRS-CRS coefficient of rolling friction (E), and the CRS-stainless steel coefficient of static friction (G). The optimal combination was determined as 0.35, 0.22, 0.09, and 0.51, respectively. Verification using static repose angle, dynamic repose angle, and UAV total seeding rate showed average relative errors below 5% for all three indices. These results demonstrate that the calibrated parameters are reliable for DEM simulation of coated rice seeds, and the proposed multi-stage method effectively improves calibration accuracy and model applicability for UAV seeding operations.

title: Pharmacological cGAS-STING pathway inhibition on neuroinflammation in animal models of traumatic brain injury: A systematic review and meta-analysis protocol.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a major cause of mortality and long-term neurological disability worldwide. Secondary injury mechanisms, particularly neuroinflammation, play a key role in determining neurological outcomes after the initial trauma. The cyclic GMP-AMP synthase stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) pathway has recently been identified as a mediator of innate immune activation following brain injury. Activation of this pathway promotes microglial activation and the release of pro-inflammatory cytokines, contributing to neuronal damage and impaired recovery. Pharmacological inhibition of the cGAS-STING signaling pathway has therefore emerged as a promising neuroprotective strategy in experimental TBI models. However, the available preclinical evidence has not yet been systematically synthesized.
METHODS: A systematic literature search was performed across MEDLINE, EMBASE and Web of Science without language or publication date restrictions. Titles and abstracts were screened independently by two reviewers, followed by independent full-text eligibility assessment. Data extraction was initiated subsequently and will be completed independently by two reviewers. Eligible studies will include in vivo animal models of TBI investigating direct or indirect pharmacological inhibition of the cGAS-STING pathway administered after injury, compared with vehicle-treated or untreated controls. The primary outcome will be quantitative measures of microglial activation within the first 72 hours post-injury, preferentially assessed using Iba1-positive cell density or percentage-stained area. Secondary outcomes will include astrocytic reactivity, cytokine expression (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6), lesion volume and neurological functional recovery. Risk of bias will be assessed using the SYRCLE tool. When appropriate, pooled effect sizes will be calculated using random-effects meta-analysis. Heterogeneity, publication bias and certainty of evidence will also be evaluated.
DISCUSSION: This systematic review and meta-analysis will help clarify the magnitude and consistency of therapeutic effects and inform the translational potential of this strategy while identifying methodological limitations that may guide future experimental and clinical research.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420261367166.

title: Predicting rate of penetration (ROP) with machine learning models: A physics-validated comparative case study of Gradient Boosting Regressor (GBR), Random Forest (RF), and K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN).
abstract: A successful drilling operation plays a vital role in the profitability of exploration and production of hydrocarbon reserves. However, these operations can come with high drilling rig rental costs. Reliable predictions of Rate of Penetration (ROP) can avoid unnecessary drilling equipment and rig rental expenses. In this study, Gradient Boosting Regressor, Random Forest, and K-Nearest Neighbours were developed to predict rate of penetration based on drilling operational data. The machine learning models were benchmarked with established empirical models, such as the Bingham and Bourgoyne and Young models, which are typically used to predict the rate of penetration. All machine learning models achieved, coefficient of determination (R2) > 0.93 and Average Absolute Percentage Error (AAPE) < 3% on the test dataset. Random Forest under Scenario 1 was identified as the most physically consistent model, attaining strong predictive performance with R2 = 0.9494 & AAPE = 1.96%, satisfying both the Weight on Bit (WOB) flounder point, and rotary speed optimum criteria used within the industry. These results support the practical use of machine learning-based ROP prediction as a reliable tool for real-time optimization of drilling parameters, offering a pathway to reduce non-productive time and rig costs while preserving the physical interpretability that drilling engineers require for field decision making.

title: Prevalence and Associated Factors of Full Immunization Coverage among children aged 12-23 months in Kenya: A multi-level logistic regression analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Full immunization coverage remains suboptimal in Kenya, despite the availability of effective vaccines. Understanding the multilevel factors influencing immunization uptake is essential for strengthening child health interventions. This study examines individual and community-level determinants of full immunization coverage among children aged 12-23 months in Kenya.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the individual and community-level factors associated with full immunization coverage among children aged from 12-23 months in Kenya using a multilevel analytical approach.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted using nationally representative survey data from Kenya. A two-level binary logistic regression model was used to identify individual- and community-level factors associated with full immunization coverage in Kenya. Adjusted odds ratios (AOR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were reported.
RESULTS: The prevalence of full immunization coverage among children aged from 12-23 months in Kenya was 79.4% (95% CI: 78.13-81.25). A total of 3790 weighted children aged from 12-23 months were included. Children whose mothers were exposed to media (AOR = 1.16, 95% CI: 1.01-1.34), delivered in health facilities (AOR = 2.88, 95% CI: 2.43-3.42), and attended antenatal care (AOR = 3.15, 95% CI: 2.10-4.73) had higher odds of full immunization. Children of average birth size (AOR = 1.68, 95% CI: 1.40-2.01) and those from rural areas (AOR = 1.44, 95% CI: 1.22-1.69) were also more likely to be fully immunized. Higher maternal education showed a strong positive association: primary (AOR = 1.60), secondary (AOR = 2.14), and higher education (AOR = 1.74). Older maternal age increased immunization odds: 25-34 years (AOR = 1.49), 35-49 years (AOR = 2.15). Conversely, households with more than two under-five children (AOR = 0.72) and higher parity (2-5 children AOR = 0.78; 6 + AOR = 0.67) had lower odds. Community-level low maternal education also reduced the odds (AOR = 0.79).
CONCLUSION AND RECOMMENDATION: Maternal age, education, parity, media exposure, antenatal care, place of delivery, place of residence, and community education levels were associated with full immunization coverage in Kenya. Interventions should focus on improving maternal education, strengthening ANC services, promoting institutional deliveries, and enhancing outreach through media and community engagement.

title: Protocol for investigating the association between Helicobacter pylori exposure, antigen-specific serological responses, and resistant versus non-resistant hypertension in a South African cohort.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension is a leading contributor to cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, with poor control in low- and middle-income countries. Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) has been associated with hypertension through inflammatory, endothelial, metabolic and immune pathways, but data from sub-Saharan Africa, particularly in resistant hypertension, are limited.
METHODS: This cross-sectional observational study will enrol 200 adults aged ≥18 at a tertiary academic hospital in Cape Town, South Africa: 80 with resistant hypertension, 80 with non-resistant hypertension and 40 with normotension. Participants will undergo standardised clinical assessment, blood pressure measurement, and collection of blood, urine and saliva. H. pylori exposure will be assessed using the Pylori DuoTect® point-of-care assay, which detects antibodies to CagA and FliD. Laboratory analyses will include lipid profile, inflammatory and nitric oxide-related markers, homocysteine, insulin indices, complete blood count, ghrelin, multiplex cytokine profiling and flow cytometric immunophenotyping. PAXgene® blood RNA samples will be retained for future exploratory analyses. Saliva will undergo exploratory H. pylori antigen testing using CerTest® kits, which are validated for stool rather than saliva. Saliva analysis will be exploratory, and results will not define the primary H. pylori exposure variable. Remaining saliva will be kept for potential future oral microbiome analyses not defined in this protocol. Multivariable logistic regression will evaluate associations between H. pylori exposure and hypertension phenotype, adjusting for demographic, lifestyle, and clinical covariates.
DISCUSSION: To our knowledge, this will be the first African study to integrate point-of-care H. pylori serology with detailed clinical, inflammatory, metabolic, and immunological profiling across resistant hypertension, non-resistant hypertension and normotension. Findings may clarify biological pathways linking H. pylori exposure to blood pressure dysregulation and inform future mechanistic and interventional studies.

title: Psychometric assessment of the Persian version of the DUSAETCS questionnaire: Duke University Self-Assessment Educational Technology Competencies.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The rapid global evolution of Information and Communication Technologies (ICT), combined with the shift toward e-learning in higher education, has made it more necessary than ever to equip faculty members with technological skills. The level of self-efficacy significantly influences technological competence in educational technology. This study aimed to translate and conduct a psychometric evaluation of the Persian version of the Duke University School of Nursing's self-assessment of educational technology competencies: DUSAETCS for faculty members.
METHOD: The psychometric properties of the DUSAETCS questionnaire, comprising 44 items, were evaluated. The original questionnaire was translated into Persian via back translation. Internal and external consistencies, factor analysis, and construct validity analysis were examined.
RESULTS: Of the initial 44 items, 26 were retained following the assessment of content validity using the Content Validity Ratio (CVR) and Content Validity Index (CVI). The overall CVI and CVR were 0.79 and 0.99, respectively. The Persian version of the questionnaire demonstrated high internal consistency, with a Cronbach's alpha coefficient of 0.92 for the total scale.
CONCLUSIONS: The findings provide preliminary evidence supporting the content validity and internal consistency of the Persian version of the DUSAETCS for assessing faculty members' educational technology competencies in the context of e-teaching. Further psychometric evaluation, particularly assessment of construct validity and other reliability measures, is recommended before broader application of the instrument.

title: Quality of maternal health services in Lagos, Nigeria: Women's perspectives across healthcare districts.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Women's perceptions of care quality during maternal health visits influence service use and maternal and neonatal outcomes. This study assesses perceived quality of maternal health services across healthcare districts in Lagos, Nigeria.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study analyzed data from 7,324 women aged 15-49 years in Lagos State from the 2022 LARCHIS Survey. It examined how demographic, reproductive, care-use, and facility factors predicted perceived maternal healthcare quality (poor/fair, good, or excellent) using multinomial logistic and mixed-effects models.
RESULTS: Among 7,324 women (mean age: 31.2 ± 5.9 years), perceived service quality varied significantly by district and facility type. Compared with District I, women in District III were less likely to rate services as good (aOR = 0.37; 95% CI: 0.24-0.56) or excellent (aOR = 0.08; 95% CI: 0.05-0.14), whereas women in District V had higher odds. Lack of response to inquiries was associated with lower odds of rating services as good (aOR = 0.12; 95% CI: 0.08-0.18) or excellent (aOR = 0.06; 95% CI: 0.03-0.16). Rude staff behavior similarly reduced the odds of good ratings (aOR = 0.15; 95% CI: 0.11-0.21) and excellent ratings (aOR = 0.06; 95% CI: 0.06-0.13). Missionary and private facilities received higher ratings than public facilities. Facility readiness-24-hour services, doctor availability, and skilled staff-predicted higher ratings, whereas long waits and closures predicted lower ratings. Staff courtesy and responsiveness were the strongest predictors.
CONCLUSION: Women's perceptions of maternal healthcare in Lagos are shaped by structural and interpersonal factors. Improving facility readiness, reducing delays, and promoting respectful care may improve experiences, service use, and maternal and neonatal outcomes.

title: Research on impact dynamic characteristics of hydraulic column cylinder barrel.
abstract: During the loading process of a hydraulic column, the magnitude and distribution of stress in the cylinder barrel are critical to the safety of the hydraulic column. Aiming at the problem of stress distribution in the cylinder barrel of a hydraulic column under liquid pressure, a mathematical model of cylinder barrel stress is established based on the thick-walled cylinder theory and the fundamental theory of rotating shells. It is concluded that the main factors affecting the stress distribution of the hydraulic column cylinder barrel are the inner diameter of the cylinder barrel, the wall thickness of the cylinder barrel, and the height of the rodless chamber of the column. Numerical simulation, response surface methodology, and experimental research are adopted. The results show that the stress of the hydraulic column cylinder barrel exhibits an "M-shaped" distribution, with the stress peak located at the bottom of the cylinder barrel and near the piston. Among the selected structural parameters, the difference between the stress peak of the cylinder barrel and the stress valley at the cavity is most significantly affected by the height of the rodless chamber, followed by the inner diameter of the cylinder barrel, while the influence of the cylinder barrel wall thickness is the smallest. Through the response surface prediction model, it is found that when the inner diameter of the cylinder barrel is 230 mm, the wall thickness is 20 mm, and the height of the rodless chamber is 795 mm, the "M-shaped" characteristic of the stress distribution in the cylinder barrel becomes more obvious, which provides useful guidance for the design and safety assessment of hydraulic columns.

title: Sequence-based coevolutionary prediction of species-specific interactomes.
abstract: Evolutionarily conserved protein-protein interactions (PPIs) reveal fundamental biological processes. However, predicting protein function solely from these interactions provides an incomplete picture of biological systems. Computational methods for predicting PPIs often struggle due to limited functional annotations in databases, making it difficult to fully understand unique biological systems. This study introduces ContextMirror2.0 (CM2.0), a coevolution-based method designed to address these limitations. Coevolutionary approaches, unlike supervised machine learning methods, do not rely on labelled datasets, proving valuable in addressing the scarcity of data for species-specific PPIs. Around 40% of CM2.0's top-1000 predicted PPIs for E. coli, S. enterica, and S. aureus are supported by experimental PPI databases. However, comparative analysis of the resulting functional communities further revealed both highly conserved interaction patterns and species-specific interactions. CM2.0 leverages coevolutionary information at the phylogenetic level to explore protein interaction dynamics and understand the functional consequences of species-specific variations. This information can inform further studies on the emergence of novel functions, adaptation to specific environments, and the development of targeted therapies.

title: Source apportionment and non-carcinogenic health risk assessment of selected heavy metals in the Turag river area of Gazipur District, Bangladesh.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Rapid industrialization in Bangladesh, especially in Gazipur District, has raised concern over heavy metal contamination of soil and water and the associated health risks to nearby residents. This study compared the concentration, spatial distribution, probable sources, and non-carcinogenic health risk of five heavy metals (Hg, Ni, Mn, Zn, and Co) in soil and water in the Turag River areas in Gazipur District.
METHODS: Soil and water samples were collected from 18 sites in the Turag River (including both industrial and non-industrial zones) and analyzed for five heavy metal concentrations (Hg, Ni, Mn, Zn, and Co) using inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry (ICP-MS). Statistical analyses included principal component analysis (PCA), hierarchical cluster analysis (HCA), and Pearson correlation analysis, while non-carcinogenic human health risks were evaluated using the USEPA-based chronic daily intake (CDI), hazard quotient (HQ), and hazard index (HI) models for both adults and children.
RESULTS: Mean soil metal concentrations followed the order Mn > Zn > Ni > Co > Hg in both zones, with markedly higher and more spatially concentrated Ni and Zn levels in the industrial zone near the Turag River areas. Spatial mapping, PCA, HCA, and correlation analyses consistently suggested a common anthropogenic influence on soil and water contamination in the industrial zone, with the strongest spatial concentrations observed near its northern boundary, compared with patterns consistent with multiple diffuse influences in the non-industrial zone. The modeled soil CDI values were generally higher for children than adults. Soil-based screening estimates indicated potential non-carcinogenic concern for children, including an Ni HQ of 1.66 in the industrial zone and cumulative hazard index values above the screening benchmark of 1 for children in both the industrial (HI = 2.32) and non-industrial (HI = 1.31) zones, while all modeled HQ and HI values for water remained below the screening benchmark of 1.
CONCLUSION: These soil-based screening estimates suggest potential non-carcinogenic concern for children, particularly regarding Ni in the industrial zone, but are based on the < 0.5 mm fraction of soil collected at 15-20 cm depth and may not represent actual exposure to ground-surface soil or airborne particles. The study highlighted the need for targeted control of potential industrial sources and child-focused environmental health monitoring in industrializing peri-urban districts of Bangladesh.

title: Sperm phospholipase C signaling via PLCζ1 and PLCδ4 is essential for Ca2+ oscillations and fertility in mice.
abstract: Fertilization-induced calcium (Ca2+) oscillations are essential for egg activation and embryonic development in mammals. The sperm-specific phospholipase C isoform, PLCζ1, is the primary trigger of these oscillations. Functional and clinical studies have linked mutations or reduced expression of PLCζ1 to male infertility. However, whether PLCζ1 alone accounts for Ca2+ release at fertilization in all mammals remains uncertain. Male mice lacking Plcζ1 exhibit subfertility and reduced litter sizes; their sperm induce delayed, low-frequency Ca2+ oscillations, indicating a compensatory mechanism. Notably, mouse sperm express high levels of PLCδ4, essential for completing the acrosome reaction (AR). In Plcζ1-null sperm, PLCδ4 is upregulated and retained post-AR. These observations suggest a secondary functional role for PLCδ4. Using CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing, we generated Plcδ4 knockout (KO) mice. Plcδ4-null sperm trigger attenuated, delayed Ca2+ oscillations and significantly reduced fertilization rates, indicating that PLCδ4 contributes to but does not independently drive Ca2+ signaling. We therefore generated a Double Knockout (DKO) mouse line lacking both sperm-enriched PLCs. DKO males were sterile, with sperm failing to induce Ca2+ oscillations, and the isolated residual Ca2+ rise was insufficient to activate eggs. These findings reveal that PLCζ1, the primary oscillator, and PLCδ4, a compensatory factor, work cooperatively within a complex, multi-component PLC system that ensures robust fertilization. This work reveals molecular specialization among mammals in initiating the fertilization Ca2+ signals. It has implications for understanding male infertility, improving assisted reproductive technologies, and developing contraceptive strategies.

title: Spruce-derived extracellular vesicles (SDEVs) improve hair loss by activating the proliferation of dermal papilla cells.
abstract: Hair loss is a global health problem, and current conventional treatments, despite their effectiveness in delaying hair loss and improving hair growth, suffer from significant side effects and limitations in individualized treatment. In recent years, the application of novel nanotechnology in dermatology and regenerative medicine has gained attention. In this context, researchers explored the potential of applying Spruce-Derived Extracellular Vesicles (SDEVs) to hair loss intervention. Through in vitro experiments and in vivo animal models, it was found that Spruce-Derived Extracellular Vesicles (SDEVs) could improve hair follicles by activating the proliferation of Dermal papilla cells (DPCs) to intervene in hair loss. Spruce-Derived Extracellular Vesicles (SDEVs) significantly improved hair weight, thickness, and luster, and reduced the inflammatory response associated with hair loss compared with conventional treatments. These findings provide new ideas for hair regrowth treatments and demonstrate the potential therapeutic value of Spruce-Derived Extracellular Vesicles (SDEVs) in hair loss prevention.

title: Stroke disability burden and rehabilitation service-capacity proxies in China, 1990-2023: A population-based analysis using GBD 2023 and national service statistics.
abstract: China's stroke burden is increasingly shaped by survival with disability, population ageing, and demand for rehabilitation and long-term support. Yet the extent to which stroke disability burden has shifted towards older-old and oldest-old adults, and how this burden relates to community and elder-care service capacity, remains insufficiently quantified. We conducted a population-based secondary analysis of Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 estimates for China from 1990 to 2023, focusing on ischaemic stroke and intracerebral haemorrhage. We examined disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), years lived with disability (YLDs), YLD share of DALYs, age-specific patterns among adults aged 50 years or older, estimated annual percentage changes (EAPCs), and three-factor decomposition of absolute DALY changes. We also linked 2023 stroke YLDs with national community health and elder-care service indicators as descriptive capacity proxies. From 1990 to 2023, the YLD share of DALYs increased from 10.5% to 22.3% for ischaemic stroke and from 1.8% to 3.3% for intracerebral haemorrhage. The crude all-age ischaemic stroke YLD rate increased by 2.75% per year (95% CI 2.68 to 2.82), while the crude all-age intracerebral haemorrhage DALY rate declined but its YLD rate and YLD share increased. Crude all-age rates were interpreted as population-level burden indicators influenced by population age structure, alongside age-stratified and decomposition analyses. Among adults aged 50 years or older, disability burden shifted towards older-old and oldest-old groups, particularly for ischaemic stroke. In 2023, combined all-age YLDs from ischaemic stroke and intracerebral haemorrhage were approximately 4.77 million, corresponding descriptively to 128.2 YLDs per community health service centre/station and 16.7 YLDs per community health bed. Stroke in China is increasingly a survivorship and disability challenge. The burden-to-capacity proxy indicators provide planning context but do not directly measure rehabilitation access, adequacy, quality, or unmet need.

title: SwimmingIndividuals: A high-performance agent-based model for marine ecosystems.
abstract: Because they are based on established theory, mechanistic models are essential for projecting ecological responses to novel conditions. Yet mechanistic agent-based model (ABM) applications have often been limited by computational constraints. This paper introduces SwimmingIndividuals, an open-source ABM framework that advances our ability to simulate physiological processes, animal movement, higher trophic level marine ecosystem dynamics, and fisheries removals at large ecological scales. The software's key contributions are a suite of mechanistic sub-models governing the full life cycle of each agent, including visual prey detection, adaptive behaviors such as diel vertical migration (DVM), a flexible bioenergetics engine with three taxon-specific metabolic architectures, and a spatial pathfinding algorithm for habitat-seeking movement. These processes are made computationally tractable through a hybrid CPU/GPU architecture written in Julia. Unlike prior ABMs that use fixed perception radii or single-equation bioenergetics, SwimmingIndividuals enables emergent ecological dynamics across populations of superindividual agents. We demonstrate the framework through three Gulf of America simulations. The model reproduced DVM, cetacean diving patterns, size-based trophic shifts, and von Bertalanffy growth curves consistent with published King Mackerel stock assessments. Long-term simulations generated realistic population dynamics and quantified impacts of fishery harvest control rules across five fleets. SwimmingIndividuals provides a powerful, flexible, open-source platform for mechanistic marine ecosystem research and ecosystem-based fisheries management.

title: Ten simple rules for a department chair.
abstract: Department chairs occupy a pivotal position in the university. Teaching, research, graduate education, and much of the academic community's professional and administrative activity are organized at the departmental level. Yet, despite the importance of the position and the considerable challenges it entails, many scientists assume the role with little or no formal preparation for academic leadership. This paper is intended as a practical primer rather than a comprehensive guide to academic leadership. The proposed rules provide a framework that prospective and current department chairs can adapt to their own institutional circumstances, experience, and leadership style.

title: Testing the effects of nicotine concentration and nicotine source claims on oral nicotine pouch packaging engagement, self-reported perceptions and use intentions, and product trial in young adults and adults: Protocol for a randomized trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Oral nicotine pouches (ONPs) are novel nicotine products and evidence on how features of ONP packaging affect product engagement, perceptions, use intentions, and behavior is limited.
OBJECTIVES: We outline the protocol for a randomized trial examining how nicotine concentration and nicotine source claims affect engagement with ONP packaging using psychophysiological measures, self-reported ONP perceptions and use intentions, and ONP trial (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06192316).
METHODS: Between 2024 and 2027, we will recruit 450 participants, comprised of: 150 young adults ages 18-24 who are susceptible but do not use tobacco; 150 young adults ages 18-24 who use tobacco; and 150 adults ages 25-65 who use tobacco. Participants complete procedures at an in-person laboratory visit. During the visit, participants complete pre-exposure self-report measures and are randomized between subjects to one of nine conditions in a 3 (Nicotine Concentration: None, Low, or High) x 3 (Nicotine Source Claim: None, Tobacco Free, or Synthetic) design. Within conditions, participants view 16 ONP pack images, in random order, reflecting different ONP brands and flavors. During exposure, we collect psychophysiological measures including heart rate, skin conductance, and visual attention. After exposure, participants complete self-report measures of ONP perceptions and use intentions, and a timed behavioral task where they are presented with ONP packages corresponding to their randomized condition and brands and flavors shown in the stimuli. Participants can try one of the products, and ONP trial is the behavioral outcome of interest. However, the packages do not contain ONPs; they contain commercially available pouches with food grade ingredients. At visit conclusion, participants are de-briefed and receive their incentive for participating.
CONCLUSIONS: This project will generate evidence on the effects of nicotine concentration and source claims on ONP packaging in young adults who are not using but susceptible to tobacco, young adults using tobacco, and adults using tobacco to inform potential regulations.

title: The mediating role of empathy in the association between interpersonal communication competence and attitudes toward disability in higher education.
abstract: Developing positive attitudes toward people with disabilities is crucial for social equality and integration. This study examines the relationship between university students' attitudes toward people with disabilities, their empathy levels, and their interpersonal communication competence, with a focus on the mediating role of empathy. Data from 587 students were collected using a cross-sectional survey design and analyzed using correlation analysis and path analysis-based mediation modeling. The findings indicate that higher empathy and communication competence are associated with more positive attitudes and lower levels of prejudice. Empathy partially mediated the association between communication competence and egalitarian attitudes, whereas the indirect association between communication competence and prejudiced attitudes was not statistically significant. In addition, demographic factors such as gender and age were associated with attitudes, with female students reporting more positive views. These results underline the relevance of empathy and communication skills for inclusive attitudes and suggest that higher education institutions may consider policies that strengthen these competencies. Overall, this study contributes to understanding how empathy and communication are associated with disability-related attitudes in higher education.

title: The role of digital and AI-based tools in music theory education.
abstract: This study examined the role of digital platforms and artificial intelligence in music theory instruction from the perspectives of both students and instructors. Using a convergent mixed-methods design, data were collected through questionnaires administered to 47 undergraduate students and 9 instructors. Quantitative responses were analyzed descriptively, while open-ended responses were examined through inductive thematic analysis. The findings indicated that students associated these tools with increased engagement, perceived support for understanding complex theoretical concepts, and individualized learning opportunities. Written responses further suggested that flexible access and visual representations were particularly valuable in facilitating comprehension. Instructors, however, emphasized the importance of clear content, accurate information, and an awareness of practical limitations in classroom implementation. Although both groups acknowledged the potential of these technologies, their reasons for valuing them differed. Overall, the findings suggest that digital and AI-based tools may be particularly valuable when they are meaningfully integrated into everyday teaching practice, rather than being used as stand-alone additions. Their perceived educational value appears to depend not only on technical sophistication but also on alignment with instructional goals. Teacher readiness also appeared to be an important consideration in the effective integration of these tools. As automation assumes an increasingly prominent role in education, adapting resources to diverse learning needs appears to be of growing importance.

title: Tranexamic acid for anemia in women of reproductive age: A systematic review of randomized trials.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The global target to halve the prevalence of anemia by 2025 has not been met. New strategies are needed. This systematic review examined the effect of tranexamic acid on anemia, menstrual health and wellbeing in women of reproductive age.
METHODS: We searched six databases from inception to 30 August 2025 and reference lists of seven related reviews. We included randomized trials comparing the effects of tranexamic acid with placebo or standard care on uterine bleeding. Eligible participants had normal menstrual bleeding or any type of non-pregnant abnormal uterine bleeding. Outcomes included hemoglobin concentration and anemia prevalence as the primary outcome, estimated blood loss, quality of life, thromboembolic events, and other adverse events. We conducted meta-analyses and assessed risk of bias (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials) and the certainty of evidence.
RESULTS: We included 17 trials in the review and 15 in the meta-analyses. None of the trials reported adequate data on hemoglobin concentration. For the anemia outcome, only one small trial contributed data (risk ratio 0.15, 95% confidence interval 0.01 to 2.74, very low certainty). Meta-analyses of secondary outcomes showed that tranexamic acid reduced objectively measured menstrual blood loss among women with heavy menstrual bleeding (6 trials, mean difference -47.0 milliliters, 95% confidence interval -56.6 to -37.4, I2 = 13%, moderate certainty) and in women with intrauterine devices (3 trials, mean difference -41.6 milliliters, 95% confidence interval -52.2 to -30.9, I2 = 64%, low certainty) and improved quality of life in women with heavy menstrual bleeding (2 trials, mean difference 0.5, 95% confidence interval 0.4 to 0.7, I2 = 0%, moderate certainty). The risk of nausea or vomiting was similar between groups (4 trials, risk ratio 1.0, 95% confidence interval 0.6 to 1.8, I2 = 0%, moderate certainty). Certainty of evidence for other outcomes ranged from very low to low, including for thromboembolic events, with only one event reported in the control arm of one trial.
CONCLUSIONS: Tranexamic acid appears to reduce menstrual blood loss, but its impact on anemia is unclear. High-quality randomized trials of TXA for menstruating women with anemia are needed.

title: Uncovering the immune microenvironmental atlas of breast cancer molecular subtypes based on single-cell transcriptomics.
abstract: Breast cancer progression is closely linked to immune cells within the tumor microenvironment (TME), but the immune landscape differences across HER2-positive (HER2+), triple-negative (TNBC), and ER-positive (ER+) subtypes have yet to be systematically characterized. In this study, we characterized immune landscape differences across HER2-positive (HER2+), triple-negative (TNBC), and ER-positive (ER+) breast cancers using single-cell RNA sequencing data, focusing on T cells, macrophages, and B cells. Our analysis revealed that cytotoxic CD8 + T cells were more abundant in TNBC but showed signs of dysfunction. Macrophage subsets, including an NDUFB8 + population, exhibited divergent functional orientations across subtypes. B cells in TNBC exhibited functional alterations, characterized by a decreased proportion of plasmablasts and an increased proportion of memory B cells. Single-cell regulatory network inference and clustering (SCENIC) analysis predicted a set of subtype-specific candidate transcription factors (TFs), including E2F8 across all subtypes and ATF7 in HER2 + tumors, whose activity correlated with clinical outcomes. Finally, mapping multicellular communication networks revealed both conserved and subtype-specific signaling pathways. Together, these results present a detailed transcriptional landscape of immune heterogeneity in breast cancer and contribute novel insights that may inform the design of subtype-specific immunotherapies.

title: Validation of chemical inactivation methods for Select Agent compliance using HPAIV and low-pathogenicity influenza A virus in tissues and cultured cells.
abstract: The US Federal Select Agent program requires that inactivation procedures be validated before treated materials can be removed from biocontainment for downstream use. Although H5 avian influenza viruses are subject to temporary exemption from the Select Agent regulatory requirements, validated inactivation workflows remain critical for safe downstream handling of HPAIV-containing materials. Common treatments, including TRIzol, TRIzol LS, formalin, and ice-cold methanol, are frequently used to facilitate virus inactivation and downstream processing. However, facility-specific inactivation validation is required for Select Agent workflows and for safe handling of HPAIV-containing materials. In this study, HPAIV (H5N1)-infected samples were used to validate inactivation of material generated in cell culture, and low-pathogenicity (H1N1)-infected lung homogenates were used to validate inactivation of animal-derived tissues. Following inactivation, column-based buffer exchange was used to remove cytotoxic inactivants before viability testing. This step did not significantly reduce recovery of infectious virus, supporting the sensitivity of this approach. In inactivation tests, residual infectious virus was assessed by plaque assay and serial blind passages. No infectious virus was detected following any of the tested conditions. These data validate several procedures for inactivating influenza A virus-containing cell cultures, fluids, and tissue samples and provide a framework for facility-specific validation of similar workflows.

title: Various aspects of upper-limb muscle strength and tennis performance: A comparative study of U12 and U14 female tennis players.
abstract: This study investigated the relationship between muscle strength and tennis performance, assessed using the International Tennis Number (ITN) on-court test, operationalized as point-based outcomes (total points and subcomponent points), in young female tennis players aged under 12 (U12) and under 14 (U14). Thirty-three players underwent a comprehensive evaluation including ITN testing, general strength tests (handgrip strength, flexed arm hang, and tennis-ball throw), isometric upper-limb muscle strength, and sense of force assessment. Results demonstrated significantly higher ITN scores and muscle strength in the U14 group, with differences largely attributable to body size and training experience. Correlation analyses revealed age-specific patterns: in U12 players, ITN scores were associated primarily with general strength measures, whereas in U14 players, they were more strongly linked to joint-specific upper-limb strength and neuromuscular characteristics. Sense of force did not differ between groups, though correlations with ITN varied depending on age and joint function. These findings suggest that, in this sample, performance in younger players was more closely associated with general strength measures, whereas in older players it was more closely associated with joint-specific upper-limb strength.

title: Visual outcomes and headache in intracranial hypertension following cerebral venous sinus thrombosis: A retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Intracranial hypertension is a frequent complication of cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVT), posing a risk for permanent visual impairment. However, long-term visual outcomes have not been systematically assessed using objective neuro-ophthalmic measures. We retrospectively evaluated consecutive adults presenting to a single-center tertiary intracranial hypertension clinic between 2019 and 2025 with intracranial hypertension following CVT. Visual outcomes were assessed using best-corrected visual acuity, automated perimetry, and optical coherence tomography measuring global peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer thickness. Headache phenotype and medication overuse were documented. Nineteen patients (11 female; mean age 33.4 ± 12.1 years) were included, with a mean follow-up of 3.4 ± 2.4 years after diagnosis of CVT-related intracranial hypertension. The transverse sinus was involved in 78.9% of cases, and complete or near-complete recanalization was achieved in 68.4%. Although visual acuity remained normal in most patients (84.2%), 26.3% had severe visual field loss and 15.8% showed retinal nerve fiber layer thinning. Headache persisted in 94.7%, most commonly as tension-type headache (63.2%), and 26.3% fulfilled criteria for medication overuse headache. Despite generally preserved visual acuity, substantial visual field deficits and persistent headache were common in CVT-related intracranial hypertension. These findings support routine neuro-ophthalmic follow-up to facilitate early detection of visual deterioration in CVT-related intracranial hypertension. As this cohort was drawn from a specialized tertiary referral clinic, these findings should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating rather than representative of the broader CVT population.

title: When AI simulates teaching personas: Linguistic dimensions of LLM-generated classroom discourse.
abstract: This study investigates how GPT-4o constructs the social role of teacher through discourse and how this discourse compares with naturally occurring classroom teaching. We generated 19,950 AI classroom teaching texts from a corpus of online college teaching using 56 teacher personas plus a baseline condition. The AI-generated texts contained the original student turns alongside the AI-teacher turns. We analyzed the resulting corpus using Lexical Multi-Dimensional Analysis (LMDA), a bottom-up corpus-linguistic method that identifies dimensions of discourse variation from recurrent patterns of lexical covariation. Five dimensions emerged: Macro-Structuring Discourse vs. Performative Stagecraft, L1-scaffolded Guidance vs. Provocative Challenge, Procedural Control vs. Rapport-driven Engagement, Evaluative Control vs. Reflective Aesthetic Engagement, and Informal Facilitation vs. Formal Deductive Exposition. Comparison with the corresponding human classroom discourse showed that GPT-4o frequently magnified teaching discourses already present in human interaction, particularly organizational, procedural, and expository discourse. It also introduced more artificial forms of teaching discourse characterized by theatrical performance, confrontation, and evaluative pressure. Mixed-effects analyses showed significant differences between human and AI discourse on all five dimensions. Persona prompting also affected dimension scores, but differentiation among the 57 conditions was uneven: many personas occupied overlapping positions, and differences occurred on only some dimensions. The findings show that GPT-4o can produce distinct forms of teaching discourse, yet many different persona prompts repeat similar discourses, suggesting a saturation point beyond which the LLM cannot yield new teaching discourses. More generally, the study demonstrates how corpus-based discourse analysis can characterize the forms of teaching that emerge when an LLM is instructed to perform a professional role.
